An advocate for a particular group is a person who works for the interests of that group.

Chinesesense: 航空的；飞机的；由飞机进行的；空中的；

Englishsense: Aerobic activity exercises and strengthens your heart and lungs.

If something or someone affects you, they make you feel a strong emotion, especially sadness or pity.
If you affect a particular characteristic or way of behaving, you pretend that it is genuine, or natural for you.
If you describe someone’s behaviour as affected, you disapprove of the fact that they behave in an unnatural way that is intended to impress other people.
If you regard someone or something with affection, you like them and are fond of them.
Your affections are your feelings of love or fondness for someone.

If a professional person such as a lawyer or doctor affiliates with an organization, they become officially connected with that organization.

个人之间或个人与组织之间的联系，从属关系；
Englishsense: If one group has an affiliation with another group, it has a close or official connection with it.
If you have an affiliation with a group or another person, you have a close or official connection with them.
If you have an affinity with someone or something, you feel that you are similar to them or that you know and understand them very well.
If people or things have an affinity with each other, they are similar in some ways.
If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or exists.
If an event affirms something, it shows that it is true or exists.
An affirmative word or gesture indicates that you agree with what someone has said or that the answer to a question is ’yes’.
If you reply to a question in the affirmative, you say ’yes’ or make a gesture that means ’yes’.
In grammar, an affirmative clause is positive and does not contain a negative word.
If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or disaster, it affects you badly and makes you suffer.

Englishsense: If you are affluent, you have a lot of money.
If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.
If you say that you cannot afford to do something or allow it to happen, you mean that you must not do it or must prevent it from happening because it would be harmful or embarrassing to you.
If someone or something affords you an opportunity or protection, they give it to you.

Chinesesense: 价格合理的;多数人买得起的；

If you are afraid that something unpleasant will happen, you are worried that it may happen and you want to avoid it.
If you want to apologize to someone or to disagree with them in a polite way, you can say I’m afraid.

African is used to describe someone, usually a black person, who comes from Africa.
African-Americans are black people living in the United States who are descended from families that originally came from Africa.

Englishsense: If something happens after a particular date or event, it happens during the period of time that follows that date or event.
If you do one thing after doing another, you do it during the period of time that follows the other thing.

You use after when you are talking about time. For example, if something is going to happen during the day after or the weekend after a particular time, it is going to happen during the following day or during the following weekend.
If you go after someone, you follow or chase them.
If you are after something, you are trying to get it.
If you call, shout, or stare after someone, you call, shout, or stare at them as they move away from you.
If you do something after someone, you do it for them, because they cannot or will not do it for themselves.
If you tell someone that one place is a particular distance after another, you mean that it is situated beyond the other place and further away from you.
If one thing is written after another thing on a page, it is written following it or underneath it.
You use after in order to give the most important aspect of something when comparing it with another aspect.
To be named after someone means to be given the same name as them.
If you say ’ after you ’ to someone, you are being polite and allowing them to go in front of you or through a doorway before you do.
After is used when telling the time. If it is, for example, ten after six, the time is ten minutes past six.
If you do something to several things one after the other or one after another, you do it to one, then the next, and so on, with no break between your actions.
If something happens day after day or year after year, it happens every day or every year, for a long time.
The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.
The afternoon is the part of each day which begins at lunchtime and ends at about six o’clock.

Chinesesense: 某个事件或已提及的时间之后；
Englishsense: If you do something or if something happens afterwards, you do it or it happens after a particular event or time that has already been mentioned. See usage note at: after

Englishsense: You use again to indicate that something happens a second time, or after it has already happened before.
You use again to indicate that something is now in a particular state or place that it used to be in.
You can use again when you want to point out that there is a similarity between the subject that you are talking about now and a previous subject.
You can use again in expressions such as but again, then again, and there again when you want to introduce a remark which contrasts with or weakens something that you have just said.
You can add again to the end of your question when you are asking someone to tell you something that you have forgotten or that they have already told you.

You can use again and again or time and again to emphasize that something happens many times.

If you have something against someone or something, you dislike them.
If something is against the law or against the rules, there is a law or a rule which says that you must not do it.
If you are moving against a current, tide, or wind, you are moving in the opposite direction to it.

If you discuss a particular set of facts or figures as against another set, you are comparing or contrasting the two sets of facts or figures.

When someone comes of age, they become legally an adult.
Someone who is under age is not legally old enough to do something, for example to buy an alcoholic drink.
You use aged followed by a number to say how old someone is.
Aged means very old.
You can refer to all people who are very old as the aged.

If something happens ahead of an event or time, it happens before that event or time.

If someone is ahead of someone else, they have made more progress and are more advanced in what they are doing.

If you come or go to someone’s aid, you try to help them when they are in danger or difficulty.

If you aim a kick or punch at someone, you try to kick or punch them.
When you take aim, you point a weapon or object at someone or something, before firing or throwing it.
If you take aim at someone or something, you criticize them strongly.

If you say that someone or something has a particular air, you mean that they give this general impression.
If you say that someone is putting on airs or giving themselves airs, you are criticizing them for behaving as if they are better than other people.

If you air your opinions, you make them known to people.

If you say that you are walking on air or floating on air, you mean that you feel extremely happy about something.

Chinesesense: 飞机升空的，空中的，在飞行中的；

Airborne means in the air or carried in the air.

An airplane is a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that enable it to fly through the air.

If you appreciate something, for example a piece of music or good food, you like it because you recognize its good qualities.
If you appreciate a situation or problem, you understand it and know what it involves.
If you appreciate something that someone has done for you or is going to do for you, you are grateful for it.

Englishsense: Appreciation of something is the recognition and enjoyment of its good qualities.

An appreciation of a situation or problem is an understanding of what it involves.
Appreciation in the value of something is an increase in its value over a period of time.
An appreciation of an artist or performer or of their work is a speech or piece of writing in which they are discussed and assessed.

The apprehension of something is awareness and understanding of it.
An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.
If a young person is apprenticed to someone, they go to work for them in order to learn their skill.
When you approach something, you get closer to it.

If you approach someone about something, you speak to them about it for the first time, often making an offer or request.
When you approach a task, problem, or situation in a particular way, you deal with it or think about it in that way.
Your approach to a task, problem, or situation is the way you deal with it or think about it.
As a future time or event approaches, it gradually gets nearer as time passes.
As you approach a future time or event, time passes so that you get gradually nearer to it.
If something approaches a particular level or state, it almost reaches that level or state.

If you approve of someone or something, you like and admire them.

When you articulate your ideas or feelings, you express them clearly in words.
If you articulate something, you say it very clearly, so that each word or syllable can be heard.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 假装的；虚伪的；矫揉造作的；
味道、外观不自然的，不真实的，添加非天然成分的；
Englishsense: Artificial objects, materials, or processes do not occur naturally and are created by human beings, for example using science or technology.
An artificial state or situation exists only because someone has created it, and therefore often seems unnatural or unnecessary.
If you describe someone or their behaviour as artificial, you disapprove of them because they pretend to have attitudes and feelings which they do not really have.
If you say that food tastes or looks artificial, you do not like it because its taste or appearance does not seem genuine, and seems to be created by added substances.
Artillery consists of large, powerful guns which are transported on wheels and used by an army.
The artillery is the section of an army which is trained to use large, powerful guns.
An artisan is someone whose job requires skill with their hands.

Chinesesense: 艺术家如小说家、诗人、导演等；
Englishsense: An artist is someone who draws or paints pictures or creates sculptures as a job or a hobby.
An artist is a person who creates novels, poems, films, or other things which can be considered as works of art.
An artist is a performer such as a musician, actor, or dancer.
If you say that someone is an artist at a particular activity, you mean they are very skilled at it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 有艺术天赋的;有艺术鉴赏力的；
Englishsense: Someone who is artistic is good at drawing or painting, or arranging things in a beautiful way.
Artistic means relating to art or artists.
An artistic design or arrangement is beautiful.
Artwork is drawings and photographs that are prepared in order to be included in something such as a book or advertisement.
Artworks are paintings or sculptures which are of high quality.

Chinesesense: 表示两件事情同时发生当…的时候，在…的同时；
事实上，实际上表示实际情况和可能情况的对比；
Englishsense: If something happens as something else happens, it happens at the same time.
You use the structure as...as when you are comparing things.
You use as...as to emphasize amounts of something.
You use as when you are indicating what someone or something is or is thought to be, or what function they have.
If you do something as a child or as a teenager, for example, you do it when you are a child or a teenager.
You use as to say how something happens or is done, or to indicate that something happens or is done in the same way as something else.
You use as in expressions like as a result and as a consequence to indicate how two situations or events are related to each other.
You use as to introduce short clauses which comment on the truth of what you are saying.
You can use as to mean ’because’ when you are explaining the reason for something.
You say as it were in order to make what you are saying sound less definite.
You use expressions such as as it is, as it turns out, and as things stand when you are making a contrast between a possible situation and what actually happened or is the case.
You use as for and as to at the beginning of a sentence in order to introduce a slightly different subject that is still connected to the previous one.
You use as to to indicate what something refers to.
If you say that something will happen as of, or in British English as from, a particular date or time, you mean that it will happen from that time on.
You use as if and as though when you are giving a possible explanation for something or saying that something appears to be the case when it is not.
Asbestos is a grey material which does not burn and which has been used as a protection against fire or heat.

Chinesesense: 升迁；升职；(君主)登基,即位；
事业、社会地位提高；晋升；
在某些宗教中指灵魂升天，进入天堂；
Englishsense: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it.
If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher position.
If something ascends, it moves up, usually vertically or into the air.
If someone ascends to an important position, they achieve it or are appointed to it. When someone ascends a throne, they become king, queen, or pope.
If you ascend in your career or in society, you gradually achieve success or a higher status.
In some religions, when someone’s soul goes to heaven, you can say that they ascend to heaven.
If something or someone ascends to a higher level, they reach a state that is better than the one they were in before.

Chinesesense: 尤指经过努力后查明，弄清，确定；
Englishsense: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.
Ash is the grey or black powdery substance that is left after something is burnt. You can also refer to this substance as ashes.
A dead person’s ashes are their remains after their body has been cremated.
An ash is a tree that has smooth grey bark and loses its leaves in winter.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: 为…感到羞耻的，感到难为情的；
羞于…的；因尴尬而不愿…的；
Englishsense: If someone is ashamed, they feel embarrassed or guilty because of something they do or they have done, or because of their appearance.
If you are ashamed of someone, you feel embarrassed to be connected with them, often because of their appearance or because you disapprove of something they have done.
If someone is ashamed to do something, they do not want to do it because they feel embarrassed about it.
Someone or something that comes ashore comes from the sea onto the shore.

Chinesesense: 亚洲人的，亚洲的英国人尤用此词指称印度、巴基斯坦和孟加拉，美国人尤用此词指称中国、朝鲜、韩国、泰国、日本和越南；
Englishsense: Someone or something that is Asian comes from or is associated with Asia. British people use this term especially to refer to India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. Americans use this term especially to refer to China, Korea, Thailand, Japan, or Vietnam.

Chinesesense: 把…放或移向一边，到一边；
同apart from通常用于美国英语；
Englishsense: If you move something aside, you move it to one side of you.
If you take or draw someone aside, you take them a little way away from a group of people in order to talk to them in private.
If you move aside, you get out of someone’s way.
If you set something such as time, money, or space aside for a particular purpose, you save it and do not use it for anything else.
If you brush or sweep aside a feeling or suggestion, you reject it.
You use aside to indicate that you have finished talking about something, or that you are leaving it out of your discussion, and that you are about to talk about something else.
An aside is a comment that a character in a play makes to the audience, which the other characters are supposed not to be able to hear.
An aside is something that you say that is not directly connected with what you are talking about.
Aside from means the same as apart from. This form is more usual in American English.

Chinesesense: 请求，征求许可、意见、谅解；
通常用于表示对询问感到恼怒或惊讶不要问我；
只要开口[便可得到]; 唾手可得；
强调反对请问，真是，这还了得；
一种正式的询问方式，表示感到困扰或心生疑虑请问；
Englishsense: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.
If you ask someone to do something, you tell them that you want them to do it.
If you ask to do something, you tell someone that you want to do it.
If you ask for something, you say that you would like it.
If you ask for someone, you say that you would like to speak to them.
If you ask someone’s permission, opinion, or forgiveness, you try to obtain it by putting a request to them.
If you ask someone to an event or place, you invite them to go there.
If someone is asking a particular price for something, they are selling it for that price.
You reply ’ don’t ask me ’ when you do not know the answer to a question, usually when you are annoyed or surprised that you have been asked.
If something is yours for the asking, you could get it very easily if you wanted to.
If you say ’ I ask you ’, you are emphasizing how much you disapprove of someone or something. [emphasis]
You can say ’ may I ask ’ as a formal way of asking a question, which shows you are annoyed or suspicious about something.
You can say ’ if you ask me ’ to emphasize that you are stating your personal opinion.
If you say that someone is asking for trouble or is asking for it, you mean that they are behaving in a way that makes it very likely that they will get into trouble.
Someone who is asleep is sleeping.
When you fall asleep, you start sleeping.
Someone who is fast asleep or sound asleep is sleeping deeply.
Asparagus is a vegetable that is long and green and has small shoots at one end. It is cooked and served whole.

Chinesesense: 建筑物或窗的朝向，方向；
Englishsense: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.
The aspect of a building or window is the direction in which it faces.
If something begins to have a new aspect, it begins to have a new appearance or quality.

In grammar, aspect is the way that a verb group shows whether an activity is continuing, is repeated, or is completed. For example, in ’They were laughing’, the verb is in the progressive aspect and shows that the action was continuing.
Asphalt is a black substance used to make the surfaces of things such as roads and playgrounds.
Some-one’s aspirations are their desire to achieve things.
If you aspire to something such as an important job, you have a strong desire to achieve it.
Aspirin is a mild drug which reduces pain and fever.

Chinesesense: 通过语言或暴力泄愤，发泄不满情绪；
粗鲁地表示愤怒或异议去你的，去死；
Englishsense: An ass is an animal which is related to a horse but which is smaller and has long ears.
If you describe someone as an ass, you think that they are silly or do silly things.
Your ass is your bottom.
To kick ass or to kick someone’s ass means to show them that you are angry with them, either by telling them or by using physical force.
Saying that someone can kiss your ass is a very rude way of expressing anger or disagreement.
If you say that someone makes an ass of themselves, you mean they behave in a way that you think is very silly.
An assassin is a person who assassinates someone.
When someone important is assassinated, they are murdered as a political act.

Chinesesense: 武器用于战争的，军用的；
人身攻击；殴打；身体侵犯；
Englishsense: An assault by an army is a strong attack made on an area held by the enemy.
Assault weapons such as rifles are intended for soldiers to use in battle rather than for purposes such as hunting.
An assault on a person is a physical attack on them.
To assault someone means to physically attack them.
An assault on someone’s beliefs is a strong criticism of them.
When people assemble or when someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.
To assemble something means to collect it together or to fit the different parts of it together.
An assembly is a large group of people who meet regularly to make decisions or laws for a particular region or country.
An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose.
When you refer to rights of assembly or restrictions on assembly, you are referring to the legal right that people have to gather together.
In a school, assembly is a gathering of all the teachers and pupils at the beginning of every school day.
The assembly of a machine, device, or object is the process of fitting its different parts together.

Chinesesense: 坚持[主张]; 要求权利；
坚持自己的主张;表现坚定；
Englishsense: If someone asserts a fact or belief, they state it firmly.
If you assert your authority, you make it clear by your behaviour that you have authority.
If you assert your right or claim to something, you insist that you have the right to it.
If you assert yourself, you speak and act in a forceful way, so that people take notice of you.
When you assess a person, thing, or situation, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them.
When you assess the amount of money that something is worth or should be paid, you calculate or estimate it.
An assessment is a consideration of someone or something and a judgment about them.
An assessment of the amount of money that something is worth or that should be paid is a calculation or estimate of the amount.

Chinesesense: 有用的物[或人]; 财富；
Englishsense: Something or someone that is an asset is considered useful or helps a person or organization to be successful.
The assets of a company or a person are all the things that they own.
If one person calls another person an asshole, they think that person is extremely stupid or has behaved in a stupid way.

Chinesesense: 分派[工作]; 布置作业；
Englishsense: If you assign a piece of work to someone, you give them the work to do.
If you assign something to someone, you say that it is for their use.
If someone is assigned to a particular place, group, or person, they are sent there, usually in order to work at that place or for that person.
If you assign a particular function or value to someone or something, you say they have it.

Chinesesense: 布置的作业;分配的任务；
Englishsense: An assignment is a task or piece of work that you are given to do, especially as part of your job or studies.
You can refer to someone being given a particular task or job as their assignment to the task or job.
When people such as immigrants assimilate into a community or when that community assimilates them, they become an accepted part of it.
If you assimilate new ideas, techniques, or information, you learn them or adopt them.

Chinesesense: 提供信息、意见或金钱帮助，援助；
Englishsense: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.
If you assist someone, you give them information, advice, or money.
If something assists in doing a task, it makes the task easier to do.

Chinesesense: 以提供信息或意见的方式给予的帮助，援助；
Englishsense: If you give someone assistance, you help them do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.
If you give someone assistance, you give them information or advice.
If someone gives a person or country assistance, they help them by giving them money.
If something is done with the assistance of a particular thing, that thing is helpful or necessary for doing it.
Someone or something that is of assistance to you is helpful or useful to you.
If you come to someone’s assistance, you take action to help them.

Chinesesense: 用于头衔或职务前，表示级别略低助理的，副的；
Englishsense: Assistant is used in front of titles or jobs to indicate a slightly lower rank. For example, an assistant director is one rank lower than a director in an organization.
Someone’s assistant is a person who helps them in their work.
An assistant is a person who works in a shop selling things to customers.

Chinesesense: 使与某个组织、事业或观点有关系;公开支持；
用于等级或头衔前，表示稍有不同或略低副的，准的；
Englishsense: If you associate someone or something with another thing, the two are connected in your mind.
If you are associated with a particular organization, cause, or point of view, or if you associate yourself with it, you support it publicly.
If you say that someone is associating with another person or group of people, you mean they are spending a lot of time in the company of people you do not approve of.
Your associates are the people you are closely connected with, especially at work.
Associate is used before a rank or title to indicate a slightly different or lower rank or title.

Chinesesense: 用于公司名称联合的，联营的；
Englishsense: If one thing is associated with another, the two things are connected with each other.
Associated is used in the name of a company that is made up of a number of smaller companies which have joined together.
An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.
Your association with a person or a thing such as an organization is the connection that you have with them.
If something has particular associations for you, it is connected in your mind with a particular memory, idea, or feeling.
If you do something in association with someone else, you do it together.
If one thing is found in association with another, they are found together.

Chinesesense: 各式各样的;五颜六色的;混杂的；
Englishsense: A group of assorted things is a group of similar things that are of different sizes or colours or have different qualities.

Chinesesense: 各式各样;五颜六色;什锦；
Englishsense: An assortment is a group of similar things that are of different sizes or colours or have different qualities.

Chinesesense: 掌管，夺取，取得[权力]; 承担责任；
呈现，具有，显露某种特质；
表现出[某种表情]; 装出，做出某种样子；
Englishsense: If you assume that something is true, you imagine that it is true, sometimes wrongly.
If someone assumes power or responsibility, they take power or responsibility.
If something assumes a particular quality, it begins to have that quality.
If you assume a particular expression or way of behaving, you start to look or behave in this way.
You can use let us assume or let’s assume when you are considering a possible situation or event, so that you can think about the consequences.

Chinesesense: 权力的取得；责任的承担；
Englishsense: If you make an assumption that something is true or will happen, you accept that it is true or will happen, often without any real proof.
Someone’s assumption of power or responsibility is their taking of it.
If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.
If you do something with assurance, you do it with a feeling of confidence and certainty.
Assurance is insurance that provides cover in the event of death.

Chinesesense: 我可以向你保证；相信我；
Englishsense: If you assure someone that something is true or will happen, you tell them that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, often in order to make them less worried.
To assure someone of something means to make certain that they will get it.
You use phrases such as I can assure you or let me assure you to emphasize the truth of what you are saying.

Chinesesense: 小行星在火星及木星轨道间围绕太阳运行；
Englishsense: An asteroid is one of the very small planets that move around the sun between Mars and Jupiter.
Asthma is a lung condition which causes difficulty in breathing.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 令人惊讶的；非常惊人的；
Englishsense: Something that is astonishing is very surprising.
An astronaut is a person who is trained for travelling in a spacecraft.
An astronomer is a scientist who studies the stars, planets, and other natural objects in space.

Chinesesense: 数量，尤指费用极其巨大的,天文数字的；
Englishsense: If you describe an amount, especially the cost of something as astronomical, you are emphasizing that it is very large indeed.
Astronomical means relating to astronomy.
Astronomy is the scientific study of the stars, planets, and other natural objects in space.
If a government gives a person from another country asylum, they allow them to stay, usually because they are unable to return home safely for political reasons.
An asylum is a psychiatric hospital.

Chinesesense: 从相隔一段距离的地方;呈…角度；
在[某一年龄时]; 在…岁时；
以，达某一速度、频率、水平或价格；
朝[某人或某物看]; 向[某人掷物]; 冲某人说话；
致力于;定位于;期望达到；
用于所有格代词和形容词最高级前，表示某人或某物在此时的某一特征最鲜明；
Englishsense: You use at to indicate the place or event where something happens or is situated.
If someone is at school or college, or at a particular school or college, they go there regularly to study.
If you are at something such as a table, a door, or someone’s side, you are next to it or them.
When you are describing where someone or something is, you can say that they are at a certain distance. You can also say that one thing is at an angle in relation to another thing.
If something happens at a particular time, that is the time when it happens or begins to happen.
If you do something at a particular age, you do it when you are that age.
You use at to express a rate, frequency, level, or price.
You use at before a number or amount to indicate a measurement.
If you look at someone or something, you look towards them. If you direct an object or a comment at someone, you direct it towards them.
You can use at after verbs such as ’smile’ or ’wave’ and before nouns referring to people to indicate that you have put on an expression or made a gesture which someone is meant to see or understand.
If you point or gesture at something, you move your arm or head in its direction so that it will be noticed by someone you are with.
If you are working at something, you are dealing with it. If you are aiming at something, you are trying to achieve it.
If something is done at someone’s invitation or request, it is done as a result of it.
You use at to say that someone or something is in a particular state or condition.
You use at before a possessive pronoun and a superlative adjective to say that someone or something has more of a particular quality than at any other time.
You use at to say how something is being done.
You use at to show that someone is doing something repeatedly.
You use at to indicate an activity or task when saying how well someone does it.
You use at to indicate what someone is reacting to.

Chinesesense: 尤指田径项目的运动员，运动选手；
运动健儿;身强力壮的人；
Englishsense: An athlete is a person who does a sport, especially athletics, or track and field events.
You can refer to someone who is fit and athletic as an athlete.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 运动的;体育的;运动员的；
Englishsense: Athletic means relating to athletes and athletics.
An athletic person is fit, and able to perform energetic movements easily.
Athletics refers to track and field sports such as running, the high jump, and the javelin.
Athletics refers to any kind of physical sports, exercise, or games.

Chinesesense: 地方或事件的情调，魅力；
Englishsense: A planet’s atmosphere is the layer of air or other gases around it.
The atmosphere of a place is the air that you breathe there.
The atmosphere of a place is the general impression that you get of it.
If a place or an event has atmosphere, it is interesting.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 大气的;大气层的;空气的；
地方、音乐等有情调的，有魅力的，有感染力的；
Englishsense: Atmospheric is used to describe something which relates to the earth’s atmosphere.
If you describe a place or a piece of music as atmospheric, you like it because it has a particular quality which is interesting or exciting and makes you feel a particular emotion.
An atom is the smallest amount of a substance that can take part in a chemical reaction.
Atomic means relating to power that is produced from the energy released by splitting atoms.
Atomic means relating to the atoms of substances.
If something is atop something else, it is on top of it.
An atrocity is a very cruel, shocking action.
If you have an attachment to someone or something, you are fond of them or loyal to them.
An attachment is a device that can be fixed onto a machine in order to enable it to do different jobs.
If someone is on attachment to another company, department, or place, they are working there temporarily.
An attachment is an extra document that is added to another document.
In computing, an attachment is a file which is attached separately to a message that you send to someone.

Chinesesense: 疾病、化学药品、昆虫等攻击，侵蚀，破坏；
积极地解决问题，开展工作；
疾病短时间的侵袭，发作；
Englishsense: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.
If you attack a person, belief, idea, or act, you criticize them strongly.
If something such as a disease, a chemical, or an insect attacks something, it harms or spoils it.
If you attack a job or a problem, you start to deal with it in an energetic way.
In games such as football, when one team attacks the opponent’s goal, they try to score a goal.
An attack of an illness is a short period in which you suffer badly from it.
You can refer to a person who attacks someone as their attacker.

Chinesesense: 通常指经过努力获得，达到；
达到，进入，实现某种状态或情况；
Englishsense: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.
If you attain a particular state or condition, you may reach it as a result of natural development or work hard to attain this state.

Chinesesense: 尝试，试图尤指做困难的事；
通常指不成功的尝试，企图，试图；
运动员创造纪录的尝试，冲击；
Englishsense: If you attempt to do something, especially something difficult, you try to do it.
If you make an attempt to do something, you try to do it, often without success.
An attempt on some-one’s life is an attempt to kill them.
In British English, if a sportsman or sportswoman makes an attempt on a sporting record, they try to beat it. In American English you say that they make an attempt to break it.

Chinesesense: 犯罪、不法行为未遂的，未得手的；
Englishsense: An attempted crime or unlawful action is an unsuccessful effort to commit the crime or action.

Chinesesense: 去[学校、教堂等]; 上学；
处理，料理[事情]; 照顾，护理受伤的人；
Englishsense: If you attend a meeting or other event, you are present at it.
If you attend an institution such as a school, college, or church, you go there regularly.
If you attend to something, you deal with it. If you attend to someone who is hurt or injured, you care for them.

Chinesesense: 到[某地]; 出席某活动；
Englishsense: Someone’s attendance at an event or an institution is the fact that they are present at the event or go regularly to the institution.
The attendance at an event is the number of people who are present at it.
If someone is in attendance at a place or an event, they are there.
If someone is in attendance on an important person, they are accompanying that person as a servant or assistant.

Chinesesense: 加油站、停车场、更衣室等的服务员，侍者；
Englishsense: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a place such as a petrol station, a car park, or a cloakroom.
You use attendant to describe something that results from a thing already mentioned or that is connected with it.

Chinesesense: 尤指大众的注意力，关注；
尤指令人讨厌的关注，殷勤；
关心/不关心；注意/不注意；
Englishsense: If you give someone or something your attention, you look at it, listen to it, or think about it carefully.
Attention is great interest that is shown in someone or something, particularly by the general public.
If someone or something is getting attention, they are being dealt with or cared for.
You can refer to someone’s efforts to help you, or the interest they show in you, as their attentions, especially if you dislike or disapprove of them.

A backward country or society does not have modern industries and machines.
A backward child has difficulty in learning.

Englishsense: If you move or look backwards, you move or look in the direction that your back is facing.
If you do something backwards, you do it in the opposite way to the usual way.
You use backwards to indicate that something changes or develops in a way that is not an improvement, but is a return to old ideas or methods.
If someone or something moves backwards and forwards, they move repeatedly first in one direction and then in the opposite direction.
In British English, if you say that someone knows something backwards, you are emphasizing that they know it very well. In American English, you say that someone knows something backward and forward.

Englishsense: A backyard is an area of land at the back of a house.
If you refer to a country’s own backyard, you are referring to its own territory or to somewhere that is very close and where that country wants to influence events.
Bacon is salted or smoked meat which comes from the back or sides of a pig.
If you bring home the bacon,you achieve what you needed to achieve.
The person in a family who brings home the bacon provides the family with the money they need to live.
If someone or something saves your bacon, they get you out of a dangerous or difficult situation.
Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause disease.
Bacterial is used to describe things that relate to or are caused by bacteria.

不明智的；错误的；不对的；

对…有不好的评价；说…的坏话；
Englishsense: Something that is bad is unpleasant, harmful, or undesirable.
You use bad to indicate that something unpleasant or undesirable is severe or great in degree.
A bad idea, decision, or method is not sensible or not correct.
If you describe a piece of news, an action, or a sign as bad, you mean that it is unlikely to result in benefit or success.
Something that is bad is of an unacceptably low standard, quality, or amount.
Someone who is bad at doing something is not skilful or successful at it.
If you say that it is bad that something happens, you mean it is unacceptable, unfortunate, or wrong.
You can say that something is not bad to mean that it is quite good or acceptable, especially when you are rather surprised about this.
A bad person has morally unacceptable attitudes and behaviour.
A bad child disobeys rules and instructions or does not behave in a polite and correct way.
If you are in a bad mood, you are angry and behave unpleasantly to people.
If you feel bad about something, you feel rather sorry or guilty about it.
If you have a bad back, heart, leg, or eye, it is injured, diseased, or weak.
Food that has gone bad is not suitable to eat because it has started to decay.
Bad language is language that contains offensive words such as swear words.
If you say that it is too bad that something is the case, you mean you are sorry or sad that it is the case.
If you say ’ too bad ’, you are indicating that nothing can be done to change the situation, and that you do not feel sorry or sympathetic about this.
If someone or something is in a bad way, they are in a bad condition or situation.
If nobody has a bad word to say about you, you are liked or admired by everyone.

Chinesesense: 徽章，证章[美国英语通常用button指金属小圆徽章] ；
Englishsense: A badge is a piece of metal or cloth which you wear to show that you belong to an organization or support a cause. American English usually uses button to refer to a small round metal badge.
Any feature which is regarded as a sign of a particular quality can be referred to as a badge.

Chinesesense: 不友好地；令人不快地；恶劣地；
不利地；负面地；有损名声地；
Englishsense: If something is done badly or goes badly, it is not very successful or effective.
If someone or something is badly hurt or badly affected, they are severely hurt or affected.
If you want or need something badly, you want or need it very much.
If someone behaves badly or treats other people badly, they act in an unkind, unpleasant, or unacceptable way.
If something reflects badly on someone or makes others think badly of them, it harms their reputation.
If a person or their job is badly paid, they are not paid very much for what they do.

Chinesesense: 囊中之物；稳操胜券；十拿九稳；
背别人甩掉的包袱；背黑锅；
Englishsense: A bag is a container made of thin paper or plastic, for example one that is used in shops to put things in that a customer has bought.
A bag is a strong container with one or two handles, used to carry things in.
A bag is the same as a handbag. See usage note at: baggage
If you have bags under your eyes, you have folds of skin there, usually because you have not had enough sleep.
If you say there is bags of something, you mean that there is a large amount of it. If you say that there are bags of things, you mean that there are a large number of them.
If someone calls a woman an old bag or a stupid bag, they are insulting her.
If you bag something that a lot of people want, you get it for yourself before anyone else can get it.
If you say that something is in the bag, you mean that you are certain that you will get it or achieve it.
If you are left holding the bag, you are put in a situation where you are responsible for something, often in an unfair way because other people fail or refuse to take responsibility for it.
If you pack your bags, you leave a place where you have been staying or living.
Your baggage consists of the bags that you take with you when you travel.
You can use baggage to refer to someone’s emotional problems, fixed ideas, or prejudices.

Chinesesense: 板球运动中三柱门上的横木；
囚犯在保释期间逃跑，弃保潜逃；
Englishsense: Bail is a sum of money that an arrested person or someone else puts forward as a guarantee that the arrested person will attend their trial in a law court. If the arrested person does not attend it, the money will be lost.
Bail is permission for an arrested person to be released after bail has been paid.
If someone is bailed, they are released while they are waiting for their trial, after paying an amount of money to the court.
In cricket, the bails are the two small pieces of wood that are laid across the top of the stumps to form the wicket.
If you bail, you use a container to remove water from a boat or from a place which is flooded.
If a prisoner jumps bail, he or she does not come back for his or her trial after being released on bail.

Chinesesense: 装饵于；给鱼钩或陷阱等上诱饵；
使上当发火；故意逗…生气；
中圈套，上当，中计[亦作rise to the bait,主要用于英国英语中] ；
Englishsense: Bait is food which you put on a hook or in a trap in order to catch fish or animals.
If you bait a hook or trap, you put bait on it or in it.
To use something as bait means to use it to trick or persuade someone to do something.
If you bait someone, you deliberately try to make them angry by teasing them.
If you take the bait, you react to something that someone has said or done exactly as they intended you to do. The expression rise to the bait is also used, mainly in British English.

Chinesesense: 蔬菜或鱼与其他配料切碎拌和后经烘烤的烤菜；
Englishsense: If you bake, you spend some time preparing and mixing together ingredients to make bread, cakes, pies, or other food which is cooked in the oven.
When a cake or bread bakes or when you bake it, it cooks in the oven without any extra liquid or fat. See usage note at: cook
If places or people become extremely hot because the sun is shining very strongly, you can say that they bake.
A vegetable or fish bake is a dish that is made by chopping up and mixing together a number of ingredients and cooking them in the oven so that they form a fairly dry solid mass.

Chinesesense: 面包或糕饼烘房；面包或糕饼店；
Englishsense: A bakery is a building where bread, pastries, and cakes are baked, or the shop where they are sold.
You can use baking to describe weather or a place that is very hot indeed.

Chinesesense: 使力量、重要性等相等；使均衡；使持平；
力量、重要性等的均衡，均势；
尤指冲突或比赛中的局面，胜利天平；
结算[账目]; 使收支相等；
银行账户的余额，余数，结存；
身体失去平衡，几近跌倒；
权衡之后；全面考虑之后；总的来说；
Englishsense: If you balance something somewhere, or if it balances there, it remains steady and does not fall.
Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up.
If you balance one thing with something different, each of the things has the same strength or importance.
A balance is a situation in which all the different parts are equal in strength or importance.
If you say that the balance tips in your favour, you start winning or succeeding, especially in a conflict or contest.
If you balance one thing against another, you consider its importance in relation to the other one.
If someone balances their budget or if a government balances the economy of a country, they make sure that the amount of money that is spent is not greater than the amount that is received.
If you balance your books or make them balance, you prove by calculation that the amount of money you have received is equal to the amount that you have spent.
The balance in your bank account is the amount of money you have in it.
The balance of an amount of money is what remains to be paid for something or what remains when part of the amount has been spent.
If something hangs in the balance, it is uncertain whether it will happen or continue.
If you keep your balance, for example when standing in a moving vehicle, you remain steady and do not fall over. If you lose your balance, you become unsteady and fall over.
If you are off balance, you are in an unsteady position and about to fall.
If you are thrown off balance by something, you are surprised or confused by it.
You can say on balance to indicate that you are stating an opinion after considering all the relevant facts or arguments.

Someone who is balanced remains calm and thinks clearly, even in a difficult situation.

Chinesesense: 剧院或电影院的楼座，楼厅；
Englishsense: A balcony is a platform on the outside of a building, above ground level, with a wall or railing around it.

A bald statement is in plain language and contains no extra explanation or information.

Englishsense: A ball is a round object that is used in games such as tennis, baseball, football, basketball, and cricket.
A ball is something or an amount of something that has a round shape.
When you ball something or when it balls, it becomes round.
The ball of your foot or the ball of your thumb is the rounded part where your toes join your foot or where your thumb joins your hand.
A ball is a large formal social event at which people dance.
A man’s balls are his testicles.
If you say that the ball is in someone’s court, you mean that it is his or her responsibility to take the next action or decision in a situation.
If you get the ball rolling, set the ball rolling, or start the ball rolling, you start something happening.
If you are having a ball, you are having a very enjoyable time.
If you keep several balls in the air, you try to do several different things at once.
If someone is on the ball, they are very alert and aware of what is happening.
If someone refuses to play ball, they are unwilling to do what someone wants them to do.

Chinesesense: 节奏舒缓的流行抒情歌曲，情歌；
Englishsense: A ballad is a long song or poem which tells a story in simple language.
A ballad is a slow, romantic, popular song.
Ballet is a type of very skilled and artistic dancing with carefully planned movements.
A ballet is an artistic work that is performed by ballet dancers.

Chinesesense: 数量激增，猛涨，快速膨胀；
Englishsense: A balloon is a small, thin, rubber bag that you blow air into so that it becomes larger and rounder or longer. Balloons are used as toys or decorations.
A balloon is a large, strong bag filled with gas or hot air, which can carry passengers in a container that hangs underneath it.
When something balloons, it increases rapidly in amount.

Chinesesense: 无记名投票；无记名选举；无记名表决；
在…中间进行无记名投票或表决；
Englishsense: A ballot is a secret vote in which people select a candidate in an election, or express their opinion about something.
A ballot is a piece of paper on which you indicate your choice or opinion in a secret vote.
If you ballot a group of people, you find out what they think about a subject by organizing a secret vote.

Chinesesense: 尤指被认为不亚于其他参加者而能够参加，获得资格参与；
Englishsense: A ballpark is a park or stadium where baseball is played.
A ballpark figure or ballpark estimate is an approximate figure or estimate.
If something such as an amount or claim is in the ballpark, it is approximately right, but not exact.

If you say that someone or something is in the ballpark, you mean that they are able to take part in a particular area of activity, especially because they are considered as good as others taking part.
A ballroom is a very large room that is used for dancing.
Bamboo is a tall tropical plant with hard, hollow stems. The young shoots of the plant can be eaten and the stems are used to make furniture.
To ban something means to state officially that it must not be done, shown, or used.
A ban is an official ruling that something must not be done, shown, or used.
If you are banned from doing something, you are officially prevented from doing it.
Bananas are long curved fruit with yellow skins.
If someone is behaving in a silly or crazy way, or if they become extremely angry, you can say that they are going bananas.

Chinesesense: 演奏铜管和打击乐器的乐队，乐团；
佩戴用或衣物上的带，箍；
用以加固或捆绑的圈，箍；
Englishsense: A band is a small group of musicians who play popular music such as jazz, rock, or pop.
A band is a group of musicians who play brass and percussion instruments.
A band of people is a group of people who have joined together because they share an interest or belief.
band is a flat, narrow strip of cloth which you wear round your head or wrists, or which forms part of a piece of clothing.
A band is a strip of something such as colour, light, land, or cloth which contrasts with the areas on either side of it.
A band is a strip or loop of metal or other strong material which strengthens something, or which holds several things together.
A band is a range of numbers or values within a system of measurement.
If something such as a tax is banded, it is divided into bands according to the value of the thing being taxed.
A bandage is a long strip of cloth which is wrapped around a wounded part of someone’s body to protect or support it.
If you bandage a wound or part of someone’s body, you tie a bandage around it.

POS: N-COUNT; SOUND 可数名词；声音词
Chinesesense: 因生气而砰地放下，猛然放下；
通常指由于未能注意到眼前的人或物撞上；
精力充沛地；热情高涨地；非常成功地；
Englishsense: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion.
If something bangs, it makes a sudden loud noise, once or several times.
If you bang a door or if it bangs, it closes suddenly with a loud noise.
If you bang on something or if you bang it, you hit it hard, making a loud noise.
If you bang something on something or if you bang it down, you quickly and violently put it on a surface, because you are angry.
If you bang a part of your body, you accidentally knock it against something and hurt yourself.
If you bang into something or someone, you bump or knock them hard, usually because you are not looking where you are going.
Bangs are hair which is cut so that it hangs over your forehead.
You can use bang to emphasize expressions that indicate an exact position or an exact time.
If you say bang goes something, you mean that it is now obvious that it cannot succeed or be achieved.
If something begins or ends with a bang, it begins or ends with a lot of energy, enthusiasm, or success. [PHR after v]
If someone or something is banished from a place or area of activity, they are sent away from it and prevented from entering it.
If you banish something unpleasant, you get rid of it.
If you banish the thought of something, you stop thinking about it.

Chinesesense: 银行营业厅；银行办事处；
与银行有业务来往；在银行有账户；
斥巨资；花费大笔的钱；倾家荡产；
尤指机器、开关、仪表的一排，一组；
通常指飞机在改变方向时倾斜飞行；
Englishsense: A bank is an institution where people or businesses can keep their money.
A bank is a building where a bank offers its services.
If you bank money, you pay it into a bank.
If you bank with a particular bank, you have an account with that bank.
You use bank to refer to a store of something. For example, a blood bank is a store of blood that is kept ready for use.
If you say that the cost of something will not break the bank, you mean that it will not cost a large sum of money.
The banks of a river, canal, or lake are the raised areas of ground along its edge.
A bank of ground is a raised area of it with a flat top and one or two sloping sides.
A bank of something is a long high mass of it.
A bank of things, especially machines, switches, or dials, is a row of them, or a series of rows.
When an aircraft banks, one of its wings rises higher than the other, usually when it is changing direction.
A banker is someone who works in banking at a senior level.
Banking is the business activity of banks and similar institutions.

Chinesesense: 破产的；倒闭的；资不抵债的；
Englishsense: People or organizations that go bankrupt do not have enough money to pay their debts.
To bankrupt a person or organization means to make them go bankrupt.
A bankrupt is a person who has been declared bankrupt by a court of law.
If you say that something is bankrupt, you are emphasizing that it lacks any value or worth.
Bankruptcy is the state of being bankrupt.
A bankruptcy is an instance of an organization or person going bankrupt.
If you refer to something’s bankruptcy, you are emphasizing that it is completely lacking in value or worth.

Chinesesense: 通常指在抗议或集会中用两根竿子撑开的横幅，标语；
在…的旗帜下；为了…的事业或信仰；
Englishsense: A banner is a long strip of cloth with something written on it. Banners are usually attached to two poles and carried during a protest or rally.
If someone does something under the banner of a particular cause, idea, or belief, they do it saying that they support that cause, idea, or belief.
A banquet is a grand formal dinner.

Chinesesense: 浸礼会教派的；浸礼会教友的；
Englishsense: A Baptist is a Christian who believes that people should not be baptized until they are old enough to understand the meaning of baptism.
Baptist means belonging or relating to Baptists.

Chinesesense: 电热炉的电热棒，电热片；
不受任何规则约束；不限任何方式方法；不择手段；
英格兰有资格在任何法庭作辩护的出庭律师职业；美国的律师职业，律师界；
Englishsense: A bar is a place where you can buy and drink alcoholic drinks.
A bar is a room in a pub or hotel where alcoholic drinks are served.
A bar is a counter on which alcoholic drinks are served.
A bar is a long, straight, stiff piece of metal.
If you say that someone is behind bars, you mean that they are in prison.
A bar of something is a piece of it which is roughly rectangular.
A bar of an electric fire is a piece of metal with wire wound round it that glows and provides heat when the fire is switched on.
If you bar a door, you place something in front of it or a piece of wood or metal across it in order to prevent it from being opened.
If you bar someone’s way, you prevent them from going somewhere or entering a place, by blocking their path.
If someone is barred from a place or from doing something, they are officially forbidden to go there or to do it.
If something is a bar to doing a particular thing, it prevents someone from doing it.
If you say that there are no holds barred when people are fighting or competing for something, you mean that they are no longer following any rules in their efforts to win.
You can use ba r when you mean ’except’. For example, all the work bar the washing means all the work except the washing.
The Bar is used to refer to the profession of a barrister in England, or of any kind of lawyer in the United States.
In music, a bar is one of the several short parts of the same length into which a piece of music is divided.
A barbecue is a piece of equipment which you use for cooking on in the open air.
If someone has a barbecue, they cook food on a barbecue in the open air.
If you barbecue food, especially meat, you cook it on a barbecue.

Chinesesense: 为男性理发的男理发师；
Englishsense: A barber is a man whose job is cutting men’s hair.
A barber’s is a shop where a barber works.

Englishsense: If a part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.
A bare surface is not covered or decorated with anything.
If a tree or a branch is bare, it has no leaves on it.
If a room, cupboard, or shelf is bare, it is empty.
An area of ground that is bare has no plants growing on it.
If someone gives you the bare facts or the barest details of something, they tell you only the most basic and important things.
If you talk about the bare minimum or the bare essentials, you mean the very least that is necessary.
Bare is used in front of an amount to emphasize how small it is.
If you bare something, you uncover it and show it.
If someone does something with their bare hands, they do it without using any weapons or tools.
If you lay something bare, you uncover it completely so that it can then be seen.
If you lay bare something or someone, you reveal or expose them.
If you bare your soul, you tell someone your most secret thoughts and feelings.
Someone who is barefoot or barefooted is not wearing anything on their feet.

Englishsense: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.
If you say that one thing had barely happened when something else happened, you mean that the first event was followed immediately by the second.

Chinesesense: 商谈；交涉；谈判；讨价还价；
极力讨价还价；提出苛刻的交易条件；
Englishsense: Something that is a bargain is good value for money, usually because it has been sold at a lower price than normal.
A bargain is an agreement, especially a formal business agreement, in which two people or groups agree what each of them will do, pay, or receive.
