You can use beast to refer to something or someone in a light-hearted way, and to mention that they have a particular quality.

Chinesesense: 通常指多次或连续地撞击，猛撞，拍打；
敲，打，击[鼓等]; 鼓等敲响；
拍打，拍动[翅膀]; 翅膀拍动；
打破[纪录等]; 超过； 突破；
战胜某个组织、问题、疾病等；
常指暂时击退，中断，中止；
没有比…更好的；什么也比不上；最好的莫过于；
警察的辖区，巡逻区；记者的负责采访的区域；
把…难住；使不明白；使无法解释；
表示惊讶或恼怒竟然有这种事？岂有此理！；
比…抢先行动；赶在…前面做某事；
Englishsense: If you beat someone or something, you hit them very hard.
To beat on, at, or against something means to hit it hard, usually several times or continuously for a period of time.
When your heart or pulse beats, it continually makes regular rhythmic movements.
If you beat a drum or similar instrument, you hit it in order to make a sound. You can also say that a drum beats.
The beat of a piece of music is the main rhythm that it has.
In music, a beat is a unit of measurement. The number of beats in a bar of a piece of music is indicated by two numbers at the beginning of the piece.
If you beat eggs, cream, or butter, you mix them thoroughly using a fork or beater.
When a bird or insect beats its wings or when its wings beat, its wings move up and down.
If you beat someone in a competition or election, you defeat them.
If someone beats a record or achievement, they do better than it.
If you beat something that you are fighting against, for example an organization, a problem, or a disease, you defeat it.
If an attack or an attempt is beaten off or is beaten back, it is stopped, often temporarily.
If you say that one thing beats another, you mean that it is better than it.
If you say you can’t beat a particular thing you mean that it is the best thing of its kind.
To beat a time limit or an event means to achieve something before that time or event.
A police officer’s or journalist’s beat is the area for which he or she is responsible.
You use beat in expressions such as ’It beats me’ or ’What beats me is’ to indicate that you cannot understand or explain something.
If you tell someone to beat it, you are telling them to go away.
You can say Can you beat it? or Can you beat that? to show that you are surprised and perhaps annoyed about something.
If you intend to do something but someone beats you to it, they do it before you do. [V inflects]
If you can’t beat them, join them means that, if someone is too strong for you to defeat, it is better to be on the same side as them.
If you say or do something without missing a beat, you continue to speak or do it, even though people might have expected you to hesitate or stop.
If you say that someone never misses a beat, you mean that they always know what is going on and how they can take advantage of it.
A police officer on the beat is on duty, walking around the area for which he or she is responsible.
If you beat time to a piece of music, you move your hand or foot up and down in time with the music. A conductor beats time to show the choir or orchestra how fast they should sing or play the music.

Chinesesense: 尤指用棍子等进行的殴打，痛打；
竞争或选举中的大败，惨败；
Englishsense: If someone is given a beating, they are hit hard many times, especially with something such as a stick.
If something such as a business, a political party, or a team takes a beating, it is defeated by a large amount in a competition or election.
If you say that something will take some beating, you mean that it is very good and it is unlikely that anything better will be done or made.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A beautiful person is very attractive to look at.
If you describe something as beautiful, you mean that it is very attractive or pleasing.
You can describe something that someone does as beautiful when they do it very skilfully.
Beauty is the state or quality of being beautiful.
A beauty is a beautiful woman.
You can say that something is a beauty when you think it is very good.
The beauties of something are its attractive qualities or features.
Beauty is used to describe people, products, and activities that are concerned with making women look beautiful.
If you say that a particular feature is the beauty of something, you mean that this feature is what makes the thing so good.
You use because when stating the reason for something.
You use because when stating the explanation for a statement you have just made.
If an event or situation occurs because of something, that thing is the reason or cause.
You use just because when you want to say that a particular situation should not necessarily make you come to a particular conclusion.
If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you.
If something beckons, it is so attractive to someone that they feel they must become involved in it.
If something beckons for someone, it is very likely to happen to them.
If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.
If something becomes someone, it makes them look attractive or it seems right for them.
If you wonder what has become of someone or something, you wonder where they are and what has happened to them.
A bedroom is a room used for sleeping in.
Your bedside is the area beside your bed.
If you talk about being at someone’s bedside, you are talking about being near them when they are ill in bed.
Your bedtime is the time when you usually go to bed.

Chinesesense: 进行缝纫等比赛或集体活动的聚会；
Englishsense: A bee is an insect with a yellow-and-black striped body that makes a buzzing noise as it flies. Bees make honey, and can sting.
If you have a bee in your bonnet about something, you are so enthusiastic or worried about it that you keep mentioning it or thinking about it.
A bee is a social event where people get together for a competition or to do something such as sew.
Beef is the meat of a cow, bull, or ox.
If someone beefs about something, they keep complaining about it.
Beer is a bitter alcoholic drink made from grain.
Beet is a crop with a thick round root. It is often used to feed animals, especially cows.
Beets are dark red roots that are eaten as a vegetable. They are often preserved in vinegar.
A beetle is an insect with a hard covering to its body.

Chinesesense: 必须先具备某一条件才能；在…之前必须具备某一条件；
摆在…面前；使面对；使面临；
Englishsense: If something happens before a particular date, time, or event, it happens earlier than that date, time, or event. See usage note at: ago
If you do one thing before doing something else, you do it earlier than the other thing.
You use before when you are talking about time. For example, if something happened the day before a particular date or event, it happened during the previous day.
If you do something before someone else can do something, you do it when they have not yet done it.
If someone has done something before, they have done it on a previous occasion. If someone has not done something before, they have never done it.
If there is a period of time or if several things are done before something happens, it takes that amount of time or effort for this thing to happen.
If a particular situation has to happen before something else happens, this situation must happen or exist in order for the other thing to happen.
If someone is before something, they are in front of it.
If you tell someone that one place is a certain distance before another, you mean that they will come to the first place first.
If you appear or come before an official person or group, you go there and answer questions.
If something happens before a particular person or group, it is seen by or happens while this person or this group is present.
If you have something such as a journey, a task, or a stage of your life before you, you must do it or live through it in the future.
When you want to say that one person or thing is more important than another, you can say that they come before the other person or thing.

Chinesesense: 引起疑问，使人想问一些人认为此用法不正确；
认为问题已获解决而绕过问题；
Englishsense: If you beg someone to do something, you ask them very anxiously or eagerly to do it.
If someone who is poor is begging, they are asking people to give them food or money.
You say ’I beg to differ ’ when you are politely emphasizing that you disagree with someone.
If you say that something is going begging, you mean that it is available but no one is using it or accepting it.
If you say that something begs a particular question, you mean that it makes people want to ask that question; some people consider that this use is incorrect.
If you say that something begs a particular question, you mean that it assumes that the question has already been answered and so does not deal with it.

Chinesesense: 从…开始；从…着手；首先做某事；
无法，难以解释、理解、想象等；
Englishsense: To begin to do something means to start doing it.
When something begins or when you begin it, it takes place from a particular time onwards.
If you begin with something, or begin by doing something, this is the first thing you do.
You use begin to mention the first thing that someone says.
If one thing began as another, it first existed in the form of the second thing.
If you say that a thing or place begins somewhere, you are talking about one of its limits or edges.
If a word begins with a particular letter, that is the first letter of that word.
If you say that you cannot begin to imagine, understand, or explain something, you are emphasizing that it is almost impossible to explain, understand, or imagine.
You use to begin with when you are talking about the first stage of a situation, event, or process.
You use to begin with to introduce the first of several things that you want to say.
A beginner is someone who has just started learning to do something and cannot do it very well yet.
The beginning of an event or process is the first part of it.
The beginnings of something are the signs or events which form the first part of it.
The beginning of a period of time is the time at which it starts.
The beginning of a piece of written material is the first words or sentences of it.
If you talk about the beginnings of a person, company, or group, you are referring to their backgrounds or origins.
You use beginning to describe someone who is in the early stages of learning to do something.

Chinesesense: 代表[亦使用 in someone’s behalf，主要用于美国英语中] ；
Englishsense: If you do something on someone’s behalf, you do it for that person as their representative. The form in someone’s behalf is also used, mainly in American English.
If you feel, for example, embarrassed or angry on someone’s behalf, you feel embarrassed or angry for them.

Chinesesense: 守规矩；举止得体；行为检点；
在科学领域运动，起作用，作出反应；
Englishsense: The way that you behave is the way that you do and say things, and the things that you do and say.
If you behave or behave yourself, you act in the way that people think is correct and proper.
In science, the way that something behaves is the things that it does.

Chinesesense: 在桌子、柜台、吧台等的后面；
在某一局势背后或幕后；
对…来说成为过去；抛到…的脑后；
Englishsense: If something is behind a thing or person, it is on the other side of them from you, or nearer their back rather than their front.
If you are walking or travelling behind someone or something, you are following them.
If someone is behind a desk, counter, or bar, they are on the other side of it from where you are.
When you shut a door or gate behind you, you shut it after you have gone through it.
The people, reason, or events behind a situation are the causes of it or are responsible for it.
If something or someone is behind you, they support you and help you.
If you refer to what is behind someone’s outside appearance, you are referring to a characteristic which you cannot immediately see or is not obvious, but which you think is there.
If you are behind someone, you are less successful than them, or have done less or advanced less.
If an experience is behind you, it happened in your past and will not happen again, or no longer affects you.
If you have a particular achievement behind you, you have managed to reach this achievement, and other people consider it to be important or valuable.
If something is behind schedule, it is not as far advanced as people had planned. If someone is behind schedule, they are not progressing as quickly at something as they had planned.
If you stay behind, you remain in a place after other people have gone.
If you leave something or someone behind, you do not take them with you when you go.
Your behind is the part of your body that you sit on.

Chinesesense: 用于说明原因的非限定性从句中因为，由于；
用于解释所说内容的原因因为，由于；
Englishsense: Being is used in non-finite clauses where you are giving the reason for something.
You can refer to any real or imaginary creature as a being.
Being is existence. Something that is in being or comes into being exists.
You can use being as to introduce a reason for what you are saying.

Chinesesense: 对宗教或政治的信仰，观点，看法；
和人们一般的认识相反；和一般看法相反；
Englishsense: Belief is a feeling of certainty that something exists, is true, or is good.
Your religious or political beliefs are your views on religious or political matters.
If it is your belief that something is the case, it is your strong opinion that it is the case.
You use beyond belief to emphasize that something is true to a very great degree or that it happened to a very great degree.
You use contrary to popular belief to introduce a statement that is the opposite to what is thought to be true by most ordinary people.
If you do one thing in the belief that another thing is true or will happen, you do it because you think, usually wrongly, that it is true or will happen.

Chinesesense: 认为…是应该的或正确的；
表示对所见所闻惊讶不已相信自己的眼睛/耳朵；
强调刚才所述之事令人吃惊信不信由你；
强调对某事感到惊讶你会相信吗？；
Englishsense: If you believe that something is true, you think that it is true, but you are not sure.
If you believe someone or if you believe what they say or write, you accept that they are telling the truth.
If you believe in fairies, ghosts, or miracles, you are sure that they exist or happen. If you believe in a god, you are sure of the existence of that god.
If you believe in a way of life or an idea, you are in favour of it because you think it is good or right.
If you believe in someone or what they are doing, you have confidence in them and think that they will be successful.

Believe is used in expressions such as I can’t believe how or it’s hard to believe that in order to express surprise, for example because something bad has happened or something very difficult has been achieved.
If you say that you cannot believe your eyes or cannot believe your ears, you are emphasizing that you are very surprised about something you have seen or heard.
You can use believe it or not to emphasize that what you have just said is surprising.
If you say would you believe it, you are emphasizing your surprise about something.
You can use believe you me to emphasize that what you are saying is true.
If you are a great believer in something, you think that it is good, right, or useful.
A believer is someone who is sure that God exists or that their religion is true.

Chinesesense: 听起来耳熟但记不真切；
非常健康的；完好无损的；
Englishsense: A bell is a device that makes a ringing sound and is used to give a signal or to attract people’s attention.
A bell is a hollow metal object shaped like a cup which has a piece hanging inside it that hits the sides and makes a sound.
If something is as clear as a bell, it is very clear indeed.
If you give someone a bell, you telephone them.
If you say that something rings a bell, you mean that it reminds you of something, but you cannot remember exactly what it is.
If something is as sound as a bell it is healthy and not damaged in any way.

Chinesesense: 胃，腹部在英国英语中属于非正式或文学用语；
资不抵债；无力偿还债务；
Englishsense: The belly of a person or animal is their stomach or abdomen. In British English, this is an informal or literary use.
If a company goes belly up, it does not have enough money to pay its debts.

Chinesesense: 属于某个类别、类型或群体；
孩子是…的，为…所拥有或监护；
属于彼此恋人用来表示亲密关系；
归属于某地或某一情形；
Englishsense: If something belongs to you, you own it.
You say that something belongs to a particular person when you are guessing, discovering, or explaining that it was produced by or is part of that person.
If someone belongs to a particular group, they are a member of that group.
If something or someone belongs in or to a particular category, type, or group, they are of that category, type, or group.
If something belongs to a particular time, it comes from that time.
If you say that something belongs to someone, you mean that person has the right to it.
If you say that a time belongs to a particular system or way of doing something, you mean that that time is or will be characterized by it.
If a baby or child belongs to a particular adult, that adult is his or her parent or the person who is looking after him or her.
When lovers say that they belong together, they are expressing their closeness or commitment to each other.
If a person or thing belongs in a particular place or situation, that is where they should be.
Your belongings are the things that you own, especially things that are small enough to be carried.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A beloved person, thing, or place is one that you feel great affection for.
Your beloved is the person that you love.

Chinesesense: 数量、比率或水平低于，小于，少于；
Englishsense: If something is below something else, it is in a lower position.
If something is below ground or below the ground, it is in the ground.
You use below in a piece of writing to refer to something that is mentioned later.
If something is below a particular amount, rate, or level, it is less than that amount, rate, or level.
If someone is below you in an organization, they are lower in rank.

Chinesesense: 表示柔道或空手道级别的段，带；
勒紧裤腰带；紧缩开支；节衣缩食；
Englishsense: A belt is a strip of leather or cloth that you fasten round your waist.
A belt in a machine is a circular strip of rubber that is used to drive moving parts or to move objects along.
A belt of land or sea is a long, narrow area of it that has some special feature.
If someone belts you, they hit you very hard.
If you belt somewhere, you move or travel there very fast.
If someone is or has a belt of a particular colour in judo or karate, they have reached the standard which that colour represents.
Something that is below the belt is cruel and unfair.
If you have to tighten your belt, you have to spend less money and manage without things because you have less money than you used to have.
If you have something under your belt, you have already achieved it or done it.

Chinesesense: 法官职位；地方执法官职位；
Englishsense: A bench is a long seat of wood or metal that two or more people can sit on.
A bench is a long, narrow table in a factory or laboratory.
In parliament, different groups sit on different benches. For example, the government sits on the government benches.
In a court of law, the bench is the judge or magistrates.
If someone serves on the bench, they work as a judge or magistrate.
If a member of a sports team is on the bench for a particular match, he or she waits at the side of the field until the manager tells them to play.
A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

Chinesesense: 弯曲[手臂、腿等]; 手臂、腿等弯曲；
路、管道等的弯曲处，转弯处；
曲解，通融，篡改规则、法律等；
使非常恼火；使极为恼怒；
Englishsense: When you bend, you move the top part of your body downwards and forwards. Plants and trees also bend.
When you bend your head, you move your head forwards and downwards.
When you bend a part of your body such as your arm or leg, or when it bends, you change its position so that it is no longer straight.
If you bend something that is flat or straight, you use force to make it curved or to put an angle in it.
When a road, beam of light, or other long thin thing bends, or when something bends it, it changes direction to form a curve or angle.
A bend in a road, pipe, or other long thin object is a curve or angle in it.
If someone bends to your wishes, they believe or do something different, usually when they do not want to.
If you bend rules or laws, you interpret them in a way that allows you to do something they would not normally allow you to do.
If you bend the truth or bend the facts, you say something that is not exactly true.
If you say that someone is bending over backwards to be helpful or kind, you are emphasizing that they are trying very hard to be helpful or kind.
If you say that someone or something drives you round the bend, you mean that you dislike them and they annoy or upset you very much.
If you say that someone is round the bend, you mean that they do foolish or silly things.
Something that is beneath another thing is under the other thing.
If you talk about what is beneath the surface of something, you are talking about the aspects of it which are hidden or not obvious.
If you say that someone or something is beneath you, you feel that they are not good enough for you or not suitable for you.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 有益的；有利的；有帮助的；
Englishsense: Something that is beneficial helps people or improves their lives.
Someone who is a beneficiary of something is helped by it.
The beneficiaries of a will are legally entitled to receive money or property from someone when that person dies.

Chinesesense: 政府提供给穷人、病人和失业人员的救济金，补助金；
Englishsense: The benefit of something is the help that you get from it or the advantage that results from it.
If something is to your benefit or is of benefit to you, it helps you or improves your life.
If you benefit from something or if it benefits you, it helps you or improves your life.
If you have the benefit of some information, knowledge, or equipment, you are able to use it so that you can achieve something.
Benefit is money that is given by the government to people who are poor, ill, or unemployed.
A benefit, or a benefit concert or dinner, is an event that is held in order to raise money for a particular charity or person.
If you give someone the benefit of the doubt, you treat them as if they are telling the truth or as if they have behaved properly, even though you are not sure that this is the case.
If you say that someone is doing something for the benefit of a particular person, you mean that they are doing it for that person.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 条件、环境良好的，宜人的；
不作为；善意忽视；顺其自然；
Englishsense: You use benign to describe someone who is kind, gentle, and harmless.
A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.
A benign tumour will not cause death or serious harm.
Benign conditions are pleasant or make it easy for something to happen.
If you describe someone’s approach to a problem as one of benign neglect, you disapprove of the fact that they are doing nothing and hoping that the problem will solve itself.
Berries are small, round fruit that grow on a bush or a tree. Some berries are edible, for example blackberries and raspberries.

Chinesesense: 船、火车、旅行拖车等的卧铺，铺位；
Englishsense: If you give someone or something a wide berth, you avoid them because you think they are unpleasant, or dangerous, or simply because you do not like them.
A berth is a bed on a boat, train, or caravan.
A berth is a space in a harbour where a ship stays for a period of time.
When a ship berths, it sails into harbour and stops at the quay.
Something that is beside something else is at the side of it or next to it.
If you are beside yourself with anger or excitement, you are extremely angry or excited. beside the point

Chinesesense: 而且，再说强调所补充的内容；
Englishsense: Besides something or beside something means in addition to it.
Besides is used to emphasize an additional point that you are making, especially one that you consider to be important.

Chinesesense: 最大努力；最高成就；最好水平；
用于道别或信件末尾万事如意，一切顺利；
尽全力；竭尽所能；尽最大努力；
综合考虑起来是最好的；
尤指冰释前嫌后最好的朋友；知己；
最好有些人认为此用法不规范；
因经验丰富最清楚，最明白；
看起来处于自己最迷人的状态；
乐观地尽可能利用逆境；
Englishsense: The best is used to refer to things of the highest quality or standard.
Someone’s best is the greatest effort or highest achievement or standard that they are capable of.
If you say that something is the best that can be done or hoped for, you think it is the most pleasant, successful, or useful thing that can be done or hoped for.
If you like something best or like it the best, you prefer it.
You can say ’ All the best ’ when you are saying goodbye to someone, or at the end of a letter.
You use best of all to indicate that what you are about to mention is the thing that you prefer or that has most advantages out of all the things you have mentioned.
If someone does something as best they can, they do it as well as they can, although it is very difficult.
You use at best to indicate that even if you describe something as favourably as possible or if it performs as well as it possibly can, it is still not very good.
If you do your best or try your best to do something, you try as hard as you can to do it, or do it as well as you can.
If you say that something is for the best, you mean it is the most desirable or helpful thing that could have happened or could be done, considering all the circumstances.
If two people are the best of friends, they are close friends, especially when they have had a disagreement or fight in the past.
If you say that someone had best do something or that they ’d best do it, you mean they ought to do it. Some people consider this to be non-standard.
If you say that a particular person knows best, you mean that they have a lot of experience and should therefore be trusted to make decisions for other people.
If you look your best, you are looking as smart and attractive as you can.
If you make the best of something, you accept an unsatisfactory situation cheerfully and try to manage as well as you can. In British English, you can also say that you make the best of a bad job.
To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

Chinesesense: 书等畅销的，抢手的，大卖的；
Englishsense: A best-selling product such as a book is very popular and a large quantity of it has been sold.
A best-selling author is an author who has sold a very large number of copies of his or her book.

Chinesesense: 十拿九稳的事；有望成功的行动；合适之选；
极有可能属实或发生的事；
通常感到恼火或好笑时表示同意或认为属实那是，说的是，一点没错；
不要认为；别指望；不一定；
表示确信对方说的不对敢打赌吗？；
Englishsense: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.
A bet is a sum of money which you give to someone when you bet.
If someone is betting that something will happen, they are hoping or expecting that it will happen.
You use expressions such as ’ I bet ’, ’ I’ll bet ’, and ’ you can bet ’ to indicate that you are sure something is true.
If you tell someone that something is a good bet, you are suggesting that it is the thing or course of action that they should choose.

You use body and soul to mean every part of you, including your mind and your emotions.
If you keep body and soul together, you have enough money to provide what you need to live.
A bodyguard is a person or a group of people employed to protect someone.

Chinesesense: 使达到沸点；使沸腾；使烧开；
使水壶或锅里的水烧开；
水壶或平底锅里的水烧开，沸腾；
Englishsense: When a hot liquid boils or when you boil it, bubbles appear in it and it starts to change into steam or vapour.
When you boil a kettle or pan, or put it on to boil, you heat the water inside it until it boils.
When a kettle or pan is boiling, the water inside it has reached boiling point.
When you boil food, or when it boils, it is cooked in boiling water. See usage note at: cook
If you are boiling with anger, you are very angry.
A boil is a red, painful swelling on your skin, which contains a thick yellow liquid called pus.
When you bring a liquid to the boil, you heat it until it boils. When it comes to the boil, it begins to boil.

Chinesesense: 感觉极热的；热得难受的；
Englishsense: Something that is boiling or boiling hot is very hot.
If you say that you are boiling or boiling hot, you mean that you feel very hot, usually unpleasantly hot. See usage note at: hot

Chinesesense: 在众人面前大胆的，放肆的，莽撞的；
色彩或图案明亮的，醒目的；
(线条) 粗重的；图案清晰的；
印刷字体粗体字，黑体字；
Englishsense: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.
Someone who is bold is not shy or embarrassed in the company of other people.
A bold colour or pattern is very bright and noticeable.
Bold lines or designs are drawn in a clear, strong way.
Bold is print which is thicker and looks blacker than ordinary printed letters.

Chinesesense: 增强[信心]; 鼓舞士气；
垫在普通枕头下的长枕，垫枕；
Englishsense: If you bolster something such as someone’s confidence or courage, you increase it.
If someone tries to bolster their position in a situation, they try to strengthen it.
A bolster is a firm pillow shaped like a long tube which is sometimes put across a bed under the ordinary pillows.

Chinesesense: 常指人或动物因受惊吓迅速逃跑，逃窜；
蔬菜生长过快，结实过早而不宜食用；
晴天霹雳；出人意表；令人大吃一惊；
Englishsense: A bolt is a long metal object which screws into a nut and is used to fasten things together.
When you bolt one thing to another, you fasten them firmly together, using a bolt.
A bolt on a door or window is a metal bar that you can slide across in order to fasten the door or window.
When you bolt a door or window, you slide the bolt across to fasten it.
If a person or animal bolts, they suddenly start to run very fast, often because something has frightened them.
If you bolt your food, you eat it so quickly that you hardly chew it or taste it.
A bolt of lightning is a flash of lightning that is seen as a white line in the sky.
A bolt of cloth is a long wide piece of it that is wound into a roll round a piece of cardboard.
When vegetables such as lettuces or onions bolt, they grow too quickly and produce flowers and seeds, and therefore become less good to eat.
If someone makes a bolt for somewhere, or makes a bolt for it, they make a sudden escape.
If a piece of news comes like a bolt from the blue, it is completely unexpected and very surprising.
If someone is sitting or standing bolt upright, they are sitting or standing very straight.
A bomb is a device which explodes and damages or destroys a large area.
Nuclear weapons are sometimes referred to as the bomb.
When people bomb a place, they attack it with bombs.

Chinesesense: 在公共场所引爆炸弹的人；
Englishsense: A bomber is a military aircraft which drops bombs.
Bombers are people who cause bombs to explode in public places.

Chinesesense: 与…紧密联系；使相互联结；使建立亲密关系；
个人或团体之间的密切联系；
与…黏合[或连接]; 使黏合或连接在一起；
政府或公司发行的公债，债券；
Englishsense: A bond between people is a strong feeling of friendship, love, or shared beliefs and experiences that unites them.
When people bond with each other, they form a relationship based on love or shared beliefs and experiences. You can also say that people bond or that something bonds them.
A bond between people or groups is a close connection that they have with each other, for example because they have a special agreement.
Bonds are feelings, duties, or customs that force you to behave in a particular way.
A bond between two things is the way in which they stick to one another or are joined in some way.
When one thing bonds with another, it sticks to it or becomes joined to it in some way. You can also say that two things bond together, or that something bonds them together.
When a government or company issues a bond, it borrows money from investors. The certificate which is issued to investors who lend money is also called a bond.

Chinesesense: 太过直白；过于直率；露骨；
毫不犹豫；毫不迟疑；二话不说；
瘦得皮包骨头；瘦骨嶙峋；
削减达到最低限度，到最小化；
Englishsense: Your bones are the hard parts inside your body which together form your skeleton.
If you bone a piece of meat or fish, you remove the bones from it before cooking it.
A bone tool or ornament is made of bone.
The bare bones of something are its most basic parts or details.
If something is too close to the bone, it makes you feel uncomfortable because it is very close to the truth or to the real nature of something.
If you say that you feel or know something in your bones, you are indicating that you are certain about it, although you cannot explain why.
If you make no bones about something, you talk openly about it, rather than trying to keep it a secret.
If you make no bones about doing something that is unpleasant or difficult or that might upset someone else, you do it without hesitating.
You can say someone is just skin and bone when you do not approve of the fact that they are very thin.
If something such as costs are cut to the bone, they are reduced to the minimum possible.
You use to the bone to indicate that you are very deeply affected by something. For example, if you feel chilled to the bone, your whole body feels extremely cold, often because you have had a shock.

Chinesesense: 保险公司付给投保人的红利，余利；
Englishsense: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone’s pay, usually because they have worked very hard.
A bonus is something good that you get in addition to something else, and which you would not usually expect.
A bonus is a sum of money that an insurance company pays to its policyholders, for example a percentage of the company’s profits.

Chinesesense: 骨瘦如柴的；瘦骨嶙峋的；
人体或动物的器官骨质的；
Englishsense: Someone who has a bony face or bony hands, for example, has a very thin face or very thin hands, with very little flesh covering their bones.
The bony parts of a person’s or animal’s body are the parts made of bone.
If you describe fish that you are eating as bony, you mean that it has a lot of bones.

Chinesesense: 一册[邮票]; 一纸板[火柴]; 一本票券；
公司或组织机构的账册，账簿，名册；
足球裁判记名警告严重犯规的球员；
完全不了解的人；一无所知的事物；谜；
旅馆、餐馆、剧院或交通工具被预订一空，满座，客满；
当权者对违法者从严惩罚；
Englishsense: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.
A book of something such as stamps, matches, or tickets is a small number of them fastened together between thin cardboard covers.
When you book something such as a hotel room or a ticket, you arrange to have it or use it at a particular time.
A company’s or organization’s books are its records of money that has been spent and earned or of the names of people who belong to it.
When a referee books a football player who has seriously broken the rules of the game, he or she officially writes down the player’s name.
When a police officer books someone, he or she officially records their name and the offence that they may be charged with.
In a very long written work such as the Bible, a book is one of the sections into which it is divided.
If you are in someone’s bad books, they are annoyed with you. If you are in their good books, they are pleased with you.
If you bring someone to book, you punish them for an offence or make them explain their behaviour officially.
If you say that someone or something is a closed book, you mean that you do not know anything about them.
If a hotel, restaurant, theatre, or transport service is fully booked, or booked solid, it is booked up.
In my book means ’in my opinion’ or ’according to my beliefs’.
If someone in authority throws the book at someone who has committed an offence, they give the offender the greatest punishment that they are allowed to.
A bookstore is a shop where books are sold.

Chinesesense: 数量的增长；频率的加快；成功；
浮木挡栅，水栅用来阻挡溢出的油扩散；
人)吼叫；[大炮或大鼓发隆隆声；
Englishsense: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.
A boom in something is an increase in its amount, frequency, or success.
If the economy or a business is booming, the amount of things being bought or sold is increasing.
On a boat, the boom is the long pole which is attached to the bottom of the sail and to the mast and which you move when you want to alter the direction in which you are sailing.
A boom is a large floating barrier that is used for stopping oil that has spilled from spreading.
When something such as someone’s voice, a cannon, or a big drum booms, it makes a loud, deep sound that lasts for several seconds.

Chinesesense: 使增长；推动；改进；使兴旺；
Englishsense: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.
If something boosts your confidence or morale, it improves it.

Chinesesense: 有正面效果的事物；起推动作用的事物；
Englishsense: A booster is something that increases a positive or desirable quality.
A booster is an extra engine in a machine such as a space rocket, which provides an extra amount of power at certain times.
A booster is a small injection of a drug that you have some time after a larger injection, in order to make sure that the first injection will remain effective.
A booster is someone who supports a sports team, organization, person, or place very enthusiastically.

Chinesesense: (步行、运动等时穿的) 厚底短筒靴；
在某人已感到虚弱或苦恼时说刻薄伤人的话，落井下石；
Englishsense: Boots are shoes that cover your whole foot and the lower part of your leg.
Boots are strong, heavy shoes which cover your ankle and which have thick soles. You wear them to protect your feet, for example when you are walking or taking part in sport.
If you boot something such as a ball, you kick it hard.
The boot of a car is a covered space at the back or front, in which you carry things such as luggage and shopping.
To boot a car means to fit a Denver boot to one of its wheels so that it cannot be driven away.
If you get the boot or are given the boot, you are told that you are not wanted any more, either in your job or by someone you are having a relationship with.
If someone puts the boot in, they attack another person by saying something cruel, often when the person is already feeling weak or upset.
You can say to boot to emphasize that you have added something else to something or to a list of things that you have just said.

Chinesesense: 餐厅或咖啡馆中的火车座，雅座；
通常设在集市的娱乐棚，售货摊；
Englishsense: A booth is a small area separated from a larger public area by screens or thin walls where, for example, people can make a telephone call or vote in private.
A booth in a restaurant or café consists of a table with long fixed seats on two or sometimes three sides of it.
A booth is a small tent or stall, usually at a fair, in which you can buy goods or watch some form of entertainment.
A booth is a stall at an exhibition, for example with a display of goods for sale or with information leaflets.

Chinesesense: 花园边上的狭长花坛，花带；
Englishsense: The border between two countries or regions is the dividing line between them. Sometimes the border also refers to the land close to this line.
A country that borders another country, a sea, or a river is next to it.
A border is a strip or band around the edge of something.
In a garden, a border is a long strip of ground along the edge planted with flowers.
If something is bordered by another thing, the other thing forms a line along the edge of it.

Chinesesense: 使厌烦透顶；使烦得要命；
令人厌烦的人；无趣的人；
令人生厌的事；无聊的事；
每年某一时期海水涌入江河的涌潮,激潮；
Englishsense: If someone or something bores you, you find them dull and uninteresting.
If someone or something bores you to tears, bores you to death, or bores you stiff, they bore you very much indeed.
You describe someone as a bore when you think that they talk in a very uninteresting way.
You can describe a situation as a bore when you find it annoying.
If you bore a hole in something, you make a deep round hole in it using a special tool.
If someone’s eyes bore into you, they stare intensely at you.
A bore is a very large wave that moves quickly up certain rivers from the sea at particular times of the year as a result of unusual tides.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 感到厌倦的；感到厌烦的；
Englishsense: If you are bored, you feel tired and impatient because you have lost interest in something or because you have nothing to do.
Boredom is the state of being bored.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Someone or something boring is so dull and uninteresting that they make people tired and impatient.

Chinesesense: 生下来[有某种疾病或问题]; 天生具有某种性格；
用于姓名前出生取名…的；
Englishsense: When a baby is born, it comes out of its mother’s body at the beginning of its life. In formal English, if you say that someone is born of someone or to someone, you mean that person is their parent.
If someone is born with a particular disease, problem, or characteristic, they have it from the time they are born.
You can use be born in front of a particular name to show that a person was given this name at birth, although they may be better known by another name.
You use born to describe someone who has a natural ability to do a particular activity or job. For example, if you are a born cook, you have a natural ability to cook well.
When an idea or organization is born, it comes into existence. If something is born of a particular emotion or activity, it exists as a result of that emotion or activity.

Chinesesense: 捡回一条命；余下的光阴不多；好景不长；
Englishsense: If you borrow something that belongs to someone else, you take it or use it for a period of time, usually with their permission.
If you borrow money from someone or from a bank, they give it to you and you agree to pay it back at some time in the future.
If you borrow a book from a library, you take it away for a fixed period of time.
If you borrow something such as a word or an idea from another language or from another person’s work, you use it in your own language or work.
Someone who is living on borrowed time or who is on borrowed time has continued to live or to do something for longer than was expected, and is likely to die or be stopped from doing it soon.
A borrower is a person or organization that borrows money.

Chinesesense: 对…颐指气使；对…指手画脚；
为自己打工；自己拿主意；
Englishsense: Your boss is the person in charge of the organization or department where you work.
If you are the boss in a group or relationship, you are the person who makes all the decisions.
If you say that someone bosses you, you mean that they keep telling you what to do in a way that is irritating.
If you are your own boss, you work for yourself or make your own decisions and do not have anyone telling you what to do.
You use both when you are referring to two people or things and saying that something is true about each of them.
You use the structure both...and when you are giving two facts or alternatives and emphasizing that each of them is true or possible.

Chinesesense: 麻烦用于淡化问题的严重性；
这不麻烦；不费事；没什么；
Englishsense: If you do not bother to do something or if you do not bother with it, you do not do it, consider it, or use it because you think it is unnecessary or because you are too lazy.
Bother means trouble or difficulty. You can also use bother to refer to an activity which causes this, especially when you would prefer not to do it or get involved with it.
You use bother to refer to serious trouble, usually when you want to make it sound less serious than it really is.
If something bothers you, or if you bother about it, it worries, annoys, or upsets you.
If someone bothers you, they talk to you when you want to be left alone or interrupt you when you are busy.
Some people say ’ bother ’ or ’ bother it ’ when they are annoyed about something.
If you say that you can’t be bothered to do something, you mean that you are not going to do it because you think it is unnecessary or because you are too lazy.
If you say ’ it’s no bother ’ after offering to do something for someone, you are emphasizing that you really want to do it and that it will take very little effort.

Chinesesense: 在最后时刻因胆怯而放弃，打退堂鼓；
Englishsense: A bottle is a glass or plastic container in which drinks and other liquids are kept. Bottles are usually round with straight sides and a narrow top.
To bottle a drink or other liquid means to put it into bottles after it has been made.
A bottle is a drinking container used by babies. It has a special rubber part at the top through which they can suck their drink.
To bottle fruit means to put it into special jars, in order to preserve it.
Bottle is used to refer to courage or boldness.
If someone hits the bottle, they drink a lot of alcohol.
If you say that someone has bottled it, you mean that they have lost their courage at the last moment and have not done something they intended to do.

Chinesesense: 最下方的；底部的；底层的；
[某市场或产业的)最差状况，低谷；
组织机构或职业架构的最底层，基层；
调查、测试或联赛中的表现最差者，最后一名；
比基尼泳装的泳裤；田径服、睡衣的裤子；
是…的真正原因；是…的根源；
找到…的真正起因；查寻到…的根源；
Englishsense: The bottom of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.
The bottom thing or layer in a series of things or layers is the lowest one.
The bottom of an object is the flat surface at its lowest point. You can also refer to the inside or outside of this surface as the bottom.
If you say that the bottom has dropped or fallen out of a market or industry, you mean that people have stopped buying the products it sells.
The bottom of a street or garden is the end farthest away from you or from your house.
The bottom of a table is the end farthest away from where you are sitting. The bottom of a bed is the end where you usually rest your feet.
The bottom of an organization or career structure is the lowest level in it, where new employees often start.
If someone is bottom or at the bottom in a survey, test, or league their performance is worse than that of all the other people involved.
Your bottom is the part of your body that you sit on.
The lower part of a bikini, tracksuit, or pair of pyjamas can be referred to as the bottoms or the bottom.
You use at bottom to emphasize that you are stating what you think is the real nature of something or the real truth about a situation.
If something is at the bottom of a problem or unpleasant situation, it is the real cause of it.
You can say that you mean something from the bottom of your heart to emphasize that you mean it very sincerely.
If you want to get to the bottom of a problem, you want to solve it by finding out its real cause.
Some people say bottoms up to each other just before drinking an alcoholic drink.
A boulder is a large rounded rock.

Chinesesense: (在柔软物体表面) 跳上跳下，蹦跳，弹跳；
向…透露[想法]; 与…探讨想法；
支票被拒付；银行拒付支票；
Englishsense: When an object such as a ball bounces or when you bounce it, it moves upwards from a surface or away from it immediately after hitting it.
The bounce of a sports field is the condition of it, which determines how high a ball will bounce on it.
If sound or light bounces off a surface or is bounced off it, it reaches the surface and is reflected back.
If something bounces or if something bounces it, it swings or moves up and down.
If you bounce on a soft surface, you jump up and down on it repeatedly.
If you bounce a child on your knee, you lift him or her up and down quickly and repeatedly for fun.
If someone bounces somewhere, they move there in an energetic way, because they are feeling happy.
If you bounce your ideas off someone, you tell them to that person, in order to find out what they think about them.
If someone bounces you into doing something you do not really want to do, they make you do it, usually by starting a process which cannot easily be stopped.
If a cheque bounces or if a bank bounces it, the bank refuses to accept it and pay out the money, because the person who wrote it does not have enough money in their account.
If an e-mail or other electronic message bounces, it is returned to the person who sent it because the address was wrong or because of a problem with one of the computers involved in sending it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 对某事并不确定或无确凿证据时，认为其肯定会，确定是；
与…紧密相连的；与…密切相关的；同…难以分开的；
我不得不说令人不快或出乎意料的事；
与…密切相关的；同…难以分开的；
数量飞快增长；表现迅速改进；
Englishsense: If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.
If you say that something is bound to happen or be true, you feel confident and certain of it, although you have no definite knowledge or evidence.
If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely associated with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other.
If a vehicle or person is bound for a particular place, they are travelling towards it.
You can say ’ I am bound to say ’ to introduce a statement expressing something that you find undesirable or unexpected.
If something is bound up in a particular form or place, it is fixed in that form or contained in that place.
If one thing is bound up with or in another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult to consider the two things separately.
Bounds are limits which normally restrict what can happen or what people can do.
If an area of land is bounded by something, that thing is situated around its edge.
If someone’s life or situation is bounded by certain things, those are its most important aspects and it is limited or restricted by them.
If a person or animal bounds in a particular direction, they move quickly with large steps or jumps.
A bound is a long or high jump.
If the quantity or performance of something bounds ahead, it increases or improves quickly and suddenly.
If you say that a feeling or quality knows no bounds, you are emphasizing that it is very strong or intense.
If a place is out of bounds, people are not allowed to go there.
If something is out of bounds, people are not allowed to do it, use it, see it, or know about it.

Chinesesense: 学科或活动的界限，边界；
Englishsense: The boundary of an area of land is an imaginary line that separates it from other areas.
The boundaries of something such as a subject or activity are the limits that people think that it has.

Chinesesense: 大量提供的东西；慷慨的赠予；
尤指为找到或杀死某人而悬赏的赏金，奖金；
Englishsense: You can refer to something that is provided in large amounts as bounty.
A bounty is money that is offered as a reward for doing something, especially for finding or killing a particular person.

Chinesesense: 尤指葡萄酒散发的香味，芬芳；
Englishsense: A bouquet is a bunch of flowers which is attractively arranged.
The bouquet of something, especially wine, is the pleasant smell that it has.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 传统中产阶级的含贬义；
马克思主义者所指的资本主义的，资产阶级的；
Englishsense: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you disapprove of them because you consider them typical of conventional middle-class people.
Marxists use bourgeois when referring to the capitalist system and to the social class that owns most of the wealth in that system.

Chinesesense: 疾病或不愉快情绪的发作；
不愉快之事大量发生的一阵，一小段时间；
Englishsense: If you have a bout of an illness or of an unpleasant feeling, you have it for a short period.
A bout of something that is unpleasant is a short time during which it occurs a great deal.
A bout is a boxing or wrestling match.

Chinesesense: 时尚商店；时装店；精品店；
Englishsense: A boutique is a small shop that sells fashionable clothes, shoes, or jewellery.

Chinesesense: 鞠躬，欠身打招呼或表示恭敬；
向压力或他人的意愿让步；屈从于；屈服于；
演员或表演者向观众鞠躬致意；
鞋带或丝带系成的蝴蝶结；
小提琴等弦乐器的弓，琴弓；
Englishsense: When you bow to someone, you briefly bend your body towards them as a formal way of greeting them or showing respect.
If you bow your head, you bend it downwards so that you are looking towards the ground, for example because you want to show respect or because you are thinking deeply about something.
If you bow to pressure or to someone’s wishes, you agree to do what they want you to do.
If you are bowed by something, you are made unhappy and anxious by it, and lose hope.
If someone bows to the inevitable and does something that they do not want to do, they do it, because circumstances force them to do it.
If an actor or entertainer takes a bow, he or she shows appreciation of an audience’s applause by bowing to them.
The front part of a ship is called the bow or the bows. The plural bows can be used to refer either to one or to more than one of these parts.
A bow is a knot with two loops and two loose ends that is used in tying shoelaces and ribbons.
A bow is a weapon for shooting arrows which consists of a long piece of curved wood with a string attached to both its ends.
The bow of a violin or other stringed instrument is a long thin piece of wood with fibres stretched along it, which you move across the strings of the instrument in order to play it.
Your bowels are the tubes in your body through which digested food passes from your stomach to your anus.
You can refer in a polite way to someone getting rid of the waste from their body by saying that they move, open, or empty their bowels.
You can refer to the parts deep inside something such as the earth, a building, or a machine as the bowels of that thing.

Chinesesense: 草地滚木球运动中用的木球；
玩草地滚木球游戏；玩保龄球；
在板球等运动中投球给击球手；
在板球等运动中因为投球手击中三柱门迫使击球手出局；
尤指愉快地乘车或船快速行驶；
椭圆形运动场；环形剧场；
主赛季后最强的大学球队参加的季后赛，杯赛；
Englishsense: A bowl is a round container with a wide uncovered top. Some kinds of bowl are used, for example, for serving or eating food from, or in cooking, while other larger kinds are used for washing or cleaning.
The contents of a bowl can be referred to as a bowl of something.
You can refer to the hollow rounded part of an object as its bowl.
Bowls is a game in which players try to roll large wooden balls as near as possible to a small wooden ball. Bowls is usually played outdoors on grass.
A set of bowls is a set of round wooden balls that you play bowls with.
If you bowl, you play the game of bowls or the game of bowling.
In a sport such as cricket, when a bowler bowls a ball, he or she sends it down the pitch towards a batsman.
In a sport such as cricket, when a batsman is bowled, he has to leave the pitch because the bowler has hit the wicket with the ball.
If you bowl along in a car or on a boat, you move along very quickly, especially when you are enjoying yourself.
A large stadium where sports or concerts take place is sometimes called a Bowl.
A bowl or bowl game is a competition in which the best college teams play, after the main season has ended.
Bowling is a game in which you roll a heavy ball down a narrow track towards a group of wooden objects and try to knock down as many of them as possible.
In a sport such as cricket, bowling is the action or activity of bowling the ball towards the batsman.

Chinesesense: 在纸张、道路等上印制或画出的方格，方框；
用在数字前表示邮政地址邮政信箱，邮箱；
黄杨小型长绿树，常用作篱笆；
按照拳击运动的规则击打；
Englishsense: A box is a square or rectangular container with hard or stiff sides. Boxes often have lids.
A box is a square or rectangle that is printed or drawn on a piece of paper, a road, or on some other surface.
In football, the box is the penalty area of the field.
A box is a small separate area in a theatre or at a sports ground or stadium, where a small number of people can sit to watch the performance or game.
Television is sometimes referred to as the box.
Box is used before a number as a postal address by organizations that receive a lot of mail.
Box is a small evergreen tree with dark leaves which is often used to form hedges.
To box means to fight someone according to the rules of boxing.
A boxer is someone who takes part in the sport of boxing.
A boxer is a dog with short hair and a rather flat face.
Boxing is a sport in which two people wearing large padded gloves fight according to special rules.

Chinesesense: 男青年，小伙子尤用于指青年男女恋爱关系时；
家伙，伙计尤用于亲切谈论某人时；
家伙，伙计用于吆喝马或狗时；
好家伙(表示激动、羡慕等情感) ；
男人总归是男人用以表示男人的典型行为不会改变；
Englishsense: A boy is a child who will grow up to be a man.
You can refer to a young man as a boy, especially when talking about relationships between boys and girls.
Someone’s boy is their son.
You can refer to a man as a boy, especially when you are talking about him in an affectionate way.
You can use boy when giving instructions to a horse or dog.
The police are sometimes referred to as the boys in blue.
Some people say ’ boy ’ or ’ oh boy ’ in order to express feelings of excitement or admiration.

If you say boys will be boys, for example when a group of men are behaving noisily or aggressively, you are suggesting in a light-hearted way that this is typical male behaviour and will never change.
If a man is described as one of the boys, he is accepted by a group of male friends who do things that are thought of as typically masculine.
If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.
Someone’s boyfriend is a man or boy with whom they are having a romantic or sexual relationship.

Chinesesense: 使做好准备面对不快的事或困难；
为保持平衡或避免摔倒使紧靠；
用以加固或支撑身体某部位的支架，托架；
Englishsense: If you brace yourself for something unpleasant or difficult, you prepare yourself for it.
If you brace yourself against something or brace part of your body against it, you press against something in order to steady your body or to avoid falling.
If you brace your shoulders or knees, you keep them stiffly in a particular position.
To brace something means to strengthen or support it with something else.
You can refer to two things of the same kind as a brace of that thing. The plural form is also brace.
A brace is a device attached to a part of a person’s body, for example to a weak leg, in order to strengthen or support it.
A brace is a metal device that can be fastened to a child’s teeth in order to help them grow straight.
Braces are a pair of straps that pass over your shoulders and fasten to your trousers at the front and back in order to stop them from falling down.

Braces or curly braces are a pair of written marks that you place around words, numbers, or parts of a computer code, for example to indicate that they are connected in some way or are separate from other parts of the writing or code.
A bracelet is a chain or band, usually made of metal, which you wear around your wrist as jewellery.

Chinesesense: 收入、年龄、价格等的范围，等级段；
固定在墙上的托架，支架，角撑架；
把…归为一类；把…相提并论；
括号，括弧[美国英语中称作parentheses] ；
Englishsense: If you say that someone or something is in a particular bracket, you mean that they come within a particular range, for example a range of incomes, ages, or prices.
Brackets are pieces of metal, wood, or plastic that are fastened to a wall in order to support something such as a shelf.
If two or more people or things are bracketed together, they are considered to be similar or related in some way.

Brackets are a pair of written marks that you place round a word, expression, or sentence in order to indicate that you are giving extra information. In British English, curved marks like these are also called brackets, but in American English, they are called parentheses.
Brackets are pair of marks that are placed around a series of symbols in a mathematical expression to indicate that those symbols function as one item within the expression.
If you brag, you say in a very proud way that you have something or have done something.

Chinesesense: 用来装饰衣服、窗帘等的布带，穗带；
把头发编成辫子；把丝线编成辫状；
Englishsense: Braid is a narrow piece of decorated cloth or twisted threads, which is used to decorate clothes or curtains.
If you braid hair or a group of threads, you twist three or more lengths of the hair or threads over and under each other to make one thick length.
A braid is a length of hair which has been divided into three or more lengths and then braided.

Chinesesense: 把…的脑袋打伤；把…脑袋打开花；
用枪把…的脑袋打开花；射中…的头部；
Englishsense: Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body’s activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.
Your brain is your mind and the way that you think.
If someone has brains or a good brain, they have the ability to learn and understand things quickly, to solve problems, and to make good decisions.
If someone is the brains behind an idea or an organization, he or she had that idea or makes the important decisions about how that organization is managed.
To brain someone means to hit them forcefully on the head.
To beat someone’s brains out or bash their brains in means to hit their head very hard, so that they are badly injured or killed.
To blow someone’s brains out means to shoot them in the head, killing them.
If someone has something on the brain, they keep thinking about it.
If you pick someone’s brains, you ask them to help you with a problem because they know more about the subject than you.

Chinesesense: 刹车；用刹车使车减速；刹住车；
Englishsense: Brakes are devices in a vehicle that make it go slower or stop.
When a vehicle or its driver brakes, or when a driver brakes a vehicle, the driver makes it slow down or stop by using the brakes.
You can use brake in a number of expressions to indicate that something has slowed down or stopped.

Chinesesense: 企业或组织的分支机构，分部，分店；
(政府或公安机关等的) 部门，机构；
Englishsense: The branches of a tree are the parts that grow out from its trunk and have leaves, flowers, or fruit growing on them.
A branch of a business or other organization is one of the offices, shops, or groups which belong to it and which are located in different places.
A branch of an organization such as the government or the police force is a department that has a particular function.
A branch of a subject is a part or type of it.
A branch of your family is a group of its members who are descended from one particular person.

Chinesesense: 思维或行为等的一种，一类；
Englishsense: A brand of a product is the version of it that is made by one particular manufacturer.
A brand of something such as a way of thinking or behaving is a particular kind of it.
If someone is branded as something bad, people think they are that thing.
When you brand an animal, you put a permanent mark on its skin in order to show who it belongs to, usually by burning a mark onto its skin.

A brand is a permanent mark on the skin of an animal, which shows who it belongs to. Usage Note: The brand of a product such as jeans, tea, or soap is its name, which can also be the name of the company that makes or sells it. The make of a car or electrical appliance such as a radio or washing machine is the name of the company that produces it. If you talk about what type of product or service you want, you are talking about its quality and what features it should have. You can also talk about types of people or of abstract things.... which type of pram to choose.... a new type of bank account.... looking for a certain type of actor. A model of car or of some other devices is a name that is given to a particular type, for example, Ford Escort or Nissan Micra. Note that type can also be used informally to mean either make or model. For example, if someone asks what type of car you have got, you could reply ’an estate’, ’a Ford’, or perhaps ’an Escort’. brand可以用来表示牛仔裤、茶或肥皂之类产品的品牌，也可以表示制造或销售这些产品的企业的名称。make用来表示生产汽车或收音机、洗衣机之类电器的制造商的名称。type指具有某种质量或特色的某类产品或服务，也可以指不同类型的人或抽象事物：which type of pram to choose选择哪种型号的婴儿车，a new type of bank account一种新型银行账户，looking for a certain type of actor寻找某一类型的演员。model表示汽车等装置设备的type特定型号，例如Ford Escort福特护卫者或Nissan Micra尼桑米克拉。注意，也可用type表示make或model，不过这是非正式的表述方式。例如，某人如果问what type of car you have got你买的是什么车, 可以回答an estate旅行车, a Ford福特或an Escort护卫者。
A brand-new object is completely new.

Chinesesense: 尤用于制作装饰品和乐器的黄铜；
交响乐队的铜管乐乐器组，铜管乐器；
常见于教堂的黄铜纪念牌；
军队或其他机构的高级军官，高层人物；
讨论基本事实；探讨实质问题；
Englishsense: Brass is a yellow-coloured metal made from copper and zinc. It is used especially for making ornaments and musical instruments.
The brass is the section of an orchestra which consists of brass wind instruments such as trumpets and horns.
Brasses are flat pieces of brass with writing or a picture cut into them, which are often found in churches.
In the army or in other organizations, the brass are the people in the highest positions.
If you get down to brass tacks, you discuss the basic, most important facts of a situation.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 通常为达到某目标勇敢面对；
尤指善于作战的印第安勇士；
Englishsense: Someone who is brave is willing to do things which are dangerous, and does not show fear in difficult or dangerous situations.
If you brave unpleasant or dangerous conditions, you deliberately expose yourself to them, usually in order to achieve something.
A brave is a young Native American man, especially one who is good at fighting.
If someone is putting on a brave face or is putting a brave face on a difficult situation, they are pretending that they are happy or satisfied when they are not.

Chinesesense: 巴西的；巴西人的；巴西文化的；
Englishsense: Brazilian means belonging or relating to Brazil, or to its people or culture.

Chinesesense: 违反，破坏条约、法律或承诺；
对条约、法律或承诺的违反，破坏；
Englishsense: If you breach an agreement, a law, or a promise, you break it.
A breach of an agreement, a law, or a promise is an act of breaking it.
A breach in a relationship is a serious disagreement which often results in the relationship ending.
If someone or something breaches a barrier, they make an opening in it, usually leaving it weakened or destroyed.
If you breach someone’s security or their defences, you manage to get through and attack an area that is heavily guarded and protected.
If you step into the breach, you do a job or task which someone else was supposed to do or has done in the past, because they are suddenly unable to do it.

Chinesesense: 通过工作等挣得的钱财，金钱；
Englishsense: Bread is a very common food made from flour, water, and yeast.
If you earn your bread doing a particular job or activity, you earn your money doing it.
If food such as fish or meat is breaded, it is covered in tiny pieces of dry bread called breadcrumbs. It can then be fried or grilled.
The breadth of something is the distance between its two sides.
The breadth of something is its quality of consisting of or involving many different things.
If you say that someone does something or something happens throughout or across the length and breadth of a place, you are emphasizing that it happens everywhere in that place.

Chinesesense: 使表层、盖子或密封破裂；撕开；
破坏，违反规则、承诺或协议；
结束[困难或不利局面]; 打破僵局；
与…决裂；断绝[联系]; 放弃；
瓦解…的决心；使丧失勇气；毁掉…的前程；
为短暂歇息而打断旅程；
减弱[势头]; 减轻力度；
消息在报纸、电视或电台发布，传播；
通常以委婉的方式透露，告知坏消息；
因悲伤或害怕嗓音突变，变调；
网球比赛中破，赢得对手的发球局；
Englishsense: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.
If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks, you are injured because a bone cracks or splits.
If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through.
When a tool or piece of machinery breaks or when you break it, it is damaged and no longer works.
If you break a rule, promise, or agreement, you do something that you should not do according to that rule, promise, or agreement.
If you break free or loose, you free yourself from something or escape from it.
If someone breaks something, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation that has existed for some time, they end it or change it.
If someone or something breaks a silence, they say something or make a noise after a long period of silence.
If there is a break in the cloud or weather, it changes and there is a short period of sunshine or fine weather.
If you break with a group of people or a traditional way of doing things, or you break your connection with them, you stop being involved with that group or stop doing things in that way.
If you break a habit or if someone breaks you of it, you no longer have that habit.
To break someone means to destroy their determination and courage, their success, or their career.
If someone breaks for a short period of time, they rest or change from what they are doing for a short period.
A break is a short period of time when you have a rest or a change from what you are doing, especially if you are working or if you are in a boring or unpleasant situation.
A break is a short holiday.
If you break your journey somewhere, you stop there for a short time so that you can have a rest.
To break the force of something such as a blow or fall means to weaken its effect, for example by getting in the way of it.
When a piece of news breaks, people hear about it from the newspapers, television, or radio.
When you break a piece of bad news to someone, you tell it to them, usually in a kind way.
A break is a lucky opportunity that someone gets to achieve something. [Informal]
If you break a record, you beat the previous record for a particular achievement.
When day or dawn breaks, it starts to grow light after the night has ended.
When a wave breaks, it passes its highest point and turns downwards, for example when it reaches the shore.
If you break a secret code, you work out how to understand it.
If someone’s voice breaks when they are speaking, it changes its sound, for example because they are sad or afraid.
When a boy’s voice breaks, it becomes deeper and sounds more like a man’s voice.
If the weather breaks or a storm breaks, it suddenly becomes rainy or stormy after a period of sunshine.
In tennis, if you break your opponent’s serve, you win a game in which your opponent is serving.
The break of day or the break of dawn is the time when it begins to grow light after the night.
You can say ’ give me a break ’ to show that you are annoyed by what someone has said or done.
If you make a break or make a break for it, you run to escape from something.

Chinesesense: 关系的破裂；计划、讨论等的失败，结束；
汽车或机器的故障，损坏；
Englishsense: The breakdown of something such as a relationship, plan, or discussion is its failure or ending.
If you have a breakdown, you become very depressed, so that you are unable to cope with your life.
If a car or a piece of machinery has a breakdown, it stops working.
A breakdown of something is a list of its separate parts.
Breakfast is the first meal of the day. It is usually eaten in the early part of the morning.
A cooked breakfast or a hot breakfast is a breakfast that consists of cooked food, such as bacon and eggs.
When you breakfast, you have breakfast. See usage note at: meal
A breakthrough is an important development or achievement.

Chinesesense: 婚姻、关系或联系的破裂，终结；
组织或国家的分裂，解体；
Englishsense: The break-up of a marriage, relationship, or association is the act of it finishing or coming to an end because the people involved decide that it is not working successfully.
The break-up of an organization or a country is the act of it separating or dividing into several parts.

Chinesesense: 衬衫、夹克或外套的胸部；
Englishsense: A woman’s breasts are the two soft, round parts on her chest that can produce milk to feed a baby.
A person’s breast is the upper part of his or her chest.
The breast is often considered to be the part of your body where your emotions are.
A bird’s breast is the front part of its body.
The breast of a shirt, jacket, or coat is the part which covers the top part of the chest.
You can refer to piece of meat that is cut from the front of a bird or lamb as breast.
If you say that someone beats their breast, you are emphasizing that they are very angry or upset about something, or that they are pretending to be very angry or upset about it.
If you make a clean breast of something, you tell someone the truth about yourself or about something wrong that you have done.

Chinesesense: 到室外呼吸新鲜空气，透口气；
令人耳目一新的事物；新鲜刺激的东西；
喘过气来；恢复正常呼吸；
通常因为震惊倒吸一口冷气；
屏息静气焦急或激动地等待；
喘不过气；上气不接下气；
但同时/但紧接着尤用于谴责某人的言论自相矛盾；
美或惊讶得令人喘不过气来；使人惊叹；
Englishsense: Your breath is the air that you let out through your mouth when you breathe. If someone has bad breath, their breath smells unpleasant.
When you take a breath, you breathe in once.
If you say that there is not a breath of wind or air, you are emphasizing that there is no wind and the air is very still.
A breath of something, is a small amount of it.
If you go outside for a breath of fresh air or for a breath of air, you go outside because it is unpleasantly warm indoors.
If you describe something new or different as a breath of fresh air, you mean that it makes a situation or subject more interesting or exciting.
When you get your breath back after doing something energetic, you start breathing normally again.
When you catch your breath while you are doing something energetic, you stop for a short time so that you can start breathing normally again.
If something makes you catch your breath, it makes you take a short breath of air, usually because it shocks you.
If you do not have time to draw breath, you do not have time to have a break from what you are doing.
If you hold your breath, you make yourself stop breathing for a few moments, for example because you are under water.
If you say that someone is holding their breath, you mean that they are waiting anxiously or excitedly for something to happen.
If you say that you won’t hold your breath, you mean that you do not expect something to happen even though someone has suggested that it might.
When someone takes their last breath, they die.
If you are out of breath, you are breathing very quickly and with difficulty because you have been doing something energetic.
You can use in the same breath or in the next breath to indicate that someone says two very different or contradictory things, especially when you are criticizing them.
If you are short of breath, you find it difficult to breathe properly, for example because you are ill. You can also say that someone suffers from shortness of breath.
If you say that something takes your breath away, you are emphasizing that it is extremely beautiful or surprising.
If you say something under your breath, you say it in a very quiet voice, often because you do not want other people to hear what you are saying.
If someone says you are wasting your breath, they mean that the person you are talking to will not take any notice and so there is no point saying anything to them.

Chinesesense: 将生气、信心或兴奋注入；为…带来；
Englishsense: When people or animals breathe, they take air into their lungs and let it out again. When they breathe smoke or a particular kind of air, they take it into their lungs and let it out again as they breathe.
If someone breathes something, they say it very quietly.
If you do not breathe a word about something, you say nothing about it, because it is a secret.
If someone breathes life, confidence, or excitement into something, they improve it by adding this quality.
If you let wine breathe, you open the bottle to allow the air to get in and improve its flavour before you drink it.
When someone breathes their last, they die.
A breed of a pet animal or farm animal is a particular type of it. For example, terriers are a breed of dog.
If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.
When animals breed, they have babies.
If you say that something breeds bad feeling or bad behaviour, you mean that it causes bad feeling or bad behaviour to develop.
You can refer to someone or something as one of a particular breed of person or thing when you want to talk about what they are like.
Someone who was born and bred in a place was born there and grew up there.
If someone says that a person has breeding, they mean that they think the person is from a good social background and has good manners.

Chinesesense: 随意轻松地进入；漫步走入；
轻松过关，轻易通过比赛或测试；
Englishsense: A breeze is a gentle wind.
If you breeze into a place or a position, you enter it in a very casual or relaxed manner.
If you breeze through something such as a game or test, you cope with it easily.
If you say that something is a breeze, you mean that it is very easy to do or to achieve.
Bricks are rectangular blocks of baked clay used for building walls, which are usually red or brown. Brick is the material made up of these blocks.
If you say that someone is a brick, you mean that they have helped you or supported you when you were in a difficult situation.
If you are banging your head against a brick wall, what you are saying or doing is not having any effect although you keep saying or doing it.
If you hit a brick wall or come up against a brick wall, you are unable to continue or make progress because something stops you.
You can use bricks and mortar to refer to houses and other buildings, especially when they are considered as an investment.
A bride is a woman who is getting married or who has just got married.

Chinesesense: 弥合[分歧]; 消除隔阂；
小提琴、吉他等弦乐器的琴马，琴桥；
Englishsense: A bridge is a structure that is built over a railway, river, or road so that people or vehicles can cross from one side to the other.
A bridge between two places is a piece of land that joins or connects them.
To bridge the gap between two people or things means to reduce it or get rid of it.
Something that bridges the gap between two very different things has some of the qualities of each of these things.
If something or someone acts as a bridge between two people, groups, or things, they connect them.
The bridge is the place on a ship from which it is steered.
The bridge of your nose is the thin top part of it, between your eyes.
The bridge of a pair of glasses is the part that rests on your nose.
The bridge of a violin, guitar, or other stringed instrument is the small piece of wood under the strings that holds them up.
A bridge is a piece of metal or plastic that holds false teeth in place by connecting them to natural teeth.
Bridge is a card game for four players in which the players begin by declaring how many tricks they expect to win.
If you burn your bridges, you do something which forces you to continue with a particular course of action, and makes it impossible for you to return to an earlier situation or relationship.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: 讲话或文章简短的，简洁的；

Englishsense: Something that is brief lasts for only a short time.
A brief speech or piece of writing does not contain too many words or details.
If you are brief, you say what you want to say in as few words as possible.
You can describe a period of time as brief if you want to emphasize that it is very short.
Men’s or women’s underpants can be referred to as briefs.
If someone briefs you, especially about a piece of work or a serious matter, they give you information that you need before you do it or consider it.
If someone gives you a brief, they officially give you responsibility for dealing with a particular thing.
If you refer to something in brief, you are referring to a shortened version of it with few details.
You can say in brief to indicate that you are about to say something in as few words as possible or to give a summary of what you have just said.
A briefcase is a case used for carrying documents in.

Chinesesense: 情况介绍会；任务下达会；
Englishsense: A briefing is a meeting at which information or instructions are given to people, especially before they do something.
Something that happens or is done briefly happens or is done for a very short period of time.
If you say or write something briefly, you use very few words or give very few details.
You can say briefly to indicate that you are about to say something in as few words as possible.

Chinesesense: 信奉某事或具有共同特点的一帮人，族；
Englishsense: A brigade is one of the groups which an army is divided into.
You can use brigade to refer to a group of people who believe strongly in a particular thing or who share a particular characteristic.

A bright idea is clever and original.
If someone looks or sounds bright, they look or sound cheerful and lively.
If the future is bright, it is likely to be pleasant or successful.
The brights on a car or other vehicle are the headlights when they are switched on fully.
If you look on the bright side, you try to be cheerful about a bad situation by thinking of some advantages that could result from it, or thinking that it is not as bad as it could have been.

Chinesesense: 开颜；露出喜色；快乐起来；
