If your eyes brighten, you suddenly look interested or excited.
If someone or something brightens a place, they make it more colourful and attractive.
If someone or something brightens a situation or the situation brightens, it becomes more pleasant, enjoyable, or favourable.
When a light brightens a place or when a place brightens, it becomes brighter or lighter.
If the weather brightens, it becomes less cloudy or rainy, and the sun starts to shine.

光线等明亮的，夺目的，灿烂的；
Englishsense: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.
You can say that something is brilliant when you are very pleased about it or think that it is very good.
A brilliant career or success is very successful.
A brilliant colour is extremely bright.
You describe light, or something that reflects light, as brilliant when it shines very brightly.

Chinesesense: 对某人提起[诉讼]; 将某人送上法庭；
提供，制作，播出电视或广播节目；
把某人带到或引到某话题；
强迫自己做令人伤心、窘迫或讨厌的事；
Englishsense: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.
If you bring something somewhere, you move it there.
If you bring something that someone wants or needs, you get it for them or carry it to them.
To bring something or someone to a place or position means to cause them to come to the place or move into that position.
If you bring something new to a place or group of people, you introduce it to that place or cause those people to hear or know about it.
To bring someone or something into a particular state or condition means to cause them to be in that state or condition.
If something brings a particular feeling, situation, or quality, it makes people experience it or have it.
If a period of time brings a particular thing, it happens during that time. [V n]
If you bring a legal action against someone or bring them to trial, you officially accuse them of doing something illegal.
If a television or radio programme is brought to you by an organization, they make it, broadcast it, or pay for it to be made or broadcast.
When you are talking, you can say that something brings you to a particular point in order to indicate that you have now reached that point and are going to talk about a new subject.
If you cannot bring yourself to do something, you cannot do it because you find it too upsetting, embarrassing, or disgusting.
If you bring up a particular subject, you introduce it into a discussion or conversation.
If someone brings up food or wind, food or air is forced up from their stomach through their mouth.
If you are on the brink of something, usually something important, terrible, or exciting, you are just about to do it or experience it.

Englishsense: A brisk activity or action is done quickly and in an energetic way.
If trade or business is brisk, things are being sold very quickly and a lot of money is being made.
If the weather is brisk, it is cold and fresh.
Someone who is brisk behaves in a busy, confident way which shows that they want to get things done quickly.

Chinesesense: 英国的；英国人的；英国文化的；
Englishsense: British means belonging or relating to the United Kingdom, or to its people or culture.

The British are the people of Great Britain. Usage Note: British describes people and things that come from anywhere in the United Kingdom, which consists of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland....British scientists. It is also used to describe anything to do with the administration of the United Kingdom and appears in the name of national organizations....the British government....British Airways. The British are the people who live in the United Kingdom. Britain or Great Britain refers to England, Scotland, and Wales, but not Northern Ireland. The British Isles are the group of islands that includes the United Kingdom and some other islands such as the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands. English describes people and things that live in or come from England. The English are the people who live in England. Chinesesense: 词义或含义广泛的，概括的；
描述或想法大致的，概括的，笼统的；
女人，娘们可能具冒犯意味；
Englishsense: Something that is broad is wide.
A broad smile is one in which your mouth is stretched very wide because you are very pleased or amused.
You use broad to describe something that includes a large number of different things or people.
You use broad to describe a word or meaning which covers or refers to a wide range of different things.
You use broad to describe a feeling or opinion that is shared by many people, or by people of many different kinds.
A broad description or idea is general rather than detailed.
A broad hint is a very obvious hint.
A broad accent is strong and noticeable.
Some men refer to women as broads. This use could cause offence.

Chinesesense: 无线电或电视广播；广播节目；电视节目；
电台或电视台广播，播出节目；
Englishsense: A broadcast is a programme, performance, or speech on the radio or on television.
To broadcast a programme means to send it out by radio waves, so that it can be heard on the radio or seen on television.

Chinesesense: 电台或电视台的广播员，播音员，节目主持人；
Englishsense: A broadcaster is someone who gives talks or takes part in interviews and discussions on radio or television programmes.

Chinesesense: 电台或电视台节目的制作播出，播放；
Englishsense: Broadcasting is the making and sending out of television and radio programmes.

Chinesesense: 扩大…的范围；增长，增加经验、受欢迎程度；
Englishsense: When something broadens, it becomes wider.
When you broaden something such as your experience or popularity or when it broadens, the number of things or people that it includes becomes greater.
If an experience broadens your mind, it makes you more willing to accept other people’s beliefs and customs.
You can use broadly to indicate that something is generally true.
Broccoli is a vegetable with green stalks and green or purple tops.

Chinesesense: 介绍产品或服务信息的小册子；
Englishsense: A brochure is a magazine or thin book with pictures that gives you information about a product or service.

Chinesesense: 线条不连贯的，断续的，中断的；
Englishsense: A broken line is not continuous but has gaps or spaces in it.
You can use broken to describe a marriage that has ended in divorce, or a home in which the parents of the family are divorced, when you think this is a sad or bad thing.
If someone talks in broken English, for example, or in broken French, they speak slowly and make a lot of mistakes because they do not know the language very well.

Chinesesense: (股票、外汇或商品) 经纪人，代理商；
国家或政府作为中间人协调，安排；
Englishsense: A broker is a person whose job is to buy and sell shares, foreign money, or goods for other people.
If a country or government brokers an agreement, a ceasefire, or a round of talks, they try to negotiate or arrange it.

Chinesesense: 经纪人收取的佣金，中介费，提成；
Englishsense: A brokerage or a brokerage firm is a company of brokers.
A brokerage fee or commission is the money charged by a broker for his or her services.
Bronze is a yellowish-brown metal which is a mixture of copper and tin.
A bronze is a statue or sculpture made of bronze.
A bronze is a bronze medal.
Something that is bronze is yellowish-brown in colour.

Chinesesense: 金雀花一种野生灌木，开许多黄色小花；
Englishsense: A broom is a kind of brush with a long handle. You use a broom for sweeping the floor.
Broom is a wild bush with a lot of tiny yellow flowers.

Chinesesense: 通常加入蔬菜或米的肉汤，汤；
Englishsense: Broth is a kind of soup. It usually has vegetables or rice in it.

Chinesesense: 兄弟；同胞；教友；国人；同行；同志；
用于某些公司或商店的名称中；
Englishsense: Your brother is a boy or a man who has the same parents as you.
You can describe a man as your brother if he belongs to the same race, religion, country, profession, or trade union as you, or if he has similar ideas to you.
Brothers is used in the names of some companies and shops.
Your brow is your forehead.
Your brows are your eyebrows.
The brow of a hill is the top part of it.

Englishsense: Something that is brown is the colour of earth or of wood.
You can describe a white-skinned person as brown when they have been sitting in the sun until their skin has become darker than usual.
If someone browns in the sun they become brown in colour.
A brown person is someone who belongs to a race of people who have brown-coloured skins.
Brown is used to describe grains that have not had their outer layers removed, and foods made from these grains.
When food browns or when you brown food, you cook it, usually for a short time on a high flame.

Chinesesense: 尤指使用电脑在万维网上浏览信息；
Englishsense: If you browse in a shop, you look at things in a fairly casual way, in the hope that you might find something you like.
If you browse through a book or magazine, you look through it in a fairly casual way.
If you browse on a computer, you search for information in computer files or on the Internet, especially on the World Wide Web.
When animals browse, they feed on plants.

Chinesesense: 尤指用来在万维网上搜索信息的浏览软件，浏览器；
Englishsense: A browser is a piece of computer software that you use to search for information on the Internet, especially on the World Wide Web.
A browser is someone who browses in a shop.

Chinesesense: 将(蔬菜、水果或植物) 碰伤；
Englishsense: A bruise is an injury which appears as a purple mark on your body, although the skin is not broken.
If you bruise a part of your body, a bruise appears on it, for example because something hits you. If you bruise easily, bruises appear when something hits you only slightly.
If a fruit, vegetable, or plant bruises or is bruised, it is damaged by being handled roughly, making a mark on the skin.
If you are bruised by an unpleasant experience, it makes you feel unhappy or upset.
A brush is an object which has a large number of bristles or hairs fixed to it. You use brushes for painting, for cleaning things, and for tidying your hair.
If you brush something or brush something such as dirt off it, you clean it or tidy it using a brush.
If you brush something with a liquid, you apply a layer of that liquid using a brush.
If you brush something somewhere, you remove it with quick light movements of your hands.
If one thing brushes against another or if you brush one thing against another, the first thing touches the second thing lightly while passing it.
If you brush past someone or brush by them, you almost touch them as you go past them.
If you have a brush with someone, you have an argument or disagreement with them. You use brush when you want to make an argument or disagreement sound less serious than it really is.
If you have a brush with a particular situation, usually an unpleasant one, you almost experience it.
Brush is an area of rough open land covered with small bushes and trees. You also use brush to refer to the bushes and trees on this land.

Chinesesense: 直截了当的；直言不讳的；直率的；
残酷无情的；难以忍受的；
Englishsense: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.
If someone expresses something unpleasant with brutal honesty or frankness, they express it in a clear and accurate way, without attempting to disguise its unpleasantness.
Brutal is used to describe things that have an unpleasant effect on people, especially when there is no attempt by anyone to reduce their effect.
Brutality is cruel and violent treatment or behaviour. A brutality is an instance of cruel and violent treatment or behaviour.

Chinesesense: 漫画中显示人物对白的气泡框，圆框；
滔滔不绝地说；洋溢着某种感情；
Englishsense: Bubbles are small balls of air or gas in a liquid.
A bubble is a hollow ball of soapy liquid that is floating in the air or standing on a surface.

A bubble is a situation in which large numbers of people want to buy shares in a company that is new or not yet financially successful, and pay more than the shares are worth. When it becomes clear that the shares are worth less than people paid for them, you can say that the bubble has burst.
In a cartoon, a speech bubble is the shape which surrounds the words which a character is thinking or saying.
When a liquid bubbles, bubbles move in it, for example because it is boiling or moving quickly.
If something bubbles, it is very busy or lively.
A feeling, influence, or activity that is bubbling away continues to occur.
Someone who is bubbling with a good feeling is so full of it that they keep expressing the way they feel to everyone around them.

Chinesesense: 雄鹿、公羚羊、公兔、雄袋鼠等雄性动物；
美洲印第安裔或非洲裔小伙子；
马猛地弓背跃起，尥起后蹄跳跃；
轻易赚来的钱；常指不义之财；
责任止于此/应由…承担责任；
Englishsense: A buck is a US or Australian dollar.
A buck is the male of various animals, including the deer, antelope, rabbit and kangaroo.
A buck is a young Native American or African American man.
If someone has buck teeth, their upper front teeth stick forward out of their mouth.
If a horse bucks, it kicks both of its back legs wildly into the air, or jumps into the air wildly with all four feet off the ground.
If you buck the trend, you obtain different results from others in the same area. If you buck the system, you get what you want by breaking or ignoring the rules.
If you get more bang for the buck, you spend your money wisely and get more for your money than if you were to spend it in a different way.
When someone makes a fast buck or makes a quick buck, they earn a lot of money quickly and easily, often by doing something which is considered to be dishonest.
If you are trying to make a buck, you are trying to earn some money.
Someone who is buck naked is not wearing any clothes at all.
If you pass the buck, you refuse to accept responsibility for something, and say that someone else is responsible.
If you say ’ The buck stops here ’ or ’ The buck stops with me’, you mean that you have to take responsibility for something and will not try to pass the responsibility on to someone else.
A bucket is a round metal or plastic container with a handle attached to its sides. Buckets are often used for holding and carrying water.
Buckets or bucket-loads of something means a large amount of it.
If someone cries buckets, they cry a lot because they are very upset. If it rains buckets, it rains a lot.
If you say that someone has kicked the bucket, you mean that they have died.

Chinesesense: 因受热或受力使弯曲，使变形；
双腿或膝盖因虚弱、劳累发软；
Englishsense: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it.
When you buckle a belt or strap, you fasten it.
If an object buckles or if something buckles it, it becomes bent as a result of very great heat or force.
If your legs or knees buckle, they bend because they have become very weak or tired.

Chinesesense: 把…消灭在萌芽状态；防患于未然；
Englishsense: A bud is a small pointed lump that appears on a tree or plant and develops into a leaf or flower.
When a tree or plant is budding, buds are appearing on it or are beginning to open.
Some men use bud as a way of addressing other men.
When a tree or plant is in bud or has come into bud, it has buds on it.
If you nip something such as bad behaviour in the bud, you stop it before it can develop very far.
A Buddhist is a person whose religion is Buddhism.
Buddhist means relating or referring to Buddhism.

Chinesesense: 朋友，同伴通常指男子的男性伙伴；
Englishsense: A buddy is a close friend, usually a male friend of a man.
Men sometimes address other men as buddy.
If one person is buddy buddy with another, they are very close friends.

Chinesesense: 英国的政府年度预算案，政府年度预算演讲；
用于广告语低价的，低廉的；
Englishsense: Your budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend. The budget for something is the amount of money that a person, organization, or country has available to spend on it.
The budget of an organization or country is its financial situation, considered as the difference between the money it receives and the money it spends.

In Britain, the Budget is the financial plan in which the government states how much money it intends to raise through taxes and how it intends to spend it. The Budget is also the speech in which this plan is announced.
If you budget certain amounts of money for particular things, you decide that you can afford to spend those amounts on those things.
Budget is used in advertising to suggest that something is being sold cheaply.
A buffalo is a wild animal like a large cow with horns that curve upwards. Buffalo are usually found in southern and eastern Africa.
A buffalo is the same as a water buffalo.
A buffalo is the same as a bison.

Chinesesense: 火车上的缓冲器；火车轨道末端的防撞栅；
Englishsense: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that prevents two things from harming each other.
If something is buffered, it is protected from harm.
The buffers on a train or at the end of a railway line are two metal discs on springs that reduce the shock when a train hits them.
A buffer is an area in a computer’s memory where information can be stored for a short time.
If you say that someone, usually a man, is an old buffer, you mean that you think they are rather foolish.

Chinesesense: 通常指旅馆或车站的餐饮部，小餐馆；
大风或海浪反复拍打，猛击；
Englishsense: A buffet is a meal of cold food that is displayed on a long table at a party or public occasion. Guests usually serve themselves from the table.
A buffet is a café, usually in a hotel or station.
On a train, the buffet or the buffet car is the carriage or car where meals and snacks are sold.
If something is buffeted by strong winds or by stormy seas, it is repeatedly struck or blown around by them.
If an economy or government is buffeted by difficult or unpleasant situations, it experiences many of them.

Chinesesense: 计算机程序中的漏洞，错误，故障；
Englishsense: A bug is an insect or similar small creature.
A bug is an illness which is caused by small organisms such as bacteria.
If there is a bug in a computer program, there is a mistake in it.
A bug is a tiny hidden microphone which transmits what people are saying.
If someone bugs a place, they hide tiny microphones in it which transmit what people are saying.
You can say that someone has been bitten by a particular bug when they suddenly become very enthusiastic about something.
If someone or something bugs you, they worry or annoy you.

Chinesesense: 把组织、系统或产品建立于；
使成为政策、系统或产品的组成部分；
使信心或信任逐渐增强；
压力、速度、声音或激情逐渐变大，逐渐增强；
Englishsense: If you build something, you make it by joining things together.
If you build something into a wall or object, you make it in such a way that it is in the wall or object, or is part of it.
If people build an organization, a society, or a relationship, they gradually form it.
If you build an organization, system, or product on something, you base it on it.
If you build something into a policy, system, or product, you make it part of it.
To build someone’s confidence or trust means to increase it gradually. If someone’s confidence or trust builds, it increases gradually.
If you build on the success of something, you take advantage of this success in order to make further progress.
If pressure, speed, sound, or excitement builds, it gradually becomes greater.
Someone’s build is the shape that their bones and muscles give to their body.
A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses and other buildings.
A building is a structure that has a roof and walls, for example a house or a factory.
Built-in devices or features are included in something as a part of it, rather than being separate.
A bulb is the glass part of an electric lamp, which gives out light when electricity passes through it.
A bulb is a root shaped like an onion that grows into a flower or plant.

Chinesesense: 庞大的身躯；巨大的体重；肥硕的体形；
Englishsense: You can refer to something’s bulk when you want to emphasize that it is very large.
You can refer to a large person’s body or to their weight or size as their bulk.
The bulk of something is most of it.
If you buy or sell something in bulk, you buy or sell it in large quantities.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Something that is bulky is large and heavy. Bulky things are often difficult to move or deal with.

Chinesesense: 预期股价上涨而买进股票以期不久可高价卖出获利的买空者，多头；
像闯进瓷器店的公牛一样；莽撞冒失；
好像公牛进了瓷器店；笨手笨脚；
Englishsense: A bull is a male animal of the cow family.
Some other male animals, including elephants and whales, are called bulls.
On the stock market, bulls are people who buy shares in expectation of a price rise, in order to make a profit by selling the shares again after a short time.
In the Roman Catholic church, a papal bull is an official statement on a particular subject that is issued by the Pope.
If you say that something is bull or a load of bull, you mean that it is complete nonsense or absolutely untrue.
If you say that someone rushes into a situation like a bull in a china shop, you are critical of them because they do not stop to think, and are insensitive to other people’s feelings.
You say that someone is like a bull in a china shop when they are very clumsy.
If you take the bull by the horns, you do something that you feel you ought to do even though it is difficult, dangerous, or unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 硬着头皮做；咬紧牙关应付；
Englishsense: A bullet is a small piece of metal with a pointed or rounded end, which is fired out of a gun.
If someone bites the bullet, they accept that they have to do something unpleasant but necessary.

Chinesesense: 电台或电视台的简明新闻，简短消息，简讯；
学校、教堂等机构或团体发放的学报，会刊，小册子；
Englishsense: A bulletin is a short news report on the radio or television.
A bulletin is a short official announcement made publicly to inform people about an important matter.
A bulletin is a regular newspaper or leaflet that is produced by an organization or group such as a school or church.
A bully is someone who uses their strength or power to hurt or frighten other people.
If someone bullies you, they use their strength or power to hurt or frighten you.
If someone bullies you into something, they make you do it by using force or threats.
Someone’s bum is the part of their body which they sit on.
A bum is a person who has no permanent home or job and who gets money by working occasionally or by asking people for money.
If someone refers to another person as a bum, they think that person is worthless or irresponsible.
Some people use bum to describe a situation that they find unpleasant or annoying.
If you bum something off someone, you ask them for it and they give it to you.
If you bum around, you go from place to place without any particular destination, either for enjoyment or because you have nothing else to do.
If the organizers of an event such as a concert want to put bums on seats, they want a lot of people to attend it.
If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.
A bump is the action or the dull sound of two heavy objects hitting each other.
A bump is a minor injury or swelling that you get if you bump into something or if something hits you.
If you have a bump while you are driving a car, you have a minor accident in which you hit something.
A bump on a road is a raised, uneven part.
If a vehicle bumps over a surface, it travels in a rough, bouncing way because the surface is very uneven.
If someone comes down to earth with a bump, they suddenly start recognizing unpleasant facts after a period of time when they have not been doing this.

Chinesesense: 表面覆有糖霜的小蛋糕；
Englishsense: Buns are small bread rolls. They are sometimes sweet and may contain dried fruit or spices.
Buns are small sweet cakes. They often have icing on the top.
If a woman has her hair in a bun, she has fastened it tightly on top of her head or at the back of her head in the shape of a ball.
Your buns are your buttocks.

Chinesesense: 扎在女子脑后两侧的发辫；
同类中最好的；出类拔萃者；精华；
Englishsense: A bunch of people is a group of people who share one or more characteristics or who are doing something together.
A bunch of flowers is a number of flowers with their stalks held or tied together.
A bunch of bananas or grapes is a group of them growing on the same stem.
A bunch of keys is a set of keys kept together on a metal ring.
A bunch of things is a number of things, especially a large number.
If a girl has her hair in bunches, it is parted down the middle and tied on each side of her head.
If clothing bunches around a part of your body, it forms a set of creases around it.
If you say someone or something is the best of the bunch or the pick of the bunch, you mean they are the best of a group of people or things.

Chinesesense: 极度，非常用于强调某人具备的某种品质或特性；
Englishsense: A bundle of things is a number of them that are tied together or wrapped in a cloth or bag so that they can be carried or stored.
You can refer to a tiny baby as a bundle.
If you describe someone as, for example, a bundle of fun, you are emphasizing that they are full of fun. If you describe someone as a bundle of nerves, you are emphasizing that they are very nervous.
If you refer to a bundle of things, you are emphasizing that there is a wide range of them.
If someone is bundled somewhere, someone pushes them there in a rough and hurried way.
To bundle software means to sell it together with a computer, or with other hardware or software, as part of a set.
If you say that something costs a bundle, or costs someone a bundle, you are emphasizing that it is expensive.

Chinesesense: 尤指船上或车上的铺位，卧铺；
Englishsense: A bunk is a bed that is fixed to a wall, especially in a ship or caravan.
If you describe something as bunk, you think that it is foolish or untrue.
If you do a bunk, you suddenly leave a place without telling anyone.

Chinesesense: 通常建于地下的掩体；地堡；
高尔夫球运动中把球击入沙坑；
Englishsense: A bunker is a place, usually underground, that has been built with strong walls to protect it against heavy gunfire and bombing.
A bunker is a container for coal or other fuel.
On a golf course, a bunker is a large area filled with sand, which is deliberately put there as an obstacle that golfers must try to avoid.
In golf, if you bunker a shot, you hit your ball into the bunker.
If you describe a problem or a responsibility as a burden, you mean that it causes someone a lot of difficulty, worry, or hard work.
A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry.
If someone burdens you with something that is likely to worry you, for example a problem or a difficult decision, they tell you about it.
The burden of proof is the task of proving that you are correct, for example when you have accused someone of a crime.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
Chinesesense: 政府或组织机构的局，所，司，处，属；
Englishsense: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.
A bureau is an office of a company or organization which has its main office in another town or country.
A bureau is a writing desk with shelves and drawers and a lid that opens to form the writing surface.
A bureau is a chest of drawers.
A bureaucracy is an administrative system operated by a large number of officials.
Bureaucracy refers to all the rules and procedures followed by government departments and similar organizations, especially when you think that these are complicated and cause long delays.

Bureaucrats are officials who work in a large administrative system. You can refer to officials as bureaucrats especially if you disapprove of them because they seem to follow rules and procedures too strictly.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Bureaucratic means involving complicated rules and procedures which can cause long delays.
A burger is a flat round mass of minced meat or vegetables, which is fried and often eaten in a bread roll.
A burial is the act or ceremony of putting a dead body into a grave in the ground.

Chinesesense: 有强烈的情感；极度渴望；
Englishsense: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.
If something is burning, it is on fire.
If you burn something, you destroy or damage it with fire.
If you burn a fuel or if it burns, it is used to produce heat, light, or energy.
If you burn something that you are cooking or if it burns, you spoil it by using too much heat or cooking it for too long.
If you burn part of your body, burn yourself, or are burnt, you are injured by fire or by something very hot.
If someone is burnt or burnt to death, they are killed by fire.
If a light is burning, it is shining.
If your face is burning, it is red because you are embarrassed or upset.
If you are burning with an emotion or are burning to do something, you feel that emotion or the desire to do that thing very strongly.
If you burn or get burned in the sun, the sun makes your skin become red and sore.
If a part of your body burns or if something burns it, it has a painful, hot or stinging feeling.
If you are burned or get burned, you lose something as a result of taking a risk, usually in a business deal.
To burn a CD-ROM means to write or copy data onto it.
A burner is a device which produces heat or a flame, especially as part of a cooker, stove, or heater.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 兴趣浓厚的；欲望强烈的；
Englishsense: You use burning to describe something that is extremely hot.
If you say that someone has burning eyes, you mean they look at you in an intense way or have bright eyes because of a strong feeling.
If you have a burning interest in something or a burning desire to do something, you are extremely interested in it or want to do it very much.
A burning issue or question is a very important or urgent one that people feel very strongly about.
If something bursts or if you burst it, it suddenly breaks open or splits open and the air or other substance inside it comes out.
If a dam bursts, or if something bursts it, it breaks apart because the force of the river is too great.
If a river bursts its banks, the water rises and goes on to the land.
When a door or lid bursts open, it opens very suddenly and violently because someone pushes it or there is great pressure behind it.
To burst into or out of a place means to enter or leave it suddenly with a lot of energy or force.
If you say that something bursts onto the scene, you mean that it suddenly starts or becomes active, usually after developing quietly for some time.
If you say that someone is about to burst with pride, anger, or another emotion, you are emphasizing the intensity of the emotion they are feeling.
When a firework or bomb bursts in the air, it explodes.
A burst of something is a sudden short period of it.

Chinesesense: 因不高兴而把头或脸贴或靠在…；
掩藏[感情]; 抛开记忆；
Englishsense: To bury something means to put it into a hole in the ground and cover it up with earth.
To bury a dead person means to put their body into a grave and cover it with earth.
If someone says they have buried one of their relatives, they mean that one of their relatives has died.
If you bury something under a large quantity of things, you put it there, often in order to hide it.
If something buries a place or person, it falls on top of them so that it completely covers them and often harms them in some way.
If you bury your head or face in something, you press your head or face against it, often because you are unhappy.
If something buries itself somewhere, or if you bury it there, it is pushed very deeply in there.
If you bury a feeling, you try not to show it. If you bury a memory, you try to forget it.
If you bury yourself in a place or in an activity such as your work, you spend all your time in that place or doing that activity, usually because you want to forget about things.
If you bury your head in something such as a book or newspaper, or bury yourself in it, you look at it closely and concentrate very hard on it.

Chinesesense: 用大客车运送；乘坐公共汽车；
Englishsense: A bus is a large motor vehicle which carries passengers from one place to another. Buses drive along particular routes, and you have to pay to travel in them.
When someone is bussed to a particular place or when they bus there, they travel there on a bus.
In some parts of the United States, when children are bused to school, they are transported by bus to a school in a different area so that children of different races can be educated together.

Chinesesense: 热带国家未开发的荒野地带，丛林地带；
Englishsense: A bush is a large plant which is smaller than a tree and has a lot of branches.
The wild, uncultivated parts of some hot countries are referred to as the bush.
If you tell someone not to beat about the bush, you mean that you want them to tell you something immediately and quickly, rather than in a complicated, indirect way.

Chinesesense: 工商企业；公司；商店；商铺；
眼前所做之事；手头的事；
需要处理的重要事情，要点；
令人不快或耗费钱财的活儿，事情；
Englishsense: Business is work relating to the production, buying, and selling of goods or services.

Business is used when talking about how many products or services a company is able to sell. If business is good, a lot of products or services are being sold and if business is bad, few of them are being sold.
A business is an organization which produces and sells goods or which provides a service.
Business is work or some other activity that you do as part of your job and not for pleasure.
You can use business to refer to a particular area of work or activity in which the aim is to make a profit.
You can use business to refer to something that you are doing or concerning yourself with.
You can use business to refer to important matters that you have to deal with.
If you say that something is your business, you mean that it concerns you personally and that other people have no right to ask questions about it or disagree with it.
You can use business to refer in a general way to an event, situation, or activity. For example, you can say something is ’a wretched business’ or you can refer to ’this assassination business’.
You can use business when describing a task that is unpleasant in some way. For example, if you say that doing something is a costly business, you mean that it costs a lot.
If two people or companies do business with each other, one sells goods or services to the other.
If you say that someone has no business to be in a place or to do something, you mean that they have no right to be there or to do it.
A company that is in business is operating and trading.
If you say you are in business, you mean you have everything you need to start something immediately.
If you say that someone means business, you mean they are serious and determined about what they are doing.
If you say to someone ’ mind your own business ’ or ’ it’s none of your business ’, you are rudely telling them not to ask about something that does not concern them.
If you make it your business to do something, you decide to do it, because you are interested in it or because you want to find out something.
If you say that you are not in the business of doing something, you are emphasizing that you do not do it, usually when you are annoyed or surprised that someone thinks you do.
If a shop or company goes out of business or is put out of business, it has to stop trading because it is not making enough money.
If you say that someone or something is the business, you mean that they are the best of their kind.
In a difficult situation, if you say it is business as usual, you mean that people will continue doing what they normally do.
A businessman is a man who works in business.
If you bust something, you break it or damage it so badly that it cannot be used.
If someone is busted, the police arrest them.
If police bust a place, they go to it in order to arrest people who are doing something illegal.
A company or fund that is bust has no money left and has been forced to close down.
If a company goes bust, it loses so much money that it is forced to close down.
A bust is a statue of the head and shoulders of a person.
You can use bust to refer to a woman’s breasts, especially when you are describing their size.

Chinesesense: 全神贯注的；心无旁骛的；埋头于…的；
热闹的；忙碌的；熙熙攘攘的；
Englishsense: When you are busy, you are working hard or concentrating on a task, so that you are not free to do anything else.
A busy time is a period of time during which you have a lot of things to do.
If you say that someone is busy thinking or worrying about something, you mean that it is taking all their attention, often to such an extent that they are unable to think about anything else.
If you busy yourself with something, you occupy yourself by dealing with it.
A busy place is full of people who are doing things or moving about.
When a telephone line is busy, you cannot make your call because the line is already being used by someone else.

Chinesesense: 引出下文，表示惊讶、难以置信、拒绝或抗议但是，可是；
表示与前面说过的话略有矛盾不过，然而；
表示前述事情并不奇怪不过，但是；
Englishsense: You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.
You use but when you are about to add something further in a discussion or to change the subject.
You use but after you have made an excuse or apologized for what you are just about to say.
You use but to introduce a reply to someone when you want to indicate surprise, disbelief, refusal, or protest.
But is used to mean ’except’.
But is used to mean ’only’.
You use buts in expressions like ’ no buts ’ and ’ ifs and buts ’ to refer to reasons someone gives for not doing something, especially when you do not think that they are good reasons.
You use cannot but, could not but, and cannot help but when you want to emphasize that you believe something must be true and that there is no possibility of anything else being the case.
You use but for to introduce the only factor that causes a particular thing not to happen or not to be completely true.
You use but then or but then again before a remark which slightly contradicts what you have just said.
You use but then before a remark which suggests that what you have just said should not be regarded as surprising.
A butcher is a shopkeeper who cuts up and sells meat. Some butchers also kill animals for meat and make foods such as sausages and meat pies.
A butcher or a butcher’s is a shop where meat is sold.
To butcher an animal means to kill it and cut it up for meat.
You can refer to someone as a butcher when they have killed a lot of people in a very cruel way, and you want to express your horror and disgust.
You can say that someone has butchered people when they have killed a lot of people in a very cruel way, and you want to express your horror and disgust.

Chinesesense: 武器或工具较粗的一端，柄；
嘲笑或批评的对象，笑柄；
Englishsense: Someone’s butt is their bottom.
The butt or the butt end of a weapon or tool is the thick end of its handle.
The butt of a cigarette or cigar is the small part of it that is left when someone has finished smoking it.
A butt is a large barrel used for collecting or storing liquid.
If someone or something is the butt of jokes or criticism, people often make fun of them or criticize them.
If a person or animal butts you, they hit you with the top of their head.

Chinesesense: 明白自己的利益所在；善于为自己打算；
Englishsense: Butter is a soft yellow substance made from cream. You spread it on bread or use it in cooking.
If you butter something such as bread or toast, you spread butter on it.
If you say that someone knows what side their bread is buttered on, you mean that they know what to do or who to please in order to stay in a good situation or to avoid a bad one.

Chinesesense: 情绪紧张；心慌意乱；忐忑不安；
Englishsense: A butterfly is an insect with large colourful wings and a thin body.
Butterfly is a swimming stroke which you do lying on your front, kicking your legs and bringing your arms over your head together.
If you have butterflies in your stomach or have butterflies, you are very nervous or excited about something.

Chinesesense: 巧妙地获取想要的东西；
Englishsense: Buttons are small hard objects sewn on to shirts, coats, or other pieces of clothing. You fasten the clothing by pushing the buttons through holes called buttonholes.
If you button a shirt, coat, or other piece of clothing, you fasten it by pushing its buttons through the buttonholes.
A button is a small object on a machine or electrical device that you press in order to operate it.
A button is a small piece of metal or plastic which you wear in order to show that you support a particular movement, organization, or person. You fasten a button to your clothes with a pin.
If you say that someone presses the right button or pushes the right button, you mean that they get what they want from a particular situation or person by behaving in a clever way.

Chinesesense: 争取或付出一定代价以获得，赢得；
划算的东西；性价比高的商品；
Englishsense: If you buy something, you obtain it by paying money for it.
If you talk about the quantity or standard of goods an amount of money buys, you are referring to the price of the goods or the value of the money.
If you buy something like time, freedom, or victory, you obtain it but only by offering or giving up something in return.
If you say that a person can be bought, you are criticizing the fact that they will give their help or loyalty to someone in return for money.
If you buy an idea or a theory, you believe and accept it.
If something is a good buy, it is of good quality and not very expensive.

Chinesesense: 大商店的采购员，进货员；买手；
Englishsense: A buyer is a person who is buying something or who intends to buy it.
A buyer is a person who works for a large store deciding what goods will be bought from manufacturers to be sold in the store.

Chinesesense: 匆忙地走动；忙得团团转；
想法在脑海中萦绕，翻腾；
充满嘈杂的谈话、活动声；
热闹有趣的气氛；时尚氛围；
词语、想法或活动时髦的；
用内线给…打电话；用蜂鸣器呼叫；
Englishsense: If something buzzes or buzzes somewhere, it makes a long continuous sound, like the noise a bee makes when it is flying.
If people are buzzing around, they are moving around quickly and busily.
If questions or ideas are buzzing around your head, or if your head is buzzing with questions or ideas, you are thinking about a lot of things, often in a confused way.
If a place is buzzing with activity or conversation, there is a lot of activity or conversation there, especially because something important or exciting is about to happen.
You can use buzz to refer to a long continuous sound, usually caused by lots of people talking at once.
If something gives you a buzz, it makes you feel very happy or excited for a short time.
If a place or event has a buzz, it has a lively, interesting and modern atmosphere.
You can use buzz to refer to a word, idea, or activity which has recently become extremely popular.
If you buzz someone, you call them, usually using an internal telephone line or a buzzer.
If an aircraft buzzes a place, it flies low over it, usually in a threatening way.

Chinesesense: 图书、音乐、绘画等由…创作，出自；
用于短语中由于，出于偶然或意外；
就本性、职业或出身而言；
根据，按照法律或某种标准；
用于表示抓住身体某部位或握住物体某部分；
乘表示长乘宽得出的居室等的面积；
Englishsense: If something is done by a person or thing, that person or thing does it.
If you say that something such as a book, a piece of music, or a painting is by a particular person, you mean that this person wrote it or created it.
If you do something by a particular means, you do it using that thing.
If you achieve one thing by doing another thing, your action enables you to achieve the first thing.
You use by in phrases such as ’by chance’ or ’by accident’ to indicate whether or not an event was planned.
If someone is a particular type of person by nature, by profession, or by birth, they are that type of person because of their nature, their profession, or the family they were born into.
If something must be done by law, it happens according to the law. If something is the case by particular standards, it is the case according to the standards.
If you say what someone means by a particular word or expression, you are saying what they intend the word or expression to refer to.
If you hold someone or something by a particular part of them, you hold that part.
Someone or something that is by something else is beside it and close to it.
If a person or vehicle goes by you, they move past you without stopping.
If you stop by a place, you visit it for a short time.
If something happens by a particular time, it happens at or before that time.
If you do something by day, you do it during the day. If you do it by night, you do it during the night.
In arithmetic, you use by before the second number in a multiplication or division sum.
You use by to talk about measurements of area. For example, if a room is twenty feet by fourteen feet, it measures twenty feet in one direction and fourteen feet in the other direction.
If something increases or decreases by a particular amount, that amount is gained or lost.
Things that are made or sold by the million or by the dozen are made or sold in those quantities.
You use by in expressions such as ’minute by minute’ and ’drop by drop’ to talk about things that happen gradually, not all at once.
If you are by yourself, you are alone.
If you do something by yourself, you succeed in doing it without anyone helping you.

Chinesesense: 通常为更快地实现某事越过，避开，绕开；
对动脉等作分流术；为…作搭桥术；
绕过城镇中心的旁道，外环路；
Englishsense: If you bypass someone or something that you would normally have to get involved with, you ignore them, often because you want to achieve something more quickly.
A bypass is a surgical operation performed on or near the heart, in which the flow of blood is redirected so that it does not flow through a part of the heart which is diseased or blocked.
If a surgeon bypasses a diseased artery or other part of the body, he or she performs an operation so that blood or other bodily fluids do not flow through it.
A bypass is a main road which takes traffic around the edge of a town rather than through its centre.
If a road bypasses a place, it goes around it rather than through it.
If you bypass a place when you are travelling, you avoid going through it.
A by-product is something which is produced during the manufacture or processing of another product.
Something that is a by-product of an event or situation happens as a result of it, although it is usually not expected or planned.
A cab is a taxi.
The cab of a truck or train is the front part in which the driver sits.

Chinesesense: 植物人;脑部受损或患重病的废人；
Englishsense: A cabbage is a round vegetable with white, green or purple leaves that is usually eaten cooked.
If someone refers to a very sick or disabled person as a cabbage, they are saying in an offensive way that the sick person is so badly brain-damaged or ill that they cannot do anything.
A cabin is a small room in a ship or boat.
A cabin is one of the areas inside a plane.
A cabin is a small wooden house, especially one in an area of forests or mountains.
A cabinet is a cupboard used for storing things such as medicine or alcoholic drinks or for displaying decorative things in.
The Cabinet is a group of the most senior ministers in a government, who meet regularly to discuss policies. See usage note at: government
A cable is a thick wire, or a group of wires inside a rubber or plastic covering, which is used to carry electricity or electronic signals.
A cable is a kind of very strong, thick rope, made of wires twisted together.
Cable is used to refer to television systems in which the signals are sent along underground wires rather than by radio waves.
A cable is the same as a telegram.
If you cable someone, you send them a message in the form of a telegram.
If a country, a city, or someone’s home is cabled, cables and other equipment are put in place so that the people there can receive cable television.
A cache is a quantity of things such as weapons that have been hidden.
A cache or cache memory is an area of computer memory that is used for temporary storage of data and can be accessed more quickly than the main memory.
A cactus is a thick fleshy plant that grows in many hot, dry parts of the world. Cacti have no leaves and many of them are covered in prickles.
A cadet is a young man or woman who is being trained in the armed services or the police.

Chinesesense: (医院、高校、商场等的)自助餐厅,食堂；
Englishsense: A cafeteria is a restaurant where you choose your food from a counter and take it to your table after paying for it. Cafeterias are usually found in public buildings such as hospitals, colleges, and stores.
Caffeine is a chemical substance found in coffee, tea, and cocoa, which affects your brain and body and makes you more active.

Chinesesense: 使焦躁不安;令心神不宁；
Englishsense: A cage is a structure of wire or metal bars in which birds or animals are kept.
If someone rattles your cage, they do something which is intended to make you feel nervous.

Chinesesense: 二者兼得;鱼与熊掌兼得；
非常抢手;非常畅销;热销；
小事一桩，易如反掌，小菜一碟常用于安慰别人；
(愚蠢、无礼、自私的行为) 非常过分，极其讨厌；
Englishsense: A cake is a sweet food made by baking a mixture of flour, eggs, sugar, and fat in an oven. Cakes may be large and cut into slices or small and intended for one person only.
Food that is formed into flat round shapes before it is cooked can be referred to as cakes.
A cake of soap is a small block of it.
If something such as blood or mud cakes, it changes from a thick liquid to a dry layer or lump.
If you think that someone wants the benefits of doing two things when it is only reasonable to expect the benefits of doing one, you can say that they want to have their cake and eat it.
If things are selling like hot cakes, a lot of people are buying them.
If you think something is very easy to do, you can say it is a piece of cake. People often say this to stop someone feeling worried about doing something they have to do.
If someone has done something very stupid, rude, or selfish, you can say that they take the cake or that what they have done takes the cake, to emphasize your surprise at their behaviour.
Calcium is a soft white element which is found in bones and teeth, and also in limestone, chalk, and marble.
If you calculate a number or amount, you discover it from information that you already have, by using arithmetic, mathematics, or a special machine.
If you calculate the effects of something, especially a possible course of action, you think about them in order to form an opinion or decide what to do.
A calculation is something that you think about and work out mathematically. Calculation is the process of working something out mathematically.
A calculation is something that you think carefully about and arrive at a conclusion on after having considered all the relevant factors.
If you describe someone’s behaviour as calculation, you are criticizing them because they seem to think only of themselves and not of other people.

Chinesesense: (某一组织、团体或个人的)日程表，纪事表，大事一览表；
Englishsense: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.
A calendar is a particular system for dividing time into periods such as years, months, and weeks, often starting from a particular point in history.
You can use calendar to refer to a series or list of events and activities which take place on particular dates, and which are important for a particular organization, community, or person.
A calf is a young cow.
Some other young animals, including elephants and whales, are called calves.
Your calf is the thick part at the back of your leg, between your ankle and your knee.

Chinesesense: 叫;称呼;将…命名;给…起名字；
召集(会议、排练等);宣布举行(选举等)；
(火车、公共汽车、船舶)停靠,停留；
随时待命的;随叫随到的；
Englishsense: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.
If you call someone or something a particular thing, you suggest they are that thing or describe them as that thing.
If you call something, you say it in a loud voice, because you are trying to attract someone’s attention.
If you call someone, you telephone them.
If you call someone such as a doctor or the police, you ask them to come to you, usually by telephoning them.
If you call someone, you ask them to come to you by shouting to them.
When you make a telephone call, you telephone someone.
If someone in authority calls something such as a meeting, rehearsal, or election, they arrange for it to take place at a particular time.
If someone is called before a court or committee, they are ordered to appear there, usually to give evidence.
If you call somewhere, you make a short visit there.
When a train, bus, or ship calls somewhere, it stops there for a short time to allow people to get on or off.
To call a game or sporting event means to cancel it, for example because of rain or bad light.
If there is a call for something, someone demands that it should happen.
If there is little or no call for something, very few people want it to be done or provided.
The call of something such as a place is the way it attracts or interests you strongly.
The call of a particular bird or animal is the characteristic sound that it makes.
If you have first call on something, you will be asked before anyone else whether you want to buy or use it.
If you say that there is no call for someone to behave in a particular way, you are criticizing their behaviour, usually because you think it is rude.
If someone is on call, they are ready to go to work at any time if they are needed, especially if there is an emergency.
If you call in sick, you telephone the place where you work to tell them you will not be coming to work because you are ill.
A caller is a person who is making a telephone call.
A caller is a person who comes to see you for a short visit.
A calling is a profession or career which someone is strongly attracted to, especially one which involves helping other people.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (帆船比赛中的)静风,风平浪静；
Englishsense: A calm person does not show or feel any worry, anger, or excitement.
If you calm someone, you do something to make them feel less angry, worried, or excited.
Calm is used to refer to a quiet, still, or peaceful atmosphere in a place.
If someone says that a place is calm, they mean that it is free from fighting or public disorder, when trouble has recently occurred there or had been expected.
To calm a situation means to reduce the amount of trouble, violence, or panic there is.
If the sea or a lake is calm, the water is not moving very much and there are no big waves.
Calm weather is pleasant weather with little or no wind.
In sailing, a flat calm or a dead calm is a condition of the sea or the weather in which there is very little wind or movement of the water.
When the sea calms, it becomes still because the wind stops blowing strongly. When the wind calms, it stops blowing strongly.
To calm a pain or an itch means to reduce it or get rid of it. [V n]
You can use the calm before the storm to refer to a quiet period in which there is little or no activity, before a period in which there is a lot of trouble or intense activity.
You can use calmly to emphasize that someone is behaving in a very controlled or ordinary way in a frightening or unusual situation.

Chinesesense: 未在拍摄时;在镜头范围之外；
(审讯)秘密地;不公开地;私下地；
Englishsense: A camera is a piece of equipment that is used for taking photographs, making films, or producing television pictures.
If someone or something is on camera, they are being filmed.
If you do something or if something happens off camera, you do it or it happens when not being filmed.
If a trial is held in camera, the public and the press are not allowed to attend.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (为某一人群提供的)营地(如难民营、战俘营、军营等)；
(拥护某人、某政策或某观念的)阵营,集团,派别；
(常指男同性恋者的举止、表演、穿着)夸张而惹人发笑的,娘娘腔的，忸怩作态的；
故作夸张地表演;装腔作势;忸怩作态；
Englishsense: A camp is a collection of huts and other buildings that is provided for a particular group of people, such as refugees, prisoners, or soldiers, as a place to live or stay.
A camp is an outdoor area with buildings, tents, or caravans where people stay on holiday.
A camp is a collection of tents or caravans where people are living or staying, usually temporarily while they are travelling.
If you camp somewhere, you stay or live there for a short time in a tent or caravan, or in the open air.
You can refer to a group of people who all support a particular person, policy, or idea as a particular camp.
If you describe someone’s behaviour, performance, or style of dress as camp, you mean that it is exaggerated and amusing, often in a way that is thought to be typical of some male homosexuals.
If a performer camps it up, they deliberately perform in an exaggerated and often amusing way.
A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.
If someone campaigns for something, they carry out a planned set of activities over a period of time in order to achieve their aim.
In a war, a campaign is a series of planned movements carried out by armed forces.
A camper is someone who is camping somewhere.
A camper is the same as a camper van.
A campus is an area of land that contains the main buildings of a university or college.

Chinesesense: (表示某事物的特点)能够，可以；
(表示有能力或机会)能，会，可以；
(用于否定句，表示情况不允许)不能，无法；
(用于否定句，表示确信某事不真实或不会发生)不可能，不会；
(通常用于疑问句，表示建议或提议帮忙)能；
(用于疑问句时,can 表示礼貌的请求，而 can’t 表示强烈请求] ；
(用于有礼貌地打断,或引导要说的话)能,可以；
(与 imagine, think, believe 等动词连用,用来加强语气)能；
(与 how 一起用于疑问句,表示感受强烈)能,能够；
(盛放食品、饮料或油漆的)罐子，金属罐，听；
承担所有指责;代人受过；
Englishsense: You use can when you are mentioning a quality or fact about something which people may make use of if they want to.
You use can to indicate that someone has the ability or opportunity to do something.
You use cannot to indicate that someone is not able to do something because circumstances make it impossible for them to do it.
You use can to indicate that something is true sometimes or is true in some circumstances.
You use cannot and can’t to state that you are certain that something is not the case or will not happen.
You use can to indicate that someone is allowed to do something. You use cannot or can’t to indicate that someone is not allowed to do something.
You use cannot or can’t when you think it is very important that something should not happen or that someone should not do something.
You use can, usually in questions, in order to make suggestions or to offer to do something.
You use can in questions in order to make polite requests. You use can’t in questions in order to request strongly that someone does something.
You use can as a polite way of interrupting someone or of introducing what you are going to say next.
You use can with verbs such as ’imagine’, ’think’, and ’believe’ in order to emphasize how you feel about a particular situation.
You use can in questions with ’how’ to indicate that you feel strongly about something.
A can is a metal container in which something such as food, drink, or paint is put. The container is usually sealed to keep the contents fresh.
When food or drink is canned, it is put into a metal container and sealed so that it will remain fresh.
The can is the toilet.
If you are canned, you are dismissed from your job.
If you have to carry the can, you have to take all the blame for something.
If you say that something such as a job that you are doing is in the can, you mean that it is completely finished.

Chinesesense: 加拿大的;加拿大人的;加拿大文化的；
Englishsense: Canadian means belonging or relating to Canada, or to its people or culture.
A Canadian is a Canadian citizen, or a person of Canadian origin.

Chinesesense: (人体内输送食物、空气等的)管,道；
Englishsense: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.
A canal is a narrow tube inside your body for carrying food, air, or other substances.

Chinesesense: 废除,废止(文件、保险单);免除(债务)；
Englishsense: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.
If someone in authority cancels a document, an insurance policy, or a debt, they officially declare that it is no longer valid or no longer legally exists.
To cancel a stamp or a cheque means to mark it to show that it has already been used and cannot be used again.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (照片)趁人不备时拍摄的，偷拍的，抓拍的；
Englishsense: When you are candid about something or with someone, you speak honestly.
A candid photograph of someone is one that was taken when the person did not know they were being photographed.
Someone’s candidacy is their position of being a candidate in an election.

Chinesesense: 攻读学位者;在读本科生(或硕士生、博士生)；
适合…的人(或物);可能有…结局的人(或物)；
Englishsense: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.
A candidate is someone who is taking an examination.
A candidate is someone who is studying for a degree at a college.
A candidate is a person or thing that is regarded as being suitable for a particular purpose or as being likely to do or be a particular thing.

Chinesesense: 一根蜡烛两头烧;起早摸黑地干;过度耗费精力；
Englishsense: A candle is a stick of hard wax with a piece of string called a wick through the middle. You light the wick in order to give a steady flame that provides light.
If you burn the candle at both ends, you try to do too many things in too short a period of time so that you have to stay up very late at night and get up very early in the morning to get them done.
If you say that one person or thing can’t hold a candle to another, you meant that the first person or thing is not nearly as good as the second.
If you say that the game is not worth the candle, you mean that something is not worth the trouble or effort needed to achieve or obtain it.
Candy is sweet foods such as toffees or chocolate.

Chinesesense: (旧时用来打人、尤其是惩罚学生的)藤条；
作为惩罚鞭打，抽打(学生)；
Englishsense: Cane is used to refer to the long, hollow, hard stems of plants such as bamboo. Strips of cane are often used to make furniture, and some types of cane can be crushed and processed to make sugar.
A cane is a long thin stick with a curved or round top which you can use to support yourself when you are walking, or which in the past was fashionable to carry with you.
A cane is a long, thin, flexible stick which in the past was used to hit people, especially children at school, as a punishment.
If a child is caned, he or she is hit with a cane as a punishment.
A cane is a tall, narrow stick, usually made of bamboo, which is used for supporting plants.

Chinesesense: (广播、电视节目中的音乐、笑声、掌声)预先录制好的；
Englishsense: Canned music, laughter, or applause on a television or radio programme has been recorded beforehand and is added to the programme to make it sound as if there is a live audience.
A cannon is a large gun, usually on wheels, which used to be used in battles.
A cannon is a heavy automatic gun, especially one that is fired from an aircraft.
If one person or thing cannons into another, they bump into them with great force.
If someone is a loose cannon, they do whatever they want and nobody can predict what they are going to do.
A canoe is a small, narrow boat that you move through the water using a stick with a wide end called a paddle.
A canon is a member of the clergy who is on the staff of a cathedral.
A canon of texts is a list of them that is accepted as genuine or important.
A canon is a general rule or principle.
A canopy is a decorated cover, often made of cloth, which is placed above something such as a bed or a seat.
A canopy is a layer of something that spreads out and covers an area, for example the branches and leaves that spread out at the top of trees in a forest.
Canvas is a strong, heavy cloth that is used for making things such as tents, sails, and bags.
A canvas is a piece of canvas or similar material on which an oil painting can be done.
A canvas is a painting that has been done on canvas.
If you are living and sleeping under canvas, you are living and sleeping in a tent.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
Englishsense: A canyon is a long, narrow valley with very steep sides.

Chinesesense: 使入选国家(足球、橄榄球、板球等)队；
首次入选国家队的选手；
(政府)限制(组织或地方议会的支出)，限定预算；
谦卑地索要；毕恭毕敬地请求；
Englishsense: A cap is a soft, flat hat with a curved part at the front which is called a peak. Caps are usually worn by men and boys.
A cap is a special hat which is worn as part of a uniform.
If a sports player is capped, they are chosen to represent their country in a team game such as football, rugby, or cricket.
If a sports player represents their country in a team game such as football, rugby, or cricket, you can say that they have been awarded a cap.
You can refer to someone who is representing their country for the first time in a team game such as football, rugby, or cricket, as a new cap.
If the government caps an organization, council, or budget, it limits the amount of money that the organization or council is allowed to spend, or limits the size of the budget.
The cap of a bottle is its lid.
A cap is a circular rubber device that a woman places inside her vagina to prevent herself from becoming pregnant.
If you cap one thing with another, you put the other thing on top.
If someone says that a good or bad event caps a series of events, they mean it is the final event in the series, and the other events were also good or bad.
If someone’s teeth are capped, covers are fixed over them so that they look better.
A cap is a small amount of explosive that is wrapped in paper. Caps are often used in toy guns.
If you go cap in hand to someone, you ask them very humbly to give you something or to do something for you.
If you have the capability or the capabilities to do something, you have the ability or the qualities that are necessary to do it.
A country’s military capability is its ability to fight in a war. See usage note at: capacity

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 熟练的;胜任的;有能力的；
Englishsense: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability to do it.
Someone who is capable has the skill or qualities necessary to do a particular thing well, or is able to do most things well.

Chinesesense: (工厂、企业、地区的)生产量,生产或运输能力；
(建筑、地方、车辆的)可容纳人数,载客量；
座无虚席的;满场的;挤满的；
Englishsense: Your capacity for something is your ability to do it, or the amount of it that you are able to do.
The capacity of something such as a factory, industry, or region is the quantity of things that it can produce or deliver with the equipment or resources that are available.
The capacity of a piece of equipment is its size or power, often measured in particular units.
The capacity of a container is its volume, or the amount of liquid it can hold, measured in units such as litres or gallons.
The capacity of a building, place, or vehicle is the number of people or things that it can hold. If a place is filled to capacity, it is as full as it can possibly be.
A capacity crowd or audience completely fills a theatre, sports stadium, or other place.
If you do something in a particular capacity, you do it as part of a particular job or duty, or because you are representing a particular organization or person.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
Englishsense: A cape is a large piece of land that sticks out into the sea from the coast.
A cape is a short cloak.

Chinesesense: (厂房、机器等)固定资产,资本资产；
(犯罪)情节严重的,可判处死刑的；
从…中捞取好处;从…中渔利；
(用于强调某一字眼具有特殊意义)地道的，彻头彻尾的；
Englishsense: Capital is a large sum of money which you use to start a business, or which you invest in order to make more money.
You can use capital to refer to buildings or machinery which are necessary to produce goods or to make companies more efficient, but which do not make money directly.
Capital is the part of an amount of money borrowed or invested which does not include interest.
The capital of a country is the city or town where its government or parliament meets.
If a place is the capital of a particular industry or activity, it is the place that is most famous for it, because it happens in that place more than anywhere else.
Capitals or capital letters are written or printed letters in the form which is used at the beginning of sentences or names. ’T’, ’B’, and ’F’ are capitals.
A capital offence is one that is so serious that the person who commits it can be punished by death.
A capital is the top part of a stone column, which is sometimes decorated with stone leaves or other patterns.
If you say that someone is making capital out of a situation, you disapprove of the way they are gaining an advantage for themselves through other people’s efforts or bad luck.
You can use phrases such as ’Life with a capital L’, to emphasize that a word has a particular significance in the situation you are talking about.
Capitalism is an economic and political system in which property, business, and industry are owned by private individuals and not by the state.
A capitalist country or system supports or is based on the principles of capitalism.
A capitalist is someone who believes in and supports the principles of capitalism.
A capitalist is someone who owns a business which they run in order to make a profit for themselves.
If you capitalize on a situation, you use it to gain some advantage for yourself.
In business, if you capitalize something that belongs to you, you sell it in order to make money.

Chinesesense: (医用或科学研究用的)密封小容器；
Englishsense: A capsule is a very small tube containing powdered or liquid medicine, which you swallow.
A capsule is a small container with a drug or other substance inside it, which is used for medical or scientific purposes.
In some plants, a capsule is a part which forms a case or container for seeds, fruit, or spores.
A space capsule is the part of a spacecraft in which people travel, and which often separates from the main rocket.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Chinesesense: (美国等国家的)警察局副巡官，消防队中队长；
担任(运动队)的队长;当…的船长(或舰长)；
Englishsense: The captain of a sports team is the player in charge of it.
The captain of a ship is the sailor in charge of it.
The captain of an aeroplane is the pilot in charge of it.
In the United States and some other countries, a captain is a police officer or fireman of fairly senior rank.
If you captain a team or a ship, you are the captain of it.

Chinesesense: 为(照片或漫画)添加说明文字；
Englishsense: A caption is the words printed underneath a picture or cartoon which explain what it is about.
When someone captions a picture or cartoon, they put a caption under it.

Chinesesense: 观众被强制的，受控制的;(市场)垄断的，没有选择权的；
Englishsense: A captive person or animal is being kept imprisoned or enclosed.

A captive audience is a group of people who are not free to leave a certain place and so have to watch or listen. A captive market is a group of people who cannot choose whether or where to buy things.
If you take someone captive or hold someone captive, you take or keep them as a prisoner.

Chinesesense: (尤指在战争中)俘虏，擒获，占领，夺取；
代表[特点);表现,体现(感情、气氛)；
吸引(注意力);激发(想象);赢得(喜爱)；
Englishsense: If you capture someone or something, you catch them, especially in a war.
If something or someone captures a particular quality, feeling, or atmosphere, they represent or express it successfully.
If something captures your attention or imagination, you begin to be interested or excited by it. If someone or something captures your heart, you begin to love them or like them very much.
If an event is captured in a photograph or on film, it is photographed or filmed.
If you capture something that you are trying to obtain in competition with other people, you succeed in obtaining it.
A car is a motor vehicle with room for a small number of passengers.
A car is one of the separate sections of a train.
Railway carriages are called cars when they are used for a particular purpose.

Chinesesense: 碳水化合物;糖类;含碳水化合物的食物；
Englishsense: Carbohydrates are substances, found in certain kinds of food, that provide you with energy. Foods such as sugar and bread that contain these substances can also be referred to as carbohydrates.
Carbon is a chemical element that diamonds and coal are made up of.
A carbon is a sheet of carbon paper.

Chinesesense: (车辆、建筑物破损或被毁后的)骨架,残体；
Englishsense: A carcass is the body of a dead animal.
The carcass of a vehicle or building is its remains after most of it has decayed or been destroyed.

Chinesesense: 银行卡;借记卡;工资卡;购物卡；
(体育比赛的)赛事安排，比赛日程；
要求…出示证明文件(表明达到买酒或饮酒的年龄等)；
处理得当;巧妙发挥优势；
摊牌;直抒己见;和盘托出(感觉、想法、计划)；
Englishsense: A card is a piece of stiff paper or thin cardboard on which something is written or printed.
A card is a piece of cardboard or plastic, or a small document, which shows information about you and which you carry with you, for example to prove your identity.
A card is a rectangular piece of plastic, issued by a bank, company, or shop, which you can use to buy things or obtain money.
A card is a folded piece of stiff paper with a picture and sometimes a message printed on it, which you send to someone on a special occasion.
A card is the same as a postcard.

A card is a piece of thin cardboard carried by someone such as a business person in order to give to other people. A card shows the name, address, telephone number, and other details of the person who carries it.
Cards are thin pieces of cardboard with numbers or pictures printed on them which are used to play various games.
If you are playing cards, you are playing a game using cards.
You can use card to refer to something that gives you an advantage in a particular situation. If you play a particular card, you use that advantage.
Card is strong, stiff paper or thin cardboard.
In computing, a card is a circuit board that can be put into a computer to provide additional memory or functions.
You can use card to refer to a series of races or matches at a particular sporting event.
If you are carded, someone in authority asks you to show a document to prove that you are old enough to do something, for example, to buy or drink alcohol. [be V-ed] [Mainly AM]
If you say that something is on the cards in British English, or in the cards in American English, you mean that it is very likely to happen.
If you say that someone will achieve success if they play their cards right, you mean that they will achieve success if they act skilfully and use the advantages that they have.
