Chinesesense: 欢快的;高兴的;兴高采烈的；
令人愉快的;令人开心的；
乐观的;开朗的;满不在乎的；
Englishsense: Someone who is cheerful is happy and shows this in their behaviour.
Something that is cheerful is pleasant and makes you feel happy.
If you describe someone’s attitude as cheerful, you mean they are not worried about something, and you think that they should be.
Cheese is a solid food made from milk. It is usually white or yellow.
Someone who has a very important job or position can be referred to as a big cheese.
If someone tells you to say ’cheese ’ when they are taking your photograph, they are indicating that they want you to smile.
A chef is a cook in a restaurant or hotel.

Chinesesense: 化学的;化学反应的;用化学方法生成的；
化学品;化合物;化学制品；
Englishsense: Chemical means involving or resulting from a reaction between two or more substances, or relating to the substances that something consists of.
Chemicals are substances that are used in a chemical process or made by a chemical process.

Chinesesense: (兼卖化妆品和某些日用品的)药店；
Englishsense: A chemist or a chemist’s is a shop where drugs and medicines are sold or given out, and where you can buy cosmetics and some household goods.
A chemist is someone who works in a chemist’s shop and is qualified to prepare and sell medicines.
A chemist is a person who does research connected with chemistry or who studies chemistry.

Chinesesense: (物质的)化学组成，化学成分，化学反应；
Englishsense: Chemistry is the scientific study of the structure of substances and of the way that they react with other substances.
The chemistry of an organism or a material is the chemical substances that make it up and the chemical reactions that go on inside it.
If you say that there is chemistry between two people, you mean that is obvious they are attracted to each other or like each other very much.

Chinesesense: (常用于治疗癌症的)化学疗法，化疗；
Englishsense: Chemotherapy is the treatment of disease using chemicals. It is often used in treating cancer.

Chinesesense: 怀有，抱有(希望);怀念(过去)；
珍视，维护，捍卫(权利、特权或原则)；
Englishsense: If you cherish something such as a hope or a pleasant memory, you keep it in your mind for a long period of time.
If you cherish someone or something, you take good care of them because you love them.
If you cherish a right, a privilege, or a principle, you regard it as important and try hard to keep it.
Cherries are small, round fruit with red skins.
A cherry or a cherry tree is a tree that cherries grow on.
Chess is a game for two people, played on a chessboard. Each player has 16 pieces, including a king. Your aim is to move your pieces so that your opponent’s king cannot escape being taken.

Chinesesense: 倾诉胸中的不快;吐苦水；
Englishsense: Your chest is the top part of the front of your body where your ribs, lungs, and heart are.
A chest is a large, heavy box used for storing things.
If you get something off your chest, you talk about something that has been worrying you.

Chinesesense: 老掉牙的话(或故事、笑话);老一套；
Englishsense: A chestnut or chestnut tree is a tall tree with broad leaves.
Chestnuts are the reddish-brown nuts that grow on chestnut trees. You can eat chestnuts.
Something that is chestnut is dark reddish-brown in colour.
If you refer to a statement, a story, or a joke as an old chestnut or a hoary chestnut, you mean that it has been repeated so often that it is no longer interesting.

Chinesesense: 试图承担力不能及的事；
Englishsense: When you chew food, you use your teeth to break it up in your mouth so that it becomes easier to swallow.
If you chew gum or tobacco, you keep biting it and moving it around your mouth to taste the flavour of it. You do not swallow it.
If you chew your lips or your fingernails, you keep biting them because you are nervous.
If a person or animal chews an object, they bite it with their teeth.
A chew is a sweet that you have to chew very hard before it becomes soft.
If you say that someone has bitten off more than they can chew, you mean that they are trying to do something which is too difficult for them.
If people chew the fat, they talk in a relaxed, informal way.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Something or someone that is chic is fashionable and sophisticated.
Chic is used to refer to a particular style or to the quality of being chic.

Chinesesense: 小妞儿(男性用语，可能具冒犯意味)；
Englishsense: A chick is a baby bird.
Some men refer to women as chicks. This use could cause offence.

Chinesesense: 高兴得太早;过早地打如意算盘；
鸡和蛋的问题(指很难决定孰先孰后、孰因孰果的情境)；
像只没头的苍蝇到处乱窜；
Englishsense: Chickens are birds which are kept on a farm for their eggs and for their meat.
If someone calls you a chicken, they mean that you are afraid to do something.
If you say that someone is counting their chickens, you mean that they are assuming that they will be successful or get something, when this is not certain.
If you describe a situation as a chicken and egg situation, you mean that it is impossible to decide which of two things caused the other one.
If someone is running round like a headless chicken or rushing around like a headless chicken, they are panicking when they should be thinking carefully about what needs to be done.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Chinesesense: (组织机构的)负责人，头儿，首领；
(用于职位头衔)主管的，首席的；
Englishsense: The chief of an organization is the person who is in charge of it.
The chief of a tribe is its leader.
Chief is used in the job titles of the most senior worker or workers of a particular kind in an organization.
The chief cause, part, or member of something is the most important one.
A child is a human being who is not yet an adult.
Someone’s children are their sons and daughters of any age.
A person’s childhood is the period of their life when they are a child.
When you chill something or when it chills, you lower its temperature so that it becomes colder but does not freeze.
When cold weather or something cold chills a person or a place, it makes that person or that place feel very cold.
If you say that something you see, hear, or feel chills you, you mean that it frightens you.
If something sends a chill through you, it gives you a sudden feeling of fear or anxiety.
A chill is a mild illness which can give you a slight fever and headache.
Chill weather is cold and unpleasant.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 恐怖的;吓人的;令人害怕的；
Englishsense: If you describe something as chilling, you mean it is frightening.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: (人际关系、反应)冷淡的，冷冰冰的，不热情的；
Englishsense: Something that is chilly is unpleasantly cold. See usage note at: cold
If you feel chilly, you feel rather cold.
You say that relations between people are chilly or that a person’s response is chilly when they are not friendly, welcoming, or enthusiastic.
A chimney is a pipe through which smoke goes up into the air, usually through the roof of a building.

Chinesesense: 坦然面对，欣然接受(令人不快或困难的局面)；
Englishsense: Your chin is the part of your face that is below your mouth and above your neck.
If you say that someone took something on the chin, you mean that they accepted an unpleasant or difficult situation bravely and without making a lot of fuss about it.
China is a hard white substance made from clay. It is used to make things such as cups, bowls, plates, and ornaments.
Cups, bowls, plates, and ornaments made of china are referred to as china.

Chinesesense: 中国的;汉语的;中国人的；
中国话;汉语;(尤指)普通话；
Englishsense: Something that is Chinese relates or belongs to China or its languages or people.
The languages that are spoken in China, especially Mandarin, are often referred to as Chinese.

Chinesesense: (瓷器上的)缺口，豁口;(家具上的)凹坑，瘪儿；
(谈判中的)筹码，讨价还价的资本；
(性格或行为)酷似父亲(或母亲)的人；
Englishsense: Chips are long, thin pieces of potato fried in oil or fat and eaten hot, usually with a meal.
Chips or potato chips are very thin slices of fried potato that are eaten cold as a snack.
A silicon chip is a very small piece of silicon with electronic circuits on it which is part of a computer or other piece of machinery.
A chip is a small piece of something or a small piece which has been broken off something.
A chip in something such as a piece of china or furniture is where a small piece has been broken off it.
If you chip something or if it chips, a small piece is broken off it.
Chips are plastic counters used in gambling to represent money.
In discussions between people or governments, a chip or a bargaining chip is something of value which one side holds, which can be exchanged for something they want from the other side.
If you describe someone as a chip off the old block, you mean that they are just like one of their parents in character or behaviour.
If you say that something happens when the chips are down, you mean it happens when a situation gets very difficult.
If you say that someone has a chip on their shoulder, you think that they feel inferior or that they believe they have been treated unfairly.
Chlorine is a strong-smelling gas that is used to clean water and to make cleaning products.

Chinesesense: (通常用热牛奶调制的)巧克力热饮；
通常为盒装的巧克力糖；
Englishsense: Chocolate is a sweet hard food made from cocoa beans. It is usually brown in colour and is eaten as a sweet.
Chocolate or hot chocolate is a drink made from a powder containing chocolate. It is usually made with hot milk.
Chocolates are small sweets or nuts covered with a layer of chocolate. They are usually sold in a box.
Chocolate is used to describe things that are dark brown in colour.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If there is a choice of things, there are several of them and you can choose the one you want.
Your choice is someone or something that you choose from a range of things.
Choice means of very high quality.
If you have no choice but to do something or have little choice but to do it, you cannot avoid doing it.
The thing or person of your choice is the one that you choose.
The item of choice is the one that most people prefer.

Chinesesense: (教堂的)唱诗班;(学校的)合唱队，合唱团；
Englishsense: A choir is a group of people who sing together, for example in a church or school.
In a church building, the choir is the area in front of the altar where the choir sits.
When you choke or when something chokes you, you cannot breathe properly or get enough air into your lungs.
To choke someone means to squeeze their neck until they are dead.
If a place is choked with things or people, it is full of them and they prevent movement in it.
The choke in a car, truck, or other vehicle is a device that reduces the amount of air going into the engine and makes it easier to start.
Cholesterol is a substance that exists in the fat, tissues, and blood of all animals. Too much cholesterol in a person’s blood can cause heart disease.

Chinesesense: 享受优厚待遇的少数人；精英；
Englishsense: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.
If you choose to do something, you do it because you want to or because you feel that it is right.
If there is little to choose between people or things or nothing to choose between them, it is difficult to decide which is better or more suitable.
The chosen few are a small group who are treated better than other people. You sometimes use this expression when you think this is unfair.

Chinesesense: 将被取消(或关闭);人将被解雇；
Englishsense: If you chop something, you cut it into pieces with strong downward movements of a knife or an axe.
A chop is a small piece of meat cut from the ribs of a sheep or pig.
When people chop and change, they keep changing their minds about what to do or how to act.
If something is for the chop or is going to get the chop, it is going to be stopped or closed. If someone is for the chop, they are going to lose their job or position.
A chord is a number of musical notes played or sung at the same time with a pleasing effect.
If something strikes a chord with you, it makes you feel sympathy or enthusiasm.
A chore is a task that you must do but that you find unpleasant or boring.
Chores are tasks such as cleaning, washing, and ironing that have to be done regularly at home.

Chinesesense: 齐声，异口同声(表示批评、反对或赞扬)；
Englishsense: A chorus is a part of a song which is repeated after each verse.
A chorus is a large group of people who sing together.
A chorus is a piece of music written to be sung by a large group of people.
A chorus is a group of singers or dancers who perform together in a show, in contrast to the soloists.
When there is a chorus of criticism, disapproval, or praise, that attitude is expressed by a lot of people at the same time.
When people chorus something, they say it or sing it together.
A Christian is someone who follows the teachings of Jesus Christ.
Christian means relating to Christianity or Christians.
Christianity is a religion that is based on the teachings of Jesus Christ and the belief that he was the son of God.
Christmas is a Christian festival when the birth of Jesus Christ is celebrated. Christmas is celebrated on the 25th of December.
Christmas is the period of several days around and including Christmas Day.

Chinesesense: 难以根除的;积习难改的；
Englishsense: A chronic illness or disability lasts for a very long time.
You can describe someone’s bad habits or behaviour as chronic when they have behaved like that for a long time and do not seem to be able to stop themselves.
A chronic situation or problem is very severe and unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 按时间顺序记述(或播放)；
Englishsense: To chronicle a series of events means to write about them or show them in broadcasts in the order in which they happened.
A chronicle is an account or record of a series of events.
Chronicle is sometimes used as part of the name of a newspaper.

Chinesesense: 辞去(工作);停止，终止(活动)；
Englishsense: When you chuck something somewhere, you throw it there in a casual or careless way.
If you chuck your job or some other activity, you stop doing it.
If your girlfriend or boyfriend chucks you, they end the relationship.
A chuck is a device for holding a tool in a machine such as a drill.
When you chuckle, you laugh quietly.
Chunks of something are thick solid pieces of it.
A chunk of something is a large amount or large part of it.

Chinesesense: 广纳众议的机构[或团体]; 兼收并蓄的活动；
Englishsense: A church is a building in which Christians worship. You usually refer to this place as church when you are talking about the time that people spend there.
A Church is one of the groups of people within the Christian religion, for example Catholics or Methodists, that have their own beliefs, clergy, and forms of worship.
You can refer to an organization, group, or area of activity as a broad church when it includes a wide range of opinions, beliefs, or styles.

Chinesesense: 搅动，搅起，扰动(水、泥浆、灰尘)；
Englishsense: A churn is a container which is used for making butter.
If something churns water, mud, or dust, it moves it about violently.
If you say that your stomach is churning, you mean that you feel sick. You can also say that something churns your stomach.
Cigars are rolls of dried tobacco leaves which people smoke.
Cigarettes are small tubes of paper containing tobacco which people smoke.
A cinema is a place where people go to watch films for entertainment.
You can talk about the cinema when you are talking about seeing a film in a cinema.
Cinema is the business and art of making films.
Cinnamon is a sweet spice used for flavouring food.

Chinesesense: (指朋友或有相同兴趣或职业的人组成的)圈子，界；
兜了一圈回到原地;循环；
在原地兜圈子;原地踏步;毫无进展；
Englishsense: A circle is a shape consisting of a curved line completely surrounding an area. Every part of the line is the same distance from the centre of the area.
A circle of something is a round flat piece or area of it.
A circle of objects or people is a group of them arranged in the shape of a circle.
If something circles an object or a place, or circles around it, it forms a circle around it.
If an aircraft or a bird circles or circles something, it moves round in a circle in the air.
To circle around someone or something, or to circle them, means to move around them.
If you circle something on a piece of paper, you draw a circle around it.
You can refer to a group of people as a circle when they meet each other regularly because they are friends or because they belong to the same profession or share the same interests.
In a theatre or cinema, the circle is an area of seats on the upper floor.
If you say that you have come full circle or have turned full circle, you mean that after a long series of events or changes the same situation that you started with still exists.
If you say that someone is going round in circles or around in circles, you mean that they are not achieving anything because they keep coming back to the same point or problem.

Chinesesense: 尤指工作时的巡回线路，巡回，巡游；
Englishsense: An electrical circuit is a complete route which an electric current can flow around.
A circuit is a series of places that are visited regularly by a person or group, especially as a part of their job.
A racing circuit is a track on which cars, motorbikes, or cycles race.
A circuit of a place or area is a journey all the way round it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (同时发送给很多人的)广告印刷品，通告；
Englishsense: Something that is circular is shaped like a circle.
A circular journey or route is one in which you go to a place and return by a different route.
A circular argument or theory is not valid because it uses a statement to prove something which is then used to prove the statement.
A circular is an official letter or advertisement that is sent to a large number of people at the same time.

Chinesesense: (在密闭场所或系统内)循环，流转，传播；
Englishsense: If a piece of writing circulates or is circulated, copies of it are passed round among a group of people.
If something such as a rumour circulates or is circulated, the people in a place tell it to each other.
When something circulates, it moves easily and freely within a closed place or system.
If you circulate at a party, you move among the guests and talk to different people.

Chinesesense: (货币等)流通/不流通/退出流通；
(一段时间)不出现在公共场合，不参加社交活动;坐牢;服刑；
Englishsense: The circulation of a newspaper or magazine is the number of copies that are sold each time it is produced.
Your circulation is the movement of blood through your body.

If something such as money is in circulation, it is being used by the public. If something is out of circulation or has been withdrawn from circulation, it is no longer available for use by the public.
If someone is out of circulation, they do not appear in public or at social gatherings for a period of time. You can also say that someone is out of circulation when they are in prison.

Chinesesense: 事件发生的情形，详情，原委；
生活状况;境况;(尤指)经济状况；
在任何情况下;无论如何；
在那种情况下;情况既然如此；
Englishsense: The circumstances of a particular situation are the conditions which affect what happens.
The circumstances of an event are the way it happened or the causes of it.
Your circumstances are the conditions of your life, especially the amount of money that you have.
Events and situations which cannot be controlled are sometimes referred to as circumstance.
You can emphasize that something must not or will not happen by saying that it must not or will not happen under any circumstances.
You can use in the circumstances or under the circumstances before or after a statement to indicate that you have considered the conditions affecting the situation before making the statement.

Chinesesense: 闹哄哄的人群;架势很大的活动；
(有时用于街道名称)环形路，环形广场，环形交叉口；
Englishsense: A circus is a group that consists of clowns, acrobats, and animals which travels around to different places and performs shows.
If you describe a group of people or an event as a circus, you disapprove of them because they attract a lot of attention but do not achieve anything useful.
Circus is sometimes used as part of the name of a street which goes in a circle.
A citation is an official document or speech which praises a person for something brave or special that they have done.
A citation from a book or other piece of writing is a passage or phrase from it.
A citation is the same as a summons.

Chinesesense: 尤指作为例证引用，援引，提及；
Englishsense: If you cite something, you quote it or mention it, especially as an example or proof of what you are saying.
To cite a person means to officially name them in a legal case. To cite a reason or cause means to state it as the official reason for your case.
If someone is cited, they are officially ordered to appear before a court.
Someone who is a citizen of a particular country is legally accepted as belonging to that country.
The citizens of a town or city are the people who live there.

Chinesesense: 公民归属；公民义务;公民责任感；
Englishsense: If you have citizenship of a country, you are legally accepted as belonging to it.
Citizenship is the fact of belonging to a community because you live in it, and the duties and responsibilities that this brings.

Chinesesense: 柑橘属水果(如橘子、柠檬、西柚)；
Englishsense: A citrus fruit is a juicy fruit with a sharp taste such as an orange, lemon, or grapefruit.
You use civic to describe people or things that have an official status in a town or city.
You use civic to describe the duties or feelings that people have because they belong to a particular community.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 民用的;平民的;非军事的；
政府的；国家的;世俗的;非宗教的；
权利公民的，公民应有的；
彬彬有礼的;斯文的;客气的；
Englishsense: You use civil to describe events that happen within a country and that involve the different groups of people in it.
You use civil to describe people or things in a country that are not connected with its armed forces.
You use civil to describe things that are connected with the state rather than with a religion.
You use civil to describe the rights that people have within a society.
Someone who is civil is polite in a formal way, but not particularly friendly.

Chinesesense: 民用的;平民的;非军用的；
Englishsense: In a military situation, a civilian is anyone who is not a member of the armed forces.
In a military situation, civilian is used to describe people or things that are not military.
A civilization is a human society with its own social organization and culture.
Civilization is the state of having an advanced level of social organization and a comfortable way of life.
You can refer to a place where you can enjoy the comforts that you consider to be necessary as civilization.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 有礼貌的;举止得体的;通情达理的；
Englishsense: If you describe a society as civilized, you mean that it is advanced and has sensible laws and customs.
If you describe a person or their behaviour as civilized, you mean that they are polite and reasonable.

Chinesesense: 声称(负有责任或享有功劳)；
索取，索要(有权拥有的东西)；
取得，获得，赢得(纪录、冠军或奖励)；
需要，要求(花时间或精力)；
(向雇主)索要，索取，讨要(钱、福利)；
(战争、疾病、事故)夺去(生命)，导致(死亡)；
Englishsense: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.
A claim is something which someone says which they cannot prove and which may be false.
If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.
If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.
A claim is a demand for something that you think you have a right to.
If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.
If you have a claim on someone or their attention, you have the right to demand things from them or to demand their attention.
If something or someone claims your attention, they need you to spend your time and effort on them.
If you claim money from the government, an insurance company, or another organization, you officially apply to them for it, because you think you are entitled to it according to their rules.
If you claim money or other benefits from your employers, you demand them because you think you deserve or need them.
If you say that a war, disease, or accident claims someone’s life, you mean that they are killed in it or by it.
Someone’s claim to fame is something quite important or interesting that they have done or that is connected with them.
If you lay claim to something you do not have, you say that it belongs to you.

Chinesesense: 将…固定(在某处)；紧紧抓住；
(将违章停放的车辆扣在原地的)夹钳，车轮固定夹；
Englishsense: A clamp is a device that holds two things firmly together.
When you clamp one thing to another, you fasten the two things together with a clamp.
To clamp something in a particular place means to put it or hold it there firmly and tightly.

A clamp is a large metal device which is fitted to the wheel of an illegally parked car or other vehicle in order to prevent it from being driven away. The driver has to pay to have the clamp removed.
To clamp a car means to fit a clamp to one of its wheels so that it cannot be driven away.

Chinesesense: (有共同利益的)集团，帮派，派系；
Englishsense: A clan is a group which consists of families that are related to each other.
You can refer to a group of people with the same interests as a clan.
When you clap, you hit your hands together to show appreciation or attract attention.
If you clap your hand or an object onto something, you put it there quickly and firmly.
If you clap someone on the back or on the shoulder, you hit their back or shoulder with your hand in a friendly way.
A clap of thunder is a sudden and loud noise of thunder.
To clarify something means to make it easier to understand, usually by explaining it in more detail.

Chinesesense: (书、论点等的)清楚，清晰易懂，明晰；
(液体、玻璃或空气的)清澈度，透明度；
Englishsense: The clarity of something such as a book or argument is its quality of being well explained and easy to understand.
Clarity is the ability to think clearly.
Clarity is the quality of being clear in outline or sound.
The clarity of a liquid, of glass, or of the air is the degree to which it is clear.

Chinesesense: 发生冲突;打斗;争论;意见不合；

If you close something such as a computer file or window, you give the computer an instruction to remove it from the screen.
When you close your eyes or your eyes close, your eyelids move downwards, so that you can no longer see.
When a place closes or is closed, work or activity stops there for a short period.
If a place such as a factory, shop, or school closes, or if it is closed, all work or activity stops there permanently.

If something such as a competition or an election is too close to call, it is not possible to predict who will win because it seems likely to be won by only a very small margin.
If you are closing on someone or something that you are following, you are getting nearer and nearer to them.

Englishsense: You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn’t to say that someone was unable to do something. See usage note at: can
You use could to indicate that something sometimes happened.
You use could have to indicate that something was a possibility in the past, although it did not actually happen.
You use could to indicate that something is possibly true, or that it may possibly happen.
You use could not or couldn’t to indicate that it is not possible that something is true.
You use could to talk about a possibility, ability, or opportunity that depends on other conditions.
You use could when you are saying that one thing or situation resembles another.
You use could, or couldn’t in questions, when you are making offers and suggestions.

You use could in questions when you are making a polite request or asking for permission to do something. Speakers sometimes use couldn’t instead of ’could’ to show that they realize that their request may be refused.
People sometimes use structures with if I could or could I as polite ways of interrupting someone or of introducing what they are going to say next.

You use could to say emphatically that someone ought to do the thing mentioned, especially when you are annoyed because they have not done it. You use why couldn’t in questions to express your surprise or annoyance that someone has not done something.
You use could when you are expressing strong feelings about something by saying that you feel as if you want to do the thing mentioned, although you do not do it.
You use could after ’if’ when talking about something that you do not have the ability or opportunity to do, but which you are imagining in order to consider what the likely consequences might be.

You use could not or couldn’t with comparatives to emphasize that someone or something has as much as is possible of a particular quality. For example, if you say ’I couldn’t be happier’, you mean that you are extremely happy.
In speech, you use how could in questions to emphasize that you feel strongly about something bad that has happened.
You say ’ I couldn’t ’ to refuse an offer of more food or drink.

If there is a danger that something unpleasant will happen, it is possible that it will happen.
If someone who has been seriously ill is out of danger, they are still ill, but they are not expected to die.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 危险的;可能带来危害的;不安全的；
Englishsense: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.
If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.
If you say that someone is dangling something attractive before you, you mean they are offering it to you in order to try to influence you in some way.

Chinesesense: 丹麦的;丹麦人的;丹麦语或文化的；
Englishsense: Danish means belonging or relating to Denmark, its people, its language, or culture.
Danish is the language spoken in Denmark.

Chinesesense: 向…挑战;激…[做]; 问…有没有胆量做；
[表示震惊和愤怒) 你竟敢，你怎么敢；
Englishsense: If you do not dare to do something, you do not have enough courage to do it, or you do not want to do it because you fear the consequences. If you dare to do something, you do something which requires a lot of courage.
If you dare someone to do something, you challenge them to prove that they are not frightened of doing it.
A dare is a challenge which one person gives to another to do something dangerous or frightening.
If you say to someone ’ don’t you dare ’ do something, you are telling them not to do it and letting them know that you are angry.
You say ’ how dare you ’’ when you are very shocked and angry about something that someone has done.
You use ’ dare I say it ’ when you know that what you are going to say will disappoint or annoy someone.
You can use ’ I dare say ’ or ’ I daresay ’ before or after a statement to indicate that you believe it is probably true.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 大胆的;敢于冒险的;勇于创新的；
Englishsense: People who are daring are willing to do or say things which are new or which might shock or anger other people.
A daring person is willing to do things that might be dangerous.
Daring is the courage to do things which might be dangerous or which might shock or anger other people.

Chinesesense: (头发、眼睛或肤色)棕色的，黑色的；
(白人) 有着棕色或黑色头发且皮肤略带棕色的，肤色深的；
(时期) 黑暗的，恐怖的，悲惨的；
(眼神或话语) 阴险的，邪恶的，不祥的；
[指与严肃或令人不快的事物相关的)黑色的；
Englishsense: When it is dark, there is not enough light to see properly, for example because it is night.
The dark is the lack of light in a place.
If you describe something as dark, you mean that it is black in colour, or a shade that is close to black.
When you use dark to describe a colour, you are referring to a shade of that colour which is close to black, or seems to have some black in it.
If someone has dark hair, eyes, or skin, they have brown or black hair, eyes, or skin.
If you describe a white person as dark, you mean that they have brown or black hair, and often a brownish skin.
A dark period of time is unpleasant or frightening.
A dark place or area is mysterious and not fully known about.
Dark thoughts are sad, and show that you are expecting something unpleasant to happen.
Dark looks or remarks make you think that the person giving them wants to harm you or that something horrible is going to happen.
If you describe something as dark, you mean that it is related to things that are serious or unpleasant, rather than light-hearted.
If you do something after dark, you do it when the sun has set and night has begun.
If you do something before dark, you do it before the sun sets and night begins.
If you are in the dark about something, you do not know anything about it.
If you describe something someone says or does as a shot in the dark or a stab in the dark, you mean they are guessing that what they say is correct or that what they do will be successful.

Chinesesense: 使变得阴郁;使心情沉重；
Englishsense: If something darkens or if a person or thing darkens it, it becomes darker.
If someone’s mood darkens or if something darkens their mood, they suddenly become rather unhappy.
If someone’s face darkens, they suddenly look angry.

Chinesesense: (用作昵称) 亲爱的，宝贝儿；
(英国一些地方用于表示友善的称呼) 亲爱的；
Englishsense: You call someone darling if you love them or like them very much.
In some parts of Britain, people call other people darling as a sign of friendliness.
Some people use darling to describe someone or something that they love or like very much.
If you describe someone as a darling, you are fond of them and think that they are nice.
The darling of a group of people is someone who is especially liked by that group.
If a person or animal darts somewhere, they move there suddenly and quickly.
If you dart a look at someone or something, or if your eyes dart to them, you look at them very quickly.
A dart is a small, narrow object with a sharp point which can be thrown or shot.
Darts is a game in which you throw darts at a round board which has numbers on it.

Chinesesense: 往食物或饮料里添加的少量，少许；
[为逃离等而)飞速奔向，猛冲向；
Englishsense: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly.
If you say that you have to dash, you mean that you are in a hurry and have to leave immediately.
A dash of something is a small quantity of it which you add when you are preparing food or mixing a drink.
A dash of a quality is a small amount of it that is found in something and often makes it more interesting or distinctive.
If you dash something against a wall or other surface, you throw or push it violently, often so hard that it breaks.
If an event or person dashes someone’s hopes or expectations, it destroys them by making it impossible that the thing that is hoped for or expected will ever happen.
If you do something in a dash, you do it very quickly, perhaps with very bad results.
A dash is a short fast race.
A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.
You can say dash or dash it or dash it all when you are rather annoyed about something.
The dash of a car is its dashboard.
If you say that someone cuts a dash, you mean that they have an attractively stylish appearance or a rather bold manner.
If you make a dash for a place, you run there very quickly, for example to escape from someone or something.
If you dash off to a place, you go there very quickly.
If you dash off a piece of writing, you write or compose it very quickly, without thinking about it very much.

POS: N-UNCOUNT; also N-PLURAL 不可数名词；复数名词
Chinesesense: 尤指可用于分析的资料，材料，数据[美国英语中通常用作复数名词;在专业或正式的英国英语中有时用作复数名词，有时用作不可数名词)；
(可存储并为计算机程序所用的) 数据；
Englishsense: You can refer to information as data, especially when it is in the form of facts or statistics that you can analyse. In American English, data is usually a plural noun. In technical or formal British English, data is sometimes a plural noun, but at other times, it is an uncount noun.
Data is information that can be stored and used by a computer program.
A database is a collection of data that is stored in a computer and that can easily be used and added to.

Chinesesense: 在信件、支票等上注明日期；
在某个日期;在某个时间；
Englishsense: A date is a specific time that can be named, for example a particular day or a particular year.
If you date something, you give or discover the date when it was made or when it began.
When you date something such as a letter or a cheque, you write that day’s date on it.
If you want to refer to an event without saying exactly when it will happen or when it happened, you can say that it will happen or happened at some date in the future or past.
To date means up until the present time.
If something dates, it goes out of fashion and becomes unacceptable to modern tastes.
If your ideas, what you say, or the things that you like or can remember date you, they show that you are quite old or older than the people you are with.
A date is an appointment to meet someone or go out with them, especially someone with whom you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship.
If you have a date with someone with whom you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship, you can refer to that person as your date.
If you are dating someone, you go out with them regularly because you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship with them. You can also say that two people are dating.
A date is a small, dark-brown, sticky fruit with a stone inside. Dates grow on palm trees in hot countries.

Chinesesense: (机构、服务等) 介绍约会的，婚介的；
Englishsense: Dating agencies or services are for people who are trying to find a girlfriend or boyfriend.
Someone’s daughter is their female child.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 使人畏惧的;令人胆怯的;让人气馁的；
Englishsense: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.
Dawn is the time of day when light first appears in the sky, just before the sun rises.
The dawn of a period of time or a situation is the beginning of it.
If something is dawning, it is beginning to develop or come into existence.
When you say that a particular day dawned, you mean it arrived or began, usually when it became light.

Chinesesense: 如今;在当代;在今天这个时代；
(在战斗、辩论或体育竞赛中) 获胜，取胜；
已过全盛时期;风光不再;不再流行；
将来有一天;总有一天;有朝一日；
挽回局面;扭转败局;转危为安;反败为胜；
(困难的任务)日常工作一部分的，常有的，难免的；
Englishsense: A day is one of the seven twenty-four hour periods of time in a week.
Day is the time when it is light, or the time when you are up and doing things.
You can refer to a particular period in history as a particular day or as particular days.
If something happens day after day, it happens every day without stopping.
In this day and age means in modern times.
If you say that something has seen better days, you mean that it is old and in poor condition.
If you call it a day, you decide to stop what you are doing because you are tired of it or because it is not successful.
If someone carries the day, they are the winner in a contest such as a battle, debate, or sporting competition.
If you say that something has had its day, you mean that the period during which it was most successful or popular has now passed.
If something makes your day, it makes you feel very happy.
If something happens day and night or night and day, it happens all the time without stopping.
One day or some day or one of these days means at some time in the future.
If you say that something happened the other day, you mean that it happened a few days ago.
If someone or something saves the day in a situation which seems likely to fail, they manage to make it successful.
If something happens from day to day or day by day, it happens each day.
To this day means up until and including the present time.
If a particular person, group, or thing wins the day, they win a battle, struggle, or competition. If they lose the day, they are defeated.
If you say that a task is all in a day’s work for someone, you mean that they do not mind doing it although it may be difficult, because it is part of their job or because they often do it.

Chinesesense: 在光天化日之下;在大白天；
Englishsense: Daylight is the natural light that there is during the day, before it gets dark.
Daylight is the time of day when it begins to get light.
If you say that a crime is committed in broad daylight, you are expressing your surprise that it is done during the day when people can see it, rather than at night.

Chinesesense: (电视或广播节目周一至周五)白天播出的，日间播放的；
Englishsense: The daytime is the part of a day between the time when it gets light and the time when it gets dark.
Daytime television and radio is broadcast during the morning and afternoon on weekdays.
Day-to-day things or activities exist or happen every day as part of ordinary life.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 辉煌的;灿烂的;艳丽的;动人的；
Englishsense: Something that is dazzling is very impressive or beautiful.
A dazzling light is very bright and makes you unable to see properly for a short time.

使突然停止发生或移动；
败局已定的;不太可能成功的；
Englishsense: A person, animal, or plant that is dead is no longer living.
Land or water that is dead contains no living things.
If you describe a place or a period of time as dead, you do not like it because there is very little activity taking place in it.
Something that is dead is no longer being used or is finished.
If you say that an idea, plan, or subject is dead, you mean that people are no longer interested in it or willing to develop it any further.
A dead language is no longer spoken or written as a means of communication, although it may still be studied.
A telephone or piece of electrical equipment that is dead is no longer functioning, for example because it no longer has any electrical power.

In sport, when a ball is dead, it has gone outside the playing area, or a situation has occurred in which the game has to be temporarily stopped, and none of the players can score points or gain an advantage.
A dead sound or colour is dull rather than lively or bright.
Dead is used to mean ’complete’ or ’absolute’, especially before the words ’centre’, ’silence’, and ’stop’.
Dead means ’precisely’ or ’exactly’.
Dead is sometimes used to mean ’very’.
If you reply ’ Over my dead body ’ when a plan or action has been suggested, you are emphasizing that you dislike it, and will do everything you can to prevent it.
If you say that something such as an idea or situation is dead and buried, you are emphasizing that you think that it is completely finished or past, and cannot happen or exist again in the future.
If you say that a person or animal dropped dead or dropped down dead, you mean that they died very suddenly and unexpectedly.
If you tell someone to drop dead, you are insulting them, rudely disagreeing with them, or refusing to do something, or telling them to stop bothering you.
If you say that someone is dead and gone, you are emphasizing that they are dead, and thinking about what happened or will happen after their death.
If you say that you feel dead or are half dead, you mean that you feel very tired or ill and very weak.
If something happens in the dead of night, at dead of night, or in the dead of winter, it happens in the middle part of the night or the winter, when it is darkest or coldest.
If you say that someone or something rises or comes back from the dead, you mean that they become active or successful again after being inactive for a while.
If you say that you wouldn’t be seen dead or be caught dead in particular clothes, places, or situations, you are expressing strong dislike or disapproval of them.
To stop dead means to suddenly stop happening or moving. To stop someone or something dead means to cause them to suddenly stop happening or moving.
If you say that someone or something is dead in the water, you are emphasizing that they have failed, and that there is little hope of them being successful in the future.
A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

Chinesesense: 为达目的不择手段的;阴险毒辣的;冷酷无情的；
非常乏味的;极其无聊的；
(尤用于强调令人不快或不受欢迎的特质) 极其，非常；
(敌人或对手)殊死的，不共戴天的；
(运动员或其动作) 极富技巧性的，极难防御的；
Englishsense: If something is deadly, it is likely or able to cause someone’s death, or has already caused someone’s death.
If you describe a person or their behaviour as deadly, you mean that they will do or say anything to get what they want, without caring about other people.
If you describe someone or something as deadly, you mean that you think they are very dull and boring.
You can use deadly to emphasize that something has a particular quality, especially an unpleasant or undesirable quality.
A deadly situation has unpleasant or dangerous consequences.
Deadly enemies or rivals fight or compete with each other in a very aggressive way.
In sport, deadly players and actions are extremely skilful and successful.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 对…充耳不闻的;不愿听…的；
Englishsense: Someone who is deaf is unable to hear anything or is unable to hear very well.
If you say that someone is deaf to people’s requests, arguments, or criticisms, you are criticizing them because they refuse to pay attention to them.

Chinesesense: 沉重打击;对…造成伤害或损失；
Englishsense: If you say that you need or have a great deal of or a good deal of a particular thing, you are emphasizing that you need or have a lot of it.
A deal of something is a lot of it.
If you make a deal, do a deal, or cut a deal, you complete an agreement or an arrangement with someone, especially in business.
If a person, company, or shop deals in a particular type of goods, their business involves buying or selling those goods.
If someone deals illegal drugs, they sell them.
If someone has had a bad deal, they have been unfortunate or have been treated unfairly.
If you deal playing cards, you give them out to the players in a game of cards.
If an event deals a blow to something or someone, it causes them great difficulties or makes failure more likely.
A dealer is a person whose business involves buying and selling things.
A dealer is someone who buys and sells illegal drugs.

Chinesesense: (通常指某汽车公司的) 特许经销商；
Englishsense: A dealership is a company that sells cars, usually for one car company.
Someone’s dealings with a person or organization are the relations that they have with them or the business that they do with them.

Chinesesense: (大学或学院的) 院长，教务长；
Englishsense: A dean is an important official at a university or college.
A dean is a priest who is the main administrator of a large church.
The dean of a group is the most important member of that group.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 对…来说心爱的;在…心中宝贵的；
(用于表示喜爱或带有屈尊俯就意味的称呼中) 亲爱的;小…；
(用于信函抬头的名字或头衔前) 亲爱的，尊敬的；
尊敬的先生/尊敬的女士(英国英语中用于正式信函的开头，美国英语中则用 Sir 或 Madam)；
(用于称呼喜爱的人) 亲爱的；
(表示伤心、失望或吃惊) 啊呀，哎哟，天哪；
使…付出巨大代价;使…饱尝苦头；
Englishsense: You use dear to describe someone or something that you feel affection for.
If something is dear to you or dear to your heart, you care deeply about it.

You use dear in expressions such as ’ my dear fellow ’, ’ dear girl ’, or ’ my dear Richard ’ when you are addressing someone whom you know and are fond of. You can also use expressions like this in a rude way to indicate that you think you are superior to the person you are addressing.
Dear is written at the beginning of a letter, followed by the name or title of the person you are writing to.
In British English, you begin formal letters with ’ Dear Sir ’ or ’ Dear Madam ’. In American English, you begin them with ’Sir’ or ’Madam’.
You can call someone dear as a sign of affection.
You can use dear in expressions such as ’ oh dear ’, ’ dear me ’, and ’ dear, dear ’ when you are sad, disappointed, or surprised about something.
You can call someone a dear when you are fond of them and think that they are nice.
If you say that something is dear, you mean that it costs a lot of money, usually more than you can afford or more than you think it should cost.
If something that someone does costs them dear, they suffer a lot as a result of it.

Chinesesense: 生死攸关的;至关重要的；
(用于形容词或动词后，表示强调)吓得要死/无聊得要命；
使…累死累活地工作或劳动；
Englishsense: Death is the permanent end of the life of a person or animal.
A particular kind of death is a particular way of dying.
The death of something is the permanent end of it.
If you say that someone is at death’s door, you mean they are very ill indeed and likely to die.
If you say that you will fight to the death for something, you are emphasizing that you will do anything to achieve or protect it, even if you suffer as a consequence.
If you refer to a fight or contest as a fight to the death, you are emphasizing that it will not stop until the death or total victory of one of the opponents.
If you say that something is a matter of life and death, you are emphasizing that it is extremely important, often because someone may die or suffer great harm if people do not act immediately.
If someone is put to death, they are executed.
You use to death after a verb to indicate that a particular action or process results in someone’s death.

You use to death after an adjective or a verb to emphasize the action, state, or feeling mentioned. For example, if you are frightened to death or bored to death, you are extremely frightened or bored.
If you say that someone works another person to death, you are emphasizing that they make them work very hard indeed, especially in a way that seems cruel or unfair.

Chinesesense: 各自发表不同观点的辩论，争论，讨论；
(议会或其他机构就某问题在投票前进行的)辩论；
存在争论的;有待讨论的;未确定的；
Englishsense: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.
A debate is a formal discussion, for example in a parliament or institution, in which people express different opinions about a particular subject and then vote on it.
If people debate a topic, they discuss it fairly formally, putting forward different views. You can also say that one person debates a topic with another person.
If you debate whether to do something or what to do, you think or talk about possible courses of action before deciding exactly what you are going to do.
If you say that a matter is open to debate, you mean that people have different opinions about it, or it has not yet been firmly decided.

Chinesesense: 被毁物的残骸;碎片;垃圾；
Englishsense: Debris is pieces from something that has been destroyed or pieces of rubbish or unwanted material that are spread around.

Chinesesense: (表示感激) 我欠你个人情/我受你的恩惠；
Englishsense: A debt is a sum of money that you owe someone.
Debt is the state of owing money.
You use debt in expressions such as I owe you a debt or I am in your debt when you are expressing gratitude for something that someone has done for you.

Chinesesense: (表演者或运动员的) 首次登台，初次露面；歌手的首次录音；
Englishsense: The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.

Chinesesense: 十年，十年期[尤指一个年代)；
Englishsense: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

Chinesesense: (尸体或死去的植物) 腐烂，腐朽，腐败;(牙齿) 遭蛀蚀；
(社会、制度、机构等) 衰败，衰退，衰落；
Englishsense: When something such as a dead body, a dead plant, or a tooth decays, it is gradually destroyed by a natural process.
If something such as a society, system, or institution decays, it gradually becomes weaker or its condition gets worse.
The deceased is used to refer to a particular person or to particular people who have recently died.
A deceased person is one who has recently died.
If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.
If you deceive yourself, you do not admit to yourself something that you know is true.
If something deceives you, it gives you a wrong impression and makes you believe something that is not true.

A doctrine is a statement of official government policy, especially foreign policy.
A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them.
A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.
If you document something, you make a detailed record of it in writing or on film or tape.

Chinesesense: 电视、广播等纪实节目;纪录片；
证据有文件记录的，来源于文件的，书面的；
Englishsense: A documentary is a television or radio programme, or a film, which shows real events or provides information about a particular subject.
Documentary evidence consists of things that are written down.
Documentation consists of documents which provide proof or evidence of something, or are a record of something.

Chinesesense: (常指用欺诈的方式故意)躲避，逃避；
Englishsense: If you dodge, you move suddenly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.
If you dodge something, you avoid it by quickly moving aside or out of reach so that it cannot hit or reach you.
If you dodge something, you deliberately avoid thinking about it or dealing with it, often by being deceitful.

Chinesesense: 公狗;犬科雄兽(雄狐、雄狼等)；
蹩脚货;粗制滥造的东西；
带有赌博性质的赛狗会，跑狗；
狗咬狗;残酷无情的竞争;自相残杀；
不接受新事物;不喜欢新玩意儿；
Englishsense: A dog is a very common four-legged animal that is often kept by people as a pet or to guard or hunt. There are many different breeds of dog.
You use dog to refer to a male dog, or to the male of some related species such as wolves or foxes.
If someone calls a man a dog, they strongly disapprove of him.
People use dog to refer to something that they consider unsatisfactory or of poor quality.
If someone, especially a man, calls a woman or girl a dog, they mean that she is very ugly, unattractive, or boring.
If problems or injuries dog you, they are with you all the time.
The dogs is a sports meeting where dogs, especially greyhounds, race and people bet on which dog will win.
You describe something as a dog’s breakfast or dog’s dinner in order to express your disapproval of it, for example because it is very untidy, badly organized, or badly done.
You use dog eat dog to express your disapproval of a situation where everyone wants to succeed and is willing to harm other people in order to do so.
If you say that something is going to the dogs, you mean that it is becoming weaker and worse in quality.
If someone tells you to let sleeping dogs lie, they are warning you not to disturb or interfere with a situation, because you are likely to cause trouble and problems.
If you say ’ You can’t teach an old dog new tricks ’, you are suggesting that someone is unwilling to try new ways of doing things.
A doll is a child’s toy which looks like a small person or baby.
A dolphin is a mammal which lives in the sea and looks like a large fish with a pointed mouth.

Chinesesense: (尤指某人有控制力、影响力或权利的)领域，范围，范畴；
Englishsense: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.
Someone’s domain is the area they own or have control over.
On the Internet, a domain is a set of addresses that shows, for example, the category or geographical area that an Internet address belongs to.
A dome is a round roof.
A dome is any object that has a similar shape to a dome.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 喜爱家庭生活的;乐于操持家务的；
非野生的;驯养的;作为宠物饲养的；
Englishsense: Domestic political activities, events, and situations happen or exist within one particular country.
Domestic duties and activities are concerned with the running of a home and family.
Domestic items and services are intended to be used in people’s homes rather than in factories or offices.
A domestic situation or atmosphere is one which involves a family and their home.
Someone who is domestic enjoys being at home and running a family.
A domestic animal is one that is not wild and is kept either on a farm to produce food or in someone’s home as a pet.
A domestic, a domestic help, or a domestic worker is a person who is paid to come to help with the work that has to be done in a house such as the cleaning, washing, and ironing.
The dominance of a particular person or thing is the fact that they are more powerful, successful, or important than other people or things.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 占支配或统治地位的;占优势的;显著的；
Englishsense: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.
A dominant gene is one that produces a particular characteristic, whether a person has only one of these genes from one parent, or two genes, one from each parent.

Chinesesense: 在…中占首要地位，在…中最具影响力；
Englishsense: To dominate a situation means to be the most powerful or important person or thing in it.
If one country or person dominates another, they have power over them.
If a building, mountain, or other object dominates an area, it is so large or impressive that you cannot avoid seeing it.

Chinesesense: (英国牛津或剑桥大学的)讲师，教师；
Englishsense: If you don clothing, you put it on.
A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge University in England.
If you donate something to a charity or other organization, you give it to them.
If you donate your blood or a part of your body, you allow doctors to use it to help someone who is ill.
A donation is something which someone gives to a charity or other organization.
A donkey is an animal which is like a horse but which is smaller and has longer ears.
For donkey’syears means for a very long time.
A donor is someone who gives a part of their body or some of their blood to be used by doctors to help a person who is ill.
Donor organs or parts are organs or parts of the body which people allow doctors to use to help people who are ill.
A donor is a person or organization who gives something, especially money, to a charity, organization, or country that needs it.
Doom is a terrible future state or event which you cannot prevent.
If you have a sense or feeling of doom, you feel that things are going very badly and are likely to get even worse.
If a fact or event dooms someone or something to a particular fate, it makes certain that they are going to suffer in some way.

Chinesesense: (商店、宾馆、戏院等的)进口，入口；
偷偷摸摸地;背地里地;不正当地；
不再想;不再做;拒…于门外；
通常指难以成功的领域中迈向目标的第一步，成功的开端；
拒绝同…谈话;拒绝向…透露信息；
介绍(新思想或新情况);使…成为可能；
Englishsense: A door is a piece of wood, glass, or metal, which is moved to open and close the entrance to a building, room, cupboard, or vehicle.
A door is the space in a wall when a door is open.
The door is the entrance to a large building such as a shop, hotel, or theatre.
Doors is used in expressions such as a few doors down or three doors up to refer to a place that is a particular number of buildings away from where you are.
When you answer the door, you go and open the door because a visitor has knocked on it or rung the bell.
If you say that someone gets or does something by the back door or through the back door, you are criticizing them for doing it secretly and unofficially.
If someone closes the door on something, they stop thinking about it or dealing with it.
If people have talks and discussions behind closed doors, they have them in private because they want them to be kept secret.
If someone goes from door to door or goes door to door, they go along a street calling at each house in turn, for example selling something.
If you talk about a distance or journey from door to door or door to door, you are talking about the distance from the place where the journey starts to the place where it finishes.

If you say that something helps someone to get their foot in the door or their toe in the door, you mean that it gives them an opportunity to start doing something new, usually in an area that is difficult to succeed in.
If someone shuts the door in your face or slams the door in your face, they refuse to talk to you or give you any information.
If you lay something at someone’s door, you blame them for an unpleasant event or situation.
If someone or something opens the door to a good new idea or situation, they introduce it or make it possible.
When you are out of doors, you are not inside a building, but in the open air.
If you see someone to the door, you go to the door with a visitor when they leave.
If someone shows you the door, they ask you to leave because they are angry with you.
A doorway is a space in a wall where a door opens and closes.
A doorway is a covered space just outside the door of a building.
A dorm is the same as a dormitory.

Chinesesense: (尤指数量很多的)一份，一次，一点；
Englishsense: A dose of medicine or a drug is a measured amount of it which is intended to be taken at one time.
You can refer to an amount of something as a dose of that thing, especially when you want to emphasize that there is a great deal of it.
If you dose a person or animal with medicine, you give them an amount of it.

Chinesesense: (因距离远而看起来)似小点之物，点状物；
散布于;星罗棋布于;遍布；
(在耗时且无关紧要的事情上)一丝不苟，注重细节；
Englishsense: A dot is a very small round mark, for example one that is used as the top part of the letter ’i’, as a full stop, or as a decimal point.
You can refer to something that you can see in the distance and that looks like a small round mark as a dot.
When things dot a place or an area, they are scattered or spread all over it.
If you arrive somewhere or do something on the dot, you arrive there or do it at exactly the time that you were supposed to.

If you say that someone dots the i’s and crosses the t’s, you mean that they pay great attention to every small detail in a task; often used to express your annoyance because such detailed work seems unnecessary and takes a very long time.
The year dot is used to mean a very long time ago.

Chinesesense: (用于单数名词前)两个的，双重的；
加倍的;双料的;可容纳两个的；
(用于单词拼写或数字中)两个的；
Englishsense: You use double to indicate that something includes or is made of two things of the same kind.
You use double before a singular noun to refer to two things of the same type that occur together, or that are connected in some way.
If something is double the amount or size of another thing, it is twice as large.
You use double to describe something which is twice the normal size or can hold twice the normal quantity of something.
A double room is a room intended for two people, usually a couple, to stay or live in.
A double bed is a bed that is wide enough for two people to sleep in.
You use double to describe a drink that is twice the normal measure.
Double is used when you are spelling a word or telling someone a number to show that a letter or digit is repeated.
When something doubles or when you double it, it becomes twice as great in number, amount, or size.
If you refer to someone as a person’s double, you mean that they look exactly like them.
If a person or thing doubles as someone or something else, they have a second job or purpose as well as their main one.
In tennis or badminton, when people play doubles, two teams consisting of two players on each team play against each other on the same court.
If you do something at the double or on the double, you do it very quickly or immediately.
When you bend double, you bend the top half of your body downwards a long way.
If you are bent double, the top half of your body is bent downwards so that your head is close to your knees.
If you are seeing double, there is something wrong with your eyes, and you can see two images instead of one.

Chinesesense: 不能肯定;认为…未必可能；
怀疑，不相信某人或某人的话；
可疑的;不确定的;不可靠的；
Englishsense: If you have doubt or doubts about something, you feel uncertain about it and do not know whether it is true or possible. If you say you have no doubt about it, you mean that you are certain it is true.
If you doubt whether something is true or possible, you believe that it is probably not true or possible.
If you doubt something, you believe that it might not be true or genuine.
If you doubt someone or doubt their word, you think that they may not be telling the truth.
You say that something is beyond doubt or beyond reasonable doubt when you are certain that it is true and it cannot be contradicted or disproved.
If you are in doubt about something, you feel unsure or uncertain about it.
You say I doubt it as a response to a question or statement about something that you think is untrue or unlikely.
If you say that something is in doubt or open to doub t, you consider it to be uncertain or unreliable.
You use no doubt to emphasize that something seems certain or very likely to you.
You use no doubt to indicate that you accept the truth of a particular point, but that you do not consider it is important or contradicts the rest of what you are saying.
If you say that something is true without doubt or without a doubt, you are emphasizing that it is definitely true.

Chinesesense: 怀疑的;疑惑的;拿不定主意的；

Englishsense: If it is doubtful that something will happen, it seems unlikely to happen or you are uncertain whether it will happen.
If you are doubtful about something, you feel unsure or uncertain about it.
If you say that something is of doubtful quality or value, you mean that it is of low quality or value.
If a sports player is doubtful for a match or event, he or she seems unlikely to play, usually because of injury.
Dough is a fairly firm mixture of flour, water, and sometimes also fat and sugar. It can be cooked to make bread, pastry, and biscuits.
You can refer to money as dough.
A doughnut is a bread-like cake made from sweet dough that has been cooked in hot fat.
A dove is a bird that looks like a pigeon but is smaller and lighter in colour. Doves are often used as a symbol of peace.
In politics, you can refer to people who support the use of peaceful methods to solve difficult situations as doves.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (尤指往南方或往地势低的地方)往，朝；
已处理的及尚未完成的；
已安排…的;要做…的;将发生…的；
沮丧的;闷闷不乐的;情绪低落的；
(尤指电脑)死机的，发生故障的；
Englishsense: To go down something such as a slope or a pipe means to go towards the ground or to a lower level.
If you are a particular distance down something, you are that distance below the top or surface of it.
You use down to say that you are looking or facing in a direction that is towards the ground or towards a lower level.
If you put something down, you put it onto a surface.
If you go or look down something such as a road or river, you go or look along it. If you are down a road or river, you are somewhere along it.
If you are travelling to a particular place, you can say that you are going down to that place, especially if you are going towards the south or to a lower level of land.
If you are down a place, you are at that place. If you go down a place, you go to that place. Some people consider this to be non-standard.
If an amount of something goes down, it decreases. If an amount of something is down, it has decreased and is at a lower level than it was.
If you say that there are a number of things down and a number to go, you are saying how many of the things have already been dealt with and how many remain to be dealt with.
Down to a particular detail means including everything, even that detail. Down to a particular person means including everyone, even that person.
If you are down to a certain amount of something, you have only that amount left.
If a situation is down to a particular person or thing, it has been caused by that person or thing.
If someone or something is down for a particular thing, it has been arranged that they will do that thing, or that thing will happen.
If you are down with an illness, you have that illness.
If you pay money down on something, you pay part of the money you owe for it.
If people shout ’ down with ’ something or someone, they are saying that they dislike them and want to get rid of them.
If you are feeling down, you are feeling unhappy or depressed.
If something is down on paper, it has been written on the paper.
If a piece of equipment, especially a computer system, is down, it is temporarily not working because of a fault.
If you say that someone downs food or a drink, you mean that they eat or drink it.
If something or someone is downed, they fall to the ground because they have been hurt or damaged in some way.
Down consists of the small, soft feathers on young birds. Down is used to make bed-covers and pillows.
Down is very fine hair.

Chinesesense: 走下坡路地;恶化地;每况愈下；
Englishsense: If something or someone is moving downhill or is downhill, they are moving down a slope or are located towards the bottom of a hill.
If you say that something is going downhill, you mean that it is becoming worse or less successful.
If you say that a task or situation is downhill after a particular stage or time, you mean that it is easy to deal with after that stage or time.
To download data means to transfer it to or from a computer along a line such as a telephone line, a radio link, or a computer network.
The downside of a situation is the aspect of it which is less positive, pleasant, or useful than its other aspects.

Chinesesense: 往楼下;顺楼梯而下;至楼下；
Englishsense: If you go downstairs in a building, you go down a staircase towards the ground floor.
If something or someone is downstairs in a building, they are on the ground floor or on a lower floor than you.
Downstairs means situated on the ground floor of a building or on a lower floor than you are.
The downstairs of a building is its lower floor or floors.
Downtown places are in or towards the centre of a large town or city, where the shops and places of business are.
If there is a downturn in the economy or in a company or industry, it becomes worse or less successful than it had been.

Chinesesense: 趋向没落的;衰退的;局势变坏的；
Englishsense: A downward movement or look is directed towards a lower place or a lower level.
If you refer to a downward trend, you mean that something is decreasing or that a situation is getting worse.
If you have a dozen things, you have twelve of them.
You can refer to a group of approximately twelve things or people as a dozen. You can refer to a group of approximately six things or people as half a dozen.
If you refer to dozens of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

Chinesesense: 通常指短期的征兵，征召；
Englishsense: A draft is an early version of a letter, book, or speech.
When you draft a letter, book, or speech, you write the first version of it.
If you are drafted, you are ordered to serve in the armed forces, usually for a limited period of time.
If people are drafted into a place, they are moved there to do a particular job.
The draft is the practice of ordering people to serve in the armed forces, usually for a limited period of time.
A draft is a written order for payment of money by a bank, especially from one bank to another.

Chinesesense: (电脑操作中)用鼠标拖动，用鼠标改变尺寸或形状；
用网(或钩子)搜索(河或湖底)；
(时间)过得很慢;活动单调乏味地进行，拖沓地进行；
令人不快的事;无聊的事；
(物体在空气或液体中移动时所受到的)阻力，抗力；
Englishsense: If you drag something, you pull it along the ground, often with difficulty.
To drag a computer image means to use the mouse to move the position of the image on the screen, or to change its size or shape.
If someone drags you somewhere, they pull you there, or force you to go there by physically threatening you.
If someone drags you somewhere you do not want to go, they make you go there.
If you say that you drag yourself somewhere, you are emphasizing that you have to make a very great effort to go there.
If you drag your foot or your leg behind you, you walk with great difficulty because your foot or leg is injured in some way.
If the police drag a river or lake, they pull nets or hooks across the bottom of it in order to look for something.
If a period of time or an event drags, it is very boring and seems to last a long time.
If something is a drag on the development or progress of something, it slows it down or makes it more difficult.
If you say that something is a drag, you mean that it is unpleasant or very dull.
If you take a drag on a cigarette or pipe that you are smoking, you take in air through it. [oft N on n] [Informal]
Drag is the resistance to the movement that is experienced by something that is moving through air or through a fluid.
Drag is the wearing of women’s clothes by a male entertainer.
If you drag your feet or drag your heels, you delay doing something or do it very slowly because you do not want to do it.

Chinesesense: 龙(故事和传说中有翼有爪且会喷火的动物)；
Englishsense: In stories and legends, a dragon is an animal like a big lizard. It has wings and claws, and breathes out fire.
If someone calls a woman, especially an older woman, a dragon, they mean that she is fierce and unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 使精疲力竭;使心力交瘁；
(金钱或资源的)大量消耗，耗竭，耗费；
Englishsense: If you drain a liquid from a place or object, you remove the liquid by causing it to flow somewhere else. If a liquid drains somewhere, it flows there.
If you drain a place or object, you dry it by causing water to flow out of it. If a place or object drains, water flows out of it until it is dry.
If you drain food or if food drains, you remove the liquid that it has been in, especially after it has been cooked or soaked in water.
A drain is a pipe that carries water or sewage away from a place, or an opening in a surface that leads to the pipe.
If someone drains a glass, they empty it by drinking what is in it.
If the colour or the blood drains or is drained from someone’s face, they become very pale. You can also say that someone’s face drains or is drained of colour.
If a feeling drains or is drained out of you, it gradually becomes less strong until you no longer feel it.
If something drains you, it leaves you feeling physically and emotionally exhausted.
If energy drains or is drained from you, you lose all energy and become very tired.
If you say that something is a drain on an organization’s finances or resources, you mean that it costs the organization a large amount of money, and you do not consider that it is worth it.
If you say that a country’s or a company’s resources or finances are drained, you mean that they are used or spent completely.
If you say that something is going down the drain, you mean that it is being destroyed or wasted.
If you say that a business is going down the drain, you mean that it is failing financially.
Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

Chinesesense: 戏剧;戏剧艺术;戏剧事业；
戏剧性事件;戏剧性情节；
Englishsense: A drama is a serious play for the theatre, television, or radio.
You use drama to refer to plays in general or to work that is connected with plays and the theatre, such as acting or producing.
You can refer to a real situation which is exciting or distressing as drama.

Chinesesense: 突如其来的;急剧的;引人注目的；
激动人心的;引人注目的;令人印象深刻的；
戏剧的;有关戏剧的;戏剧学的；
Englishsense: A dramatic change or event happens suddenly and is very noticeable and surprising.
A dramatic action, event, or situation is exciting and impressive.
You use dramatic to describe things connected with or relating to the theatre, drama, or plays.

Chinesesense: 将(身体的某部位)随意搭在…上；
Englishsense: If you drape a piece of cloth somewhere, you place it there so that it hangs down in a casual and graceful way.
If someone or something is draped in a piece of cloth, they are loosely covered by it.
If you drape a part of your body somewhere, you lay it there in a relaxed and graceful way.
Drapes are pieces of heavy fabric that you hang from the top of a window and can close to keep the light out or stop people looking in.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you have to take drastic action in order to solve a problem, you have to do something extreme and basic to solve it.
A drastic change is a very great change.

Chinesesense: 拔出，抽出，掏出(枪、刀等武器)；
(在比赛等中)抽签;(在摸彩中)抽奖；
作(比较或对比)；加以(区别)；
使倾心;使动心;强烈吸引；
使回答;使透露消息;使说出意见；
Englishsense: When you draw, or when you draw something, you use a pencil or pen to produce a picture, pattern, or diagram.
When a vehicle draws somewhere, it moves there smoothly and steadily.
If you draw somewhere, you move there slowly.
If you draw something or someone in a particular direction, you move them in that direction, usually by pulling them gently.
When you draw a curtain or blind, you pull it across a window, either to cover or to uncover it.
If someone draws a gun, knife, or other weapon, they pull it out of its container and threaten you with it.
If an animal or vehicle draws something such as a cart, carriage, or another vehicle, it pulls it along.
If you draw a deep breath, you breathe in deeply once.
If you draw on a cigarette, you breathe the smoke from it into your mouth or lungs.
To draw something such as water or energy from a particular source means to take it from that source.
If something that hits you or presses part of your body draws blood, it cuts your skin so that it bleeds. [V n]
If you draw money out of a bank, building society, or savings account, you get it from the account so that you can use it.
If you draw a salary or a sum of money, you receive a sum of money regularly.
To draw something means to choose it or to be given it, as part of a competition, game, or lottery.
A draw is a competition where people pay money for numbered or named tickets, then some of those tickets are chosen, and the owners are given prizes.
To draw something from a particular thing or place means to take or get it from that thing or place.
If you draw a particular conclusion, you decide that that conclusion is true.
If you draw a comparison, parallel, or distinction, you compare or contrast two different ideas, systems, or other things.
If you draw someone’s attention to something, you make them aware of it or make them think about it.
If someone or something draws a particular reaction, people react to it in that way.
If something such as a film or an event draws a lot of people, it is so interesting or entertaining that a lot of people go to it.
If someone or something draws you, it attracts you very strongly. [V n] [V n to n]
If someone will not be drawn or refuses to be drawn, they will not reply to questions in the way that you want them to, or will not reveal information or their opinion.
In a game or competition, if one person or team draws with another one, or if two people or teams draw, they have the same number of points or goals at the end of the game.
When an event or period of time draws to a close or draws to an end, it finishes.
If an event or period of time is drawing closer or is drawing nearer, it is approaching.
A drawback is an aspect of something or someone that makes them less acceptable than they would otherwise be.
A drawer is part of a desk, chest, or other piece of furniture that is shaped like a box and is designed for putting things in. You pull it towards you to open it.
Drawers are underpants, especially ones worn by women.
A drawing is a picture made with a pencil or pen.

Chinesesense: 恼火的;生气的;不想要的；
Englishsense: If you dread something which may happen, you feel very anxious and unhappy about it because you think it will be unpleasant or upsetting.
Dread is a feeling of great anxiety and fear about something that may happen.
Dread means terrible and greatly feared.
You can use dread to describe something that you, or a particular group of people, find annoying or undesirable.
If you say that you dread to think what might happen, you mean that you are anxious about it because it is likely to be very unpleasant.
