Chinesesense: 糟糕透顶的;令人不快的;劣质的；
(看上去或感觉到)病得不轻的,极度疲惫的,非常沮丧的；
Englishsense: If you say that something is dreadful, you mean that it is very bad or unpleasant, or very poor in quality.
Dreadful is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something bad.
If someone looks or feels dreadful, they look or feel very ill, tired, or upset.

Chinesesense: 理想的;梦幻般的;完美的；
理想;夙愿;梦寐以求的事物；
梦幻般地;美妙地;完美地；
强调极为奇怪或完全不可能再怎么想也；
超出想象的;比希望中要好的；
Englishsense: A dream is an imaginary series of events that you experience in your mind while you are asleep.
When you dream, you experience imaginary events in your mind while you are asleep.
You can refer to a situation or event as a dream if you often think about it because you would like it to happen.
If you often think about something that you would very much like to happen or have, you can say that you dream of it.
You can use dream to describe something that you think is ideal or perfect, especially if it is something that you thought you would never be able to have or experience.
If you describe something as a particular person’s dream, you think that it would be ideal for that person and that he or she would like it very much.
If you say that something is a dream, you mean that it is wonderful.
You can refer to a situation or event that does not seem real as a dream, especially if it is very strange or unpleasant.
If you say that you would not dream of doing something, you are emphasizing that you would never do it because you think it is wrong or is not possible or suitable for you.
If you say that you never dreamed that something would happen, you are emphasizing that you did not think that it would happen because it seemed very unlikely.
If you tell someone to dream on, you mean that something they are hoping for is unlikely to happen.
If you say that you are in a dream, you mean that you do not concentrate properly on what you are doing because you are thinking about other things.
If you say that someone does something like a dream, you think that they do it very well. If you say that something happens like a dream, you mean that it happens successfully without any problems.
If you describe someone or something as the person or thing of your dreams, you mean that you consider them to be ideal or perfect.
If you say that you could not imagine a particular thing in your wildest dreams, you are emphasizing that you think it is extremely strange or unlikely.
If you describe something as being beyond your wildest dreams, you are emphasizing that it is better than you could have imagined or hoped for.

Chinesesense: (在烹饪前)清洗,加工处理(鸡、鱼或肉类)；
Englishsense: A dress is a piece of clothing worn by a woman or girl. It covers her body and part of her legs.
You can refer to clothes worn by men or women as dress.
When you dress or dress yourself, you put on clothes.
If you dress someone, for example a child, you put clothes on them. See usage note at: wear
If someone dresses in a particular way, they wear clothes of a particular style or colour.
If you dress for something, you put on special clothes for it.
When someone dresses a wound, they clean it and cover it.
If you dress a salad, you cover it with a mixture of oil, vinegar, and herbs or flavourings.
To dress meat, chicken, or fish means to prepare it for cooking by cleaning it and removing the parts that you cannot eat.

Chinesesense: (通常指用来存放瓷器的)碗橱,餐具柜；
(剧院中协助演员穿戏服的)换装师,服装师；
Englishsense: A dresser is a chest of drawers, usually with a mirror on the top.
A dresser is a piece of furniture which has cupboards or drawers in the lower part and shelves in the top part. It is usually used for storing china.
A dresser is someone who works in a theatre and helps the actors and actresses to dress.
You can use dresser to refer to the kind of clothes that a person wears. For example, if you say that someone is a smart dresser, you mean that they wear smart clothes.

Chinesesense: (用油、醋、香料等制成的,拌色拉用的)调料；
Englishsense: A salad dressing is a mixture of oil, vinegar, and herbs or flavourings, which you pour over salad.
A dressing is a covering that is put on a wound to protect it while it heals.
Dried food or milk has had all the water removed from it so that it will last for a long time.

Chinesesense: 无意间进入;不知不觉陷入；
移动;动向;趋势;逐渐变化；
Englishsense: When something drifts somewhere, it is carried there by the movement of wind or water.
If someone or something drifts into a situation, they get into that situation in a way that is not planned or controlled.
If you say that someone drifts around, you mean that they travel from place to place without a plan or settled way of life.
A drift is a movement away from somewhere or something, or a movement towards somewhere or something different.
To drift somewhere means to move there slowly or gradually.
If sounds drift somewhere, they can be heard but they are not very loud.
If snow drifts, it builds up into piles as a result of the movement of the wind.
A drift is a mass of snow that has built up into a pile as a result of the movement of wind.
A drift of something is an amount of it that has been created by the movement of wind or water.
The drift of an argument or speech is the general point that is being made in it.

Chinesesense: (尤指士兵进行的)练习,训练,操练；
(为在危急情况下逃生而进行的)常规训练,演习；
Englishsense: A drill is a tool or machine that you use for making holes.
When you drill into something or drill a hole in something, you make a hole in it using a drill.
When people drill for oil or water, they search for it by drilling deep holes in the ground or in the bottom of the sea.
A drill is a way that teachers teach their students something by making them repeat it many times.
If you drill people, you teach them to do something by making them repeat it many times.
A drill is repeated training for a group of people, especially soldiers, so that they can do something quickly and efficiently.
A drill is a routine exercise or activity, in which people practise what they should do in dangerous situations.
Drill is thick cotton material which is used for making uniforms and trousers.
A drill is a long line in the earth, a few centimetres deep, which a farmer or gardener makes to plant seeds in.

Chinesesense: 酒(如啤酒、葡萄酒或威士忌)；
醉得不省人事;烂醉如泥;酩酊大醉；
比…更能喝酒;酒量比…大;灌醉；
Englishsense: When you drink a liquid, you take it into your mouth and swallow it.
To drink means to drink alcohol.
A drink is an amount of a liquid which you drink.
A drink is an alcoholic drink.
Drink is alcohol, such as beer, wine, or whisky.
If you drink yourself into a stupor or drink yourself into oblivion, you drink so much alcohol that you lose consciousness or fall deeply asleep.
If someone drinks you under the table, they drink more alcohol than you are able to on a particular occasion.
If someone takes to drink, they start to drink a lot of alcohol regularly, usually because they are depressed or worried about something.
People say ’ I’ll drink to that ’ to show that they agree with and approve of something that someone has just said.

Chinesesense: 喜欢饮酒的;经常饮酒的;贪杯的；
Englishsense: Someone’s drinking friends or companions are people they regularly drink alcohol with.
When liquid drips somewhere, or you drip it somewhere, it falls in individual small drops.
When something drips, drops of liquid fall from it.
A drip is a small individual drop of a liquid.
A drip is a piece of medical equipment by which a liquid is slowly passed through a tube into a patient’s blood.
If you say that something is dripping with a particular thing, you mean that it contains a lot of that thing.
If you call someone a drip, you mean that they are rather stupid and lacking in enthusiasm or energy.

Chinesesense: (从马路通往住宅的宽阔)车道；
(风、雨或雪朝某个方向)吹,卷,刮,冲；
驱使，迫使(某人做出极端的事情)；
强烈欲望;强烈需求;本能需求；
(为达到某目的而进行的)努力,运动；
Englishsense: When you drive somewhere, you operate a car or other vehicle and control its movement and direction.
If you drive someone somewhere, you take them there in a car or other vehicle.
A drive is a journey in a car or other vehicle.
A drive is a wide piece of hard ground, or sometimes a private road, that leads from the road to a person’s house.
If something drives a machine, it supplies the power that makes it work.
Drive is the power supplied by the engine to particular wheels in a car or other vehicle to make the vehicle move.
You use drive to refer to the mechanical part of a computer which reads the data on disks and tapes, or writes data onto them.
If you drive something such as a nail into something else, you push it in or hammer it in using a lot of effort.
In games such as cricket, golf, or football, if a player drives a ball somewhere, they kick or hit it there with a lot of force.
In golf, a drive is the first stroke a player makes from the tee.
If the wind, rain, or snow drives in a particular direction, it moves with great force in that direction.
If you drive people or animals somewhere, you make them go to or from that place.
To drive someone into a particular state or situation means to force them into that state or situation.
The desire or feeling that drives a person to do something, especially something extreme, is the desire or feeling that causes them to do it.
If you say that someone has drive, you mean they have energy and determination.
A drive is a very strong need or desire in human beings that makes them act in particular ways.
A drive is a special effort made by a group of people for a particular purpose.
Drive is used in the names of some streets.
If you ask someone what they are driving at, you are asking what they are trying to say or what they are saying indirectly.
The driver of a vehicle is the person who is driving it.
A driver is a computer program that controls a device such as a printer.
A driveway is a piece of hard ground that leads from the road to the front of a house or other building.

Chinesesense: 推动的;推进的;强有力的；
Englishsense: The driving force or idea behind something that happens or is done is the main thing that has a strong effect on it and makes it happen or be done in a particular way.

Chinesesense: 中途放下某人;中途卸下某物；
(水果味或巧克力味的)糖豆，糖果粒；
落差;垂直距离;下降距离；
(常指因不喜欢而让别人)终止谈论，不要谈论，谈到此为止；
Englishsense: If a level or amount drops or if someone or something drops it, it quickly becomes less.
If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.
If something drops onto something else, it falls onto that thing. If something drops from somewhere, it falls from that place.
If you drop something somewhere or if it drops there, you deliberately let it fall there.
If a person or a part of their body drops to a lower position, or if they drop a part of their body to a lower position, they move to that position, often in a tired and lifeless way.
To drop is used in expressions such as to be about to drop and to dance until you drop to emphasize that you are exhausted and can no longer continue doing something.
If a man drops his trousers, he pulls them down, usually as a joke or to be rude.
If your voice drops or if you drop your voice, you speak more quietly.
If you drop someone or something somewhere, you take them somewhere and leave them there, usually in a car or other vehicle.
If you drop an idea, course of action, or habit, you do not continue with it.
If someone is dropped by a sports team or organization, they are no longer included in that team or employed by that organization.
If you drop a game or part of a game in a sports competition, you lose it.
If you drop to a lower position in a sports competition, you move to that position.
A drop of a liquid is a very small amount of it shaped like a little ball. In informal English, you can also use drop when you are referring to a very small amount of something such as a drink.
Drops are a kind of medicine which you put drop by drop into your ears, eyes, or nose.
Fruit or chocolate drops are small round sweets with a fruit or chocolate flavour.
You use drop to talk about vertical distances. For example, a thirty-foot drop is a distance of thirty feet between the top of a cliff or wall and the bottom of it.
If you drop a hint, you give a hint or say something in a casual way.
If you want someone to drop the subject, drop it, or let it drop, you want them to stop talking about something, often because you are annoyed that they keep talking about it.

Chinesesense: 离经叛道者;摈弃社会习俗者；
退学的;辍学的;中途放弃的；
Englishsense: If you describe someone as a drop-out, you disapprove of the fact that they have rejected the accepted ways of society, for example by not having a regular job.
A drop-out is someone who has left school or college before they have finished their studies.
If you refer to the drop-out rate, you are referring to the number of people who leave a school or college early, or leave a course or other activity before they have finished it.
A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls.

Chinesesense: 淹没[于…中]; 置身于…中；
Englishsense: When someone drowns or is drowned, they die because they have gone or been pushed under water and cannot breathe.
If you say that a person or thing is drowning in something, you are emphasizing that they have a very large amount of it, or are completely covered in it.
If something drowns a sound, it is so loud that you cannot hear that sound properly.
If you say that someone is drowning their sorrows, you mean that they are drinking alcohol in order to forget something sad or upsetting that has happened to them.

Chinesesense: 往食物或饮料中投放麻醉药；
Englishsense: A drug is a chemical which is given to people in order to treat or prevent an illness or disease.
Drugs are substances that some people take because of their pleasant effects, but which are usually illegal.
If you drug a person or animal, you give them a chemical substance in order to make them sleepy or unconscious.
If food or drink is drugged, a chemical substance is added to it in order to make someone sleepy or unconscious when they eat or drink it.

Chinesesense: (美国兼售化妆品、家居用品、饮料、小吃等的)药店,药房；
Englishsense: In the United States, a drugstore is a shop where drugs and medicines are sold or given out, and where you can buy cosmetics, some household goods, and also drinks and snacks. See usage note at: chemist

Chinesesense: 缠绕电线或绳索的卷筒,转筒；
有规律地敲击使发出连续的击打声；
Englishsense: A drum is a musical instrument consisting of a skin stretched tightly over a round frame. You play a drum by beating it with sticks or with your hands.
A drum is a large cylindrical container which is used to store fuel or other substances.
A drum is a hollow cylindrical structure which is part of a machine, for example a washing machine.
A drum is a circular object on which wire or rope is wound and kept.
If something drums on a surface, or if you drum something on a surface, it hits it regularly, making a continuous beating sound.
If someone beats the drum or bangs the drum for something, they support it strongly.
A drummer is a person who plays a drum or drums in a band or group.

If you are drunk with a strong emotion or an experience, you are in a state of great excitement because of it.

Englishsense: If something is dry, there is no water or moisture on it or in it.
When something dries or when you dry it, it becomes dry.
When you dry the dishes after a meal, you wipe the water off the plates, cups, knives, pans, and other things when they have been washed, using a cloth.
If you say that your skin or hair is dry, you mean that it is less oily than, or not as soft as, normal.
If the weather or a period of time is dry, there is no rain or there is much less rain than average.
A dry place or climate is one that gets very little rainfall.
In the dry means in a place or at a time that is not damp, wet, or rainy.
If a river, lake, or well is dry, it is empty of water, usually because of hot weather and lack of rain.
If an oil well is dry, it is no longer producing any oil.
If you are dry, you need to drink something.
If your mouth or throat is dry, it has little or no saliva in it, and so feels very unpleasant, perhaps because you are tense or ill.
A dry cough is one that does not produce any mucus.
If someone has dry eyes, there are no tears in their eyes; often used with negatives or in contexts where you are expressing surprise that they are not crying.
If a country, state, or city is dry, it has laws or rules which forbid anyone to drink, sell, or buy alcoholic drink.
If you say that someone is sucking something dry or milking it dry, you are criticizing them for taking all the good things from it until there is nothing left.
Dry humour is very amusing, but in a subtle and clever way.
If you describe a voice as dry, you mean that it is cold or dull, and does not express any emotions.
If you describe something such as a book, play, or activity as dry, you mean that it is dull and uninteresting.
Dry bread or toast is plain and not covered with butter or jam.
Dry sherry or wine does not have a sweet taste.
If a river, lake, or well dries up, it becomes empty of water, usually because of hot weather and a lack of rain.
If a supply of something dries up, it stops.
If you dry up when you are speaking, you stop in the middle of what you were saying, because you cannot think what to say next.
A dryer is a machine for drying things. There are different kinds of dryer, for examples ones designed for drying clothes, crops, or people’s hair or hands.
Dual means having two parts, functions, or aspects.
If someone or something is dubbed a particular thing, they are given that description or name.
If a film or soundtrack in a foreign language is dubbed, a new soundtrack is added with actors giving a translation.

Englishsense: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.
If you are dubious about something, you are not completely sure about it and have not yet made up your mind about it.

If you say that someone has the dubious honour or the dubious pleasure of doing something, you are indicating that what they are doing is not an honour or pleasure at all, but is, in fact, unpleasant or bad.

Chinesesense: 急速低头或弓身(以免被打中或看见)；
(快速低头或弓身以)躲闪,闪避；
逃避,回避,推脱,推诿(义务或责任)；

很自然地就会;轻而易举;如鱼得水；
Englishsense: A duck is a very common water bird with short legs, a short neck, and a large flat beak.
A duck is a female duck. The male is called a drake.
If you duck, you move your head or the top half of your body quickly downwards to avoid something that might hit you, or to avoid being seen.
If you duck something such as a blow, you avoid it by moving your head or body quickly downwards.
If you duck into a place, you move there quickly, often in an attempt to avoid danger or to avoid being seen.
You say that someone ducks a duty or responsibility when you disapprove of the fact that they avoid it.
If someone ducks someone else, they force them or their head under water for a short time.
Some people call other people duck or ducks as a sign of affection.
You say that criticism is like water off a duck’s back or water off a duck’s back to emphasize that it is not having any effect on the person being criticized.
If you take to something like a duck to water, you discover that you are naturally good at it or that you find it very easy to do.

Chinesesense: (输送液体或气体的)管道,管子；
(人体内输送泪水、胆汁等的)导管；
Englishsense: A duct is a pipe, tube, or channel which carries a liquid or gas.
A duct is a tube in your body which carries a liquid such as tears or bile.
A dude is a man.

Chinesesense: 由于,因为(构成原因状语,有些英语国家的人认为该用法不正确)；
到期的;预期的;预定到达的；
应有的;应得的;应得到的；
(期待很长时间后)预期应得的,预计应到的；
在适当的时候;到一定的时候；
给…以应有的评价;公道地对待…；
Englishsense: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.
You can say due to to introduce the reason for something happening. Some speakers of English believe that it is not correct to use due to in this way.
If something is due at a particular time, it is expected to happen, be done, or arrive at that time.
Due attention or consideration is the proper, reasonable, or deserved amount of it under the circumstances.
Something that is due, or that is due to someone, is owed to them, either as a debt or because they have a right to it.
If someone is due for something, that thing is planned to happen or be given to them now, or very soon, often after they have been waiting for it for a long time.
Dues are sums of money that you give regularly to an organization that you belong to, for example a social club or trade union, in order to pay for being a member.
Due is used before the words ’north’, ’south’, ’east’, or ’west’ to indicate that something is in exactly the direction mentioned.
If you say that something will happen or take place in due course, you mean that you cannot make it happen any quicker and it will happen when the time is right for it.
You can say ’ to give him his due ’, or ’ giving him his due ’ when you are admitting that there are some good things about someone, even though there are things that you do not like about them.

使不强烈;使变得无光泽;使无生气；
Englishsense: If you describe someone or something as dull, you mean they are not interesting or exciting.
Someone or something that is dull is not very lively or energetic.
A dull colour or light is not bright.
You say the weather is dull when it is very cloudy.
Dull sounds are not very clear or loud.
Dull feelings are weak and not intense.
If a knife or blade is dull, it is not sharp.
If something dulls or if it is dulled, it becomes less intense, bright, or lively.

An egg is a cell that is produced in the bodies of female animals and humans. If it is fertilized by a sperm, a baby develops from it.

If someone has egg on their face or has egg all over their face, they have been made to look foolish.
Someone’s ego is their sense of their own worth. For example, if someone has a large ego, they think they are very important and valuable.

The Egyptians were the people who lived in ancient Egypt.

You can use either to introduce a noun that refers to each of two things when you are talking about both of them.

You use expressions such as to what extent, to that extent, or to the extent that when you are discussing how true a statement is, or in what ways it is true.

External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.
External means involving or intended for foreign countries.
External means happening or existing in the world in general and affecting you in some way.
External experts, for example external examiners, come into an organization from outside in order to do a particular job fairly and impartially, or to check that a particular job was done properly.
If medicine is for external use, it is intended to be used only on the outside of your body, and not to be eaten or drunk.

The extinction of a species of animal or plant is the death of all its remaining living members.

Extras are additional amounts of money that are added to the price that you have to pay for something.
Extras are things which are not necessary in a situation, activity, or object, but which make it more comfortable, useful, or enjoyable.
The extras in a film are the people who play unimportant parts, for example as members of a crowd.

If you extract a particular piece of information, you obtain it from a larger amount or source of information.

Englishsense: Your eyes are the parts of your body with which you see.
If you eye someone or something in a particular way, you look at them carefully in that way.
You use eye when you are talking about a person’s ability to judge things or about the way in which they are considering or dealing with things.
An electric eye or infrared eye is a device which can recognize the presence of people or objects by detecting the light or heat coming from them.
People sometimes talk about the eye of the camera when they are talking about something being filmed or photographed, or the way something appears in a photograph or film.
An eye on a potato is one of the dark spots from which new stems grow.
An eye is a small metal loop which a hook fits into, as a fastening on a piece of clothing.
The eye of a needle is the small hole at one end which the thread passes through.
The eye of a storm, tornado, or hurricane is the centre of it.

If you say that something happens before your eyes, in front of your eyes, or under your eyes, you are emphasizing that it happens where you can see it clearly and often implying that it is surprising or unpleasant.
If you cast your eye or run your eye over something, you look at it or read it quickly.
If something catches your eye, you suddenly notice it.
If you catch someone’s eye, you do something to attract their attention, so that you can speak to them.
To clap eyes on someone or something, or set or lay eyes on them, means to see them.

If you make eye contact with someone, you look at them at the same time as they look at you, so that you are both aware that you are looking at each other. If you avoid eye contact with someone, you deliberately do not look straight at them because you feel awkward or embarrassed.
If you close your eyes to something bad or if you shut your eyes to it, you ignore it.
If you cry your eyes out, you cry very hard.

You say ’ an eye for an eye ’ or ’ an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth ’ to refer to the idea that people should be punished according to the way in which they offended, for example if they hurt someone, they should be hurt equally badly in return.
If there is something as far as the eye can see, there is a lot of it and you cannot see anything else beyond it.
If you say that someone has an eye for something, you mean that they are good at noticing it or making judgments about it.
You use expressions such as in his eyes or to her eyes to indicate that you are reporting someone’s opinion and that other people might think differently.
If you keep your eyes open or keep an eye out for someone or something, you watch for them carefully.
If you tell someone to keep their eyes peeled for something, you are telling them to watch very carefully for it.
If you keep an eye on something or someone, you watch them carefully, for example to make sure that they are satisfactory or safe, or not causing trouble.
If you make eyes at someone, you look at them in a way which shows that you find them attractive and which is intended to get their attention.
You say ’ there’s more to this than meets the eye ’ when you think a situation is not as simple as it seems to be.
If something, especially something surprising or impressive, meets your eyes, you see it.
If you say that all eyes are on something or that the eyes of the world are on something, you mean that everyone is paying careful attention to it and what will happen.
If someone has their eye on you, they are watching you carefully to see what you do.
If you have your eye on something, you want to have it.
If you say that you did something with your eyes open or with your eyes wide open, you mean that you knew about the problems and difficulties that you were likely to have.
If something opens your eyes, it makes you aware that something is different from the way that you thought it was.
If you see eye to eye with someone, you agree with them and have the same opinions and views.
If you say that someone or something is at the eye of the storm, you mean they are the main subject of a public disagreement.
When you take your eyes off the thing you have been watching or looking at, you stop looking at it.
If someone sees or considers something through your eyes, they consider it in the way that you do, from your point of view.
If you say that you are up to your eyes in something, you are emphasizing that you have a lot of it to deal with, and often that you are very busy.

Chinesesense: 竖起眉毛表示吃惊或反对；
Englishsense: Your eyebrows are the lines of hair which grow above your eyes.
If something causes you to raise an eyebrow or to raise your eyebrows, it causes you to feel surprised or disapproving.
An eyewitness is a person who was present at an event and can therefore describe it, for example in a law court.
Fabric is cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. Fabrics are used for making things such as clothes, curtains, and sheets.
The fabric of a society or system is its basic structure, with all the customs and beliefs that make it work successfully.
The fabric of a building is its walls, roof, and the materials with which it is built.

Englishsense: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

Englishsense: The facade of a building, especially a large one, is its front wall or the wall that faces the street.
A facade is an outward appearance which is deliberately false and gives you a wrong impression about someone or something.

(地区、机构或活动领域的)外观，面貌；

Englishsense: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.
If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.
The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it.
The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time.
If you say that the face of an area, institution, or field of activity is changing, you mean its appearance or nature is changing.
If you refer to something as the particular face of an activity, belief, or system, you mean that it is one particular aspect of it, in contrast to other aspects.

If you lose face, you do something which makes you appear weak and makes people respect or admire you less. If you do something in order to save face, you do it in order to avoid appearing weak and losing people’s respect or admiration.
If something that you have planned blows up in your face, it goes wrong unexpectedly, with the result that you suffer.
If you say that someone can do something until they are blue in the face, you are emphasizing that however much they do it, it will not make any difference.
If someone or something is face down, their face or front points downwards. If they are face up, their face or front points upwards.
You can use the expression ’ on the face of the earth ’ to mean ’in the whole world’, when you are emphasizing a statement that you are making or making a very exaggerated statement.
If you say that something will be wiped off the face of the earth or disappear from the face of the earth, you mean that it will stop existing.
If you come face to face with someone, you meet them and can talk to them or look at them directly.
If you come face to face with a difficulty or reality, you cannot avoid it and have to deal with it.
If an action or belief flies in the face of accepted ideas or rules, it seems to completely oppose or contradict them.
If you take a particular action or attitude in the face of a problem or difficulty, you respond to that problem or difficulty in that way.
If someone laughs in your face, they are openly disrespectful towards you.
If you have a long face, you look very unhappy or serious.

If you make a face, you show a feeling such as dislike or disgust by putting an exaggerated expression on your face, for example by sticking out your tongue. In British English, you can also say pull a face.
You say on the face of it when you are describing how something seems when it is first considered, in order to suggest that people’s opinion may change when they know or think more about the subject.
If you put a brave face on a bad situation or put on a brave face, you try not to show how disappointed or upset you are about the situation. In American English you can also say put on a good face.
You can say that someone has set their face against something to indicate that they are opposed to it, especially when you want to suggest that they are wrong.
If you show your face somewhere, you go there and see people, although you are not welcome, are rather unwilling to go, or have not been there for some time.
If you manage to keep a straight face, you manage to look serious, although you want to laugh.
If you say something to someone’s face you say it openly in their presence.
If a feeling is written all over your face or is written across your face, it is very obvious to other people from your expression.
If someone or something faces a particular thing, person, or direction, they are positioned opposite them or are looking in that direction.
If you face someone or something, you turn so that you are looking at them.
If you have to face a person or group, you have to stand or sit in front of them and talk to them, although it may be difficult and unpleasant.
If you face or are faced with something difficult or unpleasant, or if it faces you, it is going to affect you and you have to deal with it.

You describe something as fantastic or fantastical when it seems strange and wonderful or unlikely.

You can refer to a story or situation that someone creates from their imagination and that is not based on reality as fantasy.
Fantasy is the activity of imagining things.
Fantasy football, baseball, or another sport is a game in which players choose an imaginary team and score points based on the actual performances of the members of their team in real games.

Englishsense: If one place, thing, or person is far away from another, there is a great distance between them.

If you ask how far a place is, you are asking what distance it is from you or from another place. If you ask how far someone went, you are asking what distance they travelled, or what place they reached.
When there are two things of the same kind in a place, the far one is the one that is a greater distance from you.

You can use far to refer to the part of an area or object that is the greatest distance from the centre in a particular direction. For example, the far north of a country is the part of it that is the greatest distance to the north.
A time or event that is far away in the future or the past is a long time from the present or from a particular point in time.
You can use far to talk about the extent or degree to which something happens or is true.
You can talk about how far someone or something gets to describe the progress that they make.
You can talk about how far a person or action goes to describe the degree to which someone’s behaviour or actions are extreme.
You can use far in expressions like ’ I wouldn’t go that far ’ and ’ I would go so far ’ to indicate to what extent you agree with something.

You can use far to mean ’very much’ when you are comparing two things and emphasizing the difference between them. For example, you can say that something is far better or far worse than something else to indicate that it is very much better or worse. You can also say that something is, for example, far too big to indicate that it is very much too big.
You can describe people with extreme left-wing or right-wing political views as the far left or the far right.

You can use far in expressions like ’ as far as I know ’ and ’ so far as I remember ’ to indicate that you are not absolutely sure of the statement you are about to make or have just made, and you may be wrong.

You use the expression far and away when you are comparing something or someone with others of the same kind, in order to emphasize how great the difference is between them. For example, you can say that something is far and away the best to indicate that it is definitely the best.

You use the expression by far when you are comparing something or someone with others of the same kind, in order to emphasize how great the difference is between them. For example, you can say that something is by far the best or the best by far to indicate that it is definitely the best.

If you say that something is far from a particular thing or far from being the case, you are emphasizing that it is not that particular thing or not at all the case, especially when people expect or assume that it is.
You can use the expression ’ far from it ’ to emphasize a negative statement that you have just made.
You say far be it from me to disagree, or far be it from me to criticize, when you are disagreeing or criticizing and you want to appear less hostile.
If you say that something is good as far as it goes or true so far as it goes, you mean that it is good or true only to a limited extent.
If you say that someone will go far, you mean that they will be very successful in their career.
Someone or something that is far gone is in such a bad state or condition that not much can be done to help or improve them.
Someone or something that is not far wrong, not far out, or not far off is almost correct or almost accurate.
You can use the expression ’ as far as I can see ’ when you are about to state your opinion of a situation, or have just stated it, to indicate that it is your personal opinion.
If you say that something only goes so far or can only go so far, you mean that its extent, effect, or influence is limited.

If you tell or ask someone what has happened so far, you are telling or asking them what has happened up until the present point in a situation or story, and often implying that something different might happen later.
You can say so far so good to express satisfaction with the way that a situation or activity is progressing, developing, or happening.
Thus far means up until the present point in a situation or story.
If people come from far and wide, they come from a large number of places, some of them far away. If things spread far and wide, they spread over a very large area or distance.
If you say that someone won’t go far wrong or can’t go far wrong with a particular thing or course of action, you mean that it is likely to be successful or satisfactory.

If you say that someone or something fares well or badly, you are referring to the degree of success they achieve in a particular situation or activity.
Farewell means the same as goodbye.

If you farm an area of land, you grow crops or keep animals on it.
A mink farm or a fish farm, for example, is a place where a particular kind of animal or fish is bred and kept in large quantities in order to be sold.
A farmer is a person who owns or manages a farm.
A farmhouse is the main house on a farm, usually where the farmer lives.
Farming is the activity of growing crops or keeping animals on a farm.
Farmland is land which is farmed, or which is suitable for farming.
If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

A fascination is something that fascinates people.
Fashion is the area of activity that involves styles of clothing and appearance.
A fashion is a style of clothing or a way of behaving that is popular at a particular time.
If you do something in a particular fashion or after a particular fashion, you do it in that way.
If you fashion an object or a work of art, you make it.
If you say that something was done after a fashion, you mean that it was done, but not very well.
If something is in fashion, it is popular and approved of at a particular time. If it is out of fashion, it is not popular or approved of.

Englishsense: Fast means happening, moving, or doing something at great speed. You also use fast in questions or statements about speed.
You use fast to say that something happens without any delay.
If a watch or clock is fast, it is showing a time that is later than the real time.
If you hold something fast, you hold it tightly and firmly. If something is stuck fast, it is stuck very firmly and cannot move.
If you hold fast to a principle or idea, or if you stand fast, you do not change your mind about it, even though people are trying to persuade you to.
If colours or dyes are fast, they do not come out of the fabrics they are used on when they get wet.
A fast way of life is one which involves a lot of enjoyable and expensive or dangerous activities.
If you fast, you eat no food for a period of time, usually for either religious or medical reasons, or as a protest.
Someone who is fast asleep is completely asleep.
If you say that someone is playing fast and loose, you are expressing disapproval of them for behaving in a deceitful, immoral, or irresponsible way.
If you say that someone has pulled a fast one on you, you mean that they have cheated or tricked you.
When you fasten something, you close it by means of buttons or a strap, or some other device. If something fastens with buttons or straps, you can close it in this way.
If you fasten one thing to another, you attach the first thing to the second, for example with a piece of string or tape.
If someone or something fastens your attention on a particular thing or if your attention fastens on it, you start to concentrate on it rather than on anything else.
If someone or something fastens on a particular thing, they start to concentrate on it.
If someone fastens on you, they keep following, talking to, or staying with you, when you want them to go away.

Fat is a solid or liquid substance obtained from animals or vegetables, which is used in cooking.
Fat is a substance contained in foods such as meat, cheese, and butter which forms an energy store in your body.
A fat object, especially a book, is very thick or wide.

Christians often refer to God as our Father or address him as Father.

Fatigue in metal or wood is a weakness in it that is caused by repeated stress. Fatigue can cause the metal or wood to break.

A fault in someone or something is a weakness in them or something that is not perfect.
If you cannot fault someone, you cannot find any reason for criticizing them or the things that they are doing.
A fault is a large crack in the surface of the earth.
A fault in tennis is a service that is wrong according to the rules.
If someone or something is at fault, they are to blame or are responsible for a particular situation that has gone wrong.
If you find fault with something or someone, you look for mistakes and complain about them.
If you say that someone has a particular good quality to a fault, you are emphasizing that they have more of this quality than is usual or necessary.

If you fax a document to someone, you send it from one fax machine to another.
You can refer to a copy of a document that is transmitted by a fax machine as a fax.

If you fear something unpleasant or undesirable, you are worried that it might happen or might have happened.
If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely.
If you fear for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you fear to do something, you are afraid to do it or you do not wish to do it.

If you are in fear of doing or experiencing something unpleasant or undesirable, you are very worried that you might have to do it or experience it.
If you take a particular course of action for fear of something, you take the action in order to prevent that thing happening.
You say ’ fear not ’ or ’ never fear ’ to someone when you are telling them not to worry or be frightened.
You use ’ no fear ’ to emphasize that you do not want to do something.
If someone or something puts the fear of God into you, they frighten or worry you, often deliberately.

If you feast your eyes on something, you look at it for a long time with great attention because you find it very attractive.
If you refer to an action, or the result of an action, as a feat, you admire it because it is an impressive and difficult achievement.

If someone or something features in something such as a show, exhibition, or magazine, they are an important part of it.

To feed a family or a community means to supply food for them.
When an animal feeds, it eats or drinks something.
When a baby feeds, or when you feed it, it drinks breast milk or milk from a bottle.
Animal feed is food given to animals, especially farm animals.
To feed something to a place, means to supply it to that place in a steady flow.
If you feed something into a container or piece of equipment, you put it into it.
If someone feeds you false or secret information, they deliberately tell it to you.
If you feed someone’s dislike or desire for something, you make it stronger.
If you feed a plant, you add substances to it to make it grow well.
If one thing feeds on another, it becomes stronger as a result of the other thing’s existence.
To feed information into a computer means to gradually put it into it.
If you get feedback on your work or progress, someone tells you how well or badly you are doing, and how you could improve. If you get good feedback you have worked or performed well.
Feedback is the unpleasant high-pitched sound produced by a piece of electrical equipment when part of the signal that comes out goes back into it.

Englishsense: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.
If you talk about how an experience or event feels, you talk about the emotions and sensations connected with it.

If you talk about how an object feels, you talk about the physical quality that you notice when you touch or hold it. For example, if something feels soft, you notice that it is soft when you touch it.
If you talk about how the weather feels, you describe the weather, especially the temperature or whether or not you think it is going to rain or snow.
If you feel an object, you touch it deliberately with your hand, so that you learn what it is like, for example what shape it is or whether it is rough or smooth.
If you can feel something, you are aware of it because it is touching you.
If you feel something happening, you become aware of it because of the effect it has on your body.
If you feel yourself doing something or being in a particular state, you are aware that something is happening to you which you are unable to control.
If you feel the presence of someone or something, you become aware of them, even though you cannot see or hear them.
If you feel that something is the case, you have a strong idea in your mind that it is the case.
If you feel that you should do something, you think that you should do it.
If you talk about how you feel about something, you talk about your opinion, attitude, or reaction to it.
If you feel like doing something or having something, you want to do it or have it because you are in the right mood for it and think you would enjoy it.
If you feel the effect or result of something, you experience it.
The feel of something, for example a place, is the general impression that it gives you.
If you feel for something, for example in the dark, you try to find it by moving your hand around until you touch it.
If you feel for someone, you have sympathy for them.

Englishsense: A feeling is an emotion, such as anger or happiness.
Your feelings about something are the things that you think and feel about it, or your attitude towards it.

When you refer to someone’s feelings, you are talking about the things that might embarrass, offend, or upset them. For example, if you hurt someone’s feelings, you upset them by something that you say or do.
Feeling is a way of thinking and reacting to things which is emotional and not planned rather than logical and practical.
Feeling for someone is love, affection, sympathy, or concern for them.
If you have a feeling of hunger, tiredness, or other physical sensation, you experience it.
Feeling in part of your body is the ability to experience the sense of touch in this part of the body.
If you have a feeling that something is the case or that something is going to happen, you think that is probably the case or that it is probably going to happen.
Feeling is used to refer to a general opinion that a group of people has about something.
If you have a feeling of being in a particular situation, you feel that you are in that situation.
If you have a feeling for something, you have an understanding of it or a natural ability to do it.
If something such as a place or book creates a particular kind of feeling, it creates a particular kind of atmosphere.
Bad feeling or ill feeling is bitterness or anger which exists between people, for example after they have had an argument.

Hard feelings are feelings of anger or bitterness towards someone who you have had an argument with or who has upset you. If you say ’ no hard feelings ’, you are making an agreement with someone not to be angry or bitter about something.
You say ’ I know the feeling ’ to show that you understand or feel sorry about a problem or difficult experience that someone is telling you about.
If you have mixed feelings about something or someone, you feel uncertain about them because you can see both good and bad points about them.
You use fellow to describe people who are in the same situation as you, or people you feel you have something in common with.
A fellow is a man or boy.
Your fellows are the people who you work with, do things with, or who are like you in some way.
A fellow of an academic or professional association is someone who is a specially elected member of it, usually because of their work or achievements or as a mark of honour.

Englishsense: A fellowship is a group of people that join together for a common purpose or interest.
A fellowship at a university is a post which involves research work.
Fellowship is a feeling of friendship that people have when they are talking or doing something together and sharing their experiences.
In countries where the legal system distinguishes between very serious crimes and less serious ones, a felony is a very serious crime such as armed robbery.
Someone who is female is a woman or a girl.
Women and girls are sometimes referred to as females when they are being considered as a type.
Female matters and things relate to, belong to, or affect women rather than men.
You can refer to any creature that can lay eggs or produce babies from its body as a female.
A female flower or plant contains the part that will become the fruit when it is fertilized.

In some languages, a feminine noun, pronoun, or adjective has a different form from a masculine or neuter one, or behaves in a different way.

Englishsense: A fence is a barrier between two areas of land, made of wood or wire supported by posts.
If you fence an area of land, you surround it with a fence.
A fence in show jumping or horse racing is an obstacle or barrier that horses have to jump over.
A fence is a person who receives stolen property and then sells it.
If one country tries to mend fences with another, it tries to end a disagreement or quarrel with the other country. You can also say that two countries mend fences.
If you sit on the fence, you avoid supporting a particular side in a discussion or argument.
If you fence something in, you surround it completely with a fence.
If you are fenced in by someone or something, they are so close to you that you are unable to move or leave.
If you have to fend for yourself, you have to look after yourself without relying on help from anyone else.
If you fend off unwanted questions, problems, or people, you stop them from affecting you or defend yourself from them, but often only for a short time and without dealing with them completely.

If you say that someone leads the field in a particular activity, you mean that they are better, more active, or more successful than everyone else who is involved in it.
If someone plays the field, they have a number of different romantic or sexual relationships.

If you fight back against someone or something that is attacking or harming you, you resist them actively or attack them.
If you fight back an emotion or a desire, you try very hard not to feel it, show it, or act on it.
If you fight down an emotion or a desire, you try very hard not to feel it, show it, or act on it.
If you fight off something, for example an illness or an unpleasant feeling, you succeed in getting rid of it and in not letting it overcome you.
If you fight off someone who has attacked you, you fight with them, and succeed in making them go away or stop attacking you.
If two people or groups fight something out, they fight or argue until one of them wins.

A fighter is a person who physically fights another person, especially a professional boxer.

Englishsense: A figure is a particular amount expressed as a number, especially a statistic.

If you file an object, you smooth it, shape it, or cut it with a file.
Something that is on file or on someone’s files is recorded or kept in a file or in a collection of information.
A group of people who are walking or standing in single file are in a line, one behind the other.
If you file away a document, you put it in the correct file.

If you fill a crack or hole, you put a substance into it in order to make the surface smooth again.
If a sound, smell, or light fills a space, or the air, it is very strong or noticeable.
If something fills you with an emotion, or if an emotion fills you, you experience this emotion strongly.

If you fill in a shape, you cover the area inside the lines with colour or shapes so that none of the background is showing.
If you fill someone in, you give them more details about something that you know about.
If you fill in for someone, you do the work or task that they normally do because they are unable to do it.
If you are filling in time, you are using time that is available by doing something that is not very important.
If you fill out a form or other document requesting information, you write information in the spaces on it.

If you fill up or fill yourself up with food, you eat so much that you do not feel hungry.

If someone is fingerprinted, the police take their fingerprints.
If the police fingerprint an object, they put a layer of special dust on it so that any fingerprints that are on it can be seen.
Your fingertips are the ends of your fingers.
If you say that something is at your fingertips, you approve of the fact that you can reach it easily or that it is easily available to you.

Englishsense: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.
When you finish something that you are making or producing, you reach the end of making or producing it, so that it is complete.
When something such as a course, film, or sale finishes, especially at a planned time, it ends.

You say that someone or something finishes a period of time or an event in a particular way to indicate what the final situation was like. You can also say that a period of time or an event finishes in a particular way.
If someone finishes second, for example, in a race or competition, they are in second place at the end of the race or competition.
To finish means to reach the end of saying something.
The finish of something is the end of it or the last part of it.
The finish of a race is the end of it.
If the surface of something that has been made has a particular kind of finish, it has the appearance or texture mentioned.
A fight to the finish is one in which one of the people or groups fighting is killed or completely defeated.
If you add the finishing touches to something, you add or do the last things that are necessary to complete it.
If you finish off something that you have been eating or drinking, you eat or drink the last part of it with the result that there is none left.
If someone finishes off a person or thing that is already badly injured or damaged, they kill or destroy them. »see: finish 2;
If you finish up in a particular place or situation, you are in that place or situation after doing or experiencing several things.
If you finish up something that you have been eating or drinking, you eat or drink the last part of it.
If you finish with someone or something, you stop dealing with them, being involved with them, or being interested in them.

Something that is finished no longer exists or is no longer happening.
Someone or something that is finished is no longer important, powerful, or effective.
Something that is finished or finished off in a particular way has been given a particular appearance or decoration.
Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.
A finite clause is a clause based on a verb group which indicates tense, such as ’went’, ’is waiting’, or ’will be found’, rather than on an infinitive or a participle.
The Finns are the people of Finland.

Englishsense: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.
Fire or a fire is an occurrence of uncontrolled burning which destroys buildings, forests, or other things.
A fire is a burning pile of wood, coal, or other fuel that you make, for example to use for heat, light, or cooking.
A fire is a device that uses electricity or gas to give out heat and warm a room.
When a pot or clay object is fired, it is heated at a high temperature in a special oven, as part of the process of making it.
When the engine of a motor vehicle fires, an electrical spark is produced which causes the fuel to burn and the engine to work.
If a machine is fired with a particular fuel, it operates by means of that fuel.
If you fire someone with enthusiasm, you make them feel very enthusiastic. If you fire someone’s imagination, you make them feel interested and excited.
You can use fire to refer in an approving way to someone’s energy and enthusiasm.
If an object or substance catches fire, it starts burning.
If a situation or event catches fire, it begins to be exciting and successful.
If you fight fire with fire, you deal with people attacking or threatening you by using similar methods to the ones that they are using.
If you say that someone has fire in their belly, you are expressing approval of them because they are energetic, enthusiastic, and have very strong feelings.
If something is on fire, it is burning and being damaged or destroyed by an uncontrolled fire.
If you say that someone is on fire, you mean they are very enthusiastic, excited, or passionate about something.
If you say that someone is playing with fire, you mean that they are doing something dangerous that may result in great harm for them and cause many problems.
If you set fire to something or if you set it on fire, you start it burning in order to damage or destroy it.
If you fire up a machine, you switch it on.
If you fire someone up, you make them feel very enthusiastic or motivated.
If someone fires a gun or a bullet, or if they fire, a bullet is sent from a gun that they are using.
You can use fire to refer to the shots fired from a gun or guns.
If you fire an arrow, you send it from a bow.
If you fire questions at someone, you ask them a lot of questions very quickly, one after another.
You can use fire to refer to someone’s strong criticisms of something.
If you draw fire from someone, you cause them to shoot at you, for example because they think that you are threatening them.
If you draw fire for something that you have done, you cause people to criticize you or attack you because of it.
If you hang fire, you delay making a decision about something.
If someone holds their fire or holds fire, they stop shooting or they wait before they start shooting.
If you hold fire in a situation, you delay before taking action.

If you are in the line of fire, you are in a position where someone is aiming their gun at you. If you move into their line of fire, you move into a position between them and the thing they were aiming at.
If you open fire on someone, you start shooting at them.
If you return fire or you return someone’s fire, you shoot back at someone who has shot at you.
If you come under fire or are under fire, someone starts shooting at you.
If you come under fire from someone or are under fire, they criticize you strongly.
If someone wants to say or ask something, you can say ’fire away’ as a way of showing that you are ready for them to speak.
If you fire off a shot, you send a bullet or other missile from a gun.
If you fire off a letter, question, or remark, you send or say it very quickly, often as part of a series.
If an employer fires you, they dismiss you from your job.
Firearms are guns.

Chinesesense: (通常指男性)消防队员，救火队员；
Englishsense: A fireman is a person, usually a man, whose job is to put out fires.
In a room, the fireplace is the place where a fire can be lit and the area on the wall and floor surrounding this place.

Englishsense: A firm is an organization which sells or produces something or which provides a service which people pay for.
If something is firm, it does not change much in shape when it is pressed but is not completely hard.
If something is firm, it does not shake or move when you put weight or pressure on it, because it is strongly made or securely fastened.
If someone’s grip is firm or if they perform a physical action in a firm way, they do it with quite a lot of force or pressure but also in a controlled way.
If you describe someone as firm, you mean they behave in a way that shows that they are not going to change their mind, or that they are the person who is in control.
A firm decision or opinion is definite and unlikely to change.
Firm evidence or information is based on facts and so is likely to be true.
You use firm to describe control or a basis or position when it is strong and unlikely to be ended or removed.
If people are firm friends, they have been close friends for a long time and their friendship is likely to continue.
If a price, value, or currency is firm, it is not decreasing in value or amount.
If you firm soil around a plant, you press it so that it is fairly solid rather than loose.
If someone stands firm, they refuse to change their mind about something.
If you firm up something or if it firms up, it becomes firmer and more solid.
If you firm something up or if it firms up, it becomes clearer, stronger, or more definite.
If a financial institution firms up the price or value of something, they take action to protect and maintain its price or value.

Chinesesense: 最早的;最先的;第一位的；
(强调不愿意做某事)宁可，宁愿；
(一列中)离得最近的，最前面的；
(用于工作或职位的头衔中)最高的；
(英国大学的)优等学位，一级荣誉学位；
居于首要地位;占据头等位置；
先到先接待;先到先供应;按先来后到对待；
对…一无所知;对…毫不知晓；
视…为最重要;把…放在首位；
最重要的先做;最要紧的先处理；
Englishsense: The first thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes before all the others of the same kind.
If you do something first, you do it before anyone else does, or before you do anything else.
When something happens or is done for the first time, it has never happened or been done before.
An event that is described as a first has never happened before and is important or exciting.
The first you hear of something or the first you know about it is the time when you first become aware of it.
You use first when you are talking about what happens in the early part of an event or experience, in contrast to what happens later.
In order to emphasize your determination not to do a particular thing, you can say that rather than do it, you would do something else first.
You use first when you are about to give the first in a series of items.
The first thing, person, or place in a line is the one that is nearest to you or nearest to the front.
You use first to refer to the best or most important thing or person of a particular kind.
First is used in the title of the job or position of someone who has a higher rank than anyone else with the same basic job title.
In British universities, a first is an honours degree of the highest standard.
You use first of all to introduce the first of a number of things that you want to say.
You use at first when you are talking about what happens in the early stages of an event or experience, or just after something else has happened, in contrast to what happens later.
If you say that someone or something comes first for a particular person, you mean they treat or consider that person or thing as more important than anything else.
You say ’ first come first served ’ to indicate that a group of people or things will be dealt with or given something in the order in which they arrive.
From the first means ever since something started.
If you learn or experience something at first hand, you experience it yourself or learn it directly rather than being told about it by other people.
If you say that you do not know the first thing about something, you are emphasizing that you know absolutely nothing about it.
You use first off to introduce the first of a number of things that you want to say.
If you put someone or something first, you treat or consider them as more important than anything else.
You say ’ first things first ’ when you are talking about something that should be done or dealt with before anything else because it is the most important.

Chinesesense: (政府)财政的;国库的;(尤指)税收的；
Englishsense: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

Chinesesense: 旁敲侧击地打听;拐弯抹角地谋取；
如离水之鱼(指因离开熟悉的环境而感到不适)；
海里的鱼有的是;天涯何处无芳草；
Englishsense: A fish is a creature that lives in water and has a tail and fins. There are many different kinds of fish.
Fish is the flesh of a fish eaten as food.
If you fish, you try to catch fish, either for food or as a form of sport or recreation.
If you fish a particular area of water, you try to catch fish in it.
If you say that someone is fishing for information or praise, you disapprove of the fact that they are trying to get it from someone in an indirect way.
If you feel like a fish out of water, you do not feel comfortable or relaxed because you are in an unusual or unfamiliar situation.

If you tell someone that there are plenty more fish in the sea, you are comforting them by saying that although their relationship with someone has failed, there are many other people they can have relationships with.
If you fish something out from somewhere, you take or pull it out, often after searching for it for some time.
A fisherman is a person who catches fish as a job or for sport.
Fisheries are areas of the sea where fish are caught in large quantities for commercial purposes.
A fishery is a place where fish are bred and reared.
Fishing is the sport, hobby, or business of catching fish.

Chinesesense: (政策或方法)铁拳的，残酷无情的，强硬的；
Englishsense: Your hand is referred to as your fist when you have bent your fingers in towards the palm in order to hit someone, to make an angry gesture, or to hold something.
An iron fist policy or approach is one which deals with people and situations in a very strict and cruel way.

Englishsense: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person’s body or onto a particular object.
If something is a good fit, it fits well.
If you are fitted for a particular piece of clothing, you try it on so that the person who is making it can see where it needs to be altered.
If something fits somewhere, it can be put there or is designed to be put there.
If you fit something into a particular space or place, you put it there.
If you fit something somewhere, you attach it there, or put it there carefully and securely.
If something fits something else or fits into it, it goes together well with that thing or is able to be part of it.
You can say that something fits a particular person or thing when it is appropriate or suitable for them or it.
If something is fit for a particular purpose, it is suitable for that purpose.
If someone is fit to do something, they have the appropriate qualities or skills that will allow them to do it.
If something fits someone for a particular task or role, it makes them good enough or suitable for it.
If you describe someone as fit, you mean that they are good-looking.
If you say that something or someone is fit to produce some extreme result, you are emphasizing the extreme nature of that thing or that person’s activity.
If you say that someone sees fit to do something, you mean that they are entitled to do it, but that you disapprove of their decision to do it.
If you manage to fit a person or task in, you manage to find time to deal with them.
If you fit in as part of a group, you seem to belong there because you are similar to the other people in it.
If you say that someone or something fits in, you understand how they form part of a particular situation or system.
If you fit into a particular group, you seem to belong there because you are similar to the other people in it.
If something fits into a particular situation or system, that seems to be the right place for it.
If you fit someone or something out, or you fit them up, you provide them with equipment and other things that they need.
If someone fits another person up, they try to make it seem that that person is responsible for a crime.
Someone who is fit is healthy and physically strong.
If someone has a fit they suddenly lose consciousness and their body makes uncontrollable movements.
If you have a fit of coughing or laughter, you suddenly start coughing or laughing in an uncontrollable way.
If you do something in a fit of anger or panic, you are very angry or afraid when you do it.
If you say that someone will have a fit when they hear about something, you mean that they will be very angry or shocked.
Someone who is in fits is laughing uncontrollably.
Something that happens in fits and starts or by fits and starts keeps happening and then stopping again.

Englishsense: Five is the number 5.
Fives is a British ball game in which you hit a small hard ball with a glove or bat against three walls of a court.

Englishsense: If something is fixed somewhere, it is attached there firmly or securely.
If you fix something, for example a date, price, or policy, you decide and say exactly what it will be.
If you fix something for someone, you arrange for it to happen or you organize it for them.
If you fix something which is damaged or which does not work properly, you repair it.
If you fix a problem or a bad situation, you deal with it and make it satisfactory.
You can refer to a solution to a problem as a fix.
If you fix your eyes on someone or something or if your eyes fix on them, you look at them with complete attention.
If you fix someone with a particular kind of expression, you look at them in that way.
If you fix your attention on someone or something, you think about them with complete attention.
If someone or something is fixed in your mind, you remember them well, for example because they are very important, interesting, or unusual.
If someone fixes a gun, camera, or radar on something, they point it at that thing.
If you fix the position of something, you find out exactly where it is, usually by using radar or electronic equipment.
If you get a fix on someone or something, you have a clear idea or understanding of them.
If you fix some food or a drink for someone, you make it or prepare it for them.
If you fix your hair, clothes, or make-up, you arrange or adjust them so you look neat and tidy, showing you have taken care with your appearance.
If you have your teeth fixed, you have treatment from a dentist to make your teeth even, straight, and white.
If someone fixes a race, election, contest, or other event, they make unfair or illegal arrangements or use deception to affect the result.

If you accuse someone of fixing prices, you accuse them of making unfair arrangements to charge a particular price for something, rather than allowing market forces to decide it. [V n] [V-ing] [disapproval] [BUSINESS 商]
An injection of an addictive drug such as heroin can be referred to as a fix.
You can use fix to refer to an amount of something which a person gets or wants and which helps them physically or psychologically to survive.
If you are in a fix, you are in a difficult situation, especially one that you have caused for yourself.
To fix something such as a dye or photographic image means to treat it with chemicals so that it does not lose its colour or disappear.
If you say that you will fix someone, you mean that you will stop their activities permanently.
If you say that you are fixing to do something, you mean that you are planning or intending to do it.
If you fix on a particular thing, you decide that it is the one you want and will have.
If you fix something up, you arrange it.
If you fix something up, you do work that is necessary in order to make it more suitable or attractive.
If you fix someone up with something they need, you provide it for them. [V n P with n] [Also V n P]

Englishsense: You use fixed to describe something which stays the same and does not or cannot vary.
If you say that someone has fixed ideas or opinions, you mean that they do not often change their ideas and opinions, although perhaps they should.
If someone has a fixed smile on their face, they are smiling even though they do not feel happy or pleased.
Someone who is of no fixed address, or in British English no fixed abode, does not have a permanent place to live.

Chinesesense: (房间等建筑物内的)固定装置，固定设施；
(定期举行的)体育活动，体育赛事；
Englishsense: Fixtures are pieces of furniture or equipment, for example baths and sinks, which are fixed inside a house or other building and which stay there if you move.
A fixture is a sports event which takes place on a particular date.
If you describe someone or something as a fixture in a particular place or occasion, you mean that they always seem to be there.

Chinesesense: (在售旗募捐日出售或在某个位置上作标记用的)小旗，旗状物；
旗帜(新闻用语，代指某个国家、组织或其价值观、权力)；

挥手拦下，招手叫(尤指出租车)；
Englishsense: A flag is a piece of cloth which can be attached to a pole and which is used as a sign, signal, or symbol of something, especially of a particular country.
A flag is a small piece of paper or cloth attached to a stick or pin which is sold on a flag day or used to mark a particular spot.
Journalists sometimes refer to the flag of a particular country or organization as a way of referring to the country or organization itself and its values or power.
If you flag or if your spirits flag, you begin to lose enthusiasm or energy.
A flag is the same as a flagstone.
If you fly the flag, you show that you are proud of your country, or that you support a particular cause, especially when you are in a foreign country or when few other people do.
If you flag down a vehicle, especially a taxi, you wave at it as a signal for the driver to stop.
A flake is a small thin piece of something, especially one that has broken off a larger piece.
If something such as paint flakes, small thin pieces of it come off.
If a food such as fish flakes, or if you flake it, it breaks into small thin pieces.
If you flake out, you collapse, go to sleep, or totally relax because you are very tired.

Chinesesense: 谩骂性电子邮件;攻击性电子邮件；
突然猛烈燃烧起来;突然失火；
煽动…火焰,激化(通常指不良的情绪)；
熊熊燃烧;陷入火海;被大火吞没；
Englishsense: A flame is a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is burning.
A flame is an e-mail message which severely criticizes or attacks someone.
If someone’s face flames, it suddenly looks red, usually because they are angry.
You can refer to a feeling of passion or anger as a flame of passion or a flame of anger.
If something bursts into flames or bursts into flame, it suddenly starts burning strongly.
If someone or something fans the flames of a situation or feeling, usually a bad one, they make it more intense or extreme in some way.
If something goes up in flames, it starts to burn strongly and is destroyed.
Something that is in flames is on fire.
An animal’s flank is its side, between the ribs and the hip.
A flank of an army or navy force is one side of it when it is organized for battle.
The side of anything large can be referred to as its flank.
If something is flanked by things, it has them on both sides of it, or sometimes on one side of it.

Chinesesense: 振翅;挥翅;(翅膀)拍打，抖动；
(布、皮等)扁平下垂物,垂下的部分；
(鸟翼、布条、纸片的)拍打声，拍动，拍打；
Englishsense: If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.
If a bird or insect flaps its wings or if its wings flap, the wings move quickly up and down.
If you flap your arms, you move them quickly up and down as if they were the wings of a bird.
A flap of cloth or skin, for example, is a flat piece of it that can move freely up and down or from side to side because it is held or attached by only one edge.
A flap on the wing of an aircraft is an area along the edge of the wing that can be raised or lowered to control the movement of the aircraft.
A flap is a sudden noise or movement made by a bird’s wing or by a piece of paper or cloth when it flaps.
Someone who is in a flap is in a state of great excitement, worry, or panic.

Chinesesense: 火突然烧旺，突然熊熊燃烧；
(麻烦、暴乱、冲突等)加剧，升级，愈演愈烈；
(常因气愤或难过而)张大(鼻孔),(鼻孔)张开；
(连衣裙等)底部展开，呈喇叭形展开；
(疾病、伤势)突然复发，突然恶化；
Englishsense: A flare is a small device that produces a bright flame. Flares are used as signals, for example on ships.
If a fire flares, the flames suddenly become larger.
If something such as trouble, violence, or conflict flares, it starts or becomes more violent.
If people’s tempers flare, they get angry.
If someone’s nostrils flare or if they flare them, their nostrils become wider, often because the person is angry or upset.
If something such as a dress flares, it spreads outwards at one end to form a wide shape.
Flares are trousers that are very wide at the bottom.
If a disease or injury flares up, it suddenly returns or becomes painful again.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 使闪光,使闪耀;(尤指)频闪；
(通过计算机、卫星或其他系统)快速发送，迅速播出，传送；
突然记起;猛然想起;忽地记起；
Englishsense: A flash is a sudden burst of light or of something shiny or bright.
If a light flashes or if you flash a light, it shines with a sudden bright light, especially as quick, regular flashes of light.
You talk about a flash of something when you are saying that it happens very suddenly and unexpectedly.
If something flashes past or by, it moves past you so fast that you cannot see it properly.
If something flashes through or into your mind, you suddenly think about it.
If you flash something such as an identity card, you show it to people quickly and then put it away again.
If a picture or message flashes up on a screen, or if you flash it onto a screen, it is displayed there briefly or suddenly, and often repeatedly.
If you flash news or information to a place, you send it there quickly by computer, satellite, or other system.
If you flash a look or a smile at someone, you suddenly look at them or smile at them.
If someone’s eyes flash, they suddenly show a strong emotion, especially anger.
Flash is the use of special bulbs to give more light when taking a photograph.
A flash is the same as a flashlight.
If you describe something as flash, you mean that it looks expensive, fashionable, and new.
If you describe an achievement or success as a flash in the pan, you mean that it is unlikely to be repeated and is not an indication of future achievements or success.
If you say that something happens in a flash, you mean that it happens suddenly and lasts only a very short time.
If you say that someone reacts to something quick as a flash, you mean that they react to it extremely quickly.
If your mind flashes back to something in the past, you remember it or think of it briefly or suddenly.
A flashlight is a small electric light which gets its power from batteries and which you can carry in your hand.
