A guard is a specially organized group of people, such as soldiers or policemen, who protect or watch someone or something.
On a train, a guard is a person whose job is to travel on the train in order to help passengers, check tickets, and make sure that the train travels safely and on time.
If you guard some information or advantage that you have, you try to protect it or keep it for yourself.
A guard is a protective device which covers a part of someone’s body or a dangerous part of a piece of equipment.
Some regiments in the British Army, or the soldiers in them, are referred to as Guards.
If someone catches you off guard, they surprise you by doing something you do not expect. If something catches you off guard, it surprises you by happening when you are not expecting it.
If you lower your guard, let your guard down or drop your guard, you relax when you should be careful and alert, often with unpleasant consequences.
If you mount guard or if you mount a guard, you organize people to watch or protect a person or place.
If you are on your guard or on guard, you are being very careful because you think a situation might become difficult or dangerous.
If someone is on guard, they are on duty and responsible for guarding a particular place or person.
If you stand guard, you stand near a particular person or place because you are responsible for watching or protecting them.
If someone is under guard, they are being guarded.
A guardian is someone who has been legally appointed to look after the affairs of another person, for example a child or someone who is mentally ill.
The guardian of something is someone who defends and protects it.
A guerrilla is someone who fights as part of an unofficial army, usually against an official army or police force.
If you guess something, you give an answer or provide an opinion which may not be true because you do not have definite knowledge about the matter concerned.
If you guess that something is the case, you correctly form the opinion that it is the case, although you do not have definite knowledge about it.
A guess is an attempt to give an answer or provide an opinion which may not be true because you do not have definite knowledge about the matter concerned.
If you say that something is anyone’s guess or anybody’s guess, you mean that no-one can be certain about what is really true.
You say at a guess to indicate that what you are saying is only an estimate or what you believe to be true, rather than being a definite fact.
You say I guess to show that you are slightly uncertain or reluctant about what you are saying.
If someone keeps you guessing, they do not tell you what you want to know.
You say guess what to draw attention to something exciting, surprising, or interesting that you are about to say.

Chinesesense: 做特邀嘉宾；做特邀演员；客串；
Englishsense: A guest is someone who is visiting you or is at an event because you have invited them.
A guest is someone who visits a place or organization or appears on a radio or television show because they have been invited to do so.
A guest is someone who is staying in a hotel. See usage note at: client
To guest means to take part in a performance or a match as a guest, rather than as a regular member.
If you say be my guest to someone, you are giving them permission to do something.
Guidance is help and advice.

Chinesesense: 指导方针；指导原则；准则；
Englishsense: If an organization issues guidelines on something, it issues official advice about how to do it.
A guideline is something that can be used to help you plan your actions or to form an opinion about something.
Guilt is an unhappy feeling that you have because you have done something wrong or think that you have done something wrong.
Guilt is the fact that you have done something wrong or illegal.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you feel guilty, you feel unhappy because you think that you have done something wrong or have failed to do something which you should have done.
Guilty is used of an action or fact that you feel guilty about. guilty conscience
If someone is guilty of a crime or offence, they have committed that crime or offence.
If someone is guilty of doing something wrong, they have done that thing.
A guitar is a musical instrument with six strings and a long neck. You play the guitar by plucking or strumming the strings.
A guitarist is someone who plays the guitar.
Gum is a substance, usually tasting of mint, which you chew for a long time but do not swallow.
Your gums are the areas of firm, pink flesh inside your mouth, which your teeth grow out of.
Gum is a type of glue that is used to stick two pieces of paper together.
If two things are gummed together, they are stuck together.
Gum is a sticky substance which comes from the eucalyptus tree or from various other trees and shrubs.

Chinesesense: 把…发动起来；给…加大油门；使加速；
坚持自己的立场；固执己见；一意孤行；
Englishsense: A gun is a weapon from which bullets or other things are fired.
A gun or a starting gun is an object like a gun that is used to make a noise to signal the start of a race.
To gun an engine or a vehicle means to make it start or go faster by pressing on the accelerator pedal.
If you come out with guns blazing or with all guns blazing, you put all your effort and energy into trying to achieve something.
If you jump the gun, you do something before everyone else or before the proper or right time.
If you stick to your guns, you continue to have your own opinion about something even though other people are trying to tell you that you are wrong.
Gunfire is the repeated shooting of guns.
A gunman is a man who uses a gun to commit a crime such as murder or robbery.
Gunshot is used to refer to bullets that are fired from a gun.
A gunshot is the firing of a gun or the sound of a gun being fired.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Chinesesense: 精神领袖；宗教领袖；尤指印度教的古鲁；
Englishsense: A guru is a person who some people regard as an expert or leader.
A guru is a religious and spiritual leader and teacher, especially in Hinduism.

Chinesesense: 取出动物或鱼的内脏以备烹饪；
用于制作球拍的网线、小提琴弦等的肠线；
告密；把所知和盘托出；倾诉心里话；
Englishsense: A person’s or animal’s guts are all the organs inside them.
When someone guts a dead animal or fish, they prepare it for cooking by removing all the organs from inside it.
The gut is the tube inside the body of a person or animal through which food passes while it is being digested.
Guts is the will and courage to do something which is difficult or unpleasant, or which might have unpleasant results.
A gut feeling is based on instinct or emotion rather than reason.
You can refer to someone’s stomach as their gut, especially when it is very large and sticks out.
The guts of something, for example a subject or a machine, are the key elements of it, which make it work.
To gut a building means to destroy the inside of it so that only its outside walls remain.
Gut is string made from part of the stomach of an animal. Traditionally, it is used to make the strings of sports rackets or musical instruments such as violins.
To bust a gut means to work very hard trying to achieve something.
If you hate someone’s guts, you dislike them very much indeed.
If someone spills their guts, they tell you everything about something secret or private. [V inflects] [Informal]
If you say that you are working your guts out or slogging your guts out, you are emphasizing that you are working as hard as you can.

POS: N-VOC; N-PLURAL 称呼名词；复数名词
Chinesesense: 美国英语伙计们，兄弟们，姐妹们；
盖伊模拟像英国庆祝篝火之夜焚烧的身着古装的人像；
Englishsense: A guy is a man.
Americans sometimes address a group of people, whether they are male or female, as guys or you guys.
A guy is the same as a guy rope.
In Britain, a guy is a model of a man that is made from old clothes filled with straw or paper. Guys are burned on bonfires as part of the celebrations for Guy Fawkes Night.

Chinesesense: 健身；尤指学校的体育活动；
Englishsense: A gym is a club, building, or large room, usually containing special equipment, where people go to do physical exercise and get fit.
Gym is the activity of doing physical exercises in a gym, especially at school.

Chinesesense: 吸食海洛因、可卡因等的毒瘾；
修道士或修女穿的长袍，道袍，道服；
按习惯行事的人;习惯的奴隶；
对做…习以为常;使…成为一种习惯；
Englishsense: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.
A habit is an action which is considered bad that someone does repeatedly and finds it difficult to stop doing.
A drug habit is an addiction to a drug such as heroin or cocaine.
A habit is a piece of clothing shaped like a long loose dress, which a nun or monk wears.
If you say that someone is a creature of habit, you mean that they usually do the same thing at the same time each day, rather than doing new and different things.
If you are in the habit of doing something, you do it regularly or often. If you get into the habit of doing something, you begin to do it regularly or often.
If you make a habit of doing something, you do it regularly or often.
If someone has a particular habit of mind, they usually think in that particular way.

Chinesesense: 动植物的生境，栖生地，产地；
Englishsense: The habitat of an animal or plant is the natural environment in which it normally lives or grows.

Chinesesense: 大幅缩减大小、长度;大幅降低价格；
粗制滥造的职业文人，雇佣文人；
尤指为获取机密信息侵入，非法进入他人的计算机系统；
Englishsense: If you hack something or hack at it, you cut it with strong, rough strokes using a sharp tool such as an axe or knife.
If you hack your way through an area such as a jungle or hack a path through it, you move forward, cutting back the trees or plants that are in your way.
If you hack at or hack something which is too large, too long, or too expensive, you reduce its size, length, or cost by cutting out or getting rid of large parts of it.
If you refer to a professional writer, such as a journalist, as a hack, you disapprove of them because they write for money without worrying very much about the quality of their writing.
If you refer to a politician as a hack, you disapprove of them because they are too loyal to their party and perhaps do not deserve the position they have.
If someone hacks into a computer system, they break into the system, especially in order to get secret information.
If you hack or go hacking, you go out for a ride on horseback.
A hack is a ride on horseback.
A hack is a horse which people can hire from a stable to go out riding.
If you say that someone can’t hack it or couldn’t hack it, you mean that they do not or did not have the qualities needed to do a task or cope with a situation.

Chinesesense: 赞扬，称颂人、事件或成就；
Englishsense: If a person, event, or achievement is hailed as important or successful, they are praised publicly.
Hail consists of small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky.
When it hails, hail falls like rain from the sky.
A hail of things, usually small objects, is a large number of them that hit you at the same time and with great force.
Someone who hails from a particular place was born there or lives there.
If someone or something hails from a particular background, they come from it.
If you hail someone, you call to them.
If you hail a taxi, you wave at it in order to stop it because you want the driver to take you somewhere.
Hail is used as a word of greeting.

Chinesesense: 彻底放松;玩个痛快;无拘无束；
面不改色;毫不惊慌;泰然自若；
Englishsense: Your hair is the fine threads that grow in a mass on your head.
Hair is the short, fine threads that grow on different parts of your body.
Hair is the threads that cover the body of an animal such as a dog, or make up a horse’s mane and tail.
Hairs are short, very fine threads that grow on some insects and plants.
If you let your hair down, you relax completely and enjoy yourself.
Something that makes your hair stand on end shocks or frightens you very much.
If you say that someone has not a hair out of place, you are emphasizing that they are extremely smart and neatly dressed.
If you say that someone faced with a shock or a problem does not turn a hair, you mean that they do not show any surprise or fear, and remain completely calm.
If you say that someone is splitting hairs, you mean that they are making unnecessary distinctions between things when the differences between them are so small they are not important.
If you have a haircut, someone cuts your hair for you.
A haircut is the style in which your hair has been cut.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 情况惊险刺激的，令人担忧的，令人害怕的；
Englishsense: Someone or something that is hairy is covered with hairs.
If you describe a situation as hairy, you mean that it is exciting, worrying, and rather frightening.

Chinesesense: 部分地;在某种程度上;有点；
足球、橄榄球、篮球比赛等的半场，半时，半局；
啤酒、苹果酒等的半品脱；
(儿童乘坐公共汽车或火车时的) 半价票；
用于形容词前，表示强调或夸张非常，极其；
有时用在否定句中，表示非常肯定的意思；
非常…的;更…的;非同寻常的；
两人平均分摊，平分费用；
Englishsense: Half of an amount or object is one of two equal parts that together make up the whole number, amount, or object.
You use half to say that something is only partly the case or happens to only a limited extent.
In games such as football, rugby, and basketball, matches are divided into two equal periods of time which are called halves.
A half is half a pint of a drink such as beer or cider.
A half is a half-price bus or train ticket for a child.
You use half to say that someone has parents of different nationalities. For example, if you are half German, one of your parents is German but the other is not.
You use half past to refer to a time that is thirty minutes after a particular hour.
Half means the same as half past.
You can use half before an adjective describing an extreme quality, as a way of emphasizing and exaggerating something.
Half is sometimes used in negative statements, with a positive meaning, to emphasize a particular fact or quality. For example, if you say ’ he isn’t half lucky ’, you mean that he is very lucky.
You use not half or not half as to show that you do not think something is as good or impressive as it is meant to be.
When you use an expression such as a problem and a half or a meal and a half, you are emphasizing that your reaction to it is either very favourable or very unfavourable.
If you talk about your better half or your other half you mean your wife, your husband, or the person of the opposite sex that you live with.
If you increase something by half, half of the original amount is added to it. If you decrease it by half, half of the original amount is taken away from it.
If you say that someone never does things by halves, you mean that they always do things very thoroughly.
If two people go halves, they divide the cost of something equally between them.

Chinesesense: 时间到一半;事情进行到中途；
Englishsense: Halfway means in the middle of a place or between two points, at an equal distance from each of them.
Halfway means in the middle of a period of time or of an event.
If you meet someone halfway, you accept some of the points they are making so that you can come to an agreement with them.
Halfway means reasonably.

Chinesesense: 大学或学院的学生宿舍；
乡间大庄园，府第用于住宅名称中；
厅，会堂，礼堂尤用于礼堂、音乐厅等名称中；
Englishsense: The hall in a house or flat is the area just inside the front door, into which some of the other rooms open.
A hall in a building is a long passage with doors into rooms on both sides of it.
A hall is a large room or building which is used for public events such as concerts, exhibitions, and meetings.
If students live in hall in British English, or in a hall in American English, they live in a university or college building called a hall of residence.
Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large house in the country.
Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large building, especially one where public events or concerts take place

Chinesesense: 金、银、铂制品上标明纯度、产地、制造者的印记；
Englishsense: The hallmark of something or someone is their most typical quality or feature.
A hallmark is an official mark put on things made of gold, silver, or platinum that indicates the quality of the metal, where the object was made, and who made it.

Chinesesense: 万圣节前夕10月31日晚，传说此时可见鬼巫。当晚儿童常化装成鬼巫尽情玩闹；
Englishsense: Halloween is the night of the 31st of October and is traditionally said to be the time when ghosts and witches can be seen. On Halloween, children often dress up as ghosts and witches.
A hallway in a building is a long passage with doors into rooms on both sides of it.
A hallway in a house or flat is the area just inside the front door, into which some of the other rooms open.

Chinesesense: 绘画中圣人、天使头上的光环，光轮；
Englishsense: A halo is a circle of light that is shown in pictures round the head of a holy figure such as a saint or angel.
A halo is a circle of light round a person or thing, or something that looks like a circle of light.

Chinesesense: 使生长、发展、活动等停止或中止；
军队口令立定！站住！停止前进！；
[只有小型站台、无建筑物的)小火车站；
使生长、发展、活动等完全停止；
Englishsense: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still.
When something such as growth, development, or activity halts or when you halt it, it stops completely.
’ Halt! ’ is a military order to stop walking or marching and stand still.
A halt is a very small station on a country railway line, which often consists only of a short platform and no building.
If someone calls a halt to something such as an activity, they decide not to continue with it or to end it immediately.
If someone or something comes to a halt, they stop moving.
If something such as growth, development, or activity comes or grinds to a halt or is brought to a halt, it stops completely.

Chinesesense: 蹩脚演员;表演过火的演员；
常指演员故意地表演过火，夸张做作；
Englishsense: Ham is meat from the top of the back leg of a pig, specially treated so that it can be kept for a long period of time.
A ham is a person whose hobby consists of using special radio equipment to talk to other people with the same hobby, often people who are in other countries.
A ham actor is someone who acts badly, exaggerating every emotion and gesture.
If actors or actresses ham it up, they exaggerate every emotion and gesture when they are acting, often deliberately because they think that the audience will be more amused.
A hamburger is minced meat which has been shaped into a flat circle. Hamburgers are fried or grilled and then eaten, often in a bread roll.

Chinesesense: 猛烈攻击;大力批评;严厉惩罚；
因税收政策变化、经济不景气等使企业受到打击；
在体育比赛中使惨败，大败；
通常指因恐惧而心脏快速跳动；
机械设备中的锤状物;枪上的击铁;(钢琴的) 音槌；
田径运动中所掷的链球；
满腔热情地;劲头十足地；
Englishsense: A hammer is a tool that consists of a heavy piece of metal at the end of a handle. It is used, for example, to hit nails into a piece of wood or a wall, or to break things into pieces.
If you hammer an object such as a nail, you hit it with a hammer.
If you hammer on a surface, you hit it several times in order to make a noise, or to emphasize something you are saying when you are angry.
If you hammer something such as an idea into people or you hammer at it, you keep repeating it forcefully so that it will have an effect on people.
If you say that someone hammers another person, you mean that they attack, criticize, or punish the other person severely.
If you say that businesses are being hammered, you mean that they are being unfairly harmed, for example by a change in taxes or by bad economic conditions.
In sports, if you say that one player or team hammered another, you mean that the first player or team defeated the second completely and easily.
If someone’s heart is hammering, it is beating very fast, usually because they are frightened.

In machines and instruments, a hammer is a part that hits another part. For example, in a gun the hammer causes the explosion which makes the bullet shoot out of it, and in a piano the hammers hit the strings and cause the sounds.
In athletics, a hammer is a heavy weight on a piece of wire, which the athlete throws as far as possible.
If you say that someone was going at something hammer and tongs, you mean that they were doing it with great enthusiasm or energy.
If you say that something goes, comes, or is under the hammer, you mean that it is going to be sold at an auction.

Chinesesense: 装有各种食品的礼物篮；
尤指装食品用的带盖大篮；
Englishsense: If someone or something hampers you, they make it difficult for you to do what you are trying to do.
A hamper is a basket containing food of various kinds that is given to people as a present.
A hamper is a large basket with a lid, used especially for carrying food in.

Chinesesense: 工厂或农场的工人，体力劳动者通常指男性；
通常指演出前后的鼓掌，掌声；
纸牌游戏中的手中的牌，一手牌；
一手之宽测量马匹高度的单位，等于4英寸；
空间或时间上接近的，不远的；
在…手中，从…那里尤指受到不好的待遇；
完全受某人支配;完全听命于某人；
连手带脚地，手脚一起地捆绑；
迫使某人提前行动或公开其所作所为；
为…忙得不可开交;因…应接不暇；
自行决定权;自由行动权；
迅速而大量地赚钱或花钱；
通常指经过努力后获得，得到；
常指为表示爱意而手拉手的，携着手的；
两件事密切相关地，同时并进地；
统治者用高压手段，严厉地；
常指为表示爱意而手拉手，牵手；
工作或问题办理中的，处理中的；
局势在控制下，在掌握中；
不客气的警告语别碰…，别干涉…；
马上;立即;无需询问或查证；
从另一方面来说用于引出相对照的另一点；
立即，不假思索地屏弃、拒绝等；
因失算而让…占便宜;做对…有利的事；
摊牌;亮出底牌;表明自己的真实意图；
尤指为有所改善接手，照管，担任起对…的责任；
因愤怒、绝望或厌恶而骤然举起双手；
通常指初次尝试，试身手；
洗手不干;不再管;和…断绝关系；
Englishsense: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. Each hand has four fingers and a thumb.
The hand of someone or something is their influence in an event or situation.
If you say that something is in a particular person’s hands, you mean that they are looking after it, own it, or are responsible for it.
If you ask someone for a hand with something, you are asking them to help you in what you are doing.
A hand is someone, usually a man, who does hard physical work, for example in a factory or on a farm, as part of a group of people who all do similar work.
If someone asks an audience to give someone a hand, they are asking the audience to clap loudly, usually before or after that person performs.
If a man asks for a woman’s hand in marriage, he asks her or her parents for permission to marry her.
In a game of cards, your hand is the set of cards that you are holding in your hand at a particular time or the cards that are dealt to you at the beginning of the game.
A hand is a measurement of four inches, which is used for measuring the height of a horse from its front feet to its shoulders.
The hands of a clock or watch are the thin pieces of metal or plastic that indicate what time it is.
Your hand is the style in which you write with a pen or pencil.
If something is at hand, near at hand, or close at hand, it is very near in place or time.
If someone experiences a particular kind of treatment, especially unpleasant treatment, at the hands of a person or organization, they receive it from them.
If you do something by hand, you do it using your hands rather than a machine.
When something changes hands, its ownership changes, usually because it is sold to someone else.
If you have someone eating out of your hand, they are completely under your control.
If someone is bound hand and foot, both their hands and both their feet are tied together.
If you force someone’s hand, you force them to act sooner than they want to, or to act in public when they would prefer to keep their actions secret.
If you have your hands full with something, you are very busy because of it.
If someone gives you a free hand, they give you the freedom to use your own judgment and to do exactly as you wish.
If you say that someone is making or losing money hand over fist, you mean that they are getting or losing a lot of money very quickly.
If you get your hands on something or lay your hands on something, you manage to find it or obtain it, usually after some difficulty.
If you work hand in glove with someone, you work very closely with them.
If two people are hand in hand, they are holding each other’s nearest hand, usually while they are walking or sitting together. People often do this to show their affection for each other.
If two things go hand in hand, they are closely connected and cannot be considered separately from each other.
If you have a hand in something such as an event or activity, you are involved in it.
If you say that someone such as the ruler of a country treats people with a heavy hand, you are criticizing them because they are very strict and severe with them.
If two people are holding hands, they are holding each other’s nearest hand, usually while they are walking or sitting together. People often do this to show their affection for each other.
If you ask someone to hold your hand at an event that you are worried about, you ask them to support you by being there with you.
In a competition, if someone has games or matches in hand, they have more games or matches left to play than their opponent and therefore have the possibility of scoring more points.
If you have time or money in hand, you have more time or money than you need.
The job or problem in hand is the job or problem that you are dealing with at the moment.
If a situation is in hand, it is under control.
If you do something to keep your hand in, you practise a skill or hobby occasionally in order to remain fairly good at it.
If you are on your hands and knees, your knees and feet and the palms of your hands are touching the ground.
If you lend someone a hand, you help them.
If you tell someone to keep their hands off something or to take their hands off it, you are telling them in a rather aggressive way not to touch it or interfere with it.
If you do not know something off hand, you do not know it without having to ask someone else or look it up in a book.
If you have a problem or responsibility on your hands, you have to deal with it. If it is off your hands, you no longer have to deal with it.
If someone or something is on hand, they are near and able to be used if they are needed.
You use on the one hand to introduce the first of two contrasting points, facts, or ways of looking at something. It is always followed later by on the other hand or ’on the other’.
You use on the other hand to introduce the second of two contrasting points, facts, or ways of looking at something.
If a person or a situation gets out of hand, you are no longer able to control them.
If you dismiss or reject something out of hand, you do so immediately and do not consider believing or accepting it.

A ghost or spirit that haunts a place or a person regularly appears in the place, or is seen by the person and frightens them.

Chinesesense: (have 和 has 与过去分词连用构成动词的现在完成时)；
(had 与过去分词连用构成动词的过去完成时)；
(用于对带有 have,has 或 had 的句子作肯定或否定回答)；
[having 和过去分词连用，所引导的分句中提到的动作发生在另一个动作开始之前] ；
[have 后接名词代替该名词作动词的用法，描述某一动作或事件] ；
[在英语口语或书面语中，have可以和很多名词连用以代替某个具体的动词，描述某一动作或事件] ；
[用于代替 there is, 表示某事物存在或发生了某事] ；
抓住某人身体的某部位；
跟…过不去;总想找…的茬儿；
和…讲个明白;和…争论出个结果；
Englishsense: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.
You use the form had with a past participle to form the past perfect tense of verbs.
Have is used in question tags.
You use have when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing ’have’, ’has’, or ’had’, or answering a question.
The form having with a past participle can be used to introduce a clause in which you mention an action which had already happened before another action began.

You can use have followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would be possible to use the same word as a verb. For example, you can say ’ I had a look at the photos ’ instead of ’I looked at the photos.’

In normal spoken or written English, people use have with a wide range of nouns to talk about actions and events, often instead of a more specific verb. For example people are more likely to say ’ we had ice cream ’ or ’ he’s had a shock ’ than ’we ate ice cream’, or ’he’s suffered a shock’.
You use have to say that someone or something owns a particular thing, or when you are mentioning one of their qualities or characteristics.
If you have something to do, you are responsible for doing it or must do it.

You can use have instead of ’there is’ to say that something exists or happens. For example, you can say ’ you have no alternative ’ instead of ’there is no alternative’, or ’ he had a good view from his window ’ instead of ’there was a good view from his window’.
If you have something such as a part of your body in a particular position or state, it is in that position or state.
If you have something done, someone does it for you or you arrange for it to be done.
If someone has something unpleasant happen to them, it happens to them.
If you have someone do something, you persuade, cause, or order them to do it.
If someone has you by a part of your body, they are holding you there and they are trying to hurt you or force you to go somewhere.
If you have something from someone, they give it to you.
If you have an illness or disability, you suffer from it.
If a woman has a baby, she gives birth to it. If she is having a baby, she is pregnant.
You can use have in expressions such as ’ I won’t have it ’ or ’ I’m not having that ’, to mean that you will not allow or put up with something.
You can use has it in expressions such as ’ rumour has it that ’ or ’ as legend has it ’ when you are quoting something that you have heard, but you do not necessarily think it is true.
If someone has it in for you, they do not like you and they want to make life difficult for you.
If you have it in you, you have abilities and skills which you do not usually use and which only show themselves in a difficult situation.
If you are having someone on, you are pretending that something is true when it is not true, for example as a joke or in order to tease them.

If you have it out or have things out with someone, you discuss a problem or disagreement very openly with them, even if it means having an argument, because you think this is the best way to solve the problem.
You use have to when you are saying that something is necessary or required, or must happen. If you do not have to do something, it is not necessary or required.
You can use have to in order to say that you feel certain that something is true or will happen.

Chinesesense: 安全处所;庇护所;避难所；
Englishsense: A haven is a place where people or animals feel safe, secure, and happy.
Havoc is great disorder, and confusion.
If one thing plays havoc with another or wreaks havoc on it, it prevents it from continuing or functioning as normal, or damages it.

Chinesesense: 政治上的鹰派人物，主战分子；
像鹰一样注视;警惕地监视；
Englishsense: A hawk is a large bird with a short, hooked beak, sharp claws, and very good eyesight. Hawks catch and eat small birds and animals.
In politics, if you refer to someone as a hawk, you mean that they believe in using force and violence to achieve something, rather than using more peaceful or diplomatic methods.
If someone hawks goods, they sell them by walking through the streets or knocking at people’s houses, and asking people to buy them.
You can say that someone is hawking something if you do not like the forceful way in which they are asking people to buy it.
If someone hawks, they noisily clear mucus from their throat and spit it out.
If you watch someone like a hawk, you observe them very carefully, usually to make sure that they do not make a mistake or do something you do not want them to do.

Chinesesense: 趁太阳好晒草;抓紧有利时机;不失良机；
Englishsense: Hay is grass which has been cut and dried so that it can be used to feed animals.
If you say that someone is making hay or is making hay while the sun shines, you mean that they are taking advantage of a situation that is favourable to them while they have the chance to.

Chinesesense: 使冒风险;使处于危险中；
斗胆提出;作无把握猜测；
Englishsense: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.
If you hazard someone or something, you put them into a situation which might be dangerous for them.
If you hazard or if you hazard a guess, you make a suggestion about something which is only a guess and which you know might be wrong.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 尤指对健康或安全有危险的，有危害的；
Englishsense: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people’s health or safety.
Haze is light mist, caused by particles of water or dust in the air, which prevents you from seeing distant objects clearly. Haze often forms in hot weather.
If there is a haze of something such as smoke or steam, you cannot see clearly through it.
If someone is in a haze, they are not thinking clearly or not really noticing what is happening around them.

Chinesesense: 书面英语中泛指人他，她[有些人不喜欢这种用法，更倾向于使用 he or she 或 they] ；
Englishsense: You use he to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, he is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use ’he or she’ or ’they’.
In some religions, He is used to refer to God.

Chinesesense: 队伍中的领头位置;队首;排头；
公司、组织的负责人，领导人，首脑，长，主任；
硬币的有人头像的一面，正面；
朝着某一地点行进[美国英语中亦作 are headed] ；
很可能要遭受，会招致[美国英语中亦作 is headed for] ；
充分理解并接受;打定主意；
让…自由行动;对…不加约束；
赞扬或成功冲昏…的头脑，使…骄傲自满；
表示强调大笑/大声尖叫；
吸毒后昏头昏脑的，神志不清的；
倒过来想;从全新的角度理解；
不好的事情再次出现，重新抬头；
突然决定[做某事，尤指古怪或愚蠢的事]; 心血来潮；
到了危急关头;到达关键点；
尤指在生意方面勉强逃脱困境；
有人会遭殃，有人会因此受到惩罚尤指被解雇；
Englishsense: Your head is the top part of your body, which has your eyes, mouth, and brain in it.
You can use head to refer to your mind and your mental abilities.
The head of a line of people or vehicles is the front of it, or the first person or vehicle in the line.
If someone or something heads a line or procession, they are at the front of it.
If something heads a list or group, it is at the top of it.
The head of something is the highest or top part of it.
The head of something long and thin is the end which is wider than or a different shape from the rest, and which is often considered to be the most important part.
The head of a school is the teacher who is in charge.
The head of a company or organization is the person in charge of it and in charge of the people in it.
If you head a department, company, or organization, you are the person in charge of it.
The head of an infected spot is its white or yellow centre.
The head on a glass of beer is the layer of small bubbles that form on the top of the beer.
You can use head to say how many animals of a particular type a farmer has. For example, if they have fifty head of cattle, they have fifty cows.
If you have a bad head, you have a headache.
If you toss a coin and it comes down heads, you can see the side of the coin which has a picture of a head on it.
If you are heading for a particular place, you are going towards that place. In American English, you can also say that you are headed for a particular place.

If something or someone is heading for a particular result, the situation they are in is developing in a way that makes that result very likely. In American English, you can also say that something or someone is headed for a particular result.
If a piece of writing is headed a particular title, it has that title written at the beginning of it.
If you head a ball in football, you hit it with your head in order to make it go in a particular direction.
You use a head or per head after stating a cost or amount in order to indicate that that cost or amount is for each person in a particular group.
If something or someone does your head in, they make you angry or frustrated.
From head to foot means all over your body.

If you have a head for something, you can deal with it easily. For example, if you have a head for figures, you can do arithmetic easily, and if you have a head for heights, you can climb to a great height without feeling afraid.
If you get a fact or idea into your head, you suddenly realize or think that it is true and you usually do not change your opinion about it.

If you say that someone has got something into their head, you mean that they have finally understood or accepted it, and you are usually criticizing them because it has taken them a long time to do this.
If you give someone their head, you allow them to do what they want to do, without trying to advise or stop them.
If alcoholic drink goes to your head, it makes you feel drunk.
If you say that something such as praise or success goes to someone’s head, you are criticizing them because you think that it makes them too proud or confident.
If you are head over heels or head over heels in love, you are very much in love.
If you keep your head, you remain calm in a difficult situation. If you lose your head, you panic or do not remain calm in a difficult situation.
If you knock something on the head, you stop it.
Phrases such as laugh your head off and scream your head off can be used to emphasize that someone is laughing or screaming a lot or very loudly.
If you say that someone is off their head, you mean that they have taken so many drugs that they do not know what they are doing. [N inflects] [Mainly BRIT] [Informal]
If you say that someone is off their head, you think that their ideas or behaviour are very strange, foolish, or dangerous.
If you stand an idea or argument on its head or turn it on its head, you think about it or treat it in a completely new and different way.
If something such as an idea, joke, or comment goes over someone’s head, it is too difficult for them to understand.

If someone does something over another person’s head, they do it without asking them or discussing it with them, especially when they should do so because the other person is in a position of authority.
If you say that something unpleasant or embarrassing rears its ugly head or raises its ugly head, you mean that it occurs, often after not occurring for some time.
If you stand on your head, you balance upside down with the top of your head and your hands on the ground.
If you say that you cannot make head nor tail of something or you cannot make head or tail of it, you are emphasizing that you cannot understand it at all.
If somebody takes it into their head to do something, especially something strange or foolish, they suddenly decide to do it.
If a problem or disagreement comes to a head or is brought to a head, it becomes so bad that something must be done about it.
If you bang peoples’ heads together or knock their heads together, you tell them off severely for doing something wrong or for not doing something they were asked to do.
If two or more people put their heads together, they talk about a problem they have and try to solve it.
If you keep your head above water, you just avoid getting into difficulties; used especially to talk about business.
If you say that heads will roll as a result of something bad that has happened, you mean that people will be punished for it, especially by losing their jobs.

Chinesesense: 使人头痛的事;棘手的事;难题；
Englishsense: If you have a headache, you have a pain in your head.
If you say that something is a headache, you mean that it causes you difficulty or worry.
A vehicle’s headlights are the large powerful lights at the front.

Chinesesense: 尤指报纸头版的标题，大字标题；
广播或电视里的新闻提要，简明新闻；
Englishsense: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.
The headlines are the main points of the news which are read on radio or television.
If a newspaper or magazine article is headlined a particular thing, that is the headline that introduces it.
If someone headlines a show, they are the main performer in it.
Someone or something that hits the headlines or grabs the headlines gets a lot of publicity from the media.
The headquarters of an organization are its main offices.

Chinesesense: 感情创伤愈合;情感恢复常态；
使裂痕、创伤弥合;使和好；
Englishsense: When a broken bone or other injury heals or when something heals it, it becomes healthy and normal again.
When someone’s emotional pain heals, they feel normal and happy again.
If you heal something such as a rift or a wound, or if it heals, the situation is put right so that people are friendly or happy again.

Chinesesense: 医治者;尤指通过祷告和宗教信念治疗的信仰疗法术士；
Englishsense: A healer is a person who heals people, especially a person who heals through prayer and religious faith.
A person’s health is the condition of their body and the extent to which it is free from illness or is able to resist illness.
Health is a state in which a person is not suffering from any illness and is feeling well.
When you drink to someone’s health or drink their health, you have a drink as a sign of wishing them health and happiness.
The health of something such as an organization or a system is its success and the fact that it is working well.

Chinesesense: 显示健康的;反映健康的；
有益于健康的;促进健康的；
机构或体系兴旺的，运作良好的；
Englishsense: Someone who is healthy is well and is not suffering from any illness.
If a feature or quality that you have is healthy, it makes you look well or shows that you are well.
Something that is healthy is good for your health.
A healthy organization or system is successful.
A healthy amount of something is a large amount that shows success.
If you have a healthy attitude about something, you show good sense.

Chinesesense: 颓然[倒下]; 重重地倒下；
Englishsense: A heap of things is a pile of them, especially a pile arranged in a rather untidy way.
If you heap things somewhere, you arrange them in a large pile.
If you heap praise or criticism on someone or something, you give them a lot of praise or criticism.
Heaps of something or a heap of something is a large quantity of it.
Someone who is at the bottom of the heap or at the top of the heap is low down or high up in society or an organization.
If someone collapses in a heap, they fall heavily and untidily and do not move.

Chinesesense: 法官或法庭审理案件，听取证词；
辩论或讨论中倾听意见或情况；
“听见没有？”“你听到我的话了吗？”要求对方注意听自己的话；
说得对！说得好！政治辩论或公众大会上对讲话人表示赞同的喝彩声；
Englishsense: When you hear a sound, you become aware of it through your ears.
If you hear something such as a lecture or a piece of music, you listen to it.
If you say that you can hear someone saying something, you mean that you are able to imagine hearing it.
When a judge or a court of law hears a case, or evidence in a case, they listen to it officially in order to make a decision about it.
If you hear from someone, you receive a letter or telephone call from them.
In a debate or discussion, if you hear from someone, you listen to them giving their opinion or information.
If you hear some news or information about something, you find out about it by someone telling you, or from the radio or television.
If you have heard of something or someone, you know about them, but not in great detail.

If you say that you have heard something before, you mean that you are not interested in it, or do not believe it, or are not surprised about it, because you already know about it or have experienced it.
If you say ’ Do you hear? ’ or ’ Did you hear me? ’ to someone, you are telling them in an angry or forceful way to pay attention to what you are saying.
During political debates and public meetings, people sometimes say ’ Hear hear! ’ to express their agreement with what the speaker is saying.
If you say that you can’t hear yourself think, you are complaining and emphasizing that there is a lot of noise, and that it is disturbing you or preventing you from doing something.
If you say that you won’t hear of someone doing something, you mean that you refuse to let them do it.
A person’s or animal’s hearing is the sense which makes it possible for them to be aware of sounds.
A hearing is an official meeting which is held in order to collect facts about an incident or problem.
If someone gives you a fair hearing or a hearing, they listen to you when you give your opinion about something.
If someone says something in your hearing or within your hearing, you can hear what they say because they are with you or near you.

Chinesesense: 全心全意地;真心实意地；
人本质上，实际上，内心里；
十分关心某人的利益或福祉；
通常指因感情破裂而使…伤心，使…心碎；
尤指因对他人的苦难无能为力而使…伤心，使…心碎；
我发誓所说的是真的/你敢发誓所说的是真的吗？；
激动非常;焦急万分;害怕得要命；
尽管有其他缺点但心地善良，心眼儿好；
一心想要得到;一心想要做；
全心全意地;尽心尽力地；
从…得到鼓舞;因…振作精神；
对…耿耿于怀;为…感到不快；
Englishsense: Your heart is the organ in your chest that pumps the blood around your body. People also use heart to refer to the area of their chest that is closest to their heart.
You can refer to someone’s heart when you are talking about their deep feelings and beliefs.
You use heart when you are talking about someone’s character and attitude towards other people, especially when they are kind and generous.
If you refer to things of the heart, you mean love and relationships.
The heart of something is the most central and important part of it.
The heart of a place is its centre.
The heart of a lettuce, cabbage, or other vegetable is its centre leaves.
A heart is a shape that is used as a symbol of love: ♥.
Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards. Each card in the suit is marked with one or more red symbols in the shape of a heart.
If you feel or believe something with all your heart, you feel or believe it very strongly.
If you say that someone is a particular kind of person at heart, you mean that that is what they are really like, even though they may seem very different.
If you say that someone has your interests or your welfare at heart, you mean that they are concerned about you and that is why they are doing something.
If someone breaks your heart, they make you very sad and unhappy, usually because they end a love affair or close relationship with you.
If something breaks your heart, it makes you feel very sad and depressed, especially because people are suffering but you can do nothing to help them.
If you say that someone has a broken heart, you mean that they are very sad, for example because a love affair has ended unhappily.
If you know something such as a poem by heart, you have learned it so well that you can remember it without having to read it.
If someone has a change of heart, their attitude towards something changes.
If something such as a subject or project is close to your heart or near to your heart, it is very important to you and you are very interested in it and concerned about it.
If you can do something to your heart’s content, you can do it as much as you want.

You can say ’ cross my heart ’ when you want someone to believe that you are telling the truth. You can also ask ’ cross your heart? ’, when you are asking someone if they are really telling the truth.
If you say something from the heart or from the bottom of your heart, you sincerely mean what you say.
If something gives you heart, it makes you feel more confident or happy about something.
If you want to do something but do not have the heart to do it, you do not do it because you know it will make someone unhappy or disappointed.
If you believe or know something in your heart of hearts, that is what you really believe or think, even though it may sometimes seem that you do not.
If your heart isn’t in the thing you are doing, you have very little enthusiasm for it, usually because you are depressed or are thinking about something else.
If you lose heart, you become sad and depressed and are no longer interested in something, especially because it is not progressing as you would like.
If you lose your heart to someone, you fall in love with them.
If your heart is in your mouth, you feel very excited, worried, or frightened.
If you open your heart or pour out your heart to someone, you tell them your most private thoughts and feelings.
If you say that someone’s heart is in the right place, you mean that they are kind, considerate, and generous, although you may disapprove of other aspects of their character.
If you have set your heart on something, you want it very much or want to do it very much.
If you wear your heart on your sleeve, you openly show your feelings or emotions rather than keeping them hidden.
If you put your heart and soul into something, you do it with a great deal of enthusiasm and energy.
If you take heart from something, you are encouraged and made to feel optimistic by it.
If you take something to heart, for example someone’s behaviour, you are deeply affected and upset by it.
Your heartbeat is the regular movement of your heart as it pumps blood around your body.
A heartbeat is one of the movements of your heart.

Chinesesense: 强烈的感情;尤指愤怒，激动；
雌性动物正在发情[美国英语中作 in heat] ；
Englishsense: When you heat something, you raise its temperature, for example by using a flame or a special piece of equipment.
Heat is warmth or the quality of being hot.
The heat is very hot weather.
The heat of something is the temperature of something that is warm or that is being heated.
You use heat to refer to a source of heat, for example a cooking ring or the heating system of a house.
You use heat to refer to a state of strong emotion, especially of anger or excitement.
The heat of a particular activity is the point when there is the greatest activity or excitement.
A heat is one of a series of races or competitions. The winners of a heat take part in another race or competition, against the winners of other heats.

When a female animal is on heat in British English, or in heat in American English, she is in a state where she is ready to mate with a male animal, as this will probably result in her becoming pregnant.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A heated discussion or quarrel is one where the people involved are angry and excited.
If someone gets heated about something, they get angry and excited about it.

Chinesesense: 加热器;加热装置;暖气设备;炉子；
Englishsense: A heater is a piece of equipment or a machine which is used to raise the temperature of something, especially of the air inside a room or a car.

Chinesesense: 尤指从经济角度考虑的供暖，暖气供应；
建筑物的供暖系统，暖气设备；
Englishsense: Heating is the process of heating a building or room, considered especially from the point of view of how much this costs.
Heating is the system and equipment that is used to heat a building.
If you heave something heavy or difficult to move somewhere, you push, pull, or lift it using a lot of effort.
If something heaves, it moves up and down with large regular movements.
If you heave, or if your stomach heaves, you vomit or feel sick.
If you heave a sigh, you give a big sigh.
If a place is heaving or if it is heaving with people, it is full of people.
When something heaves into view or heaves into sight, it appears.

Chinesesense: 极乐[之地]; 天堂般美好的世界；
但愿不会这样;千万不要这样;苍天不容;老天不许；
…只有靠天帮忙了;谁也帮不了…了；
想尽一切办法;竭尽全力;千方百计；
[用于以 what、when、who、why 及 how 开头的疑问句中表示强调] 到底，究竟；
Englishsense: In some religions, heaven is said to be the place where God lives, where good people go when they die, and where everyone is always happy. It is usually imagined as being high up in the sky.
You can use heaven to refer to a place or situation that you like very much.
The heavens are the sky.
You say ’ Heaven forbid! ’ to emphasize that you very much hope that something will not happen.
You say ’ Good heavens! ’ or ’ Heavens! ’ to express surprise or to emphasize that you agree or disagree with someone.
You say ’ Heaven help someone’ when you are worried that something bad is going to happen to them, often because you disapprove of what they are doing or the way they are behaving.
You can say ’ Heaven knows ’ to emphasize that you do not know something, or that you find something very surprising.
You can say ’ Heaven knows ’ to emphasize something that you feel or believe very strongly.
If you move heaven and earth to do something, you try as hard as you can to do it.
You can use in heaven’s name in questions beginning with ’what’, ’when’, ’who’, ’why’ and ’how’ to add emphasis in a way that shows that you are very angry or surprised.
If the heavens open, it suddenly starts raining very heavily.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 无比美好的;极令人愉快的；
Englishsense: Heavenly things are things that are connected with the religious idea of heaven.
Something that is heavenly is very pleasant and enjoyable.

Chinesesense: 缓慢沉痛地;费力地;沉重地；
Englishsense: If someone says something heavily, they say it in a slow way which shows a feeling such as sadness, tiredness, or annoyance.

Englishsense: When you hold something, you carry or support it, using your hands or your arms.
Hold is used in expressions such as grab hold of, catch hold of, and get hold of, to indicate that you close your hand tightly around something, for example to stop something moving or falling.

When you hold a part of your body, you put your hand on or against it, often because it hurts.
When you hold a part of your body in a particular position, you put it into that position and keep it there.
If one thing holds another in a particular position, it keeps it in that position.
If one thing is used to hold another, it is used to store it.

If a place holds something, it keeps it available for reference or for future use.
If something holds a particular amount of something, it can contain that amount.

Hold is used with words and expressions indicating an opinion or belief, to show that someone has a particular opinion or believes that something is true.
Hold is used with words such as ’fear’ or ’mystery’ to indicate someone’s feelings towards something, as if those feelings were a characteristic of the thing itself.

Hold is used with words such as ’lead’ or ’advantage’ to indicate that someone is winning or doing well in a contest.
Hold is used with nouns such as ’attention’ or ’interest’ to indicate that what you do or say keeps someone interested or listening to you.
If you hold someone responsible, liable, or accountable for something, you will blame them if anything goes wrong.
If someone holds you in a place, they keep you there as a prisoner and do not allow you to leave.
If people such as an army or a violent crowd hold a place, they control it by using force.
If you have a hold over someone, you have power or control over them, for example because you know something about them you can use to threaten them or because you are in a position of authority.

If you ask someone to hold, or to hold the line, when you are answering a telephone call, you are asking them to wait for a short time, for example so that you can find the person they want to speak to.
If you hold telephone calls for someone, you do not allow people who phone to speak to that person, but take messages instead.
If something holds at a particular value or level, or is held there, it is kept at that value or level.

If a good situation holds, it continues and does not get worse or fail.
If an argument or theory holds, it is true or valid, even after close examination.
If part of a structure holds, it does not fall or break although there is a lot of force or pressure on it.
If laws or rules hold, they exist and remain in force.
If you say that you hold to a particular opinion or belief, you are stating firmly that you continue to have that opinion or belief.
If you hold to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, you keep that promise or continue to behave according to those standards.
If someone or something holds you to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, they make you keep that promise or those standards.
If you hold forth on a subject, you speak confidently and for a long time about it, especially to a group of people.
If you get hold of an object or information, you obtain it, usually after some difficulty.
If you get hold of a fact or a subject, you learn about it and understand it well.

If you hold still, you do not move.
If something takes hold, it gains complete control or influence over a person or thing.

Chinesesense: 强调信念或情感真的，的确；
强调所说的是事实真的，确实；
表示恼怒或不耐烦天哪，哎呀；
Englishsense: You use honestly to emphasize that you are referring to your, or someone else’s, true beliefs or feelings.
You use honestly to emphasize that you are telling the truth and that you want people to believe you.
You use honestly to indicate that you are annoyed or impatient.
Honesty is the quality of being honest.
Honesty is a plant whose seeds are contained in silvery-white papery discs.
Honey is a sweet, sticky, yellowish substance that is made by bees.
You call someone honey as a sign of affection.

Chinesesense: 新工作开始或新政府成立后的和谐时期，蜜月期；
Englishsense: A honeymoon is a holiday taken by a man and a woman who have just got married.
When a recently-married couple honeymoon somewhere, they go there on their honeymoon.
You can use honeymoon to refer to a period of time after the start of a new job or new government when everyone is pleased with the person or people concerned and is nice to them.

Chinesesense: 汽车的发动机罩，引擎罩；
折叠式车篷;设备上的罩，防护罩；
Englishsense: A hood is a part of a coat which you can pull up to cover your head. It is in the shape of a triangular bag attached to the neck of the coat at the back.
A hood is a bag made of cloth, which is put over someone’s head and face so that they cannot be recognized or so that they cannot see.
The hood of a car is the metal cover over the engine at the front.
A hood is a covering on a vehicle or a piece of equipment, which is usually curved and can be removed.
A cooker hood is an electrical device fitted over a cooker above head height, and containing an extractor fan and usually a light.

Chinesesense: 用手臂、腿或脚钩住，绕住；
通常指拳击运动中的钩拳；
Englishsense: A hook is a bent piece of metal or plastic that is used for catching or holding things, or for hanging things up.
If you hook one thing to another, you attach it there using a hook. If something hooks somewhere, it can be hooked there.
If you hook your arm, leg, or foot round an object, you place it like a hook round the object in order to move it or hold it.
If you hook a fish, you catch it with a hook on the end of a line.
A hook is a short sharp blow with your fist that you make with your elbow bent, usually in a boxing match.
If you are hooked into something, or hook into something, you get involved with it.
If you hook into the Internet, you make a connection with the Internet on a particular occasion so that you can use it.
If someone gets off the hook or is let off the hook, they manage to get out of the awkward or unpleasant situation that they are in.
If you take a phone off the hook, you take the receiver off the part that it normally rests on, so that the phone will not ring.
If your phone is ringing off the hook, so many people are trying to telephone you that it is ringing constantly.

Chinesesense: 木头、金属或塑料制成的大环，大圈；
篮球运动中的篮圈，篮筐；
为取悦他人或达到目的而经受苦难，作出很大努力；
Englishsense: A hoop is a large ring made of wood, metal, or plastic.
In croquet, the hoops are the small metal arches which players hit the ball through.
A basketball hoop is the ring that players try to throw the ball into in order to score points for their team.
If someone makes you jump through hoops, they make you do lots of difficult or boring things in order to please them or achieve something.

Chinesesense: 鸟、小动物双脚跳，齐足跳行；
跳上[或下]; 快速移动；
通常指乘飞机的短途快速旅程；
非常生气的;暴跳如雷的；
措手不及地;出其不意地；
Englishsense: If you hop, you move along by jumping on one foot.
When birds and some small animals hop, they move along by jumping on both feet.
If you hop somewhere, you move there quickly or suddenly.
A hop is a short, quick journey, usually by plane.
A hop is a social event at which people mix together and dance in an informal way.
Hops are flowers that are dried and used for making beer.
If you tell someone to hop it, you are telling them in a rude way to go away.
Someone who is hopping mad is very angry.
If you are caught on the hop, you are surprised by someone doing something when you were not expecting them to and so you are not prepared for it.

Chinesesense: 对未来的希望，期望，指望；
被寄予希望的人或事物；
从最好的方面想;抱乐观的希望；
没有一线希望;毫无机会；
很高期望;很大希望;厚望；
存一线希望;抱着万分之一的希望；
表示警告他人不要做愚蠢或危险的事我希望，但愿；
表示更加礼貌和委婉我希望，我想；
在不太可能的情况下对…继续抱有希望，痴心妄想；
Englishsense: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.
If you say that you cannot hope for something, or if you talk about the only thing that you can hope to get, you mean that you are in a bad situation, and there is very little chance of improving it.
Hope is a feeling of desire and expectation that things will go well in the future.
If someone wants something to happen, and considers it likely or possible, you can refer to their hopes of that thing, or to their hope that it will happen.
If you think that the help or success of a particular person or thing will cause you to be successful or to get what you want, you can refer to them as your hope.
If you are in a difficult situation and do something and hope for the best, you hope that everything will happen in the way you want, although you know that it may not.
If you tell someone not to get their hopes up, or not to build their hopes up, you are warning them that they should not become too confident of progress or success.
If you say that someone has not got a hope in hell of doing something, you are emphasizing that they will not be able to do it.
If you have high hopes or great hopes that something will happen, you are confident that it will happen.
If you hope against hope that something will happen, you hope that it will happen, although it seems impossible.

You use ’ I hope ’ in expressions such as ’ I hope you don’t mind ’ and ’ I hope I’m not disturbing you ’, when you are being polite and want to make sure that you have not offended someone or disturbed them.
You say ’ I hope ’ when you want to warn someone not to do something foolish or dangerous.
You add ’ I hope ’ to what you are saying to make it sound more polite and less rude or less definite.
If you do one thing in the hope of another thing happening, you do it because you think it might cause or help the other thing to happen, which is what you want.
If you live in hope that something will happen, you continue to hope that it will happen, although it seems unlikely, and you realize that you are being foolish.
If you say ’ Some hope ’, or ’ Not a hope ’, you think there is no possibility that something will happen, although you may want it to happen.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 人抱有希望的，满怀希望的；
征兆、事件等给人以希望的；
Englishsense: If you are hopeful, you are fairly confident that something that you want to happen will happen.
If something such as a sign or event is hopeful, it makes you feel that what you want to happen will happen.
A hopeful action is one that you do in the hope that you will get what you want to get.
If you refer to someone as a hopeful, you mean that they are hoping and trying to achieve success in a particular career, election, or competition.

Chinesesense: 但愿，作为希望一些用词严谨者认为这种用法不正确，但实际上已被频繁地使用；
Englishsense: You say hopefully when mentioning something that you hope will happen. Some careful speakers of English think that this use of hopefully is not correct, but it is very frequently used.

Chinesesense: 无望的;注定失败的;不会成功的；
人没有希望做好…的，不行的，无能的；
糟糕透顶的;无可救药的;极坏的；
Englishsense: If you feel hopeless, you feel very unhappy because there seems to be no possibility of a better situation or success.
Someone or something thing that is hopeless is certain to fail or be unsuccessful.
If someone is hopeless at something, they are very bad at it.
You use hopeless to emphasize how bad or inadequate something or someone is.

Chinesesense: 已露端倪的;即将发生的；
Englishsense: The horizon is the line in the far distance where the sky seems to meet the land or the sea.
Your horizons are the limits of what you want to do or of what you are interested or involved in.
If something is on the horizon, it is almost certainly going to happen or be done quite soon.
Something that is horizontal is flat and level with the ground, rather than at an angle to it.
A horizontal is a line or structure that is horizontal.
A hormone is a chemical, usually occurring naturally in your body, that makes an organ of your body do something.

Chinesesense: 汽车等的喇叭;汽笛;警报器；
铜管乐器中的法国号，圆号；
号角一种简单乐器，由一根金属管组成，一端宽，一端窄；
变得谨慎行事；尤指紧缩开支；
Englishsense: On a vehicle such as a car, the horn is the device that makes a loud noise as a signal or warning.
The horns of an animal such as a cow or deer are the hard pointed things that grow from its head.
Horn is the hard substance that the horns of animals are made of. Horn is sometimes used to make objects such as spoons, buttons, or ornaments.
A horn is a musical instrument of the brass family. It is a long circular metal tube, wide at one end, which you play by blowing.
A horn is a simple musical instrument consisting of a metal tube that is wide at one end and narrow at the other. You play it by blowing into it.
A horn is a hollow curved object that is narrow at one end and wide at the other.
If you blow your own horn, you boast about yourself.
If two people lock horns, they argue about something.
If you are on the horns of a dilemma, you have to choose between two things, both of which are unpleasant or difficult.
If someone pulls in their horns or draws in their horns, they start behaving more cautiously than they did before, especially by spending less money.

Chinesesense: 令人震惊的;使人恐惧的;让人极度反感的；
Englishsense: If you describe something or someone as horrible, you do not like them at all.
You can call something horrible when it causes you to feel great shock, fear, and disgust.
Horrible is used to emphasize how bad something is.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: 攻击、事故、伤势等令人震惊的，极其可怕的，十分严重的；
Englishsense: If you describe a physical attack, accident, or injury as horrific, you mean that it is very bad, so that people are shocked when they see it or think about it.
If you describe something as horrific, you mean that it is so big that it is extremely unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 使感到震惊;使毛骨悚然;使产生反感；
Englishsense: If someone is horrified, they feel shocked or disgusted, usually because of something that they have seen or heard.

Chinesesense: 极其不愉快或可怕的经历；
极讨厌或丑陋的人或事物；
影片或故事情节恐怖的，惊悚的；
经历或事件非常不愉快的；
Englishsense: Horror is a feeling of great shock, fear, and worry caused by something extremely unpleasant.
If you have a horror of something, you are afraid of it or dislike it very much.
The horror of something, especially something that hurts people, is its very great unpleasantness.
You can refer to extremely unpleasant or frightening experiences as horrors.
If you refer to someone or something as a horror, you mean that you think they are very unpleasant or ugly.
A horror film or story is intended to be very frightening.
You can refer to an account of a very unpleasant experience or event as a horror story.
Horror of horrors is used to refer to something that you consider to be the worst part of a situation.

Chinesesense: 从知情人那里直接获悉；
Englishsense: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.
When you talk about the horses, you mean horse races in which people bet money on the horse which they think will win.
A vaulting horse is a tall piece of gymnastics equipment for jumping over.
If you hear something from the horse’s mouth, you hear it from someone who knows that it is definitely true.
If you do something on horseback, you do it while riding a horse.
A horseback ride is a ride on a horse.

Chinesesense: 橡胶或塑料制的水管，水龙带；
引导液体或气体的橡胶或塑料软管，导管；
袜类包括连裤袜、长筒袜、短袜；
Englishsense: A hose is a long, flexible pipe made of rubber or plastic. Water is directed through a hose in order to do things such as put out fires, clean cars, or water gardens.
A hose is a pipe made of rubber or plastic, along which a liquid or gas flows, for example from one part of an engine to another.
If you hose something, you wash or water it using a hose.
Hose is used to refer to tights, socks, and stockings.
Hose is an old-fashioned men’s garment that looks like a pair of very tight trousers.
A hospital is a place where people who are ill are looked after by nurses and doctors.

Chinesesense: 大型活动中公司为来访者或客户提供的招待茶点，款待；
Englishsense: Hospitality is friendly, welcoming behaviour towards guests or people you have just met.
Hospitality is the food, drink, and other privileges which some companies provide for their visitors or clients at major sporting or other public events.

Chinesesense: 举办聚会等的主人，东道主；
作为主人组织，做东举办聚会等；
某项活动的主办国或城市、机构；
国家、城市或机构主办活动；
广播、电视的节目主持人；
圣体基督教圣餐礼等宗教仪式中代表耶稣躯体的面饼；
Englishsense: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment.
If someone hosts a party, dinner, or other function, they have invited the guests and provide the food, drink, or entertainment.
A country, city, or organization that is the host of an event provides the facilities for that event to take place.
If a country, city, or organization hosts an event, they provide the facilities for the event to take place.
If a person or country plays host to an event or an important visitor, they host the event or the visit.
The host of a radio or television show is the person who introduces it and talks to the people who appear in it.
The person who hosts a radio or television show introduces it and talks to the people who appear in it.
A host of things is a lot of them.
If an area is host to living things, those creatures live and feed in that area.
A host or a host computer is the main computer in a network of computers, which controls the most important files and programs.
The host of a parasite is the plant or animal which it lives on or inside and from which it gets its food.
The Host is the bread which is used to represent the body of Christ in Christian church services such as Holy Communion.

Chinesesense: 受限制的人;不由自主的人；
Englishsense: A hostage is someone who has been captured by a person or organization and who may be killed or injured if people do not do what that person or organization demands.
If someone is taken hostage or is held hostage, they are captured and kept as a hostage.
If you say you are hostage to something, you mean that your freedom to take action is restricted by things that you cannot control.

Someone who is hostile is unfriendly and aggressive.
Hostile situations and conditions make it difficult for you to achieve something.
A hostile takeover bid is one that is opposed by the company that is being bid for.
In a war, you use hostile to describe your enemy’s forces, organizations, weapons, land, and activities.
Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.
Your hostility to something you do not approve of is your opposition to it.

Chinesesense: 天气热的;气温高的;炎热的；
议题、话题热门的，受到广泛关注的；
消息刚发布的，最新的，新近的；
风行的;走红的;炙手可热的；
常指非法获得的贵重或知名物品烫手的，难以销赃的；
比赛激烈的，双方全力以赴的；
被看好的;最有望获胜的；
焦虑不安;六神无主;举止失常；
Englishsense: Something that is hot has a high temperature.
Hot is used to describe the weather or the air in a room or building when the temperature is high.
If you are hot, you feel as if your body is at an unpleasantly high temperature.
You use hot to talk or ask about how high the temperature of something is.
Hot food is intended to be eaten as soon as it is cooked, as opposed to food that you eat when it has cooled or that you do not cook at all.
You can say that food is hot when it has a strong, burning taste caused by chillies, pepper, or ginger.
A hot issue or topic is one that is very important at the present time and is receiving a lot of publicity.
Hot news is new, recent, and fresh.
You can use hot to describe something that is very exciting and that many people want to see, use, obtain, or become involved with.
You can use hot to describe something that no one wants to deal with, often because it has been illegally obtained and is very valuable or famous.
You can describe a situation that is created by a person’s behaviour or attitude as hot when it is unpleasant and difficult to deal with.
A hot contest is one that is intense and involves a great deal of activity and determination.
If a person or team is the hot favourite, people think that they are the one most likely to win a race or competition.
Someone who has a hot temper gets angry very quickly and easily.
If someone blows hot and cold, they keep changing their attitude towards something, sometimes being very enthusiastic and at other times expressing no interest at all.
If you are hot and bothered, you are so worried and anxious that you cannot think clearly or behave sensibly.
If you say that one person has the hots for another, you mean that they feel a strong sexual attraction to that person.
A hotel is a building where people stay, for example on holiday, paying for their rooms and meals.

Chinesesense: 常指通过不断批评而逼迫某人辞职或离开某地；
Englishsense: A hound is a type of dog that is often used for hunting or racing.
If someone hounds you, they constantly disturb or speak to you in an annoying or upsetting way.
If someone is hounded out of a job or place, they are forced to leave it, often because other people are constantly criticizing them.

Chinesesense: 人一生中的某个时候，时期；
每天发生或进行某事的特定时间，固定时间；
下班后;营业或办公、学习时间以后；
在某一时段的任何时刻；
整点差…分/ 整点过…分；
在通常营业或工作、学习时间之外；
Englishsense: An hour is a period of sixty minutes.
People say that something takes or lasts hours to emphasize that it takes or lasts a very long time, or what seems like a very long time.
A clock that strikes the hour strikes when it is exactly one o’clock, two o’clock, and so on.
You can refer to a particular time or moment as a particular hour.
If you refer, for example, to someone’s hour of need or hour of happiness, you are referring to the time in their life when they are or were experiencing that condition or feeling.
You can refer to the period of time during which something happens or operates each day as the hours during which it happens or operates.
If you refer to the hours involved in a job, you are talking about how long you spend each week doing it and when you do it.
If you do something after hours, you do it outside normal business hours or the time when you are usually at work.
If you say that something happens at all hours of the day or night, you disapprove of it happening at the time that it does or as often as it does.
If something happens in the early hours or in the small hours, it happens in the early morning after midnight.
If you say that someone does something hour after hour, you are emphasizing that they do it continually for a long time.
If something happens on the hour, it happens every hour at, for example, nine o’clock, ten o’clock, and so on, and not at any number of minutes past an hour.
If you want to state the time exactly, you can give a number of minutes followed by before the hour or past the hour.
Something that happens out of hours happens at a time that is not during the usual hours of business or work.

Chinesesense: 住在一幢房子里的人;一家人；
用于餐饮场所的名称餐厅，馆，屋；
尤用于出版、借贷或服装设计等公司的名称公司，商行；
用于办公楼、私宅或豪宅名称大楼，大厦，大宅；
英国上或下议院；美国众议院；
英国学校中为进行体育竞赛等所划分的组，社；
贵族;名门望族；尤指王室，王族；
剧场、影院或其他娱乐场所的观众席;全体观众；
餐馆里的葡萄酒廉价佐餐的，未列入酒水单的；
(人、表演或演讲) 博得全场喝彩，引得哄堂大笑；
很快就打得火热;一见如故;一拍即合；
不出去工作而操持家务，当家；
餐馆或酒吧免费招待的；
管好自己的事;处理好自身问题；
Englishsense: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.
You can refer to all the people who live together in a house as the house.
House is used in the names of types of places where people go to eat and drink.
House is used in the names of types of companies, especially ones which publish books, lend money, or design clothes.
House is sometimes used in the names of office buildings and large private homes or expensive houses.
You can refer to the two main bodies of Britain’s parliament and the United States of America’s legislature as the House or a House.
You can refer to all the people at a debate as the house.
In a British school, a house is a group of children of different ages who compete against other groups in sports and other activities. Each house usually has a name.
A house is a family which has been or will be important for many generations, especially the family of a king or queen.
The house is the part of a theatre, cinema, or other place of entertainment where the audience sits. You can also refer to the audience at a particular performance as the house.
A restaurant’s house wine is the cheapest wine it sells, which is not listed by name on the wine list.
To house someone means to provide a house or flat for them to live in.
A building or container that houses something is the place where it is located or from where it operates.
If you say that a building houses a number of people, you mean that is the place where they live or where they are staying.
If a person or their performance or speech brings the house down, the audience claps, laughs, or shouts loudly because the performance or speech is very impressive or amusing.
If two people get on like a house on fire, they quickly become close friends, for example because they have many interests in common.
If you keep house, you do the cleaning and cooking for your household, and do not go out to work.
If you are given something in a restaurant or bar on the house, you do not have to pay for it.
If someone gets their house in order, puts their house in order, or sets their house in order, they arrange their affairs and solve their problems.

Chinesesense: 家庭;一家人;同住一幢房子的人；
家喻户晓的;众人皆知的；
用于王室警卫队名称中皇家的；
Englishsense: A household is all the people in a family or group who live together in a house.
The household is your home and everything that is connected with looking after it.

If you suddenly have an inspiration, you suddenly think of an idea of what to do or say.

Instability is the quality of being unstable.
If you install a piece of equipment, you fit it or put it somewhere so that it is ready to be used.
If someone is installed in a new job or important position, they are officially given the job or position, often in a special ceremony.

If you do something at someone’s instance, you do it because they have ordered or requested you to do it.

Chinesesense: (食品)已配制好的，调制快速方便的，速溶的；

If you have an instinct for something, you are naturally good at it or able to do it.
If it is your instinct to do something, you feel that it is right to do it.
Instinct is a feeling that you have that something is the case, rather than an opinion or idea based on facts.

If you instruct someone to do something, you formally tell them to do it.

An instruction is something that someone tells you to do.

Instructions are clear and detailed information on how to do something.
Instructional books or films are meant to teach people something or to offer them help with a particular problem.

Something that is an instrument for achieving a particular aim is used by people to achieve that aim.

The interpreter of something such as a piece of music is the person who performs it.
You use interpretive to describe something that provides an interpretation.
An interrogation is the act of interrogating someone.
If you interrupt someone who is speaking, you say or do something that causes them to stop.
If someone or something interrupts a process or activity, they stop it for a period of time.
If something interrupts a line, surface, or view, it stops it from being continuous or makes it look irregular.

If things are placed at particular intervals, there are spaces of a particular size between them.
If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

If an event intervenes, it happens suddenly in a way that stops, delays, or prevents something from happening.
Intervention is the act of intervening in a situation.

An interviewer is a person who is asking someone questions at an interview.

Intimacies are things that you say or do to someone you have a very close personal relationship with.
