Chinesesense: 不重要的;不严重的；次要的；
(疾病)不严重的，轻微的;(手术)小的；
未成年人(在英国和美国多数州指未满18岁的人，在法律上仍然视为儿童)；
(美国大学学科中的)辅修科目，辅修课程；
Englishsense: You use minor when you want to describe something that is less important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.
A minor illness or operation is not likely to be dangerous to someone’s life or health.
In European music, a minor scale is one in which the third note is three semitones higher than the first.
A minor is a person who is still legally a child. In Britain and most states in the United States, people are minors until they reach the age of eighteen.
At a university or college in the United States, a student’s minor is a subject that they are studying in addition to their main subject, or major.
At a university or college in the United States, if a student is, for example, a geology minor, they are studying geology as well as their main subject.
If a student at a university or college in the United States minors in a particular subject, they study it in addition to their main subject.
If you talk about a minority of people or things in a larger group, you are referring to a number of them that forms less than half of the larger group, usually much less than half.
A minority is a group of people of the same race, culture, or religion who live in a place where most of the people around them are of a different race, culture, or religion.
Mint is a herb with fresh-tasting leaves.
A mint is a sweet with a peppermint flavour. Some people suck mints in order to make their breath smell fresher.
The mint is the place where the official coins of a country are made.
To mint coins or medals means to make them in a mint.
If you say that someone makes a mint, you mean that they make a very large amount of money.
If you say that something is in mint condition, you mean that it is in perfect condition.
You use minus to show that one number or quantity is being subtracted from another.
Minus before a number or quantity means that the number or quantity is less than zero.
To be minus something means not to have that thing.
A minus is a disadvantage.
You use plus or minus to give the amount by which a particular number may vary.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 最后关头; 最后一刻；
下一刻(强调事情发生得很突然)；
非常细小的;十分微小的；
Englishsense: A minute is one of the sixty parts that an hour is divided into. People often say ’ a minute ’ or ’ minutes ’ when they mean a short length of time.
The minutes of a meeting are the written records of the things that are discussed or decided at it.
When someone minutes something that is discussed or decided at a meeting, they make a written record of it.
People often use expressions such as wait a minute or just a minute when they want to stop you doing or saying something.
If you say that something will or may happen at any minute or any minute now, you are emphasizing that it is likely to happen very soon.
If you say that you do not believe for a minute or for one minute that something is true, you are emphasizing that you do not believe that it is true.
A last-minute action is one that is done at the latest time possible.
You use the expression the next minute or expressions such as ’ one minute he was there, the next he was gone’ to emphasize that something happens suddenly.
If you say that something happens the minute something else happens, you are emphasizing that it happens immediately after the other thing.
If you say that something must be done this minute, you are emphasizing that it must be done immediately.
If you say that something is minute, you mean that it is very small.

Chinesesense: (药物或产品)神奇的，不可思议的；
Englishsense: If you say that a good event is a miracle, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.
A miracle drug or product does something that was thought almost impossible.
A miracle is a wonderful and surprising event that is believed to be caused by God.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 神奇的;奇迹般的;不可思议的；
Englishsense: If you describe a good event as miraculous, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.
If someone describes a wonderful event as miraculous, they believe that the event was caused by God.
A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.
If something mirrors something else, it has similar features to it, and therefore seems like a copy or representation of it.
If you see something reflected in water, you can say that the water mirrors it.

Chinesesense: 错误观念;错误看法;误解；
Englishsense: A misconception is an idea that is not correct.

Chinesesense: (尤指专业人员的)渎职，不端行为，不当行为；
Englishsense: Misconduct is bad or unacceptable behaviour, especially by a professional person.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (地方、形势)令人难受的，令人抑郁的；
脾气坏的;不友善的;乖戾的；
远远不足的;非常差劲的;少得可怜的；
Englishsense: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.
If you describe a place or situation as miserable, you mean that it makes you feel unhappy or depressed.
If you describe the weather as miserable, you mean that it makes you feel depressed, because it is raining or dull.
If you describe someone as miserable, you mean that you do not like them because they are bad-tempered or unfriendly.
You can describe a quantity or quality as miserable when you think that it is much smaller or worse than it ought to be.
A miserable failure is a very great one.

Chinesesense: 牢骚满腹者;爱抱怨的人；
使生活痛苦;使日子不好过；
(告诉某人其急于想知道的事)消除…的忧虑；
将(动物)人工致死以结束其痛苦；
Englishsense: Misery is great unhappiness.
Misery is the way of life and unpleasant living conditions of people who are very poor.
If you say that someone is a misery, you are critical of them because they are always com-plaining.
If someone makes your life a misery, they behave in an unpleasant way towards you over a period of time and make you very unhappy.
If you put someone out of their misery, you tell them something that they are very anxious to know.
If you put an animal out of its misery, you kill it because it is sick or injured and cannot be cured or healed.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (观点、计划)受错误思想引导的；人被错误地引导的，被引入歧途的；
Englishsense: If you describe an opinion or plan as misguided, you are critical of it because you think it is based on an incorrect idea. You can also describe people as misguided.

Chinesesense: 误导;使误信;欺骗;将…引入歧途；
Englishsense: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 误导性的;迷惑性的；欺骗性的；
Englishsense: If you describe something as misleading, you mean that it gives you a wrong idea or impression.

Chinesesense: 小姐(用于女孩或未婚女子的姓名前面)；
小姐(一些学校里孩子对女教师的称呼)；
女士，小姐(有时用于称呼年轻女子)；
小姐，皇后(用于地名或地区前，表示某地选美比赛中的冠军)；
未注意到;未觉察到;忽略掉；
不理解，没有领会(意义或重要性)；
Englishsense: You use Miss in front of the name of a girl or unmarried woman when you are speaking to her or referring to her.
In some schools, children address their women teachers as Miss.
People sometimes address young women as Miss.
Miss is used in front of the name of a place or region to refer to the young woman who has been chosen in a competition as the most beautiful woman there.
If you miss something, you fail to hit it, for example when you have thrown something at it or you have shot a bullet at it.
In sport, if you miss a shot, you fail to get the ball in the goal, net, or hole.
If you miss something, you fail to notice it.
If you miss the meaning or importance of something, you fail to understand or appreciate it.
If you miss a chance or opportunity, you fail to take advantage of it.
If you miss someone who is no longer with you or who has died, you feel sad and wish that they were still with you.
If you miss something, you feel sad because you no longer have it or are no longer doing or experiencing it.
If you miss something such as a plane or train, you arrive too late to catch it.
If you miss something such as a meeting or an activity, you do not go to it or take part in it.
If you give something a miss, you decide not to do it or not to go to it.

Chinesesense: 作为武器的投掷物，抛掷物，发射物；
Englishsense: A missile is a tube-shaped weapon that travels long distances through the air and explodes when it reaches its target.
Anything that is thrown as a weapon can be called a missile.

Chinesesense: 被去除的；缺损的；缺掉的；
Englishsense: If something is missing, it is not in its usual place, and you cannot find it.
If a part of something is missing, it has been removed or has come off, and has not been replaced.
If you say that something is missing, you mean that it has not been included, and you think that it should have been.
Someone who is missing cannot be found, and it is not known whether they are alive or dead.

Chinesesense: (尤指赴他国的)使命，重要任务；
军用飞机或航天火箭的飞行任务；
Englishsense: A mission is an important task that people are given to do, especially one that involves travelling to another country.
A mission is a group of people who have been sent to a foreign country to carry out an official task.
A mission is a special journey made by a military aeroplane or space rocket.
If you say that you have a mission, you mean that you have a strong commitment and sense of duty to do or achieve something.
A mission is the activities of a group of Christians who have been sent to a place to teach people about Christianity.
A mission is a building or group of buildings in which missionary work is carried out.
A missionary is a Christian who has been sent to a foreign country to teach people about Christianity.
Missionary is used to describe the activities of missionaries.
If you refer to someone’s enthusiasm for an activity or belief as missionary zeal, you are emphasizing that they are very enthusiastic about it.

Chinesesense: 眼睛因泪水而变得模糊不清；
Englishsense: Mist consists of a large number of tiny drops of water in the air, which make it difficult to see very far.
If a piece of glass mists or is misted, it becomes covered with tiny drops of moisture, so that you cannot see through it easily.
If someone’s eyes mist, they cannot see easily because there are tears in their eyes.

Chinesesense: 搞错;把…误认为；把…错当成；
Englishsense: If you make a mistake, you do something which you did not intend to do, or which produces a result that you do not want.
A mistake is something or part of something which is incorrect or not right.
If you mistake one person or thing for another, you wrongly think that they are the other person or thing.
If you mistake something, you fail to recognize or understand it.
You can say there is no mistaking something when you are emphasizing that you cannot fail to recognize or understand it.

Chinesesense: 绝对控制…的女人；主宰…的女人；
(精通某项活动的)女能手，女行家；
Englishsense: A married man’s mistress is a woman who is not his wife and with whom he is having a sexual relationship.
A mistress is a female teacher.
A servant’s mistress is the woman that he or she works for.
A dog’s mistress is the woman or girl who owns it.
If a woman is mistress of a situation, she has complete control over it.
If you say that a woman is a mistress of a particular activity, you mean that she is very skilled at it.
If you misunderstand someone or something, you do not understand them properly.
A misunderstanding is a failure to understand something properly, for example a situation or a person’s remarks.
You can refer to a disagreement or slight quarrel as a misunderstanding.
To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

Chinesesense: (制作糕点、调味汁等的)混合原料，混合配料；
经常大吵大闹，动不动就大打出手(美国英语用 mix it up)；
Englishsense: If two substances mix or if you mix one substance with another, you stir or shake them together, or combine them in some other way, so that they become a single substance.
If you mix something, you prepare it by mixing other things together.
A mix is a powder containing all the substances that you need in order to make something such as a cake or a sauce. When you want to use it, you add liquid.
A mix of different things or people is two or more of them together.
If two things or activities do not mix or if one thing does not mix with another, it is not a good idea to have them or do them together, because the result would be unpleasant or dangerous.
If you mix with other people, you meet them and talk to them. You can also say that people mix.
When a record producer mixes a piece of music, he or she puts together the various sounds that have been recorded in order to make the finished record.
If you say that someone mixes it, or in American English mixes it up, you mean that they often fight or argue strongly about things. [V inflects] [Informal] ]

Englishsense: If you have mixed feelings about something or someone, you feel uncertain about them because you can see both good and bad points about them.
A mixed group of people consists of people of many different types.
Mixed is used to describe something that involves people from two or more different races.
Mixed education or accommodation is intended for both males and females.
Mixed is used to describe something which includes or consists of different things of the same general kind.
A mixer is a machine used for mixing things together.
A mixer is a non-alcoholic drink such as fruit juice that you mix with strong alcohol such as gin.
If you say that someone is a good mixer, you mean that they are good at talking to people and making friends.
A mixer is a piece of equipment that is used to make changes to recorded music or film.
A mixture of things consists of several different things together.
A mixture is a substance that consists of other substances which have been stirred or shaken together.
If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.
To moan means to complain or speak in a way which shows that you are very unhappy.
A moan is a complaint.
If you have a moan, you complain about something.
A moan is a low noise.

Chinesesense: 大众[含贬义]; 尤指愤怒暴乱的群众；
Englishsense: A mob is a large, disorganized, and often violent crowd of people.
People sometimes use the mob to refer in a disapproving way to the majority of people in a country or place, especially when these people are behaving in a violent or uncontrolled way.
You can refer to the people involved in organized crime as the Mob.
If you say that someone is being mobbed by a crowd of people, you mean that the people are trying to talk to them or get near them in an enthusiastic or threatening way.

(社会)流动性的;(在职业、住所或社会阶层间)自由流动的；
(悬挂在天花板上的)风动小饰物；
Englishsense: You use mobile to describe something large that can be moved easily from place to place.
If you are mobile, you can move or travel easily from place to place, for example because you are not physically disabled or because you have your own transport.
In a mobile society, people move easily from one job, home, or social class to another.
If someone has a mobile face, the expression on their face changes quickly as their feelings change.
A mobile is a decoration which you hang from a ceiling. It usually consists of several small objects which move as the air around them moves.
A mobile is the same as a mobile phone.

Chinesesense: 动员;鼓动;召集；人们动员起来；
(国家或军队)动员起来;动员(军队)；
Englishsense: If you mobilize support or mobilize people to do something, you succeed in encouraging people to take action, especially political action. If people mobilize, they prepare to take action.
If you mobilize resources, you start to use them or make them available for use.
If a country mobilizes, or mobilizes its armed forces, or if its armed forces mobilize, they are given orders to prepare for a conflict.
If someone mocks you, they show or pretend that they think you are foolish or inferior, for example by saying something funny about you, or by imitating your behaviour.
You use mock to describe something which is not real or genuine, but which is intended to be very similar to the real thing.
Mocks are practice exams that you take as part of your preparation for real exams.

Chinesesense: 艺术、着装等的风格、文体；
(照相机、电子设备的)模式，状态；
Englishsense: A mode of life or behaviour is a particular way of living or behaving.
A mode is a particular style in art, literature, or dress.
On some cameras or electronic devices, the different modes available are the different programs or settings that you can choose when you use them.

Chinesesense: 创立(系统或过程) 的[理论描述)模型；
按特定模型制造;仿特定样式做出；
(用黏土、木头等)做…的模型;塑造；
Englishsense: A model of an object is a physical representation that shows what it looks like or how it works. The model is often smaller than the object it represents.
A model is a system that is being used and that people might want to copy in order to achieve similar results.
A model of a system or process is a theoretical description that can help you understand how the system or process works, or how it might work.
If someone such as a scientist models a system or process, they make an accurate theoretical description of it in order to understand or explain how it works.
If you say that someone or something is a model of a particular quality, you are showing approval of them because they have that quality to a large degree.
You use model to express approval of someone when you think that they perform their role or duties extremely well.
If one thing is modelled on another, the first thing is made so that it is like the second thing in some way.
If you model yourself on someone, you copy the way that they do things, because you admire them and want to be like them.
A particular model of a machine is a particular version of it. See usage note at: brand
An artist’s model is a person who stays still in a particular position so that the artist can make a picture or sculpture of them.
If someone models for an artist, they stay still in a particular position so that the artist can make a picture or sculpture of them.
A fashion model is a person whose job is to display clothes by wearing them.
If someone models clothes, they display them by wearing them.
If you model shapes or figures, you make them out of a substance such as clay or wood.
A modem is a device which uses a telephone line to connect computers or computer systems.

Englishsense: Moderate political opinions or policies are not extreme.
You use moderate to describe people or groups who have moderate political opinions or policies.
You use moderate to describe something that is neither large nor small in amount or degree.
A moderate change in something is a change that is not great.
If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent and easier to deal with or accept.

Something that is modern is new and involves the latest ideas or equipment.
People are sometimes described as modern when they have opinions or ways of behaviour that have not yet been accepted by most people in a society.
Modern is used to describe styles of art, dance, music, and architecture that have developed in recent times, in contrast to classical styles.

Chinesesense: 现代主义的;现代派的；现代风格的；
Englishsense: Modernist means relating to the ideas and methods of modern art.

You use modest to describe something such as an amount, rate, or improvement which is fairly small.
If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.
You can describe a woman as modest when she avoids doing or wearing anything that might cause men to have sexual feelings towards her. You can also describe her clothes or behaviour as modest.
If you modify something, you change it slightly, usually in order to improve it.
A word or group of words that modifies another word describes or classifies something, or restricts the meaning of the word.

Chinesesense: 建筑物中的构件，组件，模块；
(机器的)组件，部件;(尤指计算机的)模块，程序块；
Englishsense: A module is one of the separate parts of a course taught at a college or university.
A module is a part of a spacecraft which can operate by itself, often away from the rest of the spacecraft.
A module is one of a set of parts from which some buildings are made. Each module is made separately, and the completed modules are then joined together to form the building.
A module is a part of a machine, especially a computer, which performs a particular function.

Chinesesense: 莫卧儿人(16至18世纪印度的穆斯林统治者)；
(尤指新闻、影视业的)有权势的富商，大人物，大亨；
Englishsense: A Mogul was a Muslim ruler in India in the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries.
A mogul is an important, rich, and powerful businessman, especially one in the news, film, or television industry.

Englishsense: Something that is moist is slightly wet.
Moisture is tiny drops of water in the air, on a surface, or in the ground.
A mole is a natural dark spot or small dark lump on someone’s skin.
A mole is a small animal with black fur that lives underground.
A mole is a member of a government or other organization who gives secret information to the press or to a rival organization.
Molecular means relating to or involving molecules.
A molecule is the smallest amount of a chemical substance which can exist by itself.
Your mom is your mother.

Chinesesense: 有成功(或得意)的时刻；有吸引人的时刻；
下一刻，一会儿，紧接着尤指突然发生很大变化；
Englishsense: You can refer to a very short period of time, for example a few seconds, as a moment or moments.
A particular moment is the point in time at which something happens.
If you say that something will or may happen at any moment or any moment now, you are emphasizing that it is likely to happen very soon.
You use expressions such as at the moment, at this moment, and at the present moment to indicate that a particular situation exists at the time when you are speaking.
If you say that you do not believe for a moment or for one moment that something is true, you are emphasizing that you do not believe that it could possibly be true.
You use for the moment to indicate that something is true now, even if it will not be true in the future.
If you say that someone or something has their moments, you are indicating that there are times when they are successful or interesting, but that this does not happen very often.
If someone does something at the last moment, they do it at the latest time possible.

You use the expression the next moment, or expressions such as ’ one moment he was there, the next he was gone’, to emphasize that something happens suddenly, especially when it is very different from what was happening before.

You use of the moment to describe someone or something that is or was especially popular at a particular time, especially when you want to suggest that their popularity is unlikely to last long or did not last long.
If you say that something happens the moment something else happens, you are emphasizing that it happens immediately after the other thing.
Momentarily means for a short time.
Momentarily means very soon.
If a process or movement gains momentum, it keeps developing or happening more quickly and keeps becoming less likely to stop.
In physics, momentum is the mass of a moving object multiplied by its speed in a particular direction.
The monarch of a country is the king, queen, emperor, or empress.
A monarchy is a system in which a country has a monarch.
A monarchy is a country that has a monarch.
The monarchy is used to refer to the monarch and his or her family.
A monastery is a building or collection of buildings in which monks live.

Chinesesense: 尤指一国货币的，金融的；
Englishsense: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

Chinesesense: 有花不完的钱;钱多得烫手;钱多得烧包；
非常有钱的;手头宽裕的；
用行动证明自己的话；说到做到;说给钱就给钱；
(因掌握内情而下的)高明赌注；
金钱万能;有钱能使鬼推磨；
花钱填无底洞;继续砸钱；
钱花得值;物有所值；没白忙活；
Englishsense: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the sum that you have in a bank account.
Monies is used to refer to several separate sums of money that form part of a larger amount that is received or spent.
If you say that someone has money to burn, you mean that they have more money than they need or that they spend their money on things that you think are unnecessary.
If you are in the money, you have a lot of money to spend.
If you make money, you obtain money by earning it or by making a profit.
If you say that you want someone to put their money where their mouth is, you want them to spend money to improve a bad situation, instead of just talking about improving it.
If you say that the smart money is on a particular person or thing, you mean that people who know a lot about it think that this person will be successful, or this thing will happen.
If you say that money talks, you mean that if someone has a lot of money, they also have a lot of power.
If you say that someone is throwing money at a problem, you are critical of them for trying to improve it by spending money on it, instead of doing more thoughtful and practical things to improve it.

If you say that someone is throwing good money after bad, you are critical of them for trying to improve a bad situation by spending more money on it, instead of doing more thoughtful or practical things to improve it.
If you get your money’s worth, you get something which is worth the money that it costs or the effort you have put in. [PHR after v]

Chinesesense: 监听(外国无线电广播等)；
Englishsense: If you monitor something, you regularly check its development or progress, and sometimes comment on it.
If someone monitors radio broadcasts from other countries, they record them or listen carefully to them in order to obtain information.
A monitor is a machine that is used to check or record things, for example processes or substances inside a person’s body.
A monitor is a screen which is used to display certain kinds of information, for example in airports or television studios.
You can refer to a person who checks that something is done correctly, or that it is fair, as a monitor.
A monk is a member of a male religious community that is usually separated from the outside world.
A monkey is an animal with a long tail which lives in hot countries and climbs trees.
If you refer to a child as a monkey, you are saying in an affectionate way that he or she is very lively and naughty.
If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.
A monopoly is a company which is the only one providing a particular product or service.
If you say that someone does not have a monopoly on something, you mean that they are not the only person who has that thing.

Chinesesense: 庞然大物;棘手的大事情；
残忍的人;吓人的人;恶人；
Englishsense: A monster is a large imaginary creature that looks very ugly and frightening.
A monster is something which is extremely large, especially something which is difficult to manage or which is unpleasant.
Monster means extremely and surprisingly large.
If you describe someone as a monster, you mean that they are cruel, frightening, or evil.
A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.
A month is a period of about four weeks.
A monthly event or publication happens or appears every month.
You can refer to a publication that is published monthly as a monthly.
Monthly quantities or rates relate to a period of one month.
A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an event in history or of a famous person.
A monument is something such as a castle or bridge which was built a very long time ago and is regarded as an important part of a country’s history.
If you describe something as a monument to someone’s qualities, you mean that it is a very good example of the results or effects of those qualities.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: (书或音乐)丰碑式的，意义深远的，不朽的；
Englishsense: You can use monumental to emphasize the size or extent of something.
If you describe a book or musical work as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, and is likely to be important for a long time.
A monumental building or sculpture is very large and impressive.
Your mood is the way you are feeling at a particular time. If you are in a good mood, you feel cheerful. If you are in a bad mood, you feel angry and impatient.
If someone is in a mood, the way they are behaving shows that they are feeling angry and impatient.
The mood of a group of people is the way that they think and feel about an idea, event, or question at a particular time.
The mood of a place is the general impression that you get of it.
In grammar, the mood of a clause is the way in which the verb forms are used to show whether the clause is, for example, a statement, a question, or an instruction.

Chinesesense: 虚度光阴;懒散度日;闲逛；
非常高兴;乐翻了天;狂喜；
Englishsense: The moon is the object that you can often see in the sky at night. It goes round the Earth once every four weeks, and as it does so its appearance changes from a circle to part of a circle.
A moon is an object similar to a small planet that travels around a planet.
If you are mooning around, you are spending time doing nothing in particular, for example because you feel unhappy or lazy, or are worried about something.
If you moon at someone, you turn your back to them and show them your bare bottom.
If you say that something happens once in a blue moon, you are emphasizing that it does not happen very often at all.
If you say that you are over the moon, you mean that you are very pleased about something.

Chinesesense: 兼职,从事第二职业(尤指不为专职工作的老板和税收部门所知)；
Englishsense: Moonlight is the light that comes from the moon at night.
If someone moonlights, they have a second job in addition to their main job, often without informing their main employers or the tax office.

Chinesesense: 麋(出现在北欧、亚洲和北美的一种大型鹿，头上长有大而扁的鹿角。一些英国人用该词指北美亚种，用 elk 指欧洲和亚洲亚种)；
Englishsense: A moose is a large type of deer. Moose have big flat horns called antlers and are found in Northern Europe, Asia, and North America. Some British speakers use moose to refer to the North American variety of this animal, and elk to refer to the European and Asian varieties.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 勇气或职责道义上的;基于道德规范的；
(由故事、事件引出的)道德训诫，寓意；
Englishsense: Morals are principles and beliefs concerning right and wrong behaviour.
Moral means relating to beliefs about what is right or wrong.
Moral courage or duty is based on what you believe is right or acceptable, rather than on what the law says should be done.
A moral person behaves in a way that is believed by most people to be good and right.
If you give someone moral support, you encourage them in what they are doing by expressing approval.
The moral of a story or event is what you learn from it about how you should or should not behave.
Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

Chinesesense: 道义准则;道德规范;伦理学；
Englishsense: Morality is the belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable and that other behaviour is wrong.
A morality is a system of principles and values concerning people’s behaviour, which is generally accepted by a society or by a particular group of people.
The morality of something is how right or acceptable it is.

Chinesesense: 更多;较多(该词前可使用 a little，a lot，a bit，far和much)；
更像前者地;与其说是…，倒不如说是；
另外的;附加的(该词前可使用 a little，a lot，a bit，far 和 much)；
(用于 no more，no less, neither more nor less 等短语中，表示所说完全无误)多了的部分；
更有甚者;更为重要的是;此外；
Englishsense: You use more to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use ’a little’, ’a lot’, ’a bit’, ’far’, and ’much’ in front of more.

A military offensive is a carefully planned attack made by a large group of soldiers.

In sports such as American football or basketball, the offensive team is the team which has possession of the ball and is trying to score.
If you go on the offensive, go over to the offensive, or take the offensive, you begin to take strong action against people who have been attacking you.

Englishsense: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.
If you offer to do something, you say that you are willing to do it.
An offer is something that someone says they will give you or do for you.
If you offer someone information, advice, or praise, you give it to them, usually because you feel that they need it or deserve it.
If you offer someone something such as love or friendship, you show them that you feel that way towards them.
If people offer prayers, praise, or a sacrifice to God or a god, they speak to or give something to their god.
If an organization offers something such as a service or product, it provides it.
An offer in a shop is a specially low price for a specific product or something extra that you get if you buy a certain product.
If you offer a particular amount of money for something, you say that you will pay that much to buy it.
An offer is the amount of money that someone says they will pay to buy something or give to someone because they have harmed them in some way.
If you have something to offer, you have a quality or ability that makes you important, attractive, or useful.
If there is something on offer, it is available to be used or bought.
If you are open to offers, you are willing to do something if someone will pay you an amount of money that you think is reasonable.
An offering is something that is specially produced to be sold.
An offering is a gift that people offer to their God or gods as a form of worship.

Englishsense: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.
An office is a department of an organization, especially the government, where people deal with a particular kind of administrative work.
An office is a small building or room where people can go for information, tickets, or a service of some kind.
A doctor’s or dentist’s office is a place where a doctor or dentist sees their patients.
If someone holds office in a government, they have an important job or position of authority.
Someone’s good offices are the help that they give to other people who are trying to achieve something.

Chinesesense: 机构的高级职员；尤指政府机构的官员，公务员；
Englishsense: In the armed forces, an officer is a person in a position of authority.
An officer is a person who has a responsible position in an organization, especially a government organization.
Members of the police force can be referred to as officers.

官员；行政人员；高级职员；

Englishsense: Official means approved by the government or by someone in authority.
Official activities are carried out by a person in authority as part of their job.
Official things are used by a person in authority as part of their job.
If you describe someone’s explanation or reason for something as the official explanation, you are suggesting that it is probably not true, but is used because the real explanation is embarrassing.
An official is a person who holds a position of authority in an organization.
An official at a sports event is a referee, umpire, or other person who checks that the players follow the rules.
If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

Chinesesense: 投资或公司设在海外尤指税制较宽松的岛屿的,离岸的；
Englishsense: Offshore means situated or happening in the sea, near to the coast.
An offshore wind blows from the land towards the sea.
Offshore investments or companies are located in a place, usually an island, which has fewer tax regulations than most other countries.

Chinesesense: 孩子；子女；后代；动物的崽；
Englishsense: You can refer to a person’s children or to an animal’s young as their offspring.

Chinesesense: 用于询问或说明某事发生的频率多常；
Englishsense: If something often happens, it happens many times or much of the time.
You use how often to ask questions about frequency. You also use often in reported clauses and other statements to give information about the frequency of something.
If something happens every so often, it happens regularly, but with fairly long intervals between each occasion.

If you say that something happens as often as not, or more often than not, you mean that it happens fairly frequently, and that this can be considered as typical of the kind of situation you are talking about.

Chinesesense: 表示惊讶、痛苦、恼怒或喜悦等唉，啊，呀，哈；
Englishsense: You use oh to introduce a response or a comment on something that has just been said.
You use oh to express a feeling such as surprise, pain, annoyance, or happiness.
You use oh when you are hesitating while speaking, for example because you are trying to estimate something, or because you are searching for the right word.

Chinesesense: 使…顺利进行；使…正常运作；
Englishsense: Oil is a smooth, thick liquid that is used as a fuel and for making the parts of machines move smoothly. Oil is found underground.
If you oil something, you put oil onto or into it, for example to make it work smoothly or to protect it.
Oil is a smooth, thick liquid made from plants and is often used for cooking.
Oil is a smooth, thick liquid, often with a pleasant smell, that you rub into your skin or add to your bath.
Oils are oil paintings.
When an artist paints in oils, he or she uses oil paints.
If you pour oil on troubled waters, you try to calm down a difficult situation.
If someone or something oils the wheels of a process or system, they help things to run smoothly and successfully.

Chinesesense: 表示令人满意或可以接受不错的，可以的；
人安全的，健康的，无恙的；
询问对方是否领会或同意好吗，行吗，明白吗；
表示希望转换话题或做别的事情好了；
不情愿地表示接受对方观点以制止其争辩得了，行了；
Englishsense: If you say that something is okay, you find it satisfactory or acceptable.
If you say that someone is okay, you mean that they are safe and well.
You can say ’ Okay ’ to show that you agree to something.
You can say ’ Okay? ’ to check whether the person you are talking to understands what you have said and accepts it.
You can use okay to indicate that you want to start talking about something else or doing something else.
You can use okay to stop someone arguing with you by showing that you accept the point they are making, though you do not necessarily regard it as very important.
If someone in authority okays something, they officially agree to it or allow it to happen.

Englishsense: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.
You use old to talk about how many days, weeks, months, or years someone or something has lived or existed.
Something that is old has existed for a long time.
Something that is old is no longer in good condition because of its age or because it has been used a lot.
You use old to refer to something that is no longer used, that no longer exists, or that has been replaced by something else.
You use old to refer to something that used to belong to you, or to a person or thing that used to have a particular role in your life.
An old friend, enemy, or rival is someone who has been your friend, enemy, or rival for a long time.
You can use old to express affection when talking to or about someone you know.
You use any old to emphasize that the quality or type of something is not important. If you say that a particular thing is not any old thing, you are emphasizing how special or famous it is.
In the old days means in the past, before things changed.
When people refer to the good old days, they are referring to a time in the past when they think that life was better than it is now.
If you talk about people or things of old, you are referring to people or things that existed long ago but which no longer exist, or no longer exist in the same form.

Chinesesense: 皮肤橄榄色的，浅褐色的；
Englishsense: Olives are small green or black fruit with a bitter taste. Olives are often pressed to make olive oil.
An olive tree or an olive is a tree on which olives grow.
Something that is olive is yellowish-green in colour.
If someone has olive skin, the colour of their skin is light brown.

奥林匹克运动会；奥运会；

The Olympics are the Olympic Games.

Englishsense: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.
If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.
If you omit to do something, you do not do it.

Englishsense: If someone or something is on a surface or object, the surface or object is immediately below them and is supporting their weight.
If something is on a surface or object, it is stuck to it or attached to it.
If you put, throw, or drop something on a surface, you move it or drop it so that it is then supported by the surface.
You use on to say what part of your body is supporting your weight.
You use on to say that someone or something touches a part of a person’s body.
If someone has a particular expression on their face, their face has that expression.
When you put a piece of clothing on, you place it over part of your body in order to wear it. If you have it on, you are wearing it.
You can say that you have something on you if you are carrying it in your pocket or in a bag.
If someone’s eyes are on you, they are looking or staring at you.
If you hurt yourself on something, you accidentally hit a part of your body against it and that thing causes damage to you.
If you are on an area of land, you are there.
If something is situated on a place such as a road or coast, it forms part of it or is by the side of it.
If you get on a bus, train, or plane, you go into it in order to travel somewhere. If you are on it, you are travelling in it.
If there is something on a piece of paper, it has been written or printed there.
If something is on a list, it is included in it.
Books, discussions, or ideas on a particular subject are concerned with that subject.
You use on to introduce the method, principle, or system which is used to do something.
If something is done on an instrument or a machine, it is done using that instrument or machine.
If information is, for example, on tape or on computer, that is the way that it is stored.
If something is being broadcast, you can say that it is on the radio or television.
When an activity is taking place, you can say that it is on.
You use on in expressions such as ’ have a lot on ’ and ’ not have very much on ’ to indicate how busy someone is.
You use on to introduce an activity that someone is doing, particularly travelling.
When something such as a machine or an electric light is on, it is functioning or in use. When you switch it on, it starts functioning.
If you are on a committee or council, you are a member of it.
You can indicate when something happens by saying that it happens on a particular day or date.
You use on when mentioning an event that was followed by another one.
You use on to say that someone is continuing to do something.
If you say that someone goes on at you, you mean that they continually criticize you, complain to you, or ask you to do something.
You use on in expressions such as from now on and from then on to indicate that something starts to happen at the time mentioned and continues to happen afterwards.
You often use on after the adverbs ’early’, ’late’, ’far’, and their comparative forms, especially at the beginning or end of a sentence, or before a preposition.
Someone who is on a drug takes it regularly.
If you live on a particular kind of food, you eat it. If a machine runs on a particular kind of power or fuel, it uses it in order to function.
If you are on a particular income, that is the income that you have.
Taxes or profits that are obtained from something are referred to as taxes or profits on it.
When you buy something or pay for something, you spend money on it.
When you spend time or energy on a particular activity, you spend time or energy doing it.
If you say that something is not on or is just not on, you mean that it is unacceptable or impossible.
If you say that something happens on and on, you mean that it continues to happen for a very long time.
If you ask someone what they are on about or what they are going on about, you are puzzled because you cannot understand what they are talking about.
If you say that someone knows what they are on about, you are confident that what they are saying is true or makes sense, for example because they are an expert.
If someone has something on you, they have evidence that you have done something wrong or bad. If they have nothing on you, they cannot prove that you have done anything wrong or bad.

Englishsense: If something happens once, it happens one time only.
You use once with ’a’ and words like ’day’, ’week’, and ’month’ to indicate that something happens regularly, one time in each day, week, or month.
You use once with ’every’ and words like ’day’, ’week’, and ’year’ to indicate that something happens a specified number of times and on a regular basis.
If something was once true, it was true at some time in the past, but is no longer true.
If someone once did something, they did it at some time in the past.
If something happens once another thing has happened, it happens immediately afterwards.
If something happens all at once, it happens suddenly, often when you are not expecting it to happen.
If you do something at once, you do it immediately.
If a number of different things happen at once or all at once, they all happen at the same time.
For once is used to emphasize that something happens on this particular occasion, especially if it has never happened before, and may never happen again.
If something happens once again or once more, it happens again.
If something happens once and for all, it happens completely or finally.
If something happens once in a while, it happens sometimes, but not very often.
If you have done something once or twice, you have done it a few times, but not very often.
Once upon a time is used to indicate that something happened or existed a long time ago or in an imaginary world. It is often used at the beginning of children’s stories.

Englishsense: One is the number 1.
If you say that someone or something is the one person or thing of a particular kind, you are emphasizing that they are the only person or thing of that kind.
One can be used instead of ’a’ to emphasize the following noun.
You can use one instead of ’a’ to emphasize the following adjective or expression.
You can use one in front of someone’s name to indicate that you have not met them or heard of them before.
You can use one to refer to the first of two or more things that you are comparing.
You can use one or ones instead of a noun when it is clear what type of thing or person you are referring to and you are describing them or giving more information about them.
You use ones to refer to people in general.
You can use one instead of a noun group when you have just mentioned something and you want to describe it or give more information about it.
You can use one when you have been talking or writing about a group of people or things and you want to say something about a particular member of the group.

You use one in expressions such as ’ one of the biggest airports ’ or ’ one of the most experienced players ’ to indicate that something or someone is bigger or more experienced than most other things or people of the same kind.
You can use one when referring to a time in the past or in the future. For example, if you say that you did something one day, you mean that you did it on a day in the past. one day
You can use one to refer to a question, joke, remark, or subject of discussion.
You can use one to refer to an alcoholic drink.
You use one to make statements about people in general which also apply to themselves. One can be used as the subject or object of a sentence.
If a group of people does something as one, all the people do the same thing at the same time or in the same way.
If you say that someone is one for or is a one for something, you mean that they like or approve of it or enjoy doing it.
You can use for one to emphasize that a particular person is definitely reacting or behaving in a particular way, even if other people are not.
You can use expressions such as a hundred and one, a thousand and one, and a million and one to emphasize that you are talking about a large number of things or people.
You can use in one to indicate that something is a single unit, but is made up of several different parts or has several different functions.
You can use in ones and twos to indicate that people do things or something happens gradually and in small groups.
You use one after the other or one after another to say that actions or events happen with very little time between them.
The one and only can be used in front of the name of an actor, singer, or other famous person when they are being introduced on a show.
You can use one by one to indicate that people do things or that things happen in sequence, not all at the same time.
You use one or other to refer to one or more things or people in a group, when it does not matter which particular one or ones are thought of or chosen.
One or two means a few.
If you say that someone is not one to do something, you think that it is very unlikely that they would do it because it is not their normal behaviour.
If you try to get one up on someone, you try to gain an advantage over them.

Chinesesense: 面对面的；一对一的；仅限两人之间的；
Englishsense: A one-on-one situation, meeting, or contest involves only two people.

Chinesesense: 用作从句中动词或代词的宾语，指代动词主语“我”或“任何人”自己，自身；
[one 虽缺失但可理解为动词主语时，用作动词或介词的宾语] 自己，自身；

Englishsense: A speaker or writer uses oneself as the object of a verb or preposition in a clause where ’oneself’ meaning ’me’ or ’any person in general’ refers to the same person as the subject of the verb.
Oneself can be used as the object of a verb or preposition, when ’one’ is not present but is understood to be the subject of the verb.
To do something oneself means to do it without any help from anyone else.
You use oneself to emphasize that something happens to you rather than to people in general.
One-time is used to describe something such as a job, position, or role which someone used to have, or something which happened in the past.

单向付出的关系；单方受益的协议；
Englishsense: In one-way streets or traffic systems, vehicles can only travel along in one direction.
One-way describes journeys which go to just one place, rather than to that place and then back again.
A one-way ticket or fare is for a journey from one place to another, but not back again.
If you say that a course of action is a one-way ticket to a place or situation, or is a one-way journey there, you are sure that it will lead to the place or situation mentioned.

One-way glass or a one-way mirror is a piece of glass which acts as a mirror when looked at from one side, but acts as a window when looked through from the other side. They are used for watching people without their knowledge.
If you describe an agreement or a relationship as a one-way street, you mean that only one of the sides in the agreement or relationship is offering something or is benefitting from it.

Chinesesense: 进行中的；不间断的；继续存在的；
Englishsense: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.
An onion is a round vegetable with a brown skin that grows underground. It has many white layers on its inside which have a strong, sharp smell and taste.

Chinesesense: 公司服务网上开通的，网上经营的；
Englishsense: If a company goes online, its services become available on the Internet.

You use only to introduce the thing which must happen before the thing mentioned in the main part of the sentence can happen.
If you talk about the only person or thing involved in a particular situation, you mean there are no others involved in it.
An only child is a child who has no brothers or sisters.

You use only to indicate that something is no more important, interesting, or difficult, for example, than you say it is, especially when you want to correct a wrong idea that someone may get or has already got.
You use only to emphasize how small an amount is or how short a length of time is.
You use only to emphasize that you are talking about a small part of an amount or group, not the whole of it.
Only is used after ’can’ or ’could’ to emphasize that it is impossible to do anything except the rather inadequate or limited action that is mentioned.
You can use only in the expressions I only wish or I only hope in order to emphasize what you are hoping or wishing.
Only can be used to add a comment which slightly changes or limits what you have just said.
Only can be used after a clause with ’would’ to indicate why something is not done.
You can use only before an infinitive to introduce an event which happens immediately after one you have just mentioned, and which is rather surprising or unfortunate.
You can use only to emphasize how appropriate a certain course of action or type of behaviour is.
You can use only in front of a verb to indicate that the result of something is unfortunate or undesirable and is likely to make the situation worse rather than better.
If you say you only have to or have only to do one thing in order to achieve or prove a second thing, you are emphasizing how easily the second thing can be achieved or proved.
You can say that something has only just happened when you want to emphasize that it happened a very short time ago.
You use only just to emphasize that something is true, but by such a small degree that it is almost not true at all. [usu PHR before v] [emphasis]
You can use only too to emphasize that something is true or exists to a much greater extent than you would expect or like.
You can say that you are only too happy to do something to emphasize how willing you are to do it.

Englishsense: The onset of something is the beginning of it, used especially to refer to something unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 家中或花园里的装饰物，装饰品，点缀品；
建筑或家具的装饰物，装饰图案；
Englishsense: An ornament is an attractive object that you display in your home or in your garden.
Pieces of jewellery are sometimes referred to as ornaments.
Decorations and patterns on a building or a piece of furniture can be referred to as ornament.
An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.
If a child is orphaned, their parents die, or their remaining parent dies.
An orphanage is a place where orphans live and are looked after.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 正统的；规范的；广为接受的；
人正统派的，传统的，循规蹈矩的；
Englishsense: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.
If you describe someone as orthodox, you mean that they hold the older and more traditional ideas of their religion or party.
The Orthodox churches are Christian churches in Eastern Europe which separated from the western church in the eleventh century.

Chinesesense: 表示在与已提及或已知的人或事物同一类中别的，其他的，另外的，额外的；
表示与已提及的人或事物不同别的，其他的；
用于列举之后其他类似的；
一组人或事物中其余的，剩下的；
除了别的以外；其中；包括；
用于强调，表示一组人或事物中其余的，剩下的；
表示无法或不想确切说明某一，某些；
用于否定陈述后除了…以外；
Englishsense: You use other to refer to an additional thing or person of the same type as one that has been mentioned or is known about.
You use other to indicate that a thing or person is not the one already mentioned, but a different one.
You use the other to refer to the second of two things or people when the identity of the first is already known or understood, or has already been mentioned.
You use other at the end of a list or a group of examples, to refer generally to people or things like the ones just mentioned.
You use the other to refer to the rest of the people or things in a group, when you are talking about one particular person or thing.
Other people are people in general, as opposed to yourself or a person you have already mentioned.
You use other in informal expressions of time such as the other day, the other evening, or the other week to refer to a day, evening, or week in the recent past.

You use expressions like among other things or among others to indicate that there are several more facts, things, or people like the one or ones mentioned, but that you do not intend to mention them all.
If something happens, for example, every other day or every other month, there is a day or month when it does not happen between each day or month when it happens.
You use every other to emphasize that you are referring to all the rest of the people or things in a group.
You use none other than and no other than to emphasize the name of a person or thing when something about that person or thing is surprising in a particular situation.
You use nothing other than and no other than when you are going to mention a course of action, decision, or description and emphasize that it is the only one possible in the situation.
You use or other in expressions like somehow or other and someone or other to indicate that you cannot or do not want to be more precise about the information that you are giving.
You use other than after a negative statement to say that the person, item, or thing that follows is the only exception to the statement.

Chinesesense: 以其他方式；用别的方法；
及其他；或相反；或其反面；
Englishsense: You use otherwise after stating a situation or fact, in order to say what the result or consequence would be if this situation or fact was not the case.
You use otherwise before stating the general condition or quality of something, when you are also mentioning an exception to this general condition or quality.
You use otherwise to refer in a general way to actions or situations that are very different from, or the opposite to, your main statement.
You use otherwise to indicate that other ways of doing something are possible in addition to the way already mentioned.
You use or otherwise or and otherwise to mention something that is not the thing just referred to or is the opposite of that thing.

Chinesesense: 认为某事道义上正确，尤用于提出或征求建议或意见应当，应该；
认为某事可行或重要，尤用于提出或征求建议或意见应当，应该；
认为某事确实，或预计某事发生或已经发生应该/应该已经；
表示某事本应如此，但实际情况未必应该；
表示从已知情况推测某事已经发生，但不确定应该；
与过去分词连用，表示预期的事未发生或预计的情况并非如此本该，本当；
与过去分词连用，表示未做本应该做的事情本该，本当；
礼貌地告知某人自己必须做某事该，得；
Englishsense: You use ought to to mean that it is morally right to do a particular thing or that it is morally right for a particular situation to exist, especially when giving or asking for advice or opinions.
You use ought to when saying that you think it is a good idea and important for you or someone else to do a particular thing, especially when giving or asking for advice or opinions.
You use ought to to indicate that you expect something to be true or to happen. You use ought to have to indicate that you expect something to have happened already.
You use ought to to indicate that you think that something should be the case, but might not be.
You use ought to to indicate that you think that something has happened because of what you know about the situation, but you are not certain.
You use ought to have with a past participle to indicate that something was expected to happen or be the case, but it did not happen or was not the case.
You use ought to have with a past participle to indicate that although it was best or correct for someone to do something in the past, they did not actually do it.
You use ought to when politely telling someone that you must do something, for example that you must leave.

Chinesesense: 与家庭成员的姓名连用我家的；
Englishsense: You use our to indicate that something belongs or relates both to yourself and to one or more other people.
A speaker or writer sometimes uses our to indicate that something belongs or relates to people in general.
Speakers sometimes use our with the name of a member of their family.
You use ours to refer to something that belongs or relates both to yourself and to one or more other people.

Chinesesense: 泛指我们自己，人们自己当主语和宾语为同一群人时，用作动词或介词的宾语；
[用于强调第一人称复数主语；在比较正式的英语中，有时代替 us 作动词或介词的宾语以示强调] 我们自己，我们本人；
Englishsense: You use ourselves to refer to yourself and one or more other people as a group.
A speaker or writer sometimes uses ourselves to refer to people in general. Ourselves is used as the object of a verb or preposition when the subject refers to the same people.
You use ourselves to emphasize a first person plural subject. In more formal English, ourselves is sometimes used instead of ’us’ as the object of a verb or preposition, for emphasis.
If you say something such as ’We did it ourselves ’, you are indicating that something was done by you and a particular group of other people, rather than anyone else.
If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 缺少，不足，损失某一数量的钱；
棒球比赛中选手出局的；
提议或建议不能接受的，不值得考虑的；
不时髦的；不流行的；过时的；
计算或测量不准确的，错误的；
公开揭露公众人物、名人等的同性恋身份；
避开，未暴露于太阳、雨或风；
摆脱，脱离尤指令人不快的事；
通常指在对方不情愿的情况下从某人身上获得信息或工作成果；
Englishsense: When something is in a particular place and you take it out, you remove it from that place.
You can use out to indicate that you are talking about the situation outside, rather than inside buildings.
If you are out, you are not at home or not at your usual place of work.
If you say that someone is out in a particular place, you mean that they are in a different place, usually one far away.
When the sea or tide goes out, the sea moves away from the shore.
If you are out a particular amount of money, you have that amount less than you should or than you did.
If a light or fire is out or goes out, it is no longer shining or burning.
If flowers are out, their petals have opened.
If something such as a book or CD is out, it is available for people to buy.
If workers are out, they are on strike.
In a game or sport, if someone is out, they can no longer take part either because they are unable to or because they have been defeated.
In baseball, a player is out if they do not reach a base safely. When three players in a team are out in an inning, then the team is out.
If you say that a proposal or suggestion is out, you mean that it is unacceptable.
If you say that a particular thing is out, you mean that it is no longer fashionable at the present time.
If you say that a calculation or measurement is out, you mean that it is incorrect.
If someone is out to do something, they intend to do it.
If a group of people out a public figure or famous person, they reveal that person’s homosexuality against their wishes.
If you go out of a place, you leave it.
If you take something out of the container or place where it has been, you remove it so that it is no longer there.
If you look or shout out of a window, you look or shout away from the room where you are towards the outside.
If you are out of the sun, the rain, or the wind, you are sheltered from it.
If someone or something gets out of a situation, especially an unpleasant one, they are then no longer in it. If they keep out of it, they do not start being in it.
You can use out of to say that someone leaves an institution.
If you are out of range of something, you are beyond the limits of that range.
You use out of to say what feeling or reason causes someone to do something. For example, if you do something out of pity, you do it because you pity someone.
If you get something such as information or work out of someone, you manage to make them give it to you, usually when they are unwilling to give it.
If you get pleasure or an advantage out of something, you get it as a result of being involved with that thing or making use of it.
If you are out of something, you no longer have any of it.
If something is made out of a particular material, it consists of that material because it has been formed or constructed from it.
You use out of to indicate what proportion of a group of things something is true of. For example, if something is true of one out of five things, it is true of one fifth of all things of that kind.

Chinesesense: 暴力活动、疾病等的爆发，突然发生；
Englishsense: If there is an outbreak of something unpleasant, such as violence or a disease, it suddenly starts to happen.

Chinesesense: 尤指愤怒等感情的爆发，迸发；
Englishsense: An outburst of an emotion, especially anger, is a sudden strong expression of that emotion.
An outburst of violent activity is a sudden period of this activity.
The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.
Outdoor activities or things happen or are used outside and not in a building.

Chinesesense: 户外工作；野外活动；户外休闲；
Englishsense: If something happens outdoors, it happens outside in the fresh air rather than in a building.
You refer to the outdoors when talking about work or leisure activities which take place outside away from buildings.

Chinesesense: 外面的；外部的；远离中心的；
Englishsense: The outer parts of something are the parts which contain or enclose the other parts, and which are furthest from the centre.
An outfit is a set of clothes.
You can refer to an organization as an outfit.
To outfit someone or something means to provide them with equipment for a particular purpose.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 即将离职的；快要卸任的；
外向的；友好的；喜欢交际的；
Englishsense: You use outgoing to describe a person in charge of something who is soon going to leave that position.
Outgoing things such as planes, mail, and passengers are leaving or being sent somewhere.
Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

Chinesesense: 通常指集体远足，短途旅行；
Englishsense: An outing is a short enjoyable trip, usually with a group of people, away from your home, school, or place of work.
In sport, an outing is an occasion when a player competes in a particular contest or competition.

Chinesesense: 宣布…为非法；使成为非法；
Englishsense: When something is outlawed, it is made illegal.
An outlaw is a criminal who is hiding from the authorities.

Chinesesense: 廉价商品经销店；折扣店；
情感的发泄途径；思想的表达方式；
通常指墙上的电源插座；
Englishsense: An outlet is a shop or organization which sells the goods made by a particular manufacturer.
An outlet or an outlet store is a place which sells slightly damaged or outdated goods from a particular manufacturer, or goods that it made in greater quantities than needed.
If someone has an outlet for their feelings or ideas, they have a means of expressing and releasing them.
An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow away.
An outlet is a place, usually in a wall, where you can connect electrical devices to the electricity supply.

Chinesesense: 因背后的光线显示…的轮廓或外形；
Englishsense: If you outline an idea or a plan, you explain it in a general way.
An outline is a general explanation or description of something.
You say that an object is outlined when you can see its general shape because there is light behind it.
The outline of something is its general shape, especially when it cannot be clearly seen.

Chinesesense: 世界观；人生观；对生活的观点，看法；
Englishsense: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.
The outlook for something is what people think will happen in relation to it.
If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.

Chinesesense: 贸易站；前哨基地；设在国外的军事基地；
Englishsense: An outpost is a small group of buildings used for trading or military purposes, either in a distant part of your own country or in a foreign country.

Chinesesense: 计算机、文字处理器等的输出信息，输出文件；
Englishsense: Output is used to refer to the amount of something that a person or thing produces.
The output of a computer or word processor is the information that it displays on a screen or prints on paper as a result of a particular program.
If you are outraged by something, it makes you extremely shocked and angry.
Outrage is an intense feeling of anger and shock.
You can refer to an act or event which you find very shocking as an outrage.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 令人无法容忍的；骇人的；
Englishsense: If you describe something as outrageous, you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable or very shocking.
Outreach programmes and schemes try to find people who need help or advice rather than waiting for those people to come and ask for help.

Chinesesense: 直率的；公开的；直截了当的；
Englishsense: You use outright to describe behaviour and actions that are open and direct, rather than indirect.
Outright means complete and total.

Chinesesense: 在开始时/ 从一开始；
Englishsense: If something happens at the outset of an event, process, or period of time, it happens at the beginning of it. If something happens from the outset it happens from the beginning and continues to happen.

Chinesesense: 在外面；在室外；在建筑物近旁；
车道靠近路中间的，快车道的；
Englishsense: The outside of something is the part which surrounds or encloses the rest of it.
If you are outside, you are not inside a building but are quite close to it.
If you are outside a room, you are not in it but are in the passage or area next to it.
When you talk about the outside world, you are referring to things that happen or exist in places other than your own home or community.
People or things outside a country, town, or region are not in it.
On a road with two separate carriageways, the outside lanes are the ones which are closest to its centre.
Outside people or organizations are not part of a particular organization or group.
Outside a particular institution or field of activity means in other fields of activity or in general life.
Something that is outside a particular range of things is not included within it.
Something that happens outside a particular period of time happens at a different time from the one mentioned.
Outside of is used to introduce the only thing or person that prevents your main statement from being completely true.
You use at the outside to say that you think that a particular amount is the largest possible in a particular situation, or that a particular time is the latest possible time for something to happen.

Chinesesense: 某个团体或组织外部的人；
不为某一团体所接受或感觉不属其中的外人；
在竞赛中不大可能获胜的人或队伍；
Englishsense: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a particular group or organization.
An outsider is someone who is not accepted by a particular group, or who feels that they do not belong in it.
In a competition, an outsider is a competitor who is unlikely to win.
The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its centre.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Someone who is outspoken gives their opinions about things openly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 款项未支付的，未结清的；
Englishsense: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.
Money that is outstanding has not yet been paid and is still owed to someone.
Outstanding issues or problems have not yet been resolved.
Outstanding means very important or obvious.

Chinesesense: 特定方面可见的，外部的；
Englishsense: An outward journey is a journey that you make away from a place that you are intending to return to later.
The outward feelings, qualities, or attitudes of someone or something are the ones they appear to have rather than the ones that they actually have.
The outward features of something are the ones that you can see from the outside.

Chinesesense: 在重要性、益处、意义等上重于，大于，超过；
Englishsense: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.
Oval things have a shape that is like a circle but is wider in one direction than the other.
An oven is a device for cooking that is like a box with a door. You heat it and cook food inside it.

Chinesesense: 在…的上方；在…的上面；在…的上空；
部分或完全地覆盖在…的上面；
从…上面[看过去]; 隔着…交谈；
穿过，跨过，越过障碍、边界等；
突然或猛力地倒下，掉下；
在这边；到这边；在身处国；
在那边；到那边；在另一国；
多于[正常数量]; 除了…之外还；
强调发生不止一次两次/三次；
指令人疲倦、厌烦、不快地再一次，又一次，重新；
从某一疾病或经历中恢复过来；
广播或电视节目中的主持人用语下面交给…；
无线电通讯用语完毕，请回答；
板球运动中一轮6个未让对方得分的有效投球；
Englishsense: If one thing is over another thing or is moving over it, the first thing is directly above the second, either resting on it, or with a space between them.
If one thing is over another thing, it is supported by it and its ends are hanging down on each side of it.
If one thing is over another thing, it covers part or all of it.
If you lean over an object, you bend your body so that the top part of it is above the object.
If you look over or talk over an object, you look or talk across the top of it.
If a window has a view over an area of land or water, you can see the land or water through the window.
If someone or something goes over a barrier, obstacle, or boundary, they get to the other side of it by going across it, or across the top of it.
If someone or something moves over an area or surface, they move across it, from one side to the other.
If something is on the opposite side of a road or river, you can say that it is over the road or river.
If you go over to a place, you go to that place.
You can use over to indicate a particular position or place a short distance away from someone or something.
You use over to say that someone or something falls towards or onto the ground, often suddenly or violently.
If something rolls over or is turned over, its position changes so that the part that was facing upwards is now facing downwards. See usage note at: see Usage Note at above
All over a place means in every part of it.
Over here means near you, or in the country you are in.
Over there means in a place a short distance away from you, or in another country.
If something is over a particular amount, measurement, or age, it is more than that amount, measurement, or age.
Over and above an amount, especially a normal amount, means more than that amount or in addition to it.
If you say that you have some food or money over, you mean that it remains after you have used all that you need.
If you do something over, you do it again or start doing it again from the beginning.
If you say that something happened twice over, three times over and so on, you are stating the number of times that it happened and emphasizing that it happened more than once.
If you do something over again, you do it again or start doing it again from the beginning.
If you say that something is happening all over again, you are emphasizing that it is happening again, and you are suggesting that it is tiring, boring, or unpleasant.
If you say that something happened over and over or over and over again, you are emphasizing that it happened many times.
If an activity is over or all over, it is completely finished.
If you are over an illness or an experience, it has finished and you have recovered from its effects.
If you have control or influence over someone or something, you are able to control them or influence them.
You use over to indicate what a disagreement or feeling relates to or is caused by.
If something happens over a particular period of time or over something such as a meal, it happens during that time or during the meal.
You use over to indicate that you give or receive information using a telephone, radio, or other piece of electrical equipment.
The presenter of a radio or television programme says ’ over to someone’ to indicate the person who will speak next.
When people such as the police or the army are using a radio to communicate, they say ’ Over ’ to indicate that they have finished speaking and are waiting for a reply.
In cricket, an over consists of six correctly bowled balls.

Chinesesense: 上下连身的工作服，防护服；
Englishsense: You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.
Overalls consist of a single piece of clothing that combines trousers and a jacket. You wear overalls over your clothes in order to protect them while you are working.
Overalls are trousers that are attached to a piece of cloth which covers your chest and which has straps going over your shoulders.
An overall is a piece of clothing shaped like a coat that you wear over your clothes in order to protect them while you are working.

Chinesesense: 感情上受到极大影响，承受不起；
烟、毒气等熏倒，使受不了；
Englishsense: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.
If you are overcome by a feeling or event, it is so strong or has such a strong effect that you cannot think clearly.
If you are overcome by smoke or a poisonous gas, you become very ill or die from breathing it in.

Chinesesense: 洋溢着[情感]; 情感溢于言表；
过多而容纳不下的人或东西；
Englishsense: If a liquid or a river overflows, it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.
If a place or container is overflowing with people or things, it is too full of them.
If someone is overflowing with a feeling or if the feeling overflows, the person is experiencing it very strongly and shows this in their behaviour.
The overflow is the extra people or things that something cannot contain or deal with because it is not large enough.
An overflow is a hole or pipe through which liquid can flow out of a container when it gets too full.
If a place or container is filled to overflowing, it is so full of people or things that no more can fit in.

Chinesesense: 在头顶上的；在上面的；高架的；
Englishsense: You use overhead to indicate that something is above you or above the place that you are talking about.

Chinesesense: 偶然听到；无意中听到；偷听到；
Englishsense: If you overhear someone, you hear what they are saying when they are not talking to you and they do not know that you are listening.

Chinesesense: 在主题、人物、时间等上与…部分相同，与…部分交叉；
Englishsense: If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing. You can also say that two things overlap.
If one idea or activity overlaps another, or overlaps with another, they involve some of the same subjects, people, or periods of time.
If a building or window overlooks a place, you can see the place clearly from the building or window.
If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.
If you overlook someone’s faults or bad behaviour, you forgive them and take no action.
Overly means more than is normal, necessary, or reasonable.

Chinesesense: 在整个夜间；在夜里的某一时刻；
Englishsense: If something happens overnight, it happens throughout the night or at some point during the night.
You can say that something happens overnight when it happens very quickly and unexpectedly.
Overnight bags or clothes are ones that you take when you go and stay somewhere for one or two nights.
If you overnight somewhere, you spend the night there.

Chinesesense: 凌驾于；优先于；比…更重要；
以更大的权力撤销，推翻，否决；
对决定等的撤销，推翻，否决；
Englishsense: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.
If someone in authority overrides a person or their decisions, they cancel their decisions.
An override is an attempt to cancel someone’s decisions by using your authority over them or by gaining more votes than them in an election or contest.

Chinesesense: 学生、游客等来自海外的，来自外国的；
Englishsense: You use overseas to describe things that involve or are in foreign countries, usually across a sea or an ocean.
An overseas student or visitor comes from a foreign country, usually across a sea or an ocean.
If someone in authority oversees a job or an activity, they make sure that it is done properly.

Chinesesense: 使黯然失色；使相形见绌；使显得无足轻重；
楼房、树木、大型建筑物等遮蔽，遮挡；
Englishsense: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.
If you are overshadowed by a person or thing, you are less successful, important, or impressive than they are.
If one building, tree, or large structure overshadows another, it stands near it, is much taller than it, and casts a shadow over it.
If there has been an oversight, someone has forgotten to do something which they should have done.
If someone has oversight of a process or system, they are responsible for making sure that it works efficiently and correctly.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
