If a feeling overtakes you, it affects you very strongly.
When a government or leader is overthrown, they are removed from power by force.

Chinesesense: 体育比赛中为决胜负而延长的加时赛；
Englishsense: Overtime is time that you spend doing your job in addition to your normal working hours.
If you say that someone is working overtime to do something, you mean that they are using a lot of energy, effort, or enthusiasm trying to do it.
Overtime is an additional period of time that is added to the end of a sports match in which the two teams are level, as a way of allowing one of the teams to win.
If something overturns or if you overturn it, it turns upside down or on its side.
If someone in authority overturns a legal decision, they officially decide that that decision is incorrect or not valid.
To overturn a government or system means to remove it or destroy it.
An overview of a situation is a general understanding or description of it as a whole.

Englishsense: Someone who is overweight weighs more than is considered healthy or attractive. See usage note at: fat

Chinesesense: 情感、事件等使不知所措，使难以承受；
Englishsense: If you are overwhelmed by a feeling or event, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.
If a group of people overwhelm a place or another group, they gain complete control or victory over them.

If you say that something owes a great deal to a person or thing, you mean that it exists, is successful, or has its particular form mainly because of them.
If you say that you owe someone gratitude, respect, or loyalty, you mean that they deserve it from you.
If you say that you owe it to someone to do something, you mean that you should do that thing because they deserve it.
You use owing to when you are introducing the reason for something.
An owl is a bird with a flat face, large eyes, and a small sharp beak. Most owls obtain their food by hunting small animals at night.

Chinesesense: 自己所用的；具有自己特点的；特有的；
自己做的；单独干的；独立完成的；
因情况适宜而开始取得成功，开始进入良好状态；
使只与自己相关；使为自己所有；
属于自己的；关于自己的；

Englishsense: You use own to indicate that something belongs to a particular person or thing.
You use own to indicate that something is used by, or is characteristic of, only one person, thing, or group.
You use own to indicate that someone does something without any help from other people.
If you own something, it is your property.
If you have something you can call your own, it belongs only to you, rather than being controlled by or shared with someone else.
If someone or something comes into their own, they become very successful or start to perform very well because the circumstances are right.
If you get your own back on someone, you have your revenge on them because of something bad that they have done to you.
If you make something your own, you become involved in it in such a way that people think of it as being related only to you or belonging only to you, rather than to anyone else.
If you say that someone has a particular thing of their own, you mean that that thing belongs or relates to them, rather than to other people.
If someone or something has a particular quality or characteristic of their own, that quality or characteristic is especially theirs, rather than being shared by other things or people of that type.
When you are on your own, you are alone.
If you do something on your own, you do it without any help from other people.
If you say that someone does something as if they own the place or like they own the place, you are critical of them because they do it in a very arrogant way.
The owner of something is the person to whom it belongs.
Ownership of something is the state of owning it.
Oxygen is a colourless gas that exists in large quantities in the air. All plants and animals need oxygen in order to live.

Chinesesense: 世界是属于…的；尽可做想做之事或去想去之处；
Englishsense: An oyster is a large flat shellfish. Some oysters can be eaten and others produce valuable objects called pearls.
If you say that the world is someone’s oyster, you mean that they can do anything or go anywhere that they want to.
Ozone is a colourless gas which is a form of oxygen. There is a layer of ozone high above the earth’s surface.

Chinesesense: 由于焦虑或不耐烦而在…踱步；
与…齐头并进或并驾齐驱；
考查…的能力/ 展现…的才能；
Englishsense: The pace of something is the speed at which it happens or is done.
Your pace is the speed at which you walk.
A pace is the distance that you move when you take one step.
If you pace a small area, you keep walking up and down it, because you are anxious or impatient.
If you pace yourself when doing something, you do it at a steady rate.
If something keeps pace with something else that is changing, it changes quickly in response to it.
If you keep pace with someone who is walking or running, you succeed in going as fast as them, so that you remain close to them.
If you do something at your own pace, you do it at a speed that is comfortable for you.
If you put someone through their paces or make them go through their paces, you get them to show you how well they can do something.

Chinesesense: 在陪审团、委员会、会议等中安插支持者；
在竞赛中领先其他对手；
Englishsense: When you pack a bag, you put clothes and other things into it, because you are leaving a place or going on holiday.
When people pack things, for example in a factory, they put them into containers or parcels so that they can be transported and sold.
If people or things pack into a place or if they pack a place, there are so many of them that the place is full.
A pack of things is a collection of them that is sold or given together in a box or bag.
A pack is a bag containing your possessions that you carry on your back when you are travelling.
You can refer to a group of people who go around together as a pack, especially when it is a large group that you feel threatened by.
A pack of wolves or dogs is a group of them that hunt together.
A pack of playing cards is a complete set of playing cards.
If someone packs a gun, they carry it.
If someone packs a jury, committee, or meeting, they make sure that it includes people who support them.
If you say that an account is a pack of lies, you mean that it is completely untrue.
If something packs a punch, it has a very powerful effect.
If you send someone packing, you make them go away.
You can say that someone is ahead of the pack or leading the pack if they are ahead of everyone else in a race or competition.

Chinesesense: 为提高吸引力或趣味性而包装；
Englishsense: A package is a small parcel.
A package is a small container in which a quantity of something is sold. Packages are either small boxes made of thin cardboard, or bags or envelopes made of paper or plastic.
A package is a set of proposals that are made by a government or organization and which must be accepted or rejected as a group.
When a product is packaged, it is put into containers to be sold.
If something is packaged in a particular way, it is presented or advertised in that way in order to make it seem attractive or interesting.
A package tour, or in British English a package holiday, is a holiday arranged by a travel company in which your travel and your accommodation are booked for you.
Packaging is the container or covering that something is sold in.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A place that is packed is very crowded.
Something that is packed with things contains a very large number of them.
A packet is a small container in which a quantity of something is sold. Packets are either small boxes made of thin cardboard, or bags or envelopes made of paper or plastic.
A packet is a small flat parcel.
You can refer to a lot of money as a packet.
A pact is a formal agreement between two or more people, organizations, or governments to do a particular thing or to help each other.

Chinesesense: 轻步快速地走；蹑手蹑脚地走；
直升机停机坪；火箭发射台；
Englishsense: A pad is a fairly thick, flat piece of a material such as cloth or rubber. Pads are used, for example, to clean things, to protect things, or to change their shape.
A pad of paper is a number of pieces of paper which are fixed together along the top or the side, so that each piece can be torn off when it has been used.
When someone pads somewhere, they walk there with steps that are fairly quick, light, and quiet.
A pad is a platform or an area of flat, hard ground where helicopters take off and land or rockets are launched.
People can refer to the place where they live as their pad, especially if it is a flat.
The pads of a person’s fingers and toes or of an animal’s feet are the soft, fleshy parts of them.
If you pad something, you put something soft in it or over it in order to make it less hard, to protect it, or to give it a different shape.
A paddle is a short pole with a wide flat part at one end or at both ends. You hold it in your hands and use it as an oar to move a small boat through water.
If you paddle a boat, you move it through water using a paddle.
If you paddle, you walk or stand in shallow water, for example at the edge of the sea, for pleasure.

Chinesesense: 书、杂志、报纸等的页，面，版；
历史的一页指重大事件或重要时期；
在公共场合通过广播呼叫；
婚礼上新娘的男伴童，小男傧相；

Englishsense: A page is one side of one of the pieces of paper in a book, magazine, or newspaper. Each page usually has a number printed at the top or bottom.
The pages of a book, magazine, or newspaper are the pieces of paper it consists of.
You can refer to an important event or period of time as a page of history.
If someone who is in a public place is paged, they receive a message, often over a speaker, telling them that someone is trying to contact them.
A page is a small boy who accompanies the bride at a wedding.
A page is a young person who takes messages or does small jobs for members of the United States Congress or state legislatures.
In former times, a page was a young boy who was a knight’s servant and was learning to be a knight.

Chinesesense: 盛装游行[或庆典]; 露天历史剧；
Englishsense: A pageant is a colourful public procession, show, or ceremony. Pageants are usually held out of doors and often celebrate events or people from history.
A pageant or a beauty pageant is a competition in which young women are judged to decide which one is the most beautiful.
Paid workers, or people who do paid work, receive money for the work that they do.
If you are given paid holiday, you get your wages or salary even though you are not at work.
If you are well paid, you receive a lot of money for the work that you do. If you are badly paid, you do not receive much money.
If an unexpected event puts paid to someone’s hopes, chances, or plans, it completely ends or destroys them.

Chinesesense: 讨厌鬼，烦心事[英国英语亦用a pain in the arse, a pain in the backside等，美国英语亦用a pain in the ass, a pain in the butt等，但多数人认为具冒犯意味] ；
尤指为避免困境而急切想做，迫切想要做；

Englishsense: Pain is the feeling of great discomfort you have, for example when you have been hurt or when you are ill.
Pain is the feeling of unhappiness that you have when something unpleasant or upsetting happens.
If a fact or idea pains you, it makes you feel upset and disappointed.

In informal English, if you call someone or something a pain or a pain in the neck, you mean that they are very annoying or irritating. Expressions such as a pain in the arse and a pain in the backside in British English, or a pain in the ass and a pain in the butt in American English, are also used, but most people consider them offensive.
If someone is at pains to do something, they are very eager and anxious to do it, especially because they want to avoid a difficult situation.
You say that something was all you got for your pains when you are mentioning the disappointing result of situation into which you put a lot of work or effort.
If someone is ordered not to do something on pain of or under pain of death, imprisonment, or arrest, they will be killed, put in prison, or arrested if they do it.
If you take pains to do something or go to great pains to do something, you try hard to do it, because you think it is important to do it.

You can refer to two people as a pair when they are standing or walking together or when they have some kind of relationship with each other.
If one thing is paired with another, it is put with it or considered with it.
If you say that someone is or has a safe pair of hands, you mean that they are reliable and will not make any serious mistakes.

Chinesesense: 巴基斯坦的；巴基斯坦人的；巴基斯坦文化的；

You can refer to any large splendid house or other building as a palace.

If one thing pales in comparison with another, it is made to seem much less important, serious, or good by it.
If you think that someone’s actions or behaviour are not acceptable, you can say that they are beyond the pale.

A pan is a shallow metal container used for baking foods.
If something such as a film or a book is panned by journalists, they say it is very bad.
If you pan a film or television camera or if it pans somewhere, it moves slowly round so that a wide area is filmed.
If someone pans for gold, they use a shallow metal container to try to find small pieces of gold from a river.

机器、设备等的仪表板，面板；

A control panel or instrument panel is a board or surface which contains switches and controls to operate a machine or piece of equipment.

Englishsense: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.
Panic or a panic is a situation in which people are affected by a strong feeling of anxiety.
If you panic or if someone panics you, you suddenly feel anxious or afraid, and act quickly and without thinking carefully.
If you pant, you breathe quickly and loudly with your mouth open, because you have been doing something energetic.

Chinesesense: 政府或委员会发表的关于重大问题的文件，报告；
Englishsense: Paper is a material that you write on or wrap things with. The pages of this book are made of paper.
A paper is a newspaper.
You can refer to newspapers in general as the paper or the papers.
Your papers are sheets of paper with writing or information on them, which you might keep in a safe place at home.
Your papers are official documents, for example your passport or identity card, which prove who you are or which give you official permission to do something.
A paper is a long, formal piece of writing about an academic subject.
A paper is an essay written by a student.
A paper is a part of a written examination in which you answer a number of questions in a particular period of time.
A paper prepared by a government or a committee is a report on a question they have been considering or a set of proposals for changes in the law.
Paper agreements, qualifications, or profits are ones that are stated by official documents to exist, although they may not really be effective or useful.
If you paper a wall, you put wallpaper on it.
If you put your thoughts down on paper, you write them down.
If something seems to be the case on paper, it seems to be the case from what you read or hear about it, but it may not really be the case.

If you say that a promise, an agreement, or a guarantee is not worth the paper it’s written on, you mean that although it has been written down and seems to be official, it is in fact worthless because what has been promised will not be done.
A paperback is a book with a thin cardboard or paper cover.
Paperwork is the routine part of a job which involves writing or dealing with letters, reports, and records.

Chinesesense: 不符合标准的；不如预期的；
不在状态；感觉不如平常好；
不快之事不出所料，在意料之中；
Englishsense: If you say that two people or things are on a par with each other, you mean that they are equally good or bad, or equally important.
In golf, par is the number of strokes that a good player should take to get the ball into a hole or into all the holes on a particular golf course.
If you say that someone or something is below par or under par, you are disappointed in them because they are below the standard you expected.
If you say that someone or something is not up to par, you are disappointed in them because they are below the standard you expected.
If you feel below par or under par, you feel tired and unable to perform as well as you normally do.
If you say that something that happens is par for the course, you mean that you are not pleased with it but it is what you expected to happen.

Chinesesense: 使空降指突然从机构外调入；
Englishsense: A parachute is a device which enables a person to jump from an aircraft and float safely to the ground. It consists of a large piece of thin cloth attached to your body by strings.
If a person parachutes or someone parachutes them somewhere, they jump from an aircraft using a parachute.
To parachute something somewhere means to drop it somewhere by parachute.
If a person parachutes into an organization or if they are parachuted into it, they are brought in suddenly in order to help it.

Chinesesense: 庆祝重大日子或事件的游行行列；
将囚犯游街；将囚犯示众；
多得似乎没有尽头的一系列；
常指远离大街的一小排店铺；
用于街道名称中商业街；
Englishsense: A parade is a procession of people or vehicles moving through a public place in order to celebrate an important day or event.
When people parade somewhere, they walk together in a formal group or a line, usually with other people watching them.
Parade is a formal occasion when soldiers stand in lines to be seen by an officer or important person, or march in a group.
If flags or statues are paraded, they are carried in a procession.
If prisoners are paraded through the streets of a town or on television, they are shown to the public, usually in order to make the people who are holding them seem more powerful or important.
If you say that someone parades a person, you mean that they show that person to others only in order to gain some advantage for themselves.
If people parade something, they show it in public so that it can be admired.
If someone parades, they walk about somewhere in order to be seen and admired.
If someone parades a real or pretended feeling or quality, they draw attention to themselves by displaying it.
If you say that something parades as or is paraded as a good or important thing, you mean that some people say that it is good or important but you think it probably is not.
If you talk about a parade of people or things, you mean that there is a series of them that seems never to end.
A parade is a short row of shops, usually set back from the main street.
Parade is used as part of the name of a street.
A paradigm is a model for something which explains it or shows how it can be produced.
A paradigm is a clear and typical example of something.
According to some religions, paradise is a wonderful place where people go after they die, if they have led good lives.
You can refer to a place or situation that seems beautiful or perfect as paradise or a paradise.
You can use paradise to say that a place is very attractive to a particular kind of person and has everything they need for a particular activity.

Chinesesense: 自相矛盾；有矛盾特点的情况；
悖论；自相矛盾的说法；似矛盾而可能正确的说法；
Englishsense: You describe a situation as a paradox when it involves two or more facts or qualities which seem to contradict each other.
A paradox is a statement in which it seems that if one part of it is true, the other part of it cannot be true.
A paragraph is a section of a piece of writing. A paragraph always begins on a new line and contains at least one sentence.

Chinesesense: 存在或发生在不同地点或时间的相似之物，类似物；
两者间的近似之处，相似之处；
标于地图上的纬线，纬圈；
Englishsense: If something has a parallel, it is similar to something else, but exists or happens in a different place or at a different time. If it has no parallel or is without parallel, it is not similar to anything else.
If there are parallels between two things, they are similar in some ways.
If one thing parallels another, they happen at the same time or are similar, and often seem to be connected.
Parallel events or situations happen at the same time as one another, or are similar to one another.
If two lines, two objects, or two lines of movement are parallel, they are the same distance apart along their whole length.
A parallel is an imaginary line round the earth that is parallel to the equator. Parallels are shown on maps.
Something that occurs in parallel with something else occurs at the same time as it.
Parameters are factors or limits which affect the way that something can be done or made.
Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 患偏执狂的；患妄想症的；
Englishsense: If you say that someone is paranoid, you mean that they are extremely suspicious and afraid of other people.
Someone who is paranoid suffers from the mental illness of paranoia.
A parasite is a small animal or plant that lives on or inside a larger animal or plant, and gets its food from it.
If you disapprove of someone because you think that they get money or other things from other people but do not do anything in return, you can call them a parasite.
A parcel is something wrapped in paper, usually so that it can be sent to someone by post.
A parcel of land is a piece of land.
A parcel of things or people is a quantity of them.
If you say that something is part and parcel of something else, you are emphasizing that it is involved or included in it.

Chinesesense: 对不起,请再说一遍[美国英语用Pardon me?] ；
你说什么？表示惊讶或者受到冒犯；
对不起，不好意思打断一下用于引起他人注意或者打断他人；
请原谅我这么说；说句粗话您别介意；
Englishsense: You say ’ Pardon? ’ or ’ I beg your pardon? ’ or, in American English, ’ Pardon me? ’ when you want someone to repeat what they have just said because you have not heard or understood it.
People say ’ I beg your pardon? ’ when they are surprised or offended by something that someone has just said.
You say ’ I beg your pardon ’ or ’ I do beg your pardon ’ as a way of apologizing for accidentally doing something wrong, such as disturbing someone or making a mistake.
Some people say ’ Pardon me ’ instead of ’Excuse me’ when they want to politely get someone’s attention or interrupt them.
You can say things like ’ Pardon me for asking ’ or ’ Pardon my frankness ’ as a way of showing you understand that what you are going to say may sound rude.
Some people say things like ’ If you’ll pardon the expression ’ or ’ Pardon my French ’ just before or after saying something which they think might offend people.
If someone who has been found guilty of a crime is pardoned, they are officially allowed to go free and are not punished.

Chinesesense: 创始的；母公司的；总公司的；
动物、植物或有机体亲本的，亲代的；
Englishsense: Your parents are your mother and father.
An organization’s parent organization is the organization that created it and usually still controls it.
The parent animal, plant, or organism of a particular animal, plant or organism is the one that it comes from or is produced by.

Chinesesense: 父母的；父的；母的；家长的；
Englishsense: Parental is used to describe something that relates to parents in general, or to one or both of the parents of a particular child.
Parenting is the activity of bringing up and looking after your child.

Chinesesense: 有独立教堂和牧师的教区，堂区；
英格兰的乡村行政小区；
Englishsense: A parish is a village or part of a town which has its own church and priest.
A parish is a small country area in England which has its own elected council.

POS: N-COUNT; also N-IN-NAMES 可数名词；名称名词
Chinesesense: 作为特定活动场地的…园，…区；
棒球场亦用于某些棒球场名称中；
Englishsense: A park is a public area of land with grass and trees, usually in a town, where people go in order to relax and enjoy themselves.
When you park a vehicle or park somewhere, you drive the vehicle into a position where it can stay for a period of time, and leave it there.
You can refer to a place where a particular activity is carried out as a park.
A private area of grass and trees around a large country house is referred to as a park.
Some people refer to a football or rugby field as the park.
A park is a park or stadium where baseball is played. Park is also used in the names of some parks.
Parking is the action of moving a vehicle into a place in a car park or by the side of the road where it can be left.
Parking is space for parking a vehicle in.
Parliamentary is used to describe things that are connected with a parliament or with Members of Parliament.
If a prisoner is given parole, he or she is released before the official end of their prison sentence and has to promise to behave well.
If a prisoner is paroled, he or she is given parole.
Parsley is a small plant with curly leaves that are used for flavouring or decorating savoury food.

Chinesesense: 在某人看来；就某人而言；
Englishsense: A part of something is one of the pieces, sections, or elements that it consists of.
A part for a machine or vehicle is one of the smaller pieces that is used to make it.
Part of something is some of it.
If you say that something is part one thing, part another, you mean that it is to some extent the first thing and to some extent the second thing.

You can use part when you are talking about the proportions of substances in a mixture. For example, if you are told to use five parts water to one part paint, the mixture should contain five times as much water as paint.
A part in a play or film is one of the roles in it which an actor or actress can perform.
Your part in something that happens is your involvement in it.
If something or someone is part of a group or organization, they belong to it or are included in it.
The part in someone’s hair is the line running from the front to the back of their head where their hair lies in different directions.
If something or someone plays a large or important part in an event or situation, they are very involved in it and have an important effect on what happens.
If you take part in an activity, you do it together with other people.
If you say that you want no part of something, you mean that you do not want to be involved in it at all.
When you are describing people’s thoughts or actions, you can say for her part or for my part, for example, to introduce what a particular person thinks or does.
If you talk about a feeling or action on someone’s part, you are referring to something that they feel or do.
For the most part means mostly or usually.
You use in part to indicate that something exists or happens to some extent but not completely.
If you say that something happened for the best part or the better part of a period of time, you mean that it happened for most of that time.
If things that are next to each other part or if you part them, they move in opposite directions, so that there is a space between them.
If you part your hair in the middle or at one side, you make it lie in two different directions so that there is a straight line running from the front of your head to the back.
When two people part, or if one person parts from another, they leave each other.
If you are parted from someone you love, you are prevented from being with them.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: You use partial to refer to something that is not complete or whole.
If you are partial to something, you like it.
Someone who is partial supports a particular person or thing, for example in a competition or dispute, instead of being completely fair.

Chinesesense: 部分地；在某种程度上；有点儿；
Englishsense: If something happens or exists partially, it happens or exists to some extent, but not completely.
The participants in an activity are the people who take part in it.
If you participate in an activity, you take part in it.
A particle of something is a very small piece or amount of it.
In physics, a particle is a piece of matter smaller than an atom, for example an electron or a proton.
In grammar, a particle is a preposition such as ’into’ or an adverb such as ’out’ which can combine with a verb to form a phrasal verb.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 没什么重要或特别的事物或人；
Englishsense: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.
If a person or thing has a particular quality or possession, it is distinct and belongs only to them.
You can use particular to emphasize that something is greater or more intense than usual.
If you say that someone is particular, you mean that they choose things and do things very carefully, and are not easily satisfied.
You use in particular to indicate that what you are saying applies especially to one thing or person.
You use nothing in particular or nobody in particular to mean nothing or nobody important or special.
You use particularly to indicate that what you are saying applies especially to one thing or situation.
Particularly means more than usual or more than other things.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 对人或事业盲目支持的，偏袒的，有倾向性的；
Englishsense: Someone who is partisan strongly supports a particular person or cause, often without thinking carefully about the matter.
Partisans are ordinary people, rather than soldiers, who join together to fight enemy soldiers who are occupying their country.

Chinesesense: 用隔板、隔扇等隔开，分隔；
Englishsense: A partition is a wall or screen that separates one part of a room or vehicle from another.
If you partition a room, you separate one part of it from another by means of a partition.
If a country is partitioned, it is divided into two or more independent countries.

Chinesesense: 部分地；不完全地；在某种程度上；
Englishsense: You use partly to indicate that something happens or exists to some extent, but not completely.

Chinesesense: 比赛或舞蹈中做…的伙伴或搭档，与…配对；
Englishsense: Your partner is the person you are married to or are having a romantic or sexual relationship with.
Your partner is the person you are doing something with, for example dancing with or playing with in a game against two other people.
The partners in a firm or business are the people who share the ownership of it.
The partner of a country or organization is another country or organization with which they work or do business.
If you partner someone, you are their partner in a game or in a dance.
Partnership or a partnership is a relationship in which two or more people, organizations, or countries work together as partners.
If someone is a part-time worker or has a part-time job, they work for only part of each day or week.

Chinesesense: 法律协议或辩论中的一方；
Englishsense: A party is a political organization whose members have similar aims and beliefs. Usually the organization tries to get its members elected to the government of a country.
A party is a social event, often in someone’s home, at which people enjoy themselves doing things such as eating, drinking, dancing, talking, or playing games.
If you party, you enjoy yourself doing things such as going out to parties, drinking, dancing, and talking to people.
A party of people is a group of people who are doing something together, for example travelling together.
One of the people involved in a legal agreement or dispute can be referred to as a particular party.
Someone who is a party to or is party to an action or agreement is involved in it, and therefore partly responsible for it.

Chinesesense: 书、演讲、乐曲等的段，节，章；
Englishsense: A passage is a long narrow space with walls or fences on both sides, which connects one place or room with another.
A passage in a book, speech, or piece of music is a section of it that you are considering separately from the rest.
A passage is a long narrow hole or tube in your body, which air or liquid can pass along.
A passage through a crowd of people or things is an empty space that allows you to move through them.
The passage of someone or something is their movement from one place to another.
The passage of someone or something is their progress from one situation or one stage in their development to another.
The passage of a bill or act is the official acceptance of it by a parliament or legislature.
The passage of a period of time is its passing.
A passage is a journey by ship.
If you are granted passage through a country or area of land, you are given permission to go through it.
A passenger in a vehicle such as a bus, boat, or plane is a person who is travelling in it, but who is not driving it or working on it. See usage note at: client
Passenger is used to describe something that is designed for passengers, rather than for drivers or goods.

Chinesesense: 短暂的；一时的；转瞬即逝的；
Englishsense: A passing fashion, activity, or feeling lasts for only a short period of time and is not worth taking very seriously.
The passing of something such as a time or system is the fact of its coming to an end.
You can refer to someone’s death as their passing, if you want to avoid using the word ’death’ because you think it might upset or offend people.
The passing of a period of time is the fact or process of its going by.
A passing mention or reference is brief and is made while you are talking or writing about something else.
If you mention something in passing, you mention it briefly while you are talking or writing about something else.
If something changes with each passing year or with every passing day, it changes continuously.
Passion is strong sexual feelings towards someone.
Passion is a very strong feeling about something or a strong belief in something.
If you have a passion for something, you have a very strong interest in it and like it very much.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A passionate person has very strong feelings about something or a strong belief in something.
A passionate person has strong romantic or sexual feelings and expresses them in their behaviour.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 被动的；顺从的；听之任之的；
Englishsense: If you describe someone as passive, you mean that they do not take action but instead let things happen to them.
A passive activity involves watching, looking at, or listening to things rather than doing things.
Passive resistance involves showing opposition to the people in power in your country by not co-operating with them and protesting in non-violent ways.

In grammar, the passive or the passive voice is formed using ’be’ and the past participle of a verb. The subject of a passive clause does not perform the action expressed by the verb but is affected by it. For example, in ’He’s been murdered’, the verb is in the passive.

Chinesesense: 进身之阶；获取成功或幸福的途径，手段；
Englishsense: Your passport is an official document containing your name, photograph, and personal details, which you need to show when you enter or leave a country.
If you say that a thing is a passport to success or happiness, you mean that this thing makes success or happiness possible.

Chinesesense: 超过，超出某一点或阶段；
某人做某事并不令人意外；
Englishsense: The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.
Your past consists of all the things that you have done or that have happened to you.
Past events and things happened or existed before the present time.
You use past to talk about a period of time that has just finished. For example, if you talk about the past five years, you mean the period of five years that has just finished.
If a situation is past, it has ended and no longer exists.

In grammar, the past tenses of a verb are the ones used to talk about things that happened at some time before the present. The simple past tense uses the past form of a verb, which for regular verbs ends in ’-ed’, as in ’They walked back to the car’.
You use past when you are stating a time which is thirty minutes or less after a particular hour. For example, if it is twenty past six, it is twenty minutes after six o’clock.
If it is past a particular time, it is later than that time.
If you go past someone or something, you go near them and keep moving, so that they are then behind you.
If you look or point past a person or thing, you look or point at something behind them.
If something is past a place, it is on the other side of it.
If someone or something is past a particular point or stage, they are no longer at that point or stage.
If you are past doing something, you are no longer able to do it. For example, if you are past caring, you do not care about something any more because so many bad things have happened to you.
If you say that you would not put it past someone to do something bad, you mean that you would not be surprised if they did it because you think their character is bad.

Chinesesense: 面食如意大利面条、通心粉等；
Englishsense: Pasta is a type of food made from a mixture of flour, eggs, and water that is formed into different shapes and then boiled. Spaghetti, macaroni, and noodles are types of pasta.

Chinesesense: 肉、水果或蔬菜弄碎做成的酱；
制造人造宝石的铅玻璃；
Englishsense: Paste is a soft, wet, sticky mixture of a substance and a liquid, which can be spread easily. Some types of paste are used to stick things together.
Paste is a soft smooth mixture made of crushed meat, fruit, or vegetables. You can, for example, spread it onto bread or use it in cooking.
If you paste something on a surface, you put glue or paste on it and stick it on the surface.
Paste is a hard shiny glass that is used for making imitation jewellery.
Pastel colours are pale rather than dark or bright.
Pastels are also small sticks of different coloured chalks that are used for drawing pictures.
A pastel is a picture that has been done using pastels.
A pastor is a member of the Christian clergy in some Protestant churches.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 教师对学生生活辅导的；
Englishsense: The pastoral duties of a priest or other religious leader involve looking after the people he or she has responsibility for, especially by helping them with their personal problems.
If a school offers pastoral care, it is concerned with the personal needs and problems of its pupils, not just with their schoolwork.
A pastoral place, atmosphere, or idea is characteristic of peaceful country life and scenery.
A pastoral way of life is one in which people keep animals such as cows and sheep that feed off the land.
Pastry is a food made from flour, fat, and water that is mixed together, rolled flat, and baked in the oven. It is used, for example, for making pies.
A pastry is a small cake made with sweet pastry.

Chinesesense: 更好的地方[或工作、条件]; 更好的前程；
Englishsense: Pasture is land with grass growing on it for farm animals to eat.
If someone leaves for greener pastures, or in British English pastures new, they leave their job, their home, or the situation they are in for something they think will be much better.
If you put animals out to pasture, you move them out into the fields so they can eat the grass.
If you say that someone is being put out to pasture, you mean they are no longer being employed because they are considered to be too old or no longer useful.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you pat something or someone, you tap them lightly, usually with your hand held flat.
A pat of butter or something else that is soft is a small lump of it.
If you say that an answer or explanation is pat, you disapprove of it because it is too simple and sounds as if it has been prepared in advance.
If you give someone a pat on the back or if you pat them on the back, you show them that you think they have done well and deserve to be praised.
If you have an answer or explanation down pat or off pat, you have prepared and learned it so you are ready to say it at any time.
If you stand pat, you refuse to change your mind about something.

Chinesesense: 表面上与周围不同的部分；
种有某种植物或农作物的小块土地；
Englishsense: A patch on a surface is a part of it which is different in appearance from the area around it.
A patch of land is a small area of land where a particular plant or crop grows.
A patch is a piece of material which you use to cover a hole in something.
A patch is a small piece of material which you wear to cover an injured eye.
If you patch something that has a hole in it, you mend it by fastening a patch over the hole.
A patch is a piece of computer program code written as a temporary solution for dealing with a virus in computer software and distributed by the makers of the original program.
If you have or go through a bad patch or a rough patch, you have a lot of problems for a time.
If you say that someone or something is not a patch on another person or thing, you mean that they are not as good as that person or thing.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 尤指坏事物明显的，显而易见的；
Englishsense: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.
If you patent something, you obtain a patent for it.
You use patent to describe something, especially something bad, in order to indicate in an emphatic way that you think its nature or existence is clear and obvious.
A path is a long strip of ground which people walk along to get from one place to another.
Your path is the space ahead of you as you move along.
The path of something is the line which it moves along in a particular direction.
A path that you take is a particular course of action or way of achieving something.
You can say that something is in your path or blocking your path to mean that it is preventing you from doing or achieving what you want.
If you cross someone’s path or if your paths cross, you meet them by chance.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 可怜的；令人怜悯的；悲惨的；
差劲的；软弱的；令人生厌的；
Englishsense: If you describe a person or animal as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or helpless, and they make you feel very sorry for them.
If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they make you feel impatient or angry, often because they are weak or not very good.
A pathogen is any organism which can cause disease in a person, animal, or plant.
A pathway is a path which you can walk along or a route which you can take.
A pathway is a particular course of action or a way of achieving something.

Chinesesense: 考验…的耐心；使忍无可忍；
Englishsense: If you have patience, you are able to stay calm and not get annoyed, for example when something takes a long time, or when someone is not doing what you want them to do.
Patience is a card game for only one player.
If someone tries your patience or tests your patience, they annoy you so much that it is very difficult for you to stay calm.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A patient is a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor or hospital. A patient is also someone who is registered with a particular doctor. See usage note at: client
If you are patient, you stay calm and do not get annoyed, for example when something takes a long time, or when someone is not doing what you want them to do.
A patio is an area of flat blocks or concrete next to a house, where people can sit and relax or eat.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Someone who is patriotic loves their country and feels very loyal towards it.
Patriotism is love for your country and loyalty towards it.
When soldiers, police, or guards patrol an area or building, they move around it in order to make sure that there is no trouble there.
Soldiers, police, or guards who are on patrol are patrolling an area.
A patrol is a group of soldiers or vehicles that are patrolling an area.

Chinesesense: 艺术家、作家和音乐家等的赞助人，资助人；
允许慈善机构、团体和活动等使用自己的名字作宣传的代言人，名义赞助人；
酒吧、旅馆等的主顾，顾客；
Englishsense: A patron is a person who supports and gives money to artists, writers, or musicians.
The patron of a charity, group, or campaign is an important person who allows his or her name to be used for publicity.
The patrons of a place such as a pub, bar, or hotel are its customers.
A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.
A pattern is an arrangement of lines or shapes, especially a design in which the same shape is repeated at regular intervals over a surface.
A pattern is a diagram or shape that you can use as a guide when you are making something such as a model or a piece of clothing.
If you pause while you are doing something, you stop for a short period and then continue.
A pause is a short period when you stop doing something before continuing.
If something gives you pause for thought, it makes you think carefully about something, especially in a different way than you have thought about it before.
If a road or an area of ground has been paved, it has been covered with flat blocks of stone or concrete, so that it is suitable for walking or driving on.
If one thing paves the way for another, it creates a situation in which it is possible or more likely that the other thing will happen.
A pavement is a path with a hard surface, usually by the side of a road.
The pavement is the hard surface of a road.

Chinesesense: 爪子指手，尤用于形容手非常大或非常笨拙；
Englishsense: The paws of an animal such as a cat, dog, or bear are its feet, which have claws for gripping things and soft pads for walking on.
You can describe someone’s hand as their paw, especially if it is very large or if they are very clumsy.
If an animal paws something, it draws its foot over it or down it.
If one person paws another, they touch or stroke them in a way that the other person finds offensive.

Chinesesense: 为获得帮助或服务付钱给；
政府或机构通过提高价格、税率等使某人为…买单；
工作、交易或投资有…报酬，产生…利润；
工作、交易或投资有收益，盈利；
与某些名词连用，表示施予某物或做某事进行访问/给予注意；
电视节目付费的，收费的；
Englishsense: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe.
When you are paid, you get your wages or salary from your employer.
Your pay is the money that you get from your employer as wages or salary. See usage note at: salary
If you are paid to do something, someone gives you some money so that you will help them or perform some service for them.
If a government or organization makes someone pay for something, it makes them responsible for providing the money for it, for example by increasing prices or taxes.
If a job, deal, or investment pays a particular amount, it brings you that amount of money.
If a job, deal, or investment pays, it brings you a profit or earns you some money.
When you pay money into a bank account, you put the money in the account.
If a course of action pays, it results in some advantage or benefit for you.
If you pay for something that you do or have, you suffer as a result of it.
You use pay with some nouns, for example in the expressions pay a visit and pay attention, to indicate that something is given or done.
Pay television consists of programmes and channels which are not part of a public broadcasting system, and for which people have to pay.
If something that you buy or invest in pays for itself after a period of time, the money you gain from it, or save because you have it, is greater than the amount you originally spent or invested.
If you say that someone is in the pay of a certain person or group, you disapprove of the fact that they are being paid by and are working for that person or group, often secretly or illegally.
If you pay your way, you have or earn enough money to pay for what you need, without needing other people to give or lend you money.

Chinesesense: 付款额；支付的款项；支付；付款；
Englishsense: A payment is an amount of money that is paid to someone, or the act of paying this money.
Payment is the act of paying money to someone or of being paid.

Chinesesense: 用于避免麻烦的封口费，贿赂；
Englishsense: The payoff from an action is the advantage or benefit that you get from it.
A payoff is a payment which is made to someone, often secretly or illegally, so that they will not cause trouble.
A payoff is a large payment made to someone by their employer when the person has been forced to leave their job.
The people on the payroll of a company or an organization are the people who work for it and are paid by it.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 英国最低级别的男性警员；
政治上正确的；不嘲弄弱势群体的；
Englishsense: In Britain, a PC is a male police officer of the lowest rank. PC is an abbreviation for (缩略=) ’police constable’.
A PC is a computer that is used by one person at a time in a business, a school, or at home. PC is an abbreviation for (缩略=) ’personal computer’.

If you say that someone is PC, you mean that they are extremely careful not to offend or upset any group of people in society who have a disadvantage. PC is an abbreviation for (缩略=) ’politically correct’.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 遍布的；贯穿始终的；四处弥漫的；
Englishsense: Something, especially something bad, that is pervasive is present or felt throughout a place or thing.
Pests are insects or small animals which damage crops or food supplies.
You can describe someone, especially a child, as a pest if they keep bothering you.
Pesticides are chemicals which farmers put on their crops to kill harmful insects.

Chinesesense: 表示喜欢、友好的称呼宝贝，乖乖；
Englishsense: A pet is an animal that you keep in your home to give you company and pleasure.
Someone’s pet theory, project, or subject is one that they particularly support or like.
Some people call the person they are talking to ’ pet ’ to show affection or friendliness.
If you pet a person or animal, you touch them in an affectionate way.
The petals of a flower are the thin coloured or white parts which together form the flower.
A petition is a document signed by a lot of people which asks a government or other official group to do a particular thing.
A petition is a formal request made to a court of law for some legal action to be taken.
If you petition someone in authority, you make a formal request to them.
Petroleum is oil which is found under the surface of the earth or under the sea bed. Petrol and paraffin are obtained from petroleum.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 小题大做的；过于关注琐事的；
下级的；次要的；小规模的；
Englishsense: You can use petty to describe things such as problems, rules, or arguments which you think are unimportant or relate to unimportant things.
If you describe someone’s behaviour as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.
Petty is used of people or actions that are less important, serious, or great than others.
Pharmaceutical means connected with the industrial production of medicine.
Pharmaceuticals are medicines.
A pharmacy is a shop or a department in a shop where medicines are sold or given out.
Pharmacy is the job or the science of preparing medicines.

Chinesesense: 不同步的地/同步的[地]; 不协调的地/协调的地；
Englishsense: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.
If an action or change is phased over a period of time, it is done in stages.
If two things are out of phase with each other, they are not working or happening together as they should. If two things are in phase, they are working or occurring together as they should.
A PhD is a degree awarded to people who have done advanced research into a particular subject. PhD is an abbreviation for (缩略=) ’Doctor of Philosophy’.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 非凡的；不寻常的；惊人的；
Englishsense: Something that is phenomenal is so great or good that it is very unusual indeed.
A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist.
A philosopher is a person who studies or writes about philosophy.
If you refer to someone as a philosopher, you mean that they think deeply and seriously about life and other basic matters.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Philosophical means concerned with or relating to philosophy.
Someone who is philosophical does not get upset when disappointing or disturbing things happen.

Chinesesense: 哲学思想；哲学体系；哲学理论；
Englishsense: Philosophy is the study or creation of theories about basic things such as the nature of existence, knowledge, and thought, or about how people should live.
A philosophy is a particular set of ideas that a philosopher has.
A philosophy is a particular theory that someone has about how to live or how to deal with a particular situation.

Chinesesense: 装了电话的；可用电话联系的；
Englishsense: The phone is an electrical system that you use to talk to someone else in another place, by dialling a number on a piece of equipment and speaking into it.
The phone is the piece of equipment that you use when you dial someone’s phone number and talk to them.
If you say that someone picks up or puts down the phone, you mean that they lift or replace the receiver.
When you phone someone, you dial their phone number and speak to them by phone.
If you say that someone is on the phone, you mean that they are speaking to someone else by phone.
If you are on the phone, you have a phone in your home or place of work, so that you can be contacted by phone.
A photo is the same as a photograph.
A photograph is a picture that is made using a camera.
When you photograph someone or something, you use a camera to obtain a picture of them.
A photographer is someone who takes photographs as a job or hobby.

Chinesesense: 记忆精确的，能详细记录的；
Englishsense: Photographic means connected with photographs or photography.
If you have a photographic memory, you are able to remember things in great detail after you have seen them.
Photography is the skill, job, or process of producing photographs.
A phrase is a short group of words that people often use as a way of saying something. The meaning of a phrase is often not obvious from the meaning of the individual words in it.
A phrase is a small group of words which forms a unit, either on its own or within a sentence.
If you phrase something in a particular way, you express it in words in that way.
If someone has a particular turn of phrase, they have a particular way of expressing themselves in words. to coin a phrase

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 喜欢动手动脚的；有大量身体接触或碰撞的；
Englishsense: Physical qualities, actions, or things are connected with a person’s body, rather than with their mind.
Physical things are real things that can be touched and seen, rather than ideas or spoken words.
Physical means relating to the structure, size, or shape of something that can be touched and seen.
Physical means connected with physics or the laws of physics.
Someone who is physical touches people a lot, either in an affectionate way or in a rough way.
Physical is used in expressions such as physical love and physical relationships to refer to sexual relationships between people.
A physical is a medical examination, done in order to see if someone is fit and well enough to do a particular job or to join the army.

Chinesesense: 正式美国英语或过时英国英语中的医生，内科医生；
Englishsense: In formal American English or old-fashioned British English, a physician is a doctor.
A physicist is a person who does research connected with physics or who studies physics.
Physics is the scientific study of forces such as heat, light, sound, pressure, gravity, and electricity, and the way that they affect objects.
A pianist is a person who plays the piano.

A piano is a large musical instrument with a row of black and white keys. When you press these keys with your fingers, little hammers hit wire strings inside the piano which vibrate to produce musical notes.
A piece of music that is played piano is played quietly.

Chinesesense: 寻找…的口实；寻[衅]; 找碴儿；
撬开[锁]; 扒窃…中的东西；
挑挑拣拣；挑三拣四；挑剔；
收拾残局；努力恢复正常；
Englishsense: If you pick a particular person or thing, you choose that one.
You can refer to the best things or people in a particular group as the pick of that group.
When you pick flowers, fruit, or leaves, you break them off the plant or tree and collect them.
If you pick something from a place, you remove it from there with your fingers or your hand.
If you pick your nose or teeth, you remove substances from inside your nose or between your teeth.
If you pick a fight or quarrel with someone, you deliberately cause one.
If someone such as a thief picks a lock, they open it without a key, for example by using a piece of wire.
A pick is the same as a pickaxe.
If you pick and choose, you carefully choose only things that you really want and reject the others.
If you have your pick of a group of things, you are able to choose any of them that you want.
If you are told to take your pick, you can choose any one that you like from a group of things.
If you pick your way across an area, you walk across it very carefully in order to avoid obstacles or dangerous things.
When you pick up the pieces after a disaster, you do what you can to get the situation back to normal again.
When a vehicle picks up speed, it begins to move more quickly.

Chinesesense: 贸易或经济的好转，改善；
以发生性关系为目的的搭识，搭讪；
Englishsense: A pick-up or a pick-up truck is a small truck with low sides that can be easily loaded and unloaded.
A pick-up in trade or in a country’s economy is an improvement in it.
A pick-up takes place when someone picks up a person or thing that is waiting to be collected.
When a pick-up takes place, someone talks to a person in a friendly way in the hope of having a casual sexual relationship with them.

Chinesesense: 不是件轻松或愉快的事；
Englishsense: When people have a picnic, they eat a meal out of doors, usually in a field or a forest, or at the beach.
When people picnic somewhere, they have a picnic.
If you say that an experience, task, or activity is no picnic, you mean that it is quite difficult or unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 在报纸、杂志等上登载…的照片或图片；
想象；印象；心中的形象;头脑中的情景；
尤指通过他人描述弄明白情况，了解情形；
牵涉其中/不涉其中；在局内/在局外；
形容模样健康的化身/痛苦的典型；
使了解内情；向…介绍情况；
Englishsense: A picture consists of lines and shapes which are drawn, painted, or printed on a surface and show a person, thing, or scene.
A picture is a photograph.
Television pictures are the scenes which you see on a television screen.
To be pictured somewhere, for example in a newspaper or magazine, means to appear in a photograph or picture.
You can refer to a film as a picture.
If you go to the pictures, you go to a cinema to see a film.
If you have a picture of something in your mind, you have a clear idea or memory of it in your mind as if you were actually seeing it.
If you picture something in your mind, you think of it and have such a clear memory or idea of it that you seem to be able to see it.
A picture of something is a description of it or an indication of what it is like.
When you refer to the picture in a particular place, you are referring to the situation there.
If you get the picture, you understand the situation, especially one which someone is describing to you.

If you say that someone is in the picture, you mean that they are involved in the situation that you are talking about. If you say that they are out of the picture, you mean that they are not involved in the situation.

You use picture to describe what someone looks like. For example, if you say that someone is a picture of health or the picture of misery, you mean that they look extremely healthy or extremely miserable.
If you put someone in the picture, you tell them about a situation which they need to know about.

Chinesesense: 馅饼，派内有肉、蔬菜或水果的西式点心；
难以付诸实施的构想[或计划]; 渺茫的希望；空口的许诺；
Englishsense: A pie consists of meat, vegetables, or fruit baked in pastry.
If you describe an idea, plan, or promise of something good as pie in the sky, you mean that you think that it is very unlikely to happen.

Chinesesense: 断下、撕下或切下的块，片，段，截；
尤指可拆卸的部件，部分；
与不可数名词连用桩，项，条，件；
报纸或杂志上的一篇文章；一首或一部音乐作品；一段广播节目；一出戏剧；
安然无恙的；完好无损的；
说自己想说的话；毫不保留且不受打断地发表意见；
成碎片地；散了架地；成组件地；
难过或紧张得崩溃，垮掉；
把…说得一钱不值；把…批得体无完肤；
Englishsense: A piece of something is an amount of it that has been broken off, torn off, or cut off.
A piece of an object is one of the individual parts or sections which it is made of, especially a part that can be removed.
A piece of land is an area of land.
You can use piece of with many uncount nouns to refer to an individual thing of a particular kind. For example, you can refer to some advice as a piece of advice.
You can refer to an article in a newspaper or magazine, some music written by someone, a broadcast, or a play as a piece.
You can refer to a work of art as a piece.
You can refer to specific coins as pieces. For example, a 10p piece is a coin that is worth 10p.
The pieces which you use when you play a board game such as chess are the specially made objects which you move around on the board.
A piece of something is part of it or a share of it.
If you give someone a piece of your mind, you tell them very clearly that you think they have behaved badly.
If something with several different parts is all of a piece, each part is consistent with the others. If one thing is of a piece with another, it is consistent with it.
If someone or something is still in one piece after a dangerous journey or experience, they are safe and not damaged or hurt.
If you say your piece, you say everything you want to say about a particular matter without being interrupted, although people may be wanting to express opposing views.

You use to pieces in expressions such as ’smash to pieces’, and mainly in British English ’fall to pieces’ or ’take something to pieces’, when you are describing how something is broken or comes apart so that it is in separate pieces.
If you go to pieces, you are so upset or nervous that you lose control of yourself and cannot do what you should do.
If someone tears you to pieces, pulls your work to pieces, or picks your work to pieces, they criticize you or your work very severely.
If you say that someone is a nasty piece of work, you mean that they are very unkind or unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 通常指伸向大海的凸式码头，突码头，突堤；
Englishsense: A pier is a platform sticking out into water, usually the sea, which people walk along or use when getting onto or off boats.
If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.
If you have your ears or some other part of your body pierced, you have a small hole made through them so that you can wear a piece of jewellery in them.
If a light or sound pierces something or pierces through it, it is suddenly seen or heard very clearly.
If a thought, feeling, or sound pierces someone’s heart, it makes them experience a feeling, especially sadness, very strongly.
If someone pierces something that acts as a barrier, they manage to get through it.

Chinesesense: 猪猡；讨嫌的人；尤指贪婪的人，苛刻的人；
使贪婪地吃；使拼命大吃；
Englishsense: A pig is a pink or black animal with short legs and not much hair on its skin. Pigs are often kept on farms for their meat, which is called pork, ham, bacon, or gammon.
If you call someone a pig, you think that they are unpleasant in some way, especially that they are greedy or unkind.
If you say that something is, for example, a pig of a job, you mean it is very difficult.
If you say that people are pigging themselves, you are criticizing them for eating a very large amount at one meal.
If you make a pig’s ear of something you are doing, you do it very badly.
If you say ’ pigs might fly ’ after someone has said that something might happen, you are emphasizing that you think it is very unlikely.
If you say that someone is making a pig of themselves, you are criticizing them for eating a very large amount at one meal.
A pigeon is a bird, usually grey in colour, which has a fat body. Pigeons often live in towns.
A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular colour.

Chinesesense: 一个压着一个摆放整齐的叠，摞；
尤指富人或要人居住的高大宏伟的建筑物；
地毯或织物的绒面，绒毛，绒头；
处于社会或某组织的下层/上层；
Englishsense: A pile of things is a mass of them that is high in the middle and has sloping sides.
A pile of things is a quantity of things that have been put neatly somewhere so that each thing is on top of the one below.
If you pile things somewhere, you put them there so that they form a pile.
If something is piled with things, it is covered or filled with piles of things.
If you talk about a pile of something or piles of something, you mean a large amount of it.
If a group of people pile into or out of a vehicle, they all get into it or out of it in a disorganized way.
You can refer to a large impressive building as a pile, especially when it is the home of a rich important person.
Piles are wooden, concrete, or metal posts which are pushed into the ground and on which buildings or bridges are built. Piles are often used in very wet areas so that the buildings do not flood.
Piles are painful swellings that can appear in the veins inside a person’s anus.
The pile of a carpet or of a fabric such as velvet is its soft surface. It consists of a lot of little threads standing on end.
Someone who is at the bottom of the pile is low down in society or low down in an organization. Someone who is at the top of the pile is high up in society or high up in an organization.
Pilgrims are people who make a journey to a holy place for a religious reason.
If you make a pilgrimage to a holy place, you go there for a religious reason.
A pilgrimage is a journey that someone makes to a place that is very important to them.

Chinesesense: 不得不承受的苦事；不得不接受的现实；
把苦药包上糖衣；使不愉快的事变得较易接受；
Englishsense: Pills are small solid round masses of medicine or vitamins that you swallow without chewing.
If a woman is on the pill, she takes a special pill that prevents her from becoming pregnant.
If a person or group has to accept a failure or an unpleasant piece of news, you can say that it was a bitter pill or a bitter pill to swallow.
If someone does something to sweeten the pill or sugar the pill, they do it to make some unpleasant news or an unpleasant measure more acceptable.

Chinesesense: 制度、协议等的支柱，核心；
Englishsense: A pillar is a tall solid structure, which is usually used to support part of a building.
If something is the pillar of a system or agreement, it is the most important part of it or what makes it strong and successful.
If you describe someone as a pillar of society or as a pillar of the community, you approve of them because they play an important and active part in society or in the community.
A pillow is a rectangular cushion which you rest your head on when you are in bed.

Chinesesense: 驾驶[飞机等]; 为船舶引航；
试验性的方案；试点性的项目；
使新的法律或议案顺利通过；
电视的试播节目，试播集；
煤气灶具、锅炉等用于引火的常燃小火；
Englishsense: A pilot is a person who is trained to fly an aircraft.
A pilot is a person who steers a ship through a difficult stretch of water, for example the entrance to a harbour.
If someone pilots an aircraft or ship, they act as its pilot.
A pilot scheme or a pilot project is one which is used to test an idea before deciding whether to introduce it on a larger scale.
If a government or organization pilots a programme or a scheme, they test it, before deciding whether to introduce it on a larger scale.
If a government minister pilots a new law or bill through parliament, he or she makes sure that it is introduced successfully.
A pilot or a pilot episode is a single television programme that is shown in order to find out whether a particular series of programmes is likely to be popular.
A pilot is the pilot light on a gas cooker or stove, boiler, or fire.

Chinesesense: 偷取，偷盗尤指不贵重的物品；
感到手头拮据；感到囊中羞涩；
Englishsense: If you pinch a part of someone’s body, you take a piece of their skin between your thumb and first finger and give it a short squeeze.
A pinch of an ingredient such as salt is the amount of it that you can hold between your thumb and your first finger. to take something with a pinch of salt
To pinch something, especially something of little value, means to steal it.

If you say that something is possible at a pinch, or in American English if you say that something is possible in a pinch, you mean that it would be possible if it was necessary, but it might not be very comfortable or convenient.
If a person or company is feeling the pinch, they do not have as much money as they used to, and so they cannot buy the things they would like to buy.
If you are in a pinch, you are in a difficult situation.

Chinesesense: 因死亡或离别而怀念，苦苦思念，为…难过；
渴望，苦苦盼望尤指不大可能拥有的东西；
Englishsense: A pine tree or a pine is a tall tree which has very thin, sharp leaves and a fresh smell. Pine trees have leaves all year round.
If you pine for someone who has died or gone away, you want them to be with you very much and feel sad because they are not there.
If you pine for something, you want it very much, especially when it is unlikely that you will be able to have it.
A pineapple is a large oval fruit that grows in hot countries. It is sweet, juicy, and yellow inside. It has a thick brownish skin.

Chinesesense: 因窘迫、愤怒或剧烈活动而脸色发红；
非常健康；满面红光；容光焕发；
Englishsense: Pink is the colour between red and white.
If you go pink, your face turns a slightly redder colour than usual because you are embarrassed or angry, or because you are doing something energetic.
Pink is used to refer to things relating to or connected with homosexuals.
Pinks are small plants that people grow in their gardens. They have sweet-smelling pink, white, or red flowers.
If you are in the pink, you are fit, healthy, and happy.

Chinesesense: 精确地确定或指明…的位置；
定点的；定位精确的；非常精确的；
Englishsense: If you pinpoint the cause of something, you discover or explain the cause exactly.
If you pinpoint something or its position, you discover or show exactly where it is.
If something is placed with pinpoint accuracy, it is placed in exactly the right place or position.

Chinesesense: 先驱；先锋；创始人；倡导者；
Englishsense: Someone who is referred to as a pioneer in a particular area of activity is one of the first people to be involved in it and develop it.
Someone who pioneers a new activity, invention, or process is one of the first people to do it.
Pioneers are people who leave their own country or the place where they were living, and go and live in a place that has not been lived in before.
Pioneering work or a pioneering individual does something that has not been done before, for example by developing or using new methods or techniques.

Chinesesense: 通常指金属或塑料制的管子，管道；
管风琴的音管， 风管；
用管子输送，用管道运输液体或气体；
一些计算机系统中用来在程序间传送信息的管道；
Englishsense: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.
A pipe is an object which is used for smoking tobacco. You put the tobacco into the cup-shaped part at the end of the pipe, light it, and breathe in the smoke through a narrow tube.
A pipe is a simple musical instrument in the shape of a tube with holes in it. You play a pipe by blowing into it while covering and uncovering the holes with your fingers.
Pipes are the same as bagpipes.
An organ pipe is one of the long hollow tubes in which air vibrates and produces a musical note.
If liquid or gas is piped somewhere, it is transferred from one place to another through a pipe.
If someone, especially a child, pipes something, they say it in a high-pitched voice.
In some computer systems, a pipe is a method of passing information from one program to another.

Chinesesense: 常指埋于地下的石油或燃气管道，管线；
Englishsense: A pipeline is a large pipe which is used for carrying oil or gas over a long distance, often underground.
If something is in the pipeline, it has already been planned or begun.

Chinesesense: 非法复制及出售录像带、录音带、书籍、计算机程序等；
Englishsense: Pirates are sailors who attack other ships and steal property from them.
You can refer to someone who behaves in an immoral or illegal way as a pirate.
Someone who pirates video tapes, cassettes, books, or computer programs copies and sells them when they have no right to do so.
A pirate version of something is an illegal copy of it.

Chinesesense: 笑得不能自制；笑破肚皮；
Englishsense: To piss means to urinate.
If someone has a piss, they urinate.
Piss is urine.
If it is pissing with rain, it is raining very hard.
If someone is pissing themselves, or is pissing themselves laughing, they are laughing a lot.
If you take the piss out of someone, you tease them and make fun of them.
If someone tells a person to piss off, they are telling the person in a rude way to go away.
A pistol is a small gun.

Chinesesense: 地面的坑，洼；地下的穴，洞；
挖出沙砾或黏土后留下的坑，窑；
赛车道旁的检修加油站；
Englishsense: A pit is a coal mine.
A pit is a large hole that is dug in the ground.
A gravel pit or clay pit is a very large hole that is left where gravel or clay has been dug from the ground.
If two opposing things or people are pitted against one another, they are in conflict.
In motor racing, the pits are the areas at the side of the track where drivers stop to get more fuel and to repair their cars during races.
If you describe something as the pits, you mean that it is extremely bad.
A pit is the stone of a fruit or vegetable.
If you pit your wits against someone, you compete with them in a test of knowledge or intelligence.
If you have a feeling in the pit of your stomach, you have a tight or sick feeling in your stomach, usually because you are afraid or anxious.

Chinesesense: 足球、板球、曲棍球等运动的球场；
通常指仔细瞄准后用力投，掷，扔，抛；
棒球或跑柱式棒球运动中把球投给击球员；
把…定在特定的水平、难易程度等上；
船只在海浪中上下颠簸，纵摇；
Englishsense: A pitch is an area of ground that is marked out and used for playing a game such as football, cricket, or hockey.
If you pitch something somewhere, you throw it with quite a lot of force, usually aiming it carefully.
To pitch somewhere means to fall forwards suddenly and with a lot of force.
If someone is pitched into a new situation, they are suddenly forced into it.
In the game of baseball or rounders, when you pitch the ball, you throw it to the batter for them to hit it.
The pitch of a sound is how high or low it is.
If a sound is pitched at a particular level, it is produced at the level indicated.
If something is pitched at a particular level or degree of difficulty, it is set at that level.
If something such as a feeling or a situation rises to a high pitch, it rises to a high level.
If you pitch your tent, or pitch camp, you put up your tent in a place where you are going to stay. [V n]
If a boat pitches, it moves violently up and down with the movement of the waves when the sea is rough.
Pitch is a black substance that is sticky when it is hot and very hard when it is dry. Pitch is used on the bottoms of boats and on the roofs of houses to prevent water getting in.
If someone makes a pitch for something, they try to persuade people to do or buy it.

Chinesesense: 通常指筒状细颈双耳的陶罐，陶壶；
Englishsense: A pitcher is a jug.
A pitcher is a large container made of clay. Pitchers are usually round in shape and have a narrow neck and two handles shaped like ears.
In baseball, the pitcher is the person who throws the ball to the batter, who tries to hit it.

Chinesesense: 尤在恼怒或不快时用于强调行行好，发发慈悲吧；
对…表示同情；对…表示怜悯；
用于强调可惜的是，遗憾的是；
Englishsense: If you feel pity for someone, you feel very sorry for them.
If you pity someone, you feel very sorry for them.
If you say that it is a pity that something is the case, you mean that you feel disappointment or regret about it.
If someone shows pity, they do not harm or punish someone they have power over.
If you add more’s the pity to a comment, you are expressing your disappointment or regret about something.
You can say for pity’s sake to add emphasis to what you are saying, especially when you are annoyed or upset.
If you take pity on someone, you feel sorry for them and help them.
If you say the pity is that, or the pity of it is that, before a comment, you are emphasizing your disappointment or regret about something.
A pivotal role, point or figure in something is one that is very important and affects the success of that thing.
A pizza is a flat, round piece of dough covered with tomatoes, cheese, and other savoury food, and then baked in an oven.

Chinesesense: 用于测试新药效力的无效对照剂；用以安慰想象自己得病的人的安慰剂；
Englishsense: A placebo is a substance with no effects that a doctor gives to a patient instead of a drug. Placebos are used when testing new drugs or sometimes when a patient has imagined their illness.
The placement of something or someone is the act of putting them in a particular place or position.
If someone who is training gets a placement, they get a job for a period of time which is intended to give them experience in the work they are training for.
The placement of someone in a job, home, or school is the act or process of finding them a job, home, or school.
You can refer to a home that is found for someone who is unable to look after themselves, for example a child, as a placement.

Chinesesense: 某一事物肆虐造成的灾难，祸患；
Englishsense: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills large numbers of people.
Plague or the plague is a very infectious disease which usually results in death. The patient has a severe fever and swellings on his or her body.
A plague of unpleasant things is a large number of them that arrive or happen at the same time.
If you describe something as a plague, you mean that it causes a great deal of trouble or harm.
If you are plagued by unpleasant things, they continually cause you a lot of trouble or suffering.
If someone plagues you, they keep bothering you or asking you for something.
If you say that you avoid someone or something like the plague, you are emphasizing that you deliberately avoid them completely.
You say a plague on a particular person or thing when you are very irritated by them and do not want to bother with them any more.
