Englishsense: In a sport or game, if a player scores a goal or a point, they gain a goal or point.
If you score a particular number or amount, for example as a mark in a test, you achieve that number or amount.
Someone’s score in a game or test is a number, for example, a number of points or runs, which shows what they have achieved or what level they have reached.
The score in a game is the result of it or the current situation, as indicated by the number of goals, runs, or points obtained by the two teams or players.
If you score a success, a victory, or a hit, you are successful in what you are doing.
The score of a film, play, or similar production is the music which is written or used for it.
The score of a piece of music is the written version of it.
If you score a piece of music, you write it or arrange it for specific instruments or voices.
If you refer to scores of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.
A score is twenty or approximately twenty.
If you score a surface with something sharp, you cut a line or number of lines in it.
If someone scores drugs, they buy them illegally.
If things happen or exist by the score, they happen or exist in large numbers.
If you keep score of the number of things that are happening in a certain situation, you count them and record them.
If you know the score, you know what the real facts of a situation are and how they affect you, even though you may not like them.
You can use on that score or on this score to refer to something that has just been mentioned, especially an area of difficulty or concern.
If you score a point over someone, or score points off them, you gain an advantage over them, usually by saying something clever or making a better argument.
If you settle a score or settle an old score with someone, you take revenge on them for something they have done in the past.

Chinesesense: 苏格兰的;苏格兰人的;苏格兰语的；
Englishsense: Something that is Scottish belongs or relates to Scotland, its people, or its language.
If you scour something such as a place or a book, you make a thorough search of it to try to find what you are looking for.
If you scour something such as a sink, floor, or pan, you clean its surface by rubbing it hard with something rough.

Chinesesense: 倒换(无线电或电话信号)的频率(使只有持特殊仪器的人才能接收)；
Englishsense: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you.
If you scramble to a different place or position, you move there in a hurried, awkward way.
If a number of people scramble for something, they compete energetically with each other for it.
If you scramble eggs, you break them, mix them together and then heat and stir the mixture in a pan.
If a device scrambles a radio or telephone message, it interferes with the sound so that the message can only be understood by someone with special equipment.
A scrap of something is a very small piece or amount of it.
Scraps are pieces of unwanted food which are thrown away or given to animals.
If you scrap something, you get rid of it or cancel it.
Scrap metal or paper is no longer wanted for its original purpose, but may have some other use.
Scrap is metal from old or damaged machinery or cars.
You can refer to a fight or a quarrel as a scrap, especially if it is not very serious.

Chinesesense: (尤指用锋利物)刮落,削掉，擦掉；
摩擦使发出刺耳声;擦伤;蹭破；
Englishsense: If you scrape something from a surface, you remove it, especially by pulling a sharp object over the surface.
If something scrapes against something else or if someone or something scrapes something else, it rubs against it, making a noise or causing slight damage.
If you scrape a part of your body, you accidentally rub it against something hard and rough, and damage it slightly.
If you are in a scrape, you are in a difficult situation which you have caused yourself.

Chinesesense: 从零开始;从头做起;白手起家；
触及表面;隔靴搔痒;浅尝辄止；
达到标准;合格;令人满意；
Englishsense: If you scratch yourself, you rub your fingernails against your skin because it is itching.
If a sharp object scratches someone or something, it makes small shallow cuts on their skin or surface.
Scratches on someone or something are small shallow cuts.
If you do something from scratch, you do it without making use of anything that has been done before.
If you say that someone is scratching their head, you mean that they are thinking hard and trying to solve a problem or puzzle.
If you only scratch the surface of a subject or problem, you find out or do a small amount, but not enough to understand or solve it.
If you say that someone or something is not up to scratch, you mean that they are not good enough.
When someone screams, they make a very loud, high-pitched cry, for example because they are in pain or are very frightened.
If you scream something, you shout it in a loud, high-pitched voice.
When something makes a loud, high-pitched noise, you can say that it screams.
If you say that someone is a scream, you think they are very funny.

Chinesesense: (电视、电脑的)屏幕;(电影的)银幕；
放映(电影);播放(电视节目)；
检查，筛查(以确定是否患病)；
对(人、行李)进行安全检查；
转接，甄别(来电以决定是否接听)；
Englishsense: A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown. Television sets and computers have screens, and films are shown on a screen in cinemas.
You can refer to film or television as the screen.
When a film or a television programme is screened, it is shown in the cinema or broadcast on television.
A screen is a vertical panel which can be moved around. It is used to keep cold air away from part of a room, or to create a smaller area within a room.
If something is screened by another thing, it is behind it and hidden by it.
To screen for a disease means to examine people to make sure that they do not have it.
When an organization screens people who apply to join it, it investigates them to make sure that they are not likely to cause problems.
To screen people or luggage means to check them using special equipment to make sure they are not carrying a weapon or a bomb.
If you screen your telephone calls, calls made to you are connected to an answering machine or are answered by someone else, so that you can choose whether or not to speak to the people phoning you.
A screenplay is the words to be spoken in a film, and instructions about what will be seen in it.

Chinesesense: 把(纸等)揉成一团，拧成一团；
愈逼愈紧的压力(或行动)；
Englishsense: A screw is a metal object similar to a nail, with a raised spiral line around it. You turn a screw using a screwdriver so that it goes through two things, for example two pieces of wood, and fastens them together.
If you screw something somewhere or if it screws somewhere, you fix it in place by means of a screw or screws.
A screw lid or fitting is one that has a raised spiral line on the inside or outside of it, so that it can be fixed in place by twisting.
If you screw something somewhere or if it screws somewhere, you fix it in place by twisting it round and round.
If you screw something such as a piece of paper into a ball, you squeeze it or twist it tightly so that it is in the shape of a ball.
If you screw your face or your eyes into a particular expression, you tighten the muscles of your face to form that expression, for example because you are in pain or because the light is too bright.
If someone screws someone else or if two people screw, they have sex together.
Some people use screw in expressions such as screw you or screw that to show that they are not concerned about someone or something or that they feel contempt for them.
If someone says that they have been screwed, they mean that someone else has cheated them, especially by getting money from them dishonestly.
If someone screws something, especially money, out of you, they get it from you by putting pressure on you.
Prisoners often refer to prison officers as screws.
A screw is a propeller on a ship or an aircraft.
If you turn or tighten the screw on someone, you increase the pressure which is already on them, for example by using threats, in order to force them to do a particular thing.
You can refer to each of a series of threats or actions which are intended to force someone to do a particular thing as another turn of the screw.

Chinesesense: (戏剧、电影)剧本;(电视节目)广播稿；
为(电影等)写剧本;为(广播、电视节目)撰稿；
(一种语言的)书写系统，字母表；
Englishsense: The script of a play, film, or television programme is the written version of it.
The person who scripts a film or a radio or television play writes it.
You can refer to a particular system of writing as a particular script.
If you say that something which has happened is not in the script, or that someone has not followed the script, you mean that something has happened which was not expected or intended to happen.

Chinesesense: (尤指少雨地区的)低矮丛林，灌木丛；
Englishsense: If you scrub something, you rub it hard in order to clean it, using a stiff brush and water.
If you scrub dirt or stains off something, you remove them by rubbing hard.
Scrub consists of low trees and bushes, especially in an area that has very little rain.
If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

Chinesesense: 详细的检查(或审查);仔细的观察；
Englishsense: If a person or thing is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.
A sculptor is someone who creates sculptures.
A sculpture is a work of art that is produced by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay, or other materials.
Sculpture is the art of creating sculptures.
When people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.
If people scurry to do something, they do it as soon as they can.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
Englishsense: The sea is the salty water that covers about three-quarters of the earth’s surface.
You use seas when you are describing the sea at a particular time or in a particular area.
A sea is a large area of salty water that is part of an ocean or is surrounded by land.
A sea of people or things is a very large number of them together.
You can say that someone is all at sea when they are in a state of confusion or uncertainty.
At sea means on or under the sea, far away from land.
If you go or look out to sea, you go or look across the sea.
Seafood is shellfish such as lobsters, mussels, and crabs, and sometimes other sea creatures that you can eat.

Chinesesense: 封住(容器、开口);把…密封(进容器)；
盖上印信的;不能拆开看的;保密的；
Englishsense: When you seal an envelope, you close it by folding part of it over and sticking it down, so that it cannot be opened without being torn.

If you seal a container or an opening, you cover it with something in order to prevent air, liquid, or other material getting in or out. If you seal something in a container, you put it inside and then close the container tightly.
The seal on a container or opening is the part where it has been sealed.
A seal is a device or a piece of material, for example in a machine, which closes an opening tightly so that air, liquid, or other substances cannot get in or out.
A seal is something such as a piece of sticky paper or wax that is fixed to a container or door and must be broken before the container or door can be opened.
A seal is a special mark or design, for example on a document, representing someone or something. It may be used to show that something is genuine or officially approved.
If someone in authority seals an area, they stop people entering or passing through it, for example by placing barriers in the way.
To seal something means to make it definite or confirm how it is going to be.
If something sets or puts the seal on something, it makes it definite or confirms how it is going to be. [V inflects] [WRITTEN 笔语]
If a document is under seal, it is in a sealed envelope and cannot be looked at, for example because it is private.
A seal is a large animal with a rounded body and flat legs called flippers. Seals eat fish and live in and near the sea, usually in cold parts of the world.
A seam is a line of stitches which joins two pieces of cloth together.
A seam of coal is a long, narrow layer of it underneath the ground.
If something is coming apart at the seams or is falling apart at the seams, it is no longer working properly and may soon stop working completely.
If a place is very full, you can say that it is bursting at the seams.

Chinesesense: 在…中搜寻(或搜索);搜查(某地)；
Englishsense: If you search for something or someone, you look carefully for them.
If you search a place, you look carefully for something or someone there.
A search is an attempt to find something or someone by looking for them carefully.
If a police officer or someone else in authority searches you, they look carefully to see whether you have something hidden on you.
If you search for information on a computer, you give the computer an instruction to find that information.
If you go in search of something or someone, you try to find them.
You say ’ search me ’ when someone asks you a question and you want to emphasize that you do not know the answer.

Chinesesense: (一年中某项活动或某一事件发生的)节期，时期；
(水果、蔬菜等的)当令期，上市期；
(戏剧、表演的)上演期，会演期，献演期；
对(木材)作干燥处理;风干，晒干(木材)；
Englishsense: The seasons are the main periods into which a year can be divided and which each have their own typical weather conditions.
You can use season to refer to the period during each year when a particular activity or event takes place. For example, the planting season is the period when a particular plant or crop is planted.
You can use season to refer to the period when a particular fruit, vegetable, or other food is ready for eating and is widely available.
You can use season to refer to a fixed period during each year when a particular sport is played.
A season is a period in which a play or show, or a series of plays or shows, is performed in one place.
A season of films is several of them shown as a series because they are connected in some way.
The holiday or vacation season is the time when most people have their holiday.
If you season food with salt, pepper, or spices, you add them to it in order to improve its flavour.
If wood is seasoned, it is made suitable for making into furniture or for burning, usually by being allowed to dry out gradually.
If a female animal is in season, she is in a state where she is ready to have sex.

Chinesesense: 季节的;季节性的;随季节变化的；
Englishsense: A seasonal factor, event, or change occurs during one particular time of the year.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: You can use seasoned to describe a person who has a lot of experience of something. For example, a seasoned traveller is a person who has travelled a lot.
Seasoning is salt, pepper, or other spices that are added to food to improve its flavour.

Chinesesense: (公司董事会、委员会中的)席位，职位；
(组织、活动的)中心地，所在地;(豪门的)宅邸；
让权于他人;退居次要位置；
Englishsense: A seat is an object that you can sit on, for example a chair.
The seat of a chair is the part that you sit on.
If you seat yourself somewhere, you sit down.
A building or vehicle that seats a particular number of people has enough seats for that number.
The seat of a piece of clothing is the part that covers your bottom.
When someone is elected to a parliament, congress, or senate, you can say that they, or their party, have won a seat.
If someone has a seat on the board of a company or on a committee, they are a member of it.
The seat of an organization, a wealthy family, or an activity is its base.
If you take a back seat, you allow other people to have all the power and to make all the decisions.
If you take a seat, you sit down.

Chinesesense: (公共场所、正式场合的)座位安排(或设置)；
Englishsense: You can refer to the seats in a place as the seating.
The seating at a public place or a formal occasion is the arrangement of where people will sit.

Chinesesense: 秒(a second 或 seconds 往往用以表示很短的时间)；
(用于形容词最高级前)第二…的；
二级甲等/乙等优秀学位；
二级品;二等货;次货;等外品；
(拳击或国际象棋锦标赛的)副手，助手；
不比任何事物差;首屈一指；
Englishsense: A second is one of the sixty parts that a minute is divided into. People often say ’ a second ’ or ’ seconds ’ when they simply mean a very short time.
The second item in a series is the one that you count as number two.
Second is used before superlative adjectives to indicate that there is only one thing better or larger than the thing you are referring to.
You say second when you want to make a second point or give a second reason for something.
In Britain, an upper second is a good honours degree and a lower second is an average honours degree.
If you have seconds, you have a second helping of food.
Seconds are goods that are sold cheaply in shops because they have slight faults.
The seconds of someone who is taking part in a boxing match or chess tournament are the people who assist and encourage them.
If you second a proposal in a meeting or debate, you formally express your agreement with it so that it can then be discussed or voted on.
If you second what someone has said, you say that you agree with them or say the same thing yourself.
If you experience something at second hand, you are told about it by other people rather than experiencing it yourself.
If you say that something is second to none, you are emphasizing that it is very good indeed or the best that there is.
If you say that something is second only to something else, you mean that only that thing is better or greater than it.
If you are seconded somewhere, you are sent there temporarily by your employer in order to do special duties.

Chinesesense: 第二位的;次要的;从属的；
(疾病、感染)继发性的，第二期的；
Englishsense: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.
Secondary diseases or infections happen as a result of another disease or infection that has already happened.
Secondary education is given to pupils between the ages of 11 or 12 and 17 or 18.

Chinesesense: (用于列举观点或给出原因)第二，其次；
Englishsense: You say secondly when you want to make a second point or give a second reason for something.
Secrecy is the act of keeping something secret, or the state of being kept secret.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If something is secret, it is known about by only a small number of people, and is not told or shown to anyone else.
A secret is a fact that is known by only a small number of people, and is not told to anyone else.
If you say that a particular way of doing things is the secret of achieving something, you mean that it is the best or only way to achieve it.
Something’s secrets are the things about it which have never been fully explained.
If you do something in secret, you do it without anyone else knowing.
If you say that someone can keep a secret, you mean that they can be trusted not to tell other people a secret that you have told them.
If you make no secret of something, you tell others about it openly and clearly.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Chinesesense: (工会、政党、俱乐部等的)干事,书记员；
Englishsense: A secretary is a person who is employed to do office work, such as typing letters, answering phone calls, and arranging meetings.
The secretary of an organization such as a trade union, a political party, or a club is its official manager.
The secretary of a company is the person who has the legal duty of keeping the company’s records.
Secretary is used in the titles of ministers and officials who are in charge of main government departments.

Chinesesense: 把…切成片;把…分成段(或组等)；
Englishsense: A section of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.
If something is sectioned, it is divided into sections.
A section of an official document such as a report, law, or constitution is one of the parts into which it is divided.
A section is a diagram of something such as a building or a part of the body. It shows how the object would appear to you if it were cut from top to bottom and looked at from the side.

Chinesesense: 军事管制区;军事防御区；
Englishsense: A particular sector of a country’s economy is the part connected with that specified type of industry.
A sector of a large group is a smaller group which is part of it.
A sector is an area of a city or country which is controlled by a military force.
A sector is a part of a circle which is formed when you draw two straight lines from the centre of the circle to the edge.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 世俗的;现世的;非宗教的；
Englishsense: You use secular to describe things that have no connection with religion.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

Chinesesense: 使…免遭攻击(或伤害);保卫;保护；
固定不动的;绑紧的;系牢的；
安心的;心里踏实的;无忧无虑的；
Englishsense: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.
If you secure a place, you make it safe from harm or attack.
A secure place is tightly locked or well protected, so that people cannot enter it or leave it.
If you secure an object, you fasten it firmly to another object.
If an object is secure, it is fixed firmly in position.
If you describe something such as a job as secure, it is certain not to change or end.
A secure base or foundation is strong and reliable.
If you feel secure, you feel safe and happy and are not worried about life.
If a loan is secured, the person who lends the money may take property such as a house from the person who borrows the money if they fail to repay it.

Chinesesense: 防卫;保安措施;安全工作；
Englishsense: Security refers to all the measures that are taken to protect a place, or to ensure that only people with permission enter it or leave it.
A feeling of security is a feeling of being safe and free from worry.
If something is security for a loan, you promise to give that thing to the person who lends you money, if you fail to pay the money back.
Securities are stocks, shares, bonds, or other certificates that you buy in order to earn regular interest from them or to sell them later for a profit.
A sedan is a car with seats for four or more people, a fixed roof, and a boot that is separate from the part of the car that you sit in.
Sediment is solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid, especially earth and pieces of rock that have been carried along and then left somewhere by water, ice, or wind.
If something seduces you, it is so attractive that it makes you do something that you would not otherwise do.
If someone seduces another person, they use their charm to persuade that person to have sex with them.

Chinesesense: 看出;看上，欣赏(某种特质)；
(表示暂不作决定)看看吧，再说吧；
(表示试图记起某事或找到某物)让我想一想，让我看看；
(用于向某人解释某事物并鼓励其倾听和理解)你瞧，你知道，看吧；
到时候你就知道了;你等着瞧吧；
Englishsense: When you see something, you notice it using your eyes.
If you see someone, you visit them or meet them.
If you see an entertainment such as a play, film, concert, or sports game, you watch it.
If you see that something is true or exists, you realize by observing it that it is true or exists.
If you see what someone means or see why something happened, you understand what they mean or understand why it happened.
If you see someone or something as a certain thing, you have the opinion that they are that thing.

If you see a particular quality in someone, you believe they have that quality. If you ask what someone sees in a particular person or thing, you want to know what they find attractive about that person or thing.
If you see something happening in the future, you imagine it, or predict that it will happen.
If a period of time or a person sees a particular change or event, it takes place during that period of time or while that person is alive.
You can use see in expressions to do with finding out information. For example, if you say ’ I’ll see what’s happening ’, you mean that you intend to find out what is happening.
You can use see to promise to try and help someone. For example, if you say ’ I’ll see if I can do it ’, you mean that you will try to do the thing concerned.
If you see that something is done or if you see to it that it is done, you make sure that it is done.
If you see someone to a particular place, you accompany them to make sure that they get there safely, or to show politeness.
If you see a lot of someone, you often meet each other or visit each other.
If you are seeing someone, you spend time with them socially, and are having a romantic or sexual relationship.
Some writers use see in expressions such as we saw and as we have seen to refer to something that has already been explained or described.
See is used in books to indicate to readers that they should look at another part of the book, or at another book, because more information is given there.
You can use seeing that or seeing as to introduce a reason for what you are saying.
You can say ’ I see ’ to indicate that you understand what someone is telling you.
People say ’ I’ll see ’ or ’ We’ll see ’ to indicate that they do not intend to make a decision immediately, and will decide later.
People say ’ let me see ’ or ’ let’s see ’ when they are trying to remember something, or are trying to find something.
If you try to make someone see sense or see reason, you try to make them realize that they are wrong or are being stupid.
You can say ’ you see ’ when you are explaining something to someone, to encourage them to listen and understand.
’ See you ’, ’ be seeing you ’, and ’ see you later ’ are ways of saying goodbye to someone when you expect to meet them again soon.
You can say ’ You’ll see ’ to someone if they do not agree with you about what you think will happen in the future, and you believe that you will be proved right.

Chinesesense: (网球、羽毛球等体育项目中的)种子选手；
将(选手或参赛队)排列名次；
衰老;风光不再;衰退;退化；
Englishsense: A seed is the small, hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows.
If you seed a piece of land, you plant seeds in it.
You can refer to the seeds of something when you want to talk about the beginning of a feeling or process that gradually develops and becomes stronger or more important.
In sports such as tennis or badminton, a seed is a player who has been ranked according to his or her ability.
When a player or a team is seeded in a sports competition, they are ranked according to their ability.
If vegetable plants go to seed or run to seed, they produce flowers and seeds as well as leaves.
If you say that someone or something has gone to seed or has run to seed, you mean that they have become much less attractive, healthy, or efficient.
If you seek something such as a job or a place to live, you try to find one.
When someone seeks something, they try to obtain it.
If you seek someone’s help or advice, you contact them in order to ask for it.
If you seek to do something, you try to do it.

Chinesesense: 寻找者;寻求者;追求者;谋求者；
Englishsense: A seeker is someone who is looking for or trying to get something.

Chinesesense: (在描述自己的感觉、想法、经历时用于缓和语气)好像，似乎；
Englishsense: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.
You use seem when you are describing your own feelings or thoughts, or describing something that has happened to you, in order to make your statement less forceful.
If you say that you cannot seem or could not seem to do something, you mean that you have tried to do it and were unable to.

Chinesesense: 貌似，看似(但可能并非如此)；
Englishsense: If something is seemingly the case, you mean that it appears to be the case, even though it may not really be so.
You use seemingly when you want to say that something seems to be true.

Chinesesense: (秘密)逐渐外泄;(不快的情感)逐渐释放；
Englishsense: If something such as liquid or gas seeps somewhere, it flows slowly and in small amounts into a place where it should not go.
If something such as secret information or an unpleasant emotion seeps somewhere, it comes out gradually.
A segment of something is one part of it, considered separately from the rest.
A segment of fruit such as an orange or grapefruit is one of the sections into which it is easily divided.
A segment of a circle is one of the two parts into which it is divided when you draw a straight line through it.
A segment of a market is one part of it, considered separately from the rest.
If a company segments a market, it divides it into separate parts, usually in order to improve marketing opportunities.

If someone or something is of service to you, they help you or are useful to you.

Englishsense: A set of things is a number of things that belong together or that are thought of as a group.

In mathematics, a set is a group of mathematical quantities that have some characteristic in common.
A band’s or musician’s set is the group of songs or tunes that they perform at a concert.
You can refer to a group of people as a set if they meet together socially or have the same interests and lifestyle.
The set for a play, film, or television show is the furniture and scenery that is on the stage when the play is being performed or in the studio where filming takes place.
The set of someone’s face or part of their body is the way that it is fixed in a particular expression or position, especially one that shows determination.
A set is an appliance. For example, a television set is a television.
If you set something somewhere, you put it there, especially in a careful or deliberate way.
If something is set in a particular place or position, it is in that place or position. [v-link ADJ prep/adv]
If something is set into a surface, it is fixed there and does not stick out.

When you set a clock or control, you adjust it to a particular point or level.
If you set a date, price, goal, or level, you decide what it will be.
If you set a certain value on something, you think it has that value.
If you set something such as a record, an example, or a precedent, you do something that people will want to copy or try to achieve.
If someone sets you a task or aim or if you set yourself a task or aim, you need to succeed in doing it.
To set an examination or a question paper means to decide what questions will be asked in it.
You use set to describe something which is fixed and cannot be changed. [usu ADJ n]
A set book must be studied by students taking a particular course.
If a play, film, or story is set in a particular place or period of time, the events in it take place in that place or period.
If you are set to do something, you are ready to do it or are likely to do it. If something is set to happen, it is about to happen or likely to happen.
If you are set on something, you are strongly determined to do or have it. If you are set against something, you are strongly determined not to do or have it.
If you set your face or jaw, you put on a fixed expression of determination.
When something such as jelly, melted plastic, or cement sets, it becomes firm or hard.
When the sun sets, it goes below the horizon.
To set a trap means to prepare it to catch someone or something.
When someone sets the table, they prepare it for a meal by putting plates and cutlery on it.
If someone sets a poem or a piece of writing to music, they write music for the words to be sung to.
If someone sets the scene or sets the stage for an event to take place, they make preparations so that it can take place.
If you say that someone is set in their ways, you are being critical of the fact that they have fixed habits and ideas which they will not easily change, even though they may be old-fashioned.
If you set up a temporary structure, you place it or build it somewhere.
If you set up a device or piece of machinery, you do the things that are necessary for it to be able to start working.
If you set up somewhere or set yourself up somewhere, you establish yourself in a new business or new area.
If you set up home or set up shop, you buy a house or business of your own and start living or working there.
If something sets up something such as a process, it creates it or causes it to begin.
If something sets you up for something, it puts you in a good condition or position to deal with it, for example by making you feel healthy and energetic.
If you are set up by someone, they make it seem that you have done something wrong when you have not.
A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

A table setting is the complete set of equipment that one person needs to eat a meal, including knives, forks, spoons, and glasses.

Englishsense: If people settle an argument or problem, or if something settles it, they solve it, for example by making a decision about who is right or about what to do.

If you settle a bill or debt, you pay the amount that you owe.
If something is settled, it has all been decided and arranged.
To settle money on someone means to formally give it to them, for example in a will.
When people settle a place or in a place, or when a government settles them there, they start living there permanently.
If you settle yourself somewhere or settle somewhere, you sit down or make yourself comfortable.
If something settles or if you settle it, it sinks slowly down and becomes still.
If your eyes settle on or upon something, you stop looking around and look at that thing for some time.
When birds or insects settle on something, they land on it from above.

The settlement of a debt is the act of paying back money that you owe.
A settlement is a place where people have come to live and have built homes.
The settlement of a group of people is the process in which they settle in a place where people from their country have never lived before.
Settlers are people who go to live in a new country.
A particular set-up is a particular system or way of organizing something.
If you describe a situation as a set-up, you mean that people have planned it in order to deceive you or to make it look as if you have done something wrong.
The set-up of computer hardware or software is the process of installing it and making it ready to use.
Seven is the number 7.
Seventeen is the number 17.
The seventh item in a series is the one that you count as number seven.
A seventh is one of seven equal parts of something.

Chinesesense: 七十几(指 70 至 79 之间的数字)；
七十年代(指 1970 年至 1979 年)；
Englishsense: Seventy is the number 70.

When you talk about the seventies, you are referring to numbers between 70 and 79. For example, if you are in your seventies, you are aged between 70 and 79. If the temperature is in the seventies, it is between 70 and 79.
The seventies is the decade between 1970 and 1979.
To sever something means to cut completely through it or to cut it completely off.
If you sever a relationship or connection that you have with someone, you end it suddenly and completely.
Several is used to refer to an imprecise number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two.

When you sew something such as clothes, you make them or repair them by joining pieces of cloth together by passing thread through them with a needle.
When something such as a hand or finger is sewn back by a doctor, it is joined with the patient’s body using a needle and thread.
Sewage is waste matter such as faeces or dirty water from homes and factories, which flows away through sewers.

You can refer to a person’s sexuality when you are talking about whether they are sexually attracted to people of the same sex or a different sex.

Englishsense: A shade of a particular colour is one of its different forms. For example, emerald green and olive green are shades of green.

If you say that a place or person is shaded by objects such as trees, you mean that the place or person cannot be reached, harmed, or bothered by strong sunlight because those objects are in the way.
If you shade your eyes, you put your hand or an object partly in front of your face in order to prevent a bright light from shining into your eyes.
Shade is darkness or shadows as they are shown in a picture.
The shades of something abstract are its many, slightly different forms.
If something shades into something else, there is no clear division between the two things, so that you cannot tell where or when the first thing ends and the second thing begins.

A shade is the same as a lampshade.

If someone shadows you, they follow you very closely wherever you go.

If you say that something is true without a shadow of a doubt or without a shadow of doubt, you are emphasizing that there is no doubt at all that it is true.
If you live in the shadow of someone or in their shadow, their achievements and abilities are so great that you are not noticed or valued.
If you say that someone is a shadow of their former self, you mean that they are much less strong or capable than they used to be.

If you shake yourself or your body, you make a lot of quick, small, repeated movements without moving from the place where you are.
If you shake your head, you turn it from side to side in order to say ’no’ or to show disbelief or sadness.
If you are shaking, or a part of your body is shaking, you are making quick, small movements that you cannot control, for example because you are cold or afraid.
If you have the shakes, your body is shaking a lot because you are afraid or ill, or because you have drunk too much alcohol.
If you shake your fist or an object such as a stick at someone, you wave it in the air in front of them because you are angry with them.
If a force shakes something, or if something shakes, it moves from side to side or up and down with quick, small, but sometimes violent movements.
To shake something into a certain place or state means to bring it into that place or state by moving it quickly up and down or from side to side.
If your voice is shaking, you cannot control it properly and it sounds very unsteady, for example because you are nervous or angry.
If an event or a piece of news shakes you, or shakes your confidence, it makes you feel upset and unable to think calmly.
If an event shakes a group of people or their beliefs, it causes great uncertainty and makes them question their beliefs.
If you shake someone out of an attitude or belief that you disapprove of, you cause them to change their attitude or belief to one that is more responsible or sensible.
A shake is the same as a milkshake.

If you say that someone or something is no great shakes, you mean that they are not very skilful or effective.
If you shake someone’s hand or shake someone by the hand, you shake hands with them.

If you shake hands with someone, you take their right hand in your own for a few moments, often moving it up and down slightly, when you are saying hello or goodbye to them, congratulating them, or agreeing on something. You can also say that two people shake hands.

If you shame someone close to you, you make people lose their respect for that person, by behaving in an unacceptable way.
If you shame someone into doing something, you force them to do it by making them feel ashamed not to.
If you say that something is a shame, you are expressing your regret about it and indicating that you wish it had happened differently.

If someone puts you to shame, they make you feel ashamed because they do something much better than you do.

Englishsense: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example whether they are round, square, curved, or fat.

The shape of something that is planned or organized is its structure and character.
Someone or something that shapes a situation or an activity has a very great influence on the way it develops.
If you shape an object, you give it a particular shape, using your hands or a tool.
If you say that something is the shape of things to come, you mean that it is the start of a new trend or development, and in future things will be like this.
If you say, for example, that you will not accept something in any shape or form, or in any way, shape or form, you are emphasizing that you will not accept it in any circumstances.
If someone or something is in shape, or in good shape, they are in a good state of health or in a good condition. If they are in bad shape, they are in a bad state of health or in a bad condition.
You can use in the shape of to state exactly who or what you are referring to, immediately after referring to them in a general way.
If you lick, knock, or whip someone or something into shape, you use whatever methods are necessary to change or improve them so that they are in the condition that you want them to be in.
If something is out of shape, it is no longer in its proper or original shape, for example because it has been damaged or wrongly handled.
If you are out of shape, you are unhealthy and unable to do a lot of physical activity without getting tired.
If you say that things or people of a certain type come in all shapes and sizes, you mean that there are a large number of them, and that they are often very different from each other.
When something takes shape, it develops or starts to appear in such a way that it becomes fairly clear what its final form will be.

If you share a task, duty, or responsibility with someone, you each carry out or accept part of it. You can also say that two people share something.

If one person or thing shares a quality or characteristic with another, they have the same quality or characteristic. You can also say that two people or things share something.
If you share something that you have with someone, you give some of it to them or let them use it.
If you share something personal such as a thought or a piece of news with someone, you tell them about it.
If something is divided or distributed among a number of different people or things, each of them has, or is responsible for, a share of it.
If you have or do your share of something, you have or do an amount that seems reasonable to you, or to other people.
A shareholder is a person who owns shares in a company.
A shark is a very large fish. Some sharks have very sharp teeth and may attack people.
If you refer to a person as a shark, you disapprove of them because they trick people out of their money by giving bad advice about buying, selling, or investments.

Chinesesense: 人敏锐的，灵敏的，敏捷的，机灵的；
(言辞)激烈的，尖锐的，尖刻的，严厉的；
(变化、动作、感情等)急剧的，骤然的，大幅度的，强烈的；
(差异)明显的，鲜明的;(图像、声音等)清晰的；
(味道或气味)强烈的，苦的，冲的；
(用于音符后)升半音的(常用＃符号表示)；
(活动或工作中)最困难的部分，最危险的部分；
Englishsense: A sharp point or edge is very thin and can cut through things very easily. A sharp knife, tool, or other object has a point or edge of this kind.
You can describe a shape or an object as sharp if part of it or one end of it comes to a point or forms an angle.
A sharp bend or turn is one that changes direction suddenly.
If you describe someone as sharp, you are praising them because they are quick to notice, hear, understand, or react to things.
If someone says something in a sharp way, they say it suddenly and rather firmly or angrily, for example because they are warning or criticizing you.
A sharp change, movement, or feeling occurs suddenly, and is great in amount, force, or degree.
A sharp difference, image, or sound is very easy to see, hear, or distinguish.
A sharp taste or smell is rather strong or bitter, but is often also clear and fresh.
A sharp wind, or sharp cold, is so strong or intense that it almost hurts you when you are exposed to it.
Sharp clothes are neat, elegant, and fashionable.
Sharp is used after stating a particular time to show that something happens at exactly the time stated.
Sharp is used after a letter representing a musical note to show that the note should be played or sung half a tone higher. Sharp is often represented by the symbol #.
If you say that someone is at the sharp end of a particular activity or type of work, you mean that they are involved in the most difficult or dangerous aspects of it.

Chinesesense: (感觉、理解)加强;使加深;(技巧)提高;使改善；
(分歧、差异等)加剧;使加深;使加重；
Englishsense: If your senses, understanding, or skills sharpen or are sharpened, you become better at noticing things, thinking, or doing something.
If you sharpen an object, you make its edge very thin or you make its end pointed.
If disagreements or differences between people sharpen, or if they are sharpened, they become bigger or more important.

Chinesesense: 使(梦想、希望或信念)粉碎;使破灭；
使非常惊愕;使受到极大打击；
Englishsense: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.
If something shatters your dreams, hopes, or beliefs, it completely destroys them.
If someone is shattered by an event, it shocks and upsets them very much.

Chinesesense: (少量地)削减，缩减;使略有下降；
Englishsense: When a man shaves, he removes the hair from his face using a razor or shaver so that his face is smooth.
If someone shaves a part of their body, they remove the hair from it so that it is smooth.
If you shave someone, you remove the hair from their face or another part of their body so that it is smooth.
If you shave off part of a piece of wood or other material, you cut very thin pieces from it.
If you shave a small amount off something such as a record, cost, or price, you reduce it by that amount.
If you describe a situation as a close shave, you mean that there was nearly an accident or a disaster but it was avoided.
To shear a sheep means to cut its wool off.
A pair of shears is a garden tool like a very large pair of scissors. Shears are used especially for cutting hedges.
A sheep is a farm animal which is covered with thick curly hair called wool. Sheep are kept for their wool or for their meat.
If you say that a group of people are like sheep, you disapprove of them because if one person does something, all the others copy that person.

Chinesesense: (用于强调)纯粹的，完全的，十足的；
Englishsense: You can use sheer to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.
A sheer cliff or drop is extremely steep or completely vertical.
Sheer material is very thin, light, and delicate.

Chinesesense: (玻璃、金属、木头等的)大块薄片，薄板；
(覆盖在其他物体上的)一大片，一层；
一团，一片，一股(迅速移动的火或水)；
Englishsense: A sheet is a large rectangular piece of cotton or other cloth that you sleep on or cover yourself with in a bed.
A sheet of paper is a rectangular piece of paper.
You can use sheet to refer to a piece of paper which gives information about something.
A sheet of glass, metal, or wood is a large, flat, thin piece of it.
A sheet of something is a thin wide layer of it over the surface of something else.
A sheet of fire or water is a fast-moving mass of it that is difficult to see through.
In sailing, a sheet is a line or rope used for controlling the position of a sail on a boat.

Chinesesense: (固定在墙上或橱柜上的)架子，搁板；
搁板状岩石;突出的岩石;(水下的)暗礁，陆架；
搁置的;闲置的;没人要的；
Englishsense: A shelf is a flat piece of wood, metal, or glass which is attached to a wall or to the sides of a cupboard. Shelves are used for keeping things on.
A shelf is a section of rock on a cliff or mountain or underwater that sticks out like a shelf.
If you buy something off the shelf, you buy something that is not specially made for you.
If you say that someone or something is on the shelf, you mean that no one wants them.

Chinesesense: (躲避恶劣天气或危险的)遮蔽物，庇护处，掩体；
(尤指躲避恶劣天气或危险的)遮蔽，庇护，掩蔽；
为(受到警察或其他人追捕的人)提供避难所;窝藏;庇护；
Englishsense: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.
If a place provides shelter, it provides you with a place to stay or live, especially when you need protection from bad weather or danger.
A shelter is a building where homeless people can sleep and get food.
If you shelter in a place, you stay there and are protected from bad weather or danger.
If a place or thing is sheltered by something, it is protected by that thing from wind and rain.
If you shelter someone, usually someone who is being hunted by police or other people, you provide them with a place to stay or live.
A shepherd is a person, especially a man, whose job is to look after sheep.
If you are shepherded somewhere, someone takes you there to make sure that you arrive at the right place safely.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Chinesesense: (美国由选举产生的)县治安官；
(英格兰和威尔士境内挂名的名誉)郡长，郡督；
Englishsense: In the United States, a sheriff is a person who is elected to make sure that the law is obeyed in a particular county.
In Scotland, a sheriff is a legal officer whose chief duty is to act as judge in a Sheriff Court. These courts deal with all but the most serious crimes and with most civil actions.
In England and Wales, the Sheriff of a city or county is a person who is elected or appointed to carry out mainly ceremonial duties.

Chinesesense: (为阻挡阳光直射而)挡住，遮住(眼睛)；
(体育运动的)盾形奖牌，盾形徽章；
Englishsense: Something or someone which is a shield against a particular danger or risk provides protection from it.
If something or someone shields you from a danger or risk, they protect you from it.
If you shield your eyes, you put your hand above your eyes to protect them from direct sunlight.
A shield is a large piece of metal or leather which soldiers used to carry to protect their bodies while they were fighting.
A shield is a sports prize or badge that is shaped like a shield.

Chinesesense: (意见、情况、政策)有所变动，稍作改变;使发生些许变化；
轮班;当班时间;轮班职工；
Englishsense: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.
If someone’s opinion, a situation, or a policy shifts or is shifted, it changes slightly.
If someone shifts the responsibility or blame for something onto you, they unfairly make you responsible or make people blame you for it, instead of them.
If a shop or company shifts goods, they sell goods that are difficult to sell.
If you shift gears in a car, you put the car into a different gear.

If a group of factory workers, nurses, or other people work shifts, they work for a set period before being replaced by another group, so that there is always a group working. Each of these set periods is called a shift. You can also use shift to refer to a group of workers who work together on a particular shift.
Shifting is used to describe something which is made up of parts that are continuously moving and changing position in relation to other parts.

Chinesesense: (技巧或活动方面)出色，出类拔萃；
一见倾心;一见钟情;一眼就看上；
Englishsense: When the sun or a light shines, it gives out bright light.
If you shine a torch or other light somewhere, you point it there, so that you can see something when it is dark.
Something that shines is very bright and clear because it is reflecting light.
Something that has a shine is bright and clear because it is reflecting light.
If you shine a wooden, leather, or metal object, you make it bright by rubbing or polishing it.
Someone who shines at a skill or activity does it extremely well.
If you say that someone has taken a shine to another person, you mean that he or she liked them very much at their first meeting.

Chinesesense: (成就)辉煌的，值得钦佩的;(品质)出色的,卓越的；
Englishsense: A shining achievement or quality is a very good one which should be greatly admired.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 闪亮的;反光的;有光泽的；
Englishsense: Shiny things are bright and reflect light.
A ship is a large boat which carries passengers or cargo.
If people or things are shipped somewhere, they are sent there on a ship or by some other means of transport.
A shipment is an amount of a particular kind of cargo that is sent to another country on a ship, train, aeroplane, or other vehicle.
The shipment of a cargo somewhere is the sending of it there by ship, train, aeroplane, or some other vehicle.
Shipping is the transport of cargo as a business, especially on ships.
You can refer to the amount of money that you pay to a company to transport cargo as shipping.
You can refer to ships as shipping when considering them as a group.
A shirt is a piece of clothing that you wear on the upper part of your body. Shirts have a collar, sleeves, and buttons down the front.

Chinesesense: (生病或害怕时的)腹泻,拉肚子；
[表示愤怒、不耐烦或厌恶)该死,妈的；
狠揍;痛扁;把…打得屁滚尿流；
灾难临头;惹麻烦;走霉运；
一点不在乎;毫不关心;根本不放在心上；
遇到大麻烦;陷入困境;倒大霉；
(虽然不喜欢却不得不接受)糟透了，倒霉；
Englishsense: Some people use shit to refer to solid waste matter from the body of a human being or animal.
To shit means to get rid of solid waste matter from the body.
To have a shit means to get rid of solid waste matter from the body.
If someone has the shits, liquid waste matter keeps coming out of their body because they are ill or afraid.
People sometimes refer to things that they do not like as shit.
People sometimes insult someone they do not like by referring to them as a shit.
Shit is used to express anger, impatience, or disgust.
If someone says they are shitting themselves, they mean that they are very frightened.
To beat or kick the shit out of someone means to beat or kick them so violently that they are badly injured.
If someone says that the shit hit the fan, they mean that there was suddenly a lot of trouble or angry arguments.
If someone says that they do not give a shit about something, they mean that they do not care about it at all.
If someone is in the shit or in deep shit, they are in a lot of trouble.
Tough shit can be used as a way of telling someone that they will have to accept a situation they do not like because they have no choice.

Chinesesense: (因寒冷或惧怕而)哆嗦，颤抖，发抖；
Englishsense: When you shiver, your body shakes slightly because you are cold or frightened.

Chinesesense: 震惊;惊愕;令人震惊的事；
(因行为粗鲁或不道德而)使不快，使气愤，使厌恶，使反感；
(通告、事件等)令人惊愕的，令人震惊的；
(对经济、传统、生活方式的)冲击，撞击；
Englishsense: If you have a shock, something suddenly happens which is unpleasant, upsetting, or very surprising.
Shock is a person’s emotional and physical condition when something very frightening or upsetting has happened to them.
If someone is in shock, they are suffering from a serious physical condition in which their blood is not flowing round their body properly, for example because they have had a bad injury.
If something shocks you, it makes you feel very upset, because it involves death or suffering and because you had not expected it.
If someone or something shocks you, it upsets or offends you because you think it is rude or morally wrong.
A shock announcement or event is one which shocks people because it is unexpected.
A shock is something sudden and unexpected that threatens the economy, traditions, or way of life of a group of people.
A shock is the force of something suddenly hitting or pulling something else.
A shock is the same as an electric shock.
A shock is a shock absorber.
A shock of hair is a very thick mass of hair on a person’s head.
A short, sharp shock is a punishment that is fairly harsh and severe but only lasts for a short time.

Chinesesense: 令人震惊的;令人愤慨的;不道德的；
Englishsense: You can say that something is shocking if you think that it is very bad.
You can say that something is shocking if you think that it is morally wrong.
Shoes are objects which you wear on your feet. They cover most of your foot and you wear them over socks or stockings.
A shoe is the same as a horseshoe.
When a blacksmith shoes a horse, they fix horseshoes onto its feet.
If you fill someone’s shoes or step into their shoes, you take their place by doing the job they were doing.
If you talk about being in someone’s shoes, you talk about what you would do or how you would feel if you were in their situation.

Chinesesense: (突然并迅速地)伸出，扔出，抛出；
搬起石头砸自己的脚;自作自受；
Englishsense: If someone shoots a person or an animal, they kill them or injure them by firing a bullet or arrow at them.
To shoot means to fire a bullet from a weapon such as a gun.
If someone or something shoots in a particular direction, they move in that direction quickly and suddenly.
If you shoot something somewhere or if it shoots somewhere, it moves there quickly and suddenly.
If you shoot a look at someone, you look at them quickly and briefly, often in a way that expresses your feelings.
If someone shoots to fame, they become famous or successful very quickly.
When people shoot a film or shoot photographs, they make a film or take photographs using a camera.
Shoots are plants that are beginning to grow, or new parts growing from a plant or tree.
In sports such as football or basketball, when someone shoots, they try to score by kicking, throwing, or hitting the ball towards the goal.
When someone shoots pool or shoots craps, they play a game of pool or the dice game called craps.
If you shoot the breeze or shoot the bull with someone, you talk to them about things which are not very serious or important.
If you shoot yourself in the foot, something you say or do causes you harm.
A shooter is a person who shoots a gun.
A shooter is a gun.
A shooting is an occasion when someone is killed or injured by being shot with a gun.
Shooting is hunting animals with a gun as a leisure activity.
The shooting of a film is the act of filming it.

Chinesesense: (商店、办事处、公司)休息，下班，打烊，停业，歇业；
谈论本行工作;三句话不离本行；
Englishsense: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.
When you shop, you go to shops and buy things.
You can refer to a place where a particular service is offered as a particular type of shop.
You can refer to a place where things are made or done as a particular kind of shop.
If you shop someone, you report them to the police for doing something illegal.
If something is happening all over the shop, it is happening in many different places or throughout a wide area.
If you set up shop, you start a business.
When a shop, office, or firm shuts up shop, it stops doing business and closes, either at the end of the day or permanently. [V inflects] [【语域标签】：BRIT 英]
If you say that people are talking shop, you mean that they are talking about their work, and this is boring for other people who do not do the same work.

Chinesesense: 从商店购买来的东西(尤指食品)；
Englishsense: When you do the shopping, you go to shops and buy things.
Your shopping is the things that you have bought from shops, especially food.
The shores or the shore of a sea, lake, or wide river is the land along the edge of it. Someone who is on shore is on the land rather than on a ship.
When someone or something reaches the shores of a country or continent, they arrive in that country or continent.
A shoreline is the edge of a sea, lake, or wide river.

Chinesesense: 似乎过得很快的;短暂的；
(距离、长度等)短的，不长的，不远的；
说话简短粗暴的;简慢无礼的；
(尤指在一时找不到厕所的情况下)内急，突然感觉要上厕所；
冒傻气的;不聪明的;愚蠢的;不理智的；
缺乏，缺少(某种优良品质)；
(因雇主付不起全工时工钱而出现的)短工时，开工不足；
使突然终止;使突然中断；
干净利落地处理(或打败);迅速解决；
少量烈酒(如威士忌、杜松子酒、伏特加等)；
(尤指正片放映前的)电影短片；
Englishsense: If something is short or lasts for a short time, it does not last very long.
If you talk about a short hour, day, or year, you mean that it seems to have passed very quickly or will seem to pass very quickly.
A short speech, letter, or book does not have many words or pages in it.
Someone who is short is not as tall as most people are.
Something that is short measures only a small amount from one end to the other.
If you are short of something or if it is short, you do not have enough of it. If you are running short of something or if it is running short, you do not have much of it left.
If someone or something is or stops short of a place, they have not quite reached it. If they are or fall short of an amount, they have not quite achieved it.
Short of a particular thing means except for that thing or without actually doing that thing.
If something is cut short or stops short, it is stopped before people expect it to or before it has finished.
If a name or abbreviation is short for another name, it is the short version of that name.
If you have a short temper, you get angry very easily.
If you are short with someone, you speak briefly and rather rudely to them, because you are impatient or angry.
If you are caught short or are taken short, you feel a sudden strong need to urinate, especially when you cannot easily find a toilet.
If a person or thing is called something for short, that is the short version of their name.
If you go short of something, especially food, you do not have as much of it as you want or need.
You use in short when you have been giving a lot of details and you want to give a conclusion or summary.

You use nothing short of or little short of to emphasize how great or extreme something is. For example, if you say that something is nothing short of a miracle or nothing short of disastrous, you are emphasizing that it is a miracle or it is disastrous.
If you say that someone is, for example, several cards short of a full deck or one sandwich short of a picnic, you think they are stupid, foolish, or crazy.
If someone or something is short on a particular good quality, they do not have as much of it as you think they should have.
If someone stops short of doing something, they come close to doing it but do not actually do it.
If workers are put on short time, they are asked to work fewer hours than the normal working week, because their employer can not afford to pay them a full time wage.
If something pulls you up short or brings you up short, it makes you suddenly stop what you are doing.
If you make short work of someone or something, you deal with them or defeat them very quickly.
Shorts are trousers with very short legs, that people wear in hot weather or for taking part in sports.
Shorts are men’s underpants with short legs.
A short is a small amount of a strong alcoholic drink such as whisky, gin, or vodka, rather than a weaker alcoholic drink that you can drink in larger quantities.
A short is a short film, especially one that is shown before the main film at the cinema.
If there is a shortage of something, there is not enough of it.
Someone’s or something’s shortcomings are the faults or weaknesses which they have.

Chinesesense: 使时间变短;缩短(…的时间)；
Englishsense: If you shorten an event or the length of time that something lasts, or if it shortens, it does not last as long as it would otherwise do or as it used to do.
If you shorten an object or if it shortens, it becomes smaller in length.
If you shorten a name or other word, you change it by removing some of the letters.

Chinesesense: 没好气地;不耐烦地;粗鲁地;气冲冲地；
Englishsense: If something happens shortly after or before something else, it happens not long after or before it. If something is going to happen shortly, it is going to happen soon.
If you speak to someone shortly, you speak to them in a cross or impatient way.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Short-term is used to describe things that will last for a short time, or things that will have an effect soon rather than in the distant future.

Chinesesense: 一张照片;(电影的)一组镜头；
立刻;飞快地;毫不迟疑地；
没把握的尝试;不大可能成功的尝试；
布满，充满，富有(某种因素或特征)；
Englishsense: A shot is an act of firing a gun.
Someone who is a good shot can shoot well. Someone who is a bad shot cannot shoot well.
In sports such as football, golf, or tennis, a shot is an act of kicking, hitting, or throwing the ball, especially in an attempt to score a point.
A shot is a photograph or a particular sequence of pictures in a film.
If you have a shot at something, you attempt to do it.
A shot of a drug is an injection of it.
A shot of a strong alcoholic drink is a small glass of it.
If you give something your best shot, you do it as well as you possibly can.
If you describe someone’s actions as a shot across the bows of another person, you mean that it is a warning to that person to stop or change what they are doing.
The person who calls the shots is in a position to tell others what to do.
If you do something like a shot, you do it without any delay or hesitation.
If you describe something as a long shot, you mean that it is unlikely to succeed, but is worth trying.
People sometimes use the expression by a long shot to emphasize the opinion they are giving.
If something is shot through with an element or feature, it contains a lot of that element or feature.
A shotgun is a gun used for shooting birds and animals which fires a lot of small metal balls at one time.

Chinesesense: (表示给出指示或公布官方命令)应该，必须；
(表示与说话者的意愿相反)本应；
(表示预期或可能性)应该会，可能；
(用于疑问句中表示征求意见、同意或咨询情况)可以，应该；
(通过假设自己处于对方立场会怎么做来提出建议)应该，可以，会；
(用在条件从句中表示事件发生的可能性)将要，假定要；
(用在由 that引导的从句中，放在某些动词、名词和形容词之后，表示将来的事件或情况)应该，能够，竟然会；
(与第一人称连用，表示没有把握)会，可能；
(与第一人称连用表示客气的请求等)想要，将会；
(强调所经历的事有趣、令人震惊等)实在该，真该，真应当；
(用在由who，what等引导的疑问结构中，后接but，强调某件事令人惊讶或震惊)居然；
Englishsense: You use should when you are saying what would be the right thing to do or the right state for something to be in.
You use should to give someone an order to do something, or to report an official order.

If you say that something should have happened, you mean that it did not happen, but that you wish it had. If you say that something should not have happened, you mean that it did happen, but that you wish it had not.

You use should when you are saying that something is probably the case or will probably happen in the way you are describing. If you say that something should have happened by a particular time, you mean that it will probably have happened by that time.
You use should in questions when you are asking someone for advice, permission, or information.
You say ’ I should ’, usually with the expression ’if I were you’, when you are giving someone advice by telling them what you would do if you were in their position.
You use should in conditional clauses when you are talking about things that might happen.
You use should in ’that’ clauses after certain verbs, nouns, and adjectives when you are talking about a future event or situation.
You use should in expressions such as I should think and I should imagine to indicate that you think something is true but you are not sure.
You use should in expressions such as I should like and I should be happy to show politeness when you are saying what you want to do, or when you are requesting, offering, or accepting something.
You use should in expressions such as You should have seen us and You should have heard him to emphasize how funny, shocking, or impressive something that you experienced was.
You use should in question structures which begin with words like ’who’ and ’what’ and are followed by ’but’ to emphasize how surprising or shocking a particular event was.

Chinesesense: (问题、责任等)由…承担，落在…肩上；
惴惴不安;小心翼翼;小心提防；
Englishsense: Your shoulders are between your neck and the tops of your arms.
The shoulders of a piece of clothing are the parts that cover your shoulders.
When you talk about someone’s problems or responsibilities, you can say that they carry them on their shoulders.
If you shoulder the responsibility or the blame for something, you accept it.
If you shoulder something heavy, you put it across one of your shoulders so that you can carry it more easily.
If you shoulder someone aside or if you shoulder your way somewhere, you push past people roughly using your shoulder.
A shoulder is a joint of meat from the upper part of the front leg of an animal.
If someone offers you a shoulder to cry on or is a shoulder to cry on, they listen sympathetically as you talk about your troubles.
If you say that someone or something stands head and shoulders above other people or things, you mean that they are a lot better than them.
If you say that someone is looking over their shoulder, you mean that they feel anxious all the time about what someone may do to them.
If two or more people stand shoulder to shoulder, they are standing next to each other, with their shoulders touching. [PHR after v]
If people work or stand shoulder to shoulder, they work together in order to achieve something, or support each other.

Chinesesense: (通常指生气时或希望远方的人能听见时而)大叫，嚷，高呼；
成功在望;有成功的机会；
Englishsense: If you shout, you say something very loudly, usually because you want people a long distance away to hear you or because you are angry.
If you say that someone is in with a shout of achieving or winning something, you mean that they have a chance of achieving or winning it.
If you are in a pub and someone you are with says ’ It’s your shout ’ or ’ It’s my shout ’, they mean that it is your turn or their turn to buy a round of drinks.

Chinesesense: 乱放;乱塞;随便放;胡乱丢；
情况不妙时;别无选择时;形势十分糟糕时；
Englishsense: If you shove someone or something, you push them with a quick, violent movement.
If you shove something somewhere, you push it there quickly and carelessly.
If you talk about what you think will happen if push comes to shove, you are talking about what you think will happen if a situation becomes very bad or difficult.
A shovel is a tool with a long handle that is used for lifting and moving earth, coal, or snow.
If you shovel earth, coal, or snow, you lift and move it with a shovel.
If you shovel something somewhere, you push a lot of it quickly into that place.

Chinesesense: (图画、图表、影像或文章)描绘，描述，展示，说明；
给…看;向…出示(或展示);指给…看；
使露出;使显现;使变得显著；
表现，体现，流露出(态度、品质或情感);(态度等)体现，流露；
显示出，表露出，流露出(某种品质或特征);(品质或特征)表露，显示；
(情感、品质等的)流露，表露，体现；
(尤指包括音乐、舞蹈、滑稽剧等不同内容的)演出，表演；
(赛马比赛中赛马)名列前三甲；
在…方面做出了成绩;在…方面有结果；
(用来威胁或警告别人)我要让你看看，你就等着瞧吧；
这恰恰证明;这正好表明；
Englishsense: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.
If a picture, chart, film, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it.
If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to.
If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.
If you show someone how to do something, you do it yourself so that they can watch you and learn how to do it.
If something shows or if you show it, it is visible or noticeable.
If you show a particular attitude, quality, or feeling, or if it shows, you behave in a way that makes this attitude, quality, or feeling clear to other people.
If something shows a quality or characteristic or if that quality or characteristic shows itself, it can be noticed or observed.
A show of a feeling or quality is an attempt by someone to make it clear that they have that feeling or quality.
If you say that something is for show, you mean that it has no real purpose and is done just to give a good impression.
If a company shows a profit or a loss, its accounts indicate that it has made a profit or a loss.
If a person you are expecting to meet does not show, they do not arrive at the place where you expect to meet them.
A television or radio show is a programme on television or radio.
A show in a theatre is an entertainment or concert, especially one that includes different items such as music, dancing, and comedy.
If someone shows a film or television programme, it is broadcast or appears on television or in the cinema.
A show is a public exhibition of things, such as works of art, fashionable clothes, or things that have been entered in a competition.
To show things such as works of art means to put them in an exhibition where they can be seen by the public.
In a horse race, if a horse shows, it finishes first, second, or third.
A show home, house, or flat is one of a group of new homes. The building company decorates it and puts furniture in it, and people who want to buy one of the homes come and look round it.
If a question is decided by a show of hands, people vote on it by raising their hands to indicate whether they vote yes or no.
If you have something to show for your efforts, you have achieved something as a result of what you have done.
You can say ’ I’ll show you ’ to threaten or warn someone that you are going to make them admit that they are wrong.
If you say it just goes to show or it just shows that something is the case, you mean that what you have just said or experienced demonstrates that it is the case.
If you say that someone is running the show, you mean that they are in control or in charge of a situation.
If you say that someone steals the show, you mean that they get a lot of attention or praise because they perform better than anyone else in a show or other event.

Chinesesense: (展览会、博物馆等的)玻璃柜，玻璃陈列柜；
Englishsense: A showcase is a glass container with valuable objects inside it, for example at an exhibition or in a museum.
You use showcase to refer to a situation or setting in which something is displayed or presented to its best advantage.
If something is showcased, it is displayed or presented to its best advantage.

Chinesesense: (落下的东西)一大批，一阵，一连串；
Englishsense: A shower is a device for washing yourself. It consists of a pipe which ends in a flat cover with a lot of holes in it so that water comes out in a spray.
A shower is a small enclosed area containing a shower.
The showers or the shower in a place such as a sports centre is the area containing showers.
If you have a shower, you wash yourself by standing under a spray of water from a shower.
If you shower, you wash yourself by standing under a spray of water from a shower.
A shower is a short period of rain, especially light rain.
You can refer to a lot of things that are falling as a shower of them.
If you are showered with a lot of small objects or pieces, they are scattered over you.
If you shower a person with presents or kisses, you give them a lot of presents or kisses in a very generous and extravagant way.
A shower is a party or celebration at which the guests bring gifts.
If you refer to a group of people as a particular kind of shower, you disapprove of them.
If you shred something such as food or paper, you cut it or tear it into very small, narrow pieces.
If you cut or tear food or paper into shreds, you cut or tear it into small, narrow pieces.
If there is not a shred of something, there is not even a small amount of it.
If you tear someone to shreds or rip them to shreds, you criticize them very thoroughly and severely.

Chinesesense: (因惊讶或疼痛等)尖叫;尖声笑；
Englishsense: When someone shrieks, they make a short, very loud cry, for example because they are suddenly surprised, are in pain, or are laughing.
If you shriek something, you shout it in a loud, high-pitched voice.
Shrimps are small shellfish with long tails and many legs.
A shrine is a place of worship which is associated with a particular holy person or object.
A shrine is a place that people visit and treat with respect because it is connected with a dead person or with dead people that they want to remember.

Chinesesense: (通常指布料、衣服等洗后)缩水，收缩，缩小，皱缩；
(因害怕、震惊或厌恶)退缩，畏缩，避开；
Englishsense: If cloth or clothing shrinks, it becomes smaller in size, usually as a result of being washed.
If something shrinks or something else shrinks it, it becomes smaller.
If you shrink away from someone or something, you move away from them because you are frightened, shocked, or disgusted by them.
If you do not shrink from a task or duty, you do it even though it is unpleasant or dangerous.
A shrink is a psychiatrist.
Shrubs are plants that have several woody stems.

Chinesesense: 耸肩(表示不感兴趣、不知道或不在乎)；
Englishsense: If you shrug, you raise your shoulders to show that you are not interested in something or that you do not know or care about something.

Chinesesense: (因担忧、恐惧、厌恶或寒冷)发抖，打颤，战栗；
(机器、交通工具等)强烈震动，剧烈抖动；
不敢设想;想到…不寒而栗；
Englishsense: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.
If something such as a machine or vehicle shudders, it shakes suddenly and violently.
If something sends a shudder or shudders through a group of people, it makes them worried or afraid.
If you say that you shudder to think what would happen in a particular situation, you mean that you expect it to be so bad that you do not really want to think about it.

Chinesesense: (通常因不舒服或难为情)挪动双脚，坐立不安；
将(纸张等)变换位置;打乱…的次序；
Englishsense: If you shuffle somewhere, you walk there without lifting your feet properly off the ground.
If you shuffle around, you move your feet about while standing or you move your bottom about while sitting, often because you feel uncomfortable or embarrassed.
If you shuffle playing cards, you mix them up before you begin a game.
If you shuffle things such as pieces of paper, you move them around so that they are in a different order.
If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

Chinesesense: 使(商店、酒吧等公共场所)关门，停止营业，休息；
故意忽视;故意不予理会;对…视若罔闻；
Englishsense: If you shut something such as a door or if it shuts, it moves so that it fills a hole or a space.
If you shut your eyes, you lower your eyelids so that you cannot see anything.
If your mouth shuts or if you shut your mouth, you place your lips firmly together.
When a store, bar, or other public building shuts or when someone shuts it, it is closed and you cannot use it until it is open again.
If you say that someone shuts their eyes to something, you mean that they deliberately ignore something which they should deal with.
If someone tells you to keep your mouth shut about something, they are telling you not to let anyone else know about it.
If you keep your mouth shut, you do not express your opinions about something, even though you would like to.
If someone tells you to shut your mouth or shut your face, they are telling you very rudely to stop talking.
The shutter in a camera is the part which opens to allow light through the lens when a photograph is taken.
Shutters are wooden or metal covers fitted on the outside of a window. They can be opened to let in the light, or closed to keep out the sun or the cold.

Chinesesense: 往来于两地之间的航班(或班车、火车)；
使频繁往来于(两地之间)；
Englishsense: A shuttle is the same as a space shuttle.
A shuttle is a plane, bus, or train which makes frequent journeys between two places.
If someone or something shuttles or is shuttled from one place to another place, they frequently go from one place to the other.
A shuttle is a piece of equipment used in weaving. It takes a thread backwards and forwards over the other threads in order to make a piece of cloth.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 犹豫的;不情愿的;害怕的;有所顾忌的；
一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳;一回吃亏两回学乖；
Englishsense: A shy person is nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.
If you are shy of doing something, you are unwilling to do it because you are afraid of what might happen.
When a horse shies, it moves away suddenly, because something has frightened it.
You say ’ once bitten, twice shy ’ when you want to indicate that someone will not do something a second time because they had a bad experience the first time they did it.
If you fight shy of something, you try very hard to avoid it.
A number or amount that is just shy of another number or amount is just under it.
Your siblings are your brothers and sisters.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
