ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (常指在生理上，有时也指在精神上)生病的，有病的；
(笑话、故事等)令人毛骨悚然的，病态的，不健康的；
Englishsense: If you are sick, you are ill. Sick usually means physically ill, but it can sometimes be used to mean mentally ill.
If you are sick, the food that you have eaten comes up from your stomach and out of your mouth. If you feel sick, you feel as if you are going to be sick.
Sick is vomit.
If you say that you are sick of something or sick and tired of it, you are emphasizing that you are very annoyed by it and want it to stop.
If you describe something such as a joke or story as sick, you mean that it deals with death or suffering in an unpleasantly humorous way.
If you say that something or someone makes you sick, you mean that they make you feel angry or disgusted.
If you are off sick, you are not at work because you are ill.
If you say that you are worried sick, you are emphasizing that you are extremely worried.
Sickness is the state of being ill or unhealthy.
Sickness is the uncomfortable feeling that you are going to vomit.
A sickness is a particular illness.

Chinesesense: (洞或容器垂直的)内侧面，内壁；
(某地区、表面或物体一分为二的)一边，一侧；
(有车流来往的道路的)方向，侧；
(城镇或世界的)另一端，遥远的地方；
(人体自腋下至臀部的)体侧,肋部；
(在…)身边，(在…)旁边(给予支持或安慰)；
(牛肉、猪肉等沿脊骨劈开的)一边，半只，一扇；
(争论或交易中)一方的观点(或立场)；
令(家人或朋友)失望(或难堪)；
兼职;在正事之外;作为副业；
暂且不管;把…暂搁置一边；
把…拉到一边去(私下交谈)；
(在争论或战争中)支持一方，站在…一边；
在某一日期或事件之前；
Englishsense: The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.
The side of an object, building, or vehicle is any of its flat surfaces which is not considered to be its front, its back, its top, or its bottom.
The sides of a hollow or a container are its inside vertical surfaces.
The sides of an area or surface are its edges.
The two sides of an area, surface, or object are its two halves.
The two sides of a road are its two halves on which traffic travels in opposite directions.
If you talk about the other side of a town or of the world, you mean a part of the town or of the world that is very far from where you are.
Your sides are the parts of your body between your front and your back, from under your arms to your hips.
If someone is by your side or at your side, they stay near you and give you comfort or support.
The two sides of something flat, for example a piece of paper, are its two flat surfaces. You can also refer to one side of a piece of paper filled with writing as one side of writing.
One side of a tape or record is what you can hear or record if you play the tape or record from beginning to end without turning it over.
A side of beef, bacon, or other meat consists of the meat from half the animal cut along its backbone.
Side is used to describe things that are not the main or most important ones of their kind.
The different sides in a war, argument, or negotiation are the groups of people who are opposing each other.
The different sides of an argument or deal are the different points of view or positions involved in it.
If one person or country sides with another, they support them in an argument or a war. If people or countries side against another person or country, they support each other against them.
In sport, a side is a team.
A particular side of something such as a situation or someone’s character is one aspect of it.
The mother’s side and the father’s side of your family are your mother’s relatives and your father’s relatives.
If two people or things are side by side, they are next to each other.
If people work or live side by side, they work or live closely together in a friendly way.
If you say that someone has let the side down, you mean that they have embarrassed their family or friends by behaving badly or not doing well at something.
If something moves from side to side, it moves repeatedly to the left and to the right.
If you are on someone’s side, you are supporting them in an argument or a war.
If something is on your side or if you have it on your side, it helps you when you are trying to achieve something.
If you get on the wrong side of someone, you do something to annoy them and make them dislike you. If you stay on the right side of someone, you try to please them and avoid annoying them.

If you say that something is on the small side, you are saying politely that you think it is slightly too small. If you say that someone is on the young side, you are saying politely that you think they are slightly too young.
If someone does something on the side, they do it in addition to their main work.
If you have one type of food with another food on the side, you have an amount of the second food served with the first.
If you put something to one side or put it on one side, you temporarily ignore it in order to concentrate on something else.
If you take someone to one side or draw them to one side, you speak to them privately, usually in order to give them advice or a warning.
If you take sides or take someone’s side in an argument or war, you support one of the sides against the other.
If you say that something will not happen this side of a date or event, you mean that it will not happen before that date or event.

Chinesesense: 把…排除在外;使靠边;不重视；
使(运动员)下场;使退出比赛；
Englishsense: A sideline is something that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.
The sidelines are the lines marking the long sides of the playing area, for example on a football field or tennis court.
If you are on the sidelines in a situation, you do not influence events at all, either because you have chosen not to be involved, or because other people have not involved you.
If someone or something is sidelined, they are made to seem unimportant and not included in what people are doing.
In sports, if a player is sidelined, he or she is prevented from playing for a period of time, for example because of an injury.
A sidewalk is a path with a hard surface by the side of a road.

Chinesesense: 使大为吃惊;使极为困惑;使大为不快；
Englishsense: Sideways means from or towards the side of something or someone.
If you are moved sideways at work, you move to another job at the same level as your old job.
If you are knocked sideways by something, it makes you feel very surprised, confused, or upset.

Chinesesense: (军队或警察对某地的)围困，包围，围攻；
(警察、士兵、新闻记者等)包围，围住；
遭受严厉批评;承受巨大压力；
Englishsense: A siege is a military or police operation in which soldiers or police surround a place in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.
If police, soldiers, or journalists lay siege to a place, they surround it in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.
If someone or something is under siege, they are being severely criticized or put under a great deal of pressure.
If you sift a powder such as flour or sand, you put it through a sieve in order to remove large pieces or lumps.
If you sift through something such as evidence, you examine it thoroughly.

Chinesesense: 风发出叹息般的声音，悲鸣；
Englishsense: When you sigh, you let out a deep breath, as a way of expressing feelings such as disappointment, tiredness, or pleasure.
If you sigh something, you say it with a sigh.
If the wind sighs through a place, it moves through the place with a sound like a sigh.
If people breathe or heave a sigh of relief, they feel happy that something unpleasant has not happened or is no longer happening.

Chinesesense: 乍一看;一见之下;初看时；
在望;在即;临近;即将产生；
不好看;不雅观;有碍观瞻；
以…为奋斗目标;志在必得;决心做到；
在未见实物的情况下;事先未经检查；
Englishsense: Someone’s sight is their ability to see.
The sight of something is the act of seeing it or an occasion on which you see it.
A sight is something that you see.
If you sight someone or something, you suddenly see them, often briefly.
The sights of a weapon such as a rifle are the part which helps you aim it more accurately.
The sights are the places that are interesting to see and that are often visited by tourists.
You can use a sight to mean a lot. For example, if you say that something is a sight worse than it was before, you are emphasizing that it is much worse than it was.
If you catch sight of someone, you suddenly see them, often briefly.
If you say that something seems to have certain characteristics at first sight, you mean that it appears to have the features you describe when you first see it but later it is found to be different.
If something is in sight or within sight, you can see it. If it is out of sight, you cannot see it.
If a result or a decision is in sight or within sight, it is likely to happen within a short time.
If you lose sight of an important aspect of something, you no longer pay attention to it because you are worrying about less important things.
If you know someone by sight, you can recognize them when you see them, although you have never met them and talked to them.
If someone is ordered to do something on sight, they have to do it without delay, as soon as a person or thing is seen.
If you say that someone or something is not a pretty sight, you mean that it is not pleasant to look at.
If you set your sights on something, you decide that you want it and try hard to get it.
If you agree to buy something sight unseen, you agree to buy it, even though you have not seen it and do not know what condition it is in.

Chinesesense: (尤指对不寻常或意外事物的)所见，目睹；
Englishsense: A sighting of something, especially something unusual or unexpected is an occasion on which it is seen.

Chinesesense: 打手势语;为(节目或表演)配手语；
招牌;标牌;指示牌;告示牌;标志；
在…上签名;在…上签字;签署；
已签字盖章的;已成定局的；
Englishsense: A sign is a mark or shape that always has a particular meaning, for example in mathematics or music.
A sign is a movement of your arms, hands, or head which is intended to have a particular meaning.
If you sign, you communicate with someone using sign language. If a programme or performance is signed, someone uses sign language so that deaf people can understand it.
A sign is a piece of wood, metal, or plastic with words or pictures on it. Signs give you information about something, or give you a warning or an instruction.
If there is a sign of something, there is something which shows that it exists or is happening.

When you sign a document, you write your name on it, usually at the end or in a special space. You do this to indicate that you have written the document, that you agree with what is written, or that you were present as a witness.
If an organization signs someone or if someone signs for an organization, they sign a contract agreeing to work for that organization for a specified period of time.
In astrology, a sign or a sign of the zodiac is one of the twelve areas into which the heavens are divided.
If you say that there is no sign of someone, you mean that they have not yet arrived, although you are expecting them to come.
If you say that an agreement is signed and sealed, or signed, sealed and delivered, you mean that it is absolutely definite because everyone involved has signed all the legal documents.

Chinesesense: (以手势、声音、行动等发出的)信号，暗号；
(用手势、声音等)发信号，发暗号，示意；
(传输信息的无线电、光波或电流)信号；
Englishsense: A signal is a gesture, sound, or action which is intended to give a particular message to the person who sees or hears it.
If you signal to someone, you make a gesture or sound in order to send them a particular message.
If an event or action is a signal of something, it suggests that this thing exists or is going to happen.
If someone or something signals an event, they suggest that the event is happening or likely to happen.
A signal is a piece of equipment beside a railway, which indicates to train drivers whether they should stop the train or not.
A signal is a series of radio waves, light waves, or changes in electrical current which may carry information.
You use signal to describe a success or failure when you are emphasizing the fact that it has occurred and are indicating that the consequences are significant.

Chinesesense: 为(某人)所特有的;体现个体特征的；
Englishsense: Your signature is your name, written in your own characteristic way, often at the end of a document to indicate that you wrote the document or that you agree with what it says.
A signature item is typical of or associated with a particular person.
If you put your signature to a document, you sign it as a way of officially showing that you agree with what is written.
The significance of something is the importance that it has, usually because it will have an effect on a situation or shows something about a situation.

Englishsense: You say ’ Sorry ’ or ’ I’m sorry ’ as a way of apologizing to someone for something that you have done which has upset them or caused them difficulties, or when you bump into them accidentally.
If you are sorry about a situation, you feel regret, sadness, or disappointment about it.

You use I’m sorry or sorry as an introduction when you are telling a person something that you do not think they will want to hear, for example when you are disagreeing with them or giving them bad news.
If someone says ’ You’ll be sorry ’, they are threatening you or warning you and suggesting that something unpleasant will happen to you because of your actions.
You use the expression I’m sorry to say to express regret together with disappointment or disapproval.
You say ’ I’m sorry ’ to express your regret and sadness when you hear sad or unpleasant news.
If you feel sorry for someone who is unhappy or in an unpleasant situation, you feel sympathy and sadness for them.
You say that someone is feeling sorry for themselves when you disapprove of the fact that they keep thinking unhappily about their problems, rather than trying to be cheerful and positive.
You say ’ Sorry? ’ when you have not heard something that someone has said and you want them to repeat it.
You use sorry when you correct yourself and use different words to say what you have just said, especially when what you say the second time does not use the words you would normally choose to use.
If someone or something is in a sorry state, they are in a bad state, mentally or physically.

Englishsense: If you talk about a particular sort of something, you are talking about a class of things that have particular features in common and that belong to a larger group of related things.
You describe someone as a particular sort when you are describing their character.
If you sort things, you separate them into different classes, groups, or places, for example so that you can do different things with them.
If you get a problem or the details of something sorted, you do what is necessary to solve the problem or organize the details.
All sorts of things or people means a large number of different things or people.
If you describe something as a thing of sorts or as a thing of a sort, you are suggesting that the thing is of a rather poor quality or standard.
You use sort of when you want to say that your description of something is not very accurate.
If you are out of sorts, you feel slightly unwell, upset, or annoyed.

(用于否定句中)一个人(也没有)；
灵乐(一种主要由美国黑人音乐家表演的流行音乐，源出福音唱诗及布鲁斯乐曲)；
出卖灵魂;做违背良心的事；
Englishsense: Your soul is the part of you that consists of your mind, character, thoughts, and feelings. Many people believe that your soul continues existing after your body is dead.
The soul of a nation or a political movement is its basic nature and beliefs.
You can refer to someone as a particular kind of soul when you are describing their character or condition.
You use soul in negative statements like not a soul to mean nobody at all.
Soul or soul music is a type of pop music performed mainly by black American musicians. It developed from gospel and blues music and often expresses deep emotions.
You can refer to the number of people who live in a particular place as souls.
If you say that someone sells their soul, you mean that they do something immoral or bad in order to get something they want such as success or money.

Englishsense: A sound is something that you hear.
Sound is energy that travels in waves through air, water, or other substances, and can be heard.
The sound on a television, radio, or CD player is what you hear coming from the machine. Its loudness can be controlled.
A singer’s or band’s sound is the distinctive quality of their music.
If something such as a horn or a bell sounds or if you sound it, it makes a noise.
If you sound a warning, you publicly give it. If you sound a note of caution or optimism, you say publicly that you are cautious or optimistic.
When you are describing a noise, you can talk about the way it sounds.
When you talk about the way someone sounds, you are describing the impression you have of them when they speak.
When you are describing your impression or opinion of something you have heard about or read about, you can talk about the way it sounds.
You can describe your impression of something you have heard about or read about by talking about the sound of it.
If a structure, part of someone’s body, or someone’s mind is sound, it is in good condition or healthy.
Sound advice, reasoning, or evidence is reliable and sensible.
If you describe someone’s ideas as sound, you mean that you approve of them and think they are correct.
If someone is in a sound sleep, they are sleeping very deeply.
Soup is liquid food made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in water.
If you say that someone is in the soup, you mean they are in trouble.

Englishsense: Something that is sour has a sharp, unpleasant taste like the taste of a lemon.
Sour milk is milk that has an unpleasant taste because it is no longer fresh.
Someone who is sour is bad-tempered and unfriendly.
If a situation or relationship turns sour or goes sour, it stops being enjoyable or satisfactory.
If a friendship, situation, or attitude sours or if something sours it, it becomes less friendly, enjoyable, or hopeful.
If you refer to someone’s attitude as sour grapes, you mean that they say that something is worthless or undesirable because they want it themselves but cannot have it.

In business, if a person or firm sources a product or a raw material, they find someone who will supply it.
A source is a person or book that provides information for a news story or for a piece of research.
The source of a difficulty is its cause.
The source of a river or stream is the place where it begins.

Chinesesense: 南方的;在南部的;来自南部的；
Englishsense: Southern means in or from the south of a region, state, or country.
A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

Englishsense: A sovereign state or country is independent and not under the authority of any other country.
Sovereign is used to describe the person or institution that has the highest power in a country.
A sovereign is a king, queen, or other royal ruler of a country.
Sovereignty is the power that a country has to govern itself or another country or state.

Chinesesense: (苏联的各级)苏维埃，委员会，代表会议；
Englishsense: Soviet is used to describe something that belonged or related to the former Soviet Union.
The Soviets were the people of the former Soviet Union.
A soviet was an elected local, regional, or national council in the former Soviet Union.
Soy flour, butter, or other food is made from soybeans.
Soybeans are the same as soya beans.

Chinesesense: 温泉疗养地;矿泉疗养地；
温泉疗养院;温泉疗养中心；
Englishsense: A spa is a place where water with minerals in it comes out of the ground. People drink the water or go in it in order to improve their health.
A health spa is a kind of hotel where people go to do exercise and have special treatments in order to improve their health.

Chinesesense: (活动或储藏用的)空间，场所，面积；
(思考问题、个人成长所需的)时间，余地，空间；
(文件中用于讨论某个话题的)版面，篇幅；
(新闻记者将进行后续报道时所说的话)请继续关注；
Englishsense: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space.
A particular kind of space is the area that is available for a particular activity or for putting a particular kind of thing in.
If a place gives a feeling of space, it gives an impression of being large and open.
If you give someone space to think about something or to develop as a person, you allow them the time and freedom to do this.
The amount of space for a topic to be discussed in a document is the number of pages available to discuss the topic.
A space of time is a period of time.
Space is the area beyond the Earth’s atmosphere, where the stars and planets are.
Space is the whole area within which everything exists.
If you space a series of things, you arrange them so that they are not all together but have gaps or intervals of time between them.
If you are staring into space, you are looking straight in front of you, without actually looking at anything in particular, for example because you are thinking or because you are feeling shocked.
If you describe someone or something as a waste of space, you are indicating that you have a very low opinion of them.
Journalists write ’ Watch this space ’ in order to indicate in an informal way that they will be giving more information about something in the future.
A spacecraft is a rocket or other vehicle that can travel in space.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A spacious room or other place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.
Spaghetti is a type of pasta. It looks like long pieces of string and is usually served with a sauce.
A span is the period of time between two dates or events during which something exists, functions, or happens.
Your concentration span or your attention span is the length of time you are able to concentrate on something or be interested in it.
If something spans a long period of time, it lasts throughout that period of time or relates to that whole period of time.
If something spans a range of things, all those things are included in it.
The span of something that extends or is spread out sideways is the total width of it from one end to the other.
A bridge or other structure that spans something such as a river or a valley stretches right across it.

Chinesesense: 西班牙的;西班牙人的;西班牙语(或文化)的；
Englishsense: Spanish means belonging or relating to Spain, or to its people, language, or culture.
Spanish is the main language spoken in Spain, and in many countries in South and Central America.
The Spanish are the people who come from Spain.

Englishsense: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.
You use spare to describe something that is not being used by anyone, and is therefore available for someone to use.
If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.
If you spare time or another resource for a particular purpose, you make it available for that purpose.
If a person or a place is spared, they are not harmed, even though other people or places have been.
If you spare someone an unpleasant experience, you prevent them from suffering it.
Someone who is described as spare is tall and not at all fat.
Something such as a room that is spare is very plain with no unnecessary features.

If you spare no effort in doing something, you do it as well as possible, without worrying about the amount of work involved. If you spare no expense in doing it, you do it as well as possible, without trying to save money.
If you spare a thought for an unfortunate person, you make an effort to think sympathetically about them and their bad luck.
A spark is a tiny bright piece of burning material that flies up from something that is burning.
A spark is a flash of light caused by electricity. It often makes a loud sound.
If something sparks, sparks of fire or light come from it.
If a burning object or electricity sparks a fire, it causes a fire.
A spark of a quality or feeling, especially a desirable one, is a small but noticeable amount of it.
If one thing sparks another, the first thing causes the second thing to start happening.
If sparks fly between people, they discuss something in an excited or angry way.
Sparkling drinks are slightly fizzy.
If a company is described as having sparkling figures or sparkling results, it has performed very well and made a lot of money.
Spatial is used to describe things relating to areas.
Your spatial ability is your ability to see and understand the relationships between shapes, spaces, and areas.
Spawn is a soft, jelly-like substance containing the eggs of fish, or of animals such as frogs.
When fish or animals such as frogs spawn, they lay their eggs.
If something spawns something else, it causes it to happen or to be created.

Englishsense: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.
When someone speaks to a group of people, they make a speech.
If you speak for a group of people, you make their views and demands known, or represent them.
If you speak a foreign language, you know the language and are able to have a conversation in it.
People sometimes mention something that has been written by saying what the author speaks of.
If two people are not speaking, they no longer talk to each other because they have quarrelled.
If you say that something speaks to you of a quality, experience, or feeling, you mean that it is evidence of it or expresses it.
If you say that something speaks for itself, you mean that its meaning or quality is so obvious that it does not need explaining or pointing out.
If you say ’ Speak for yourself ’ when someone has said something, you mean that what they have said is only their opinion or applies only to them.
If a person or thing is spoken for or has been spoken for, someone has claimed them or asked for them, so no-one else can have them.

If you say that actions speak louder than words, you mean that people’s actions show their real attitudes, rather than what they say. This expression is sometimes used to advise a person to do something positive.
Nothing to speak of means ’hardly anything’ or ’only unimportant things’.
You can use not to speak of when adding something which your previous statement also applies to, or applies to even more than other things.
If you speak well of someone or speak highly of someone, you say good things about them. If you speak ill of someone, you criticize them.
You use so to speak to draw attention to the fact that you are describing or referring to something in a way that may be amusing or unusual rather than completely accurate.
If you are on speaking terms with someone, you are quite friendly with them and often talk to them.

A speaker of a particular language is a person who speaks it, especially one who speaks it as their first language.

A speaker is a person who is speaking.
A speaker is a piece of electrical equipment, for example part of a radio or set of equipment for playing CDs or tapes, through which sound comes out.
A spear is a weapon consisting of a long pole with a sharp metal point attached to the end.
If you spear something, you push or throw a pointed object into it.
Asparagus or broccoli spears are individual stalks of asparagus or broccoli.

You use special to describe something that relates to one particular person, group, or place.

A specialist is a person who has a particular skill or knows a lot about a particular subject.

Specially is used to mean more than usually or more than other things.
Someone’s specialty is a particular type of work that they do most or do best, or a subject that they know a lot about.
A specialty of a particular place is a special food or product that is always very good there.
A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

You use specifically to emphasize that something is given special attention and considered separately from other things of the same kind.
You use specifically to add something more precise or exact to what you have already said.
You use specifically to indicate that something has a restricted nature, as opposed to being more general in nature.
If you state or describe something specifically, you state or describe it precisely and clearly.
A specification is a requirement which is clearly stated, for example about the necessary features in the design of something.
If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.
If you specify what should happen or be done, you explain it in an exact and detailed way.

You can use specimen to refer to someone who has a quality of a particular kind.

A spectator is someone who watches something, especially a sporting event.

A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing.
A spectrum is a range of light waves or radio waves within particular frequencies.
If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.
If someone speculates financially, they buy property, stocks, or shares, in the hope of being able to sell them again at a higher price and make a profit.

Speculative is used to describe activities which involve buying goods or shares, or buildings and properties, in the hope of being able to sell them again at a higher price and make a profit.

Englishsense: Speech is the ability to speak or the act of speaking.
Your speech is the way in which you speak.
Speech is spoken language.
A speech is a formal talk which someone gives to an audience.
A speech is a group of lines spoken by a character in a play.

Chinesesense: (某事发生或进展的)速度，进度；

Englishsense: The speed of something is the rate at which it moves or travels.
The speed of something is the rate at which it happens or is done.
Speed is very fast movement or travel.
Speed is a very fast rate at which something happens or is done.
If you speed somewhere, you move or travel there quickly, usually in a vehicle.
Someone who is speeding is driving a vehicle faster than the legal speed limit.
Speed is an illegal drug such as amphetamine which some people take to increase their energy and excitement.
If you are up to speed, you have all the most recent information that you need about something.

Englishsense: A speedy process, event, or action happens or is done very quickly.

Englishsense: When you spell a word, you write or speak each letter in the word in the correct order.
Someone who can spell knows the correct order of letters in words.
If something spells a particular result, often an unpleasant one, it suggests that this will be the result.
A spell of a particular type of weather or a particular activity is a short period of time during which this type of weather or activity occurs.
A spell is a situation in which events are controlled by a magical power.
If something or someone casts their spell on you or casts a spell on you, you are fascinated or charmed by them.
If you are under someone ’s spell, you are so fascinated by them that you cannot think about anything else.

Chinesesense: 正确拼写单词的能力;拼写；
Englishsense: A spelling is the correct order of the letters in a word.
Spelling is the ability to spell words in the correct way. It is also an attempt to spell a word in the correct way.
When you spend money, you pay money for things that you want.
If you spend time or energy doing something, you use your time or effort doing it.
If you spend a period of time in a place, you stay there for a period of time.
The spend on a particular thing is the amount of money that is spent on it, or will be spent.
A sperm is a cell which is produced in the sex organs of a male animal and can enter a female animal’s egg and fertilize it.
Sperm is used to refer to the liquid that contains sperm when it is produced.

A sphere of activity or interest is a particular area of activity or interest.
A sphere of people is a group of them who are similar in social status or who have the same interests.
A country’s sphere of influence is an area of the world where it has a lot of influence.

Chinesesense: 香料，佐料，调料，调味品(如肉桂、姜、辣椒粉等)；
使活泼生动;给…增添趣味；

If you spice something that you say or do, you add excitement or interest to it.
Spice is something which makes life more exciting.

Englishsense: Spicy food is strongly flavoured with spices.
A spider is a small creature with eight legs. Most types of spider make structures called webs in which they catch insects for food.

Chinesesense: 偷偷往(饮料中)搀烈性酒(或毒品)；
Englishsense: A spike is a long piece of metal with a sharp point.

If there is a spike in the price, volume, or amount of something, the price, volume, or amount of it suddenly increases.

If your drink is spiked, someone has added alcohol or drugs to it without telling you.

Chinesesense: 使(袋子、盒子等中盛放的东西)洒出，涌出；
Englishsense: If a liquid spills or if you spill it, it accidentally flows over the edge of a container.
A spill is an amount of liquid that has spilled from a container.
If the contents of a bag, box, or other container spill or are spilled, they come out of the container onto a surface.
If people or things spill out of a place, they come out of it in large numbers.
If light spills or is spilled into a place, it shines brightly into it, usually through a gap.
If you spill someone’s blood, you kill them or wound them.

Chinesesense: (用甩干机或洗衣机)甩干衣服，给…脱水；
带倾向性的解释(或说法)；
(飞机的)螺旋式急遽下坠，向下旋冲；
(网球或板球运动中球的) 快速旋转，旋转运动；
Englishsense: If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.
When you spin washing, it is turned round and round quickly in a spin drier or a washing machine to get the water out.
If your head is spinning, you feel unsteady or confused, for example because you are drunk, ill, or excited.
If someone puts a certain spin on an event or situation, they interpret it and try to present it in a particular way.
In politics, spin is the way in which political parties try to present everything they do in a positive way to the public and the media.
If you go for a spin or take a car for a spin, you make a short journey in a car just to enjoy yourself.
If someone spins a story, they give you an account of something that is untrue or only partly true.
When people spin, they make thread by twisting together pieces of a fibre such as wool or cotton using a device or machine.
If a plane goes into a spin, it falls very rapidly towards the ground in a spiral movement.
In a game such as tennis or cricket, if you put spin on a ball, you deliberately make it spin rapidly when you hit it or throw it.
If you say that someone is in a spin or in a flat spin, you mean that they are confused and unable to act sensibly because of something that has happened.
Spinach is a vegetable with large dark green leaves that you chop up and boil in water before eating.
Spinal means relating to your spine.

Chinesesense: (动物身体上的)棘状突起;(植物上的)棘，刺，针；
Englishsense: Your spine is the row of bones down your back.
The spine of a book is the narrow stiff part which the pages and covers are attached to.
Spines are also long, sharp points on an animal’s body or on a plant.
A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.
If something spirals or is spiralled somewhere, it grows or moves in a spiral curve.
If an amount or level spirals, it rises quickly and at an increasing rate.
If an amount or level spirals downwards, it falls quickly and at an increasing rate.

Chinesesense: 精神(指某一群体特有的思想、信念、目标)；
(法律、协议等的)原意,实质，精神；
(用作燃料、清洗等用途的)酒精；
精神上(在某地或和某人在一起，但实际上本人并不在场)；
Englishsense: Your spirit is the part of you that is not physical and that consists of your character and feelings.
A person’s spirit is the non-physical part of them that is believed to remain alive after their death.
A spirit is a ghost or supernatural being.
Spirit is the courage and determination that helps people to survive in difficult times and to keep their way of life and their beliefs.
Spirit is the liveliness and energy that someone shows in what they do.
The spirit in which you do something is the attitude you have when you are doing it.
A particular kind of spirit is the feeling of loyalty to a group that is shared by the people who belong to the group.
A particular kind of spirit is the set of ideas, beliefs, and aims that are held by a group of people.
The spirit of something such as a law or an agreement is the way that it was intended to be interpreted or applied.
You can refer to a person as a particular kind of spirit if they show a certain characteristic or if they show a lot of enthusiasm in what they are doing.
Your spirits are your feelings at a particular time, especially feelings of happiness or unhappiness.
If someone or something is spirited away, or if they are spirited out of somewhere, they are taken from a place quickly and secretly without anyone noticing.
Spirits are strong alcoholic drinks such as whisky and gin.
Spirit or spirits is an alcoholic liquid that is used as a fuel, for cleaning things, or for other purposes. There are many kinds of spirit.
If you enter into the spirit of something, you take part in it in an enthusiastic way.
If you say you are somewhere in spirit or with someone in spirit, you mean that although you are not with them, you feel as though you are with them because you are thinking about them a lot.
You use in spirit when you are talking about someone’s true nature.
The spirit of the age or the spirit of the times is the set of ideas, beliefs, and aims that is typical of people in a particular period in history.

Chinesesense: 宗教上的；宗教信仰上的；
灵歌(原为美国黑奴所唱的一种宗教歌曲)；
Englishsense: Spiritual means relating to people’s thoughts and beliefs, rather than to their bodies and physical surroundings.
Spiritual means relating to people’s religious beliefs.
A spiritual is a religious song of the type originally sung by black slaves in America.
Your spiritual home is the place where you feel that you belong, usually because your ideas or attitudes are the same as those of the people who live there.

Chinesesense: 唾液，唾沫(常指唾沫星子)；
吐唾沫(常表示憎恨或轻蔑)；
(机器) 噼啪作响;(煮着的食物)毕剥作响；
极像…的人;和…一模一样的人；
Englishsense: Spit is the watery liquid produced in your mouth. You usually use spit to refer to an amount of it that has been forced out of someone’s mouth.
If someone spits, they force an amount of liquid out of their mouth, often to show hatred or contempt.
If you spit liquid or food somewhere, you force a small amount of it out of your mouth.
If something such as a machine or food that is cooking spits, it sends out small amounts of something, making a series of short, sharp noises.
If someone spits an insult or comment, they say it in an angry or hostile way.
If it is spitting, it is raining very lightly.
A spit is a long rod which is pushed through a piece of meat and hung over an open fire to cook the meat.
A spit of land is a long, flat, narrow piece of land that sticks out into the sea.
If one place is within spitting distance of another, they are very close to each other.
If you say that one person is the spitting image of another, you mean that they look very similar.
You use in spite of to introduce a fact which makes the rest of the statement you are making seem surprising.
If you do something in spite of yourself, you do it although you did not really intend to or expect to.
If you do something cruel out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.
If you do something cruel to spite someone, you do it in order to hurt or upset them.

Chinesesense: 洒泼上去的一点儿;添加进去的少量；
(与周围颜色形成强烈对照的)一片鲜艳颜色；
Englishsense: If you splash about or splash around in water, you hit or disturb the water in a noisy way, causing some of it to fly up into the air.
If you splash a liquid somewhere or if it splashes, it hits someone or something and scatters in a lot of small drops.
A splash is the sound made when something hits water or falls into it.
A splash of a liquid is a small quantity of it that falls on something or is added to something.
A splash of colour is an area of a bright colour which contrasts strongly with the colours around it.
If a magazine or newspaper splashes a story, it prints it in such a way that it is very noticeable.
If you make a splash, you become noticed or become popular because of something that you have done.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (建筑、艺术作品)壮丽的，华丽的，美妙的；
Englishsense: If you say that something is splendid, you mean that it is very good.
If you describe a building or work of art as splendid, you mean that it is beautiful, impressive, and extremely well made.
You can say ’ splendid ’ in a conversation to indicate that you approve of a particular situation or something that someone has said.

Chinesesense: 使(团体)意见不合；使分裂；
使(木头、衣服)开裂，出现裂缝;撕开；
Englishsense: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.
If an organization splits or is split, one group of members disagrees strongly with the other members, and may form a group of their own.
A split in an organization is a disagreement between its members.
A split between two things is a division or difference between them.
If something such as wood or a piece of clothing splits or is split, a long crack or tear appears in it.
A split is a long crack or tear.
If two or more people split something, they share it between them.

Chinesesense: (因在其上写违法的内容而)使(选票)无效；
战利品;因成功获得的好处；
Englishsense: If you spoil something, you prevent it from being successful or satisfactory.
If you spoil children, you give them everything they want or ask for. This is considered to have a bad effect on a child’s character.
If you spoil yourself or spoil another person, you give yourself or them something nice as a treat or do something special for them.
If food spoils or if it is spoilt, it is no longer fit to be eaten.
If someone spoils their vote, they write something illegal on their voting paper, usually as a protest about the election, and their vote is not accepted.
The spoils of something are things that people get as a result of winning a battle or of doing something successfully.
If you say that someone is spoilt for choice or spoiled for choice, you mean that they have a great many things of the same type to choose from.
A spokesman is a male spokesperson.
A spokesperson is a person who speaks as the representative of a group or organization.
A spokeswoman is a female spokesperson.

Chinesesense: 海绵(一种海洋动物，体圆而柔软)；
Englishsense: Sponge is a very light soft substance with lots of little holes in it, which can be either artificial or natural. It is used to clean things or as a soft layer.
A sponge is a sea animal with a soft round body made of natural sponge.
A sponge is a piece of sponge that you use for washing yourself or for cleaning things.
If you sponge something, you clean it by wiping it with a wet sponge.
A sponge is a light cake or pudding made from flour, eggs, sugar, and sometimes fat.
If you say that someone sponges off other people or sponges on them, you mean that they regularly get money from other people when they should be trying to support themselves.

Chinesesense: (常出于广告目的而)赞助，资助；
倡议，发起(某项提议或建议)；
(一国)坐视(某次袭击事件)而不顾，支持；
赞助(电视节目);做…的广告赞助商；
赞助人;资助人;倡议者;发起人;主办者；
Englishsense: If an organization or an individual sponsors something such as an event or someone’s training, they pay some or all of the expenses connected with it, often in order to get publicity for themselves.

In Britain, if you sponsor someone who is doing something to raise money for charity, for example trying to walk a certain distance, you agree to give them a sum of money for the charity if they succeed in doing it.
If you sponsor a proposal or suggestion, you officially put it forward and support it.
When a country or an organization such as the United Nations sponsors negotiations between countries, it suggests holding the negotiations and organizes them.
If one country accuses another of sponsoring attacks on it, they mean that the other country does not do anything to prevent the attacks, and may even encourage them.
If a company or organization sponsors a television programme, they pay to have a special advertisement shown at the beginning and end of the programme, and at each commercial break.
A sponsor is a person or organization that sponsors something or someone.

Chinesesense: 资助金;赞助金;资金支持；
Englishsense: Sponsorship is financial support given by a sponsor.
Sponsorship of something is the act of sponsoring it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 自然的，自发的(指由于内部原因而非外界影响所引起的)；
Englishsense: Spontaneous acts are not planned or arranged, but are done because someone suddenly wants to do them.
A spontaneous event happens because of processes within something rather than being caused by things outside it.
A spoon is an object used for eating, stirring, and serving food. One end of it is shaped like a shallow bowl and it has a long handle.
You can refer to an amount of food resting on a spoon as a spoon of food.
If you spoon food into something, you put it there with a spoon.
If you think that someone has a lot of advantages because they have a rich or influential family, you can say that they have been born with a silver spoon in their mouth.
Sports are games such as football and basketball and other competitive leisure activities which need physical effort and skill.
If you say that someone is a sport or a good sport, you mean that they cope with a difficult situation or teasing in a cheerful way.
If you say that someone sports something such as a distinctive item of clothing, you mean that they wear it without any shyness.

Chinesesense: 与体育运动有关的;体育运动用的；
Englishsense: Sporting means relating to sports or used for sports.
If you have a sporting chance of doing something, it is quite likely that you will do that thing.
Spots are small, round, coloured areas on a surface.
Spots on a person’s skin are small lumps or marks.
A spot of a liquid is a small amount of it.
If you have a spot of something, you have a small amount of it.
You can refer to a particular place as a spot.
A spot in a television or radio show is a part of it that is regularly reserved for a particular performer or type of entertainment.
If you spot something or someone, you notice them.
If you are on the spot, you are at the actual place where something is happening.
If you do something on the spot, you do it immediately.
If you put someone on the spot, you cause them to have to answer a difficult question or make a difficult decision.
If you are in a tight spot, you are in a difficult situation.

Chinesesense: 成为公众关注的焦点;受到瞩目；
备受(媒体和公众的)关注；
Englishsense: A spotlight is a powerful light, for example in a theatre, which can be directed so that it lights up a small area.
If something spotlights a particular problem or situation, it makes people notice it and think about it.
Someone or something that is in the spotlight is getting a great deal of public attention.
If someone or something comes under the spotlight, they are thoroughly examined, especially by journalists and the public.
Someone’s spouse is the person they are married to.

Chinesesense: (懒洋洋地)伸开四肢坐着(或躺着)；
(城市的)杂乱无章地扩展的地区；
肆意扩展;杂乱无章地延伸；
Englishsense: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie down with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.
If you say that a place sprawls, you mean that it covers a large area of land.
You can use sprawl to refer to an area where a city has grown outwards in an uncontrolled way.
If something sprawls, its structure is disorganized or it lacks direction.

Chinesesense: (尤指用于植被的)喷水器，喷雾器；
Englishsense: Spray is a lot of small drops of water which are being thrown into the air.
A spray is a liquid kept under pressure in a can or other container, which you can force out in very small drops.
If you spray a liquid somewhere or if it sprays somewhere, drops of the liquid cover a place or shower someone.
If a lot of small things spray somewhere or if something sprays them, they are scattered somewhere with a lot of force.
If someone sprays bullets somewhere, they fire a lot of bullets at a group of people or things.
If something is sprayed, it is painted using paint kept under pressure in a container.
When someone sprays against insects, they cover plants or crops with a chemical which prevents insects feeding on them.
A spray is a piece of equipment for spraying water or another liquid, especially over growing plants.
A spray of flowers or leaves is a number of flowers or leaves on one stem or branch.

Chinesesense: 伸出，张开,叉开(手臂、双手、手指、双腿等)；
将…分散(在一段时间内);分期做；
(尤指为某一特殊场合准备的)丰盛饭菜，盛宴；
(书籍、杂志、报纸中)横贯两版的篇幅；
Englishsense: If you spread something somewhere, you open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.
If you spread your arms, hands, fingers, or legs, you stretch them out until they are far apart.
If you spread a substance on a surface or spread the surface with the substance, you put a thin layer of the substance over the surface.
Spread is a soft food which is put on bread.
If something spreads or is spread by people, it gradually reaches or affects a larger and larger area or more and more people.
If something such as a liquid, gas, or smoke spreads or is spread, it moves outwards in all directions so that it covers a larger area.
If you spread something over a period of time, it takes place regularly or continuously over that period, rather than happening at one time.
If you spread something such as wealth or work, you distribute it evenly or equally. [V n] [V n prep]
A spread of ideas, interests, or other things is a wide variety of them.
A spread is a large meal, especially one that has been prepared for a special occasion.
A spread is two pages of a book, magazine, or newspaper that are opposite each other when you open it at a particular place.
Spread is used to refer to the difference between the price that a seller wants someone to pay for a particular stock or share and the price that the buyer is willing to pay.
If you sprinkle a thing with something such as a liquid or powder, you scatter the liquid or powder over it.
If something is sprinkled with particular things, it has a few of them throughout it and they are far apart from each other.
If it is sprinkling, it is raining very lightly.
The sprint is a short, fast running race.
A sprint is a short race in which the competitors run, drive, ride, or swim very fast.
A sprint is a fast run that someone does, either at the end of a race or because they are in a hurry.
If you sprint, you run or ride as fast as you can over a short distance.

Chinesesense: (植物、蔬菜、种子)发芽，抽芽，长芽；
(出于食用目的)使(豆子、种子等)发芽；
Englishsense: When plants, vegetables, or seeds sprout, they produce new shoots or leaves.
When leaves, shoots, or plants sprout somewhere, they grow there.
If a garden or other area of land sprouts plants, they start to grow there.
If you sprout beans or seeds, you make them grow small shoots before eating them. You usually do this by soaking them in water.
If something such as hair sprouts from a person or animal, or if they sprout it, it grows on them.
If a large number of things have appeared or developed somewhere, you can say that they have sprouted there or that the place has sprouted them.
Sprouts are vegetables that look like tiny cabbages. They are also called brussels sprouts.
Sprouts are new shoots on plants.
If one thing spurs you to do another, it encourages you to do it.
If something spurs a change or event, it makes it happen faster or sooner.
Something that acts as a spur to something else encourages a person or organization to do that thing or makes it happen more quickly.
Spurs are small metal wheels with sharp points that are attached to the heels of a rider’s boots. The rider uses them to make their horse go faster.
The spur of a hill or mountain is a piece of ground which sticks out from its side.
If you do something on the spur of the moment, you do it suddenly, without planning it beforehand.
If you win your spurs or earn your spurs, you achieve a particular status by proving that you can do something skilfully.

Chinesesense: 从事间谍活动;充当间谍；
Englishsense: A spy is a person whose job is to find out secret information about another country or organization.
A spy satellite or spy plane obtains secret information about another country by taking photographs from the sky.
Someone who spies for a country or organization tries to find out secret information about another country or organization.
If you spy on someone, you watch them secretly.
If you spy someone or something, you notice them.

Chinesesense: (专门处理某类犯罪的)警察分队；
(将从中挑选运动员组队参赛的)运动队，大名单；
Englishsense: A squad is a section of a police force that is responsible for dealing with a particular type of crime.
A squad is a group of players from which a sports team will be chosen.
A squad of soldiers is a small group of them.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (用于长度单位前表示面积)平方的；
(用于长度面积后表示四方形物的边长)长宽为…的；
使成二次幂;将(数字)平方；
使(不同想法或行动)协调一致；
将圆的变成方的;做不可能做到的事；
(因行动失败而)重新开始，重起炉灶；
不适宜做某工作的人;与环境格格不入的人；
Englishsense: A square is a shape with four sides that are all the same length and four corners that are all right angles.
In a town or city, a square is a flat open place, often in the shape of a square.
Something that is square has a shape the same as a square or similar to a square.
Square is used before units of length when referring to the area of something. For example, if something is three metres long and two metres wide, its area is six square metres.
Square is used after units of length when you are giving the length of each side of something that is square in shape.
To square a number means to multiply it by itself. For example, 3 squared is 3 x 3, or 9. 3 squared is usually written as 32.
The square of a number is the number produced when you multiply that number by itself. For example, the square of 3 is 9.
If you square two different ideas or actions with each other or if they square with each other, they fit or match each other.
If you square something with someone, you ask their permission or check with them that what you are doing is acceptable to them.
If you say that someone squares the circle, you mean that they bring together two things which are normally thought to be so different that they cannot exist together.
If you are back to square one, you have to start dealing with something from the beginning again because the way you were dealing with it has failed.
If you describe someone as a square peg in a round hole, you mean that they are completely unsuitable for the job they are doing or the situation they are in.
Squarely means directly or in the middle, rather than indirectly or at an angle.
If something such as blame or responsibility lies squarely with someone, they are definitely the person responsible.
If you face something squarely, you face it directly, without trying to avoid it.

Chinesesense: 果汁饮料(通常为浓缩瓶装，饮时掺水)；
Englishsense: If someone or something is squashed, they are pressed or crushed with such force that they become injured or lose their shape.
If people or things are squashed into a place, they are put or pushed into a place where there is not enough room for them to be.
If you say that getting a number of people into a small space is a squash, you mean that it is only just possible for them all to get into it.
If you squash something that is causing you trouble, you put a stop to it, often by force.
Squash is a game in which two players hit a small rubber ball against the walls of a court using rackets.
Squash is a drink made from fruit juice, sugar, and water. Squash is sold in bottles in a concentrated form to which you add water.
A squash is one of a family of vegetables that have thick skin and soft or firm flesh inside.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 擅自占用(闲置房屋或土地)；
Englishsense: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.
If you describe someone or something as squat, you mean they are short and thick, usually in an unattractive way.
People who squat occupy an unused building or unused land without having a legal right to do so.
A squat is an empty building that people are living in illegally, without paying any rent or any property tax.

Chinesesense: 压榨，挤出(液体或软的东西)；
(常因害怕或保护眼睛而)紧闭(双眼)；
Englishsense: If you squeeze something, you press it firmly, usually with your hands.
If you squeeze a liquid or a soft substance out of an object, you get the liquid or substance out by pressing the object.
If you squeeze your eyes shut or if your eyes squeeze shut, you close them tightly, usually because you are frightened or to protect your eyes from something such as strong sunlight.
If you squeeze a person or thing somewhere or if they squeeze there, they manage to get through or into a small space.
If you say that getting a number of people into a small space is a squeeze, you mean that it is only just possible for them all to get into it.
If you squeeze something out of someone, you persuade them to give it to you, although they may be unwilling to do this.

If a government squeezes the economy, they put strict controls on people’s ability to borrow money or on their own departments’ freedom to spend money, in order to control the country’s rate of inflation.
Someone’s squeeze is their boyfriend or girlfriend.
If you squint at something, you look at it with your eyes partly closed.
If someone has a squint, their eyes look in different directions from each other.
A squirrel is a small animal with a long furry tail. Squirrels live mainly in trees.

Chinesesense: (通常指令人不快的感觉的)突发的一阵；
Englishsense: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.
If you stab something or stab at it, you push at it with your finger or with something pointed that you are holding.
If you have a stab at something, you try to do it.
You can refer to a sudden, usually unpleasant feeling as a stab of that feeling.

If you say that someone has stabbed you in the back, you mean that they have done something very harmful to you when you thought that you could trust them. You can refer to an action of this kind as a stab in the back.
If something stabilizes, or is stabilized, it becomes stable.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 接受同一经纪人服务的一群人；
Englishsense: If something is stable, it is not likely to change or come to an end suddenly.
If someone has a stable personality, they are calm and reasonable and their mood does not change suddenly.
You can describe someone who is seriously ill as stable when their condition has stopped getting worse.
Chemical substances are described as stable when they tend to remain in the same chemical or atomic state.
If an object is stable, it is firmly fixed in position and is not likely to move or fall.
A stable or stables is a building in which horses are kept.
A stable or stables is an organization that breeds and trains horses for racing.
When horses are stabled, they are put into a stable.
You can say that someone has a stable of people when they manage and promote the careers of that group of people.

If you say that someone has closed or shut the stable door after the horse has bolted, you mean that they have tried to prevent something happening but they have done so too late to prevent damage being done.

Chinesesense: 在(某组织机构中)安插(对自己有利的人员)；
Englishsense: A stack of things is a pile of them.
If you stack a number of things, you arrange them in neat piles.
If you say that someone has stacks of something, you mean that they have a lot of it.

If people who are walking or dancing are in step, they are moving their feet forward at exactly the same time as each other. If they are out of step, their feet are moving forward at different times.
If people are in step with each other, their ideas or opinions are the same. If they are out of step with each other, their ideas or opinions are different.
If you tell someone to step on it, you are telling them to go faster or hurry up.
If you do something step by step, you do it by progressing gradually from one stage to the next.
If someone tells you to watch your step, they are warning you to be careful about how you behave or what you say so that you do not get into trouble.
Someone’s stepfather is the man who has married their mother after the death or divorce of their father.

Chinesesense: 立体声磁带播放机;立体声激光唱片播放机;立体音响；
Englishsense: Stereo is used to describe a sound system in which the sound is played through two speakers.
A stereo is a cassette or CD player with two speakers.

Chinesesense: 模式化的形象(或特征);固定模式;刻板印象;陈规老套；
Englishsense: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.
If someone is stereotyped as something, people form a fixed general idea or image of them, so that it is assumed that they will behave in a particular way.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Something that is sterile is completely clean and free from germs.
A person or animal that is sterile is unable to have or produce babies.
A sterile situation is lacking in energy and new ideas.

Chinesesense: 深感不安的;焦虑的;担心的；
(故意)让…独自烦恼(而不加劝慰)；
Englishsense: A stew is a meal which you make by cooking meat and vegetables in liquid at a low temperature.
When you stew meat, vegetables, or fruit, you cook them slowly in liquid in a closed dish.
If you are in a stew, you feel very worried.
If you let a person stew or if you leave them to stew, you deliberately allow them to worry about something for a while, rather than telling them something which would make them feel better.

Chinesesense: (用于某一特定用途的)木条，木棍；
严厉的批评;大肆的取笑；
Englishsense: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree.
A stick is a long thin piece of wood which is used for supporting someone’s weight or for hitting people or animals.
A stick is a long thin piece of wood which is used for a particular purpose.
Some long thin objects that are used in sports are called sticks.
A stick of something is a long thin piece of it.
If you give someone some stick, you criticize them or tease them roughly.
If you say that someone lives in the sticks, you mean that they live a long way from any large cities.
If you say that something is a stick to beat someone with, you mean that it is used, or could be used, as a basis for criticism.
If someone gets the wrong end of the stick or gets hold of the wrong end of the stick, they do not understand something correctly and get the wrong idea about it.
If you say that there are more things than you could or can shake a stick at, you are emphasizing in a humorous way that there are a lot of them.
If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.
If you stick a pointed object in something, or if it sticks in something, it goes into it or through it by making a cut or hole.
If something is sticking out from a surface or object, it extends up or away from it. If something is sticking into a surface or object, it is partly in it.
If you stick one thing to another, you attach it using glue, sticky tape, or another sticky substance.
If one thing sticks to another, it becomes attached to it and is difficult to remove.
If something sticks in your mind, you remember it for a long time.
If you give someone or something a name and the name sticks, it becomes the name which most people use to refer to that person or thing.
If someone manages to make a charge or accusation stick, they show that the person accused is guilty of the crime or action they are accused of.
If something which can usually be moved sticks, it becomes fixed in one position.
If you are in an unpleasant or difficult situation and you say that you cannot stick it, you mean that you cannot bear to remain there long.
If you say that someone can stick something, especially a job, or if you tell them where to stick it, you are rudely refusing it or emphasizing that you do not want it or like it.

Chinesesense: (正面有字或画的)小贴纸，不粘胶贴纸；
Englishsense: A sticker is a small piece of paper or plastic, with writing or a picture on one side, which you can stick onto a surface.

Chinesesense: 黏性的;涂有黏性物质的；
Englishsense: A sticky substance is soft, or thick and liquid, and can stick to other things. Sticky things are covered with a sticky substance.
A sticky situation involves problems or is embarrassing.
Sticky weather is unpleasantly hot and damp.
If someone comes to a sticky end or meets a sticky end, they suffer very badly or die in an unpleasant way.

Chinesesense: (门、抽屉等)难打开的，不灵活的，发紧的；
(行为)拘谨的，生硬的，不太友好的；
酒烈性的，酒精度数高的；
Englishsense: Something that is stiff is firm or does not bend easily.
Something such as a door or drawer that is stiff does not move as easily as it should.
If you are stiff, your muscles or joints hurt when you move, because of illness or because of too much exercise.
Stiff behaviour is rather formal and not very friendly or relaxed.
Stiff can be used to mean difficult or severe.
A stiff drink is a large amount of a strong alcoholic drink.
A stiff wind is blowing quite strongly.
If you are bored stiff, worried stiff, or scared stiff, you are extremely bored, worried, or scared.
If someone stifles something you consider to be a good thing, they prevent it from continuing.
If you stifle a yawn or laugh, you prevent yourself from yawning or laughing.
If you stifle your natural feelings or behaviour, you prevent yourself from having those feelings or behaving in that way.
If something has a stigma attached to it, people think it is something to be ashamed of.
The stigma of a flower is the top of the centre part which takes in pollen.
