Chinesesense: 但是;尽管如此;(虽然…)还是；
(与 further, another, more 等连用强调数量惊人或极大)更，还；
(与比较级连用强调某种特点)更，还要；
(饮料)不含碳酸气的，不冒泡的；
Englishsense: If a situation that used to exist still exists, it has continued and exists now.
If something that has not yet happened could still happen, it is possible that it will happen. If something that has not yet happened is still to happen, it will happen at a later time.
If you say that there is still an amount of something left, you are emphasizing that there is that amount left.
You use still to emphasize that something remains the case or is true in spite of what you have just said.
You use still to indicate that a problem or difficulty is not really worth worrying about.
You use still in expressions such as still further, still another, and still more to show that you find the number or quantity of things you are referring to surprising or excessive.
You use still with comparatives to indicate that something has even more of a quality than something else.
If you stay still, you stay in the same position and do not move.
If air or water is still, it is not moving.
Drinks that are still do not contain any bubbles of carbon dioxide.
If a place is still, it is quiet and shows no sign of activity.
If a sound stills or is stilled, it becomes quiet.
A still is a photograph taken from a cinema film which is used for publicity purposes.
A still is a piece of equipment used to make strong alcoholic drinks by a process called distilling.
To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.
If you are stimulated by something, it makes you feel full of ideas and enthusiasm.
If something stimulates a part of a person’s body, it causes it to move or start working.
A stimulus is something that encourages activity in people or things.

Chinesesense: 使感到刺痛;使感到灼痛；
(警方为抓捕罪犯精心设计的)圈套；
煞风景的结局;令人不愉快的结尾；
Englishsense: If a plant, animal, or insect stings you, a sharp part of it, usually covered with poison, is pushed into your skin so that you feel a sharp pain.
The sting of an insect or animal is the part that stings you.
If you feel a sting, you feel a sharp pain in your skin or other part of your body.
If a part of your body stings, or if a substance stings it, you feel a sharp pain there.
If someone’s remarks sting you, they make you feel hurt and annoyed.
A sting is a clever secret plan carried out by the police in order to catch criminals.
If an announcement or decision has a sting in the tail or a sting in its tail, it contains a critical and unpleasant part, normally at the end.
If something takes the sting out of a situation, it makes it less unpleasant.

Chinesesense: 发出恶臭;散发难闻气味；
令人讨厌;让人反感;让人感觉糟糕；
(引人注意的)发怒，大吵大闹，泄愤；
Englishsense: To stink means to smell extremely unpleasant.
If you say that something stinks, you mean that you disapprove of it because it involves ideas, feelings, or practices that you do not like.
If someone makes a stink about something they are angry about, they show their anger in order to make people take notice.

Chinesesense: (在某地的)工作时间，活动时间；
Englishsense: A stint is a period of time which you spend doing a particular job or activity or working in a particular place.

Chinesesense: (因不舒服)稍稍活动;(睡醒前)挪动身体；
打动;激起，激发(强烈的感情)；
(回忆、感情或情绪)产生，苏醒，萌动;引发;唤起；
受到轻微影响;小受打击；
Englishsense: If you stir a liquid or other substance, you move it around or mix it in a container using something such as a spoon.
If you stir, you move slightly, for example because you are uncomfortable or beginning to wake up.
If you do not stir from a place, you do not move from it.
If something stirs or if the wind stirs it, it moves gently in the wind.
If you stir yourself, or if something stirs you into action, you move in order to start doing something.
If something stirs you, it makes you react with a strong emotion.
If a particular memory, feeling, or mood stirs or is stirred in you, you begin to think about it or feel it.
If an event causes a stir, it causes great excitement, shock, or anger among people.

If you say that someone has been shaken but not stirred by an experience, you mean that they have been slightly disturbed or emotionally affected by it, but not deeply enough to change their behaviour or way of thinking.

Chinesesense: (通常指因奔跑或大笑引起的)肋部剧痛，岔气；
Englishsense: If you stitch cloth, you use a needle and thread to join two pieces together or to make a decoration.
Stitches are the short pieces of thread that have been sewn in a piece of cloth.
In knitting and crochet, a stitch is a loop made by one turn of wool around a knitting needle or crochet hook.
If you sew or knit something in a particular stitch, you sew or knit in a way that produces a particular pattern.
When doctors stitch a wound, they use a special needle and thread to sew the skin together.
A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the skin of a wound together.
A stitch is a sharp pain in your side, usually caused by running or laughing a lot.
If you are in stitches, you cannot stop laughing.

Chinesesense: (尤指经过特殊饲养的)家畜，牲畜；
(回答、说法或做事方式)老一套的，陈腐的；
作出整体估量;全面分析；
Englishsense: Stocks are shares in the ownership of a company, or investments on which a fixed amount of interest will be paid.
A company’s stock is the amount of money which the company has through selling shares.
If a shop stocks particular goods, it keeps a supply of them to sell.
A shop’s stock is the total amount of goods which it has available to sell.
If you stock something such as a cupboard, shelf, or room, you fill it with food or other things.
If you have a stock of things, you have a supply of them stored in a place ready to be used.
The stock of something is the total amount of it that is available in a particular area.
If you are from a particular stock, you are descended from a particular group of people.
Stock are cattle, sheep, pigs, or other animals which are kept by a farmer, usually ones which have been specially bred.
A stock answer, expression, or way of doing something is one that is very commonly used, especially because people cannot be bothered to think of something new.
Stock is a liquid, usually made by boiling meat, bones, or vegetables in water, that is used to give flavour to soups and sauces.
In former times, the stocks were an instrument of punishment. A criminal’s hands and legs were locked into holes in a wooden frame while people threw things at them.
If goods are in stock, a shop has them available to sell. If they are out of stock, it does not.
If you take stock, you pause to think about all the aspects of a situation or event before deciding what to do next.
Stockings are items of women’s clothing which fit closely over their feet and legs. Stockings are usually made of nylon or silk and are held in place by suspenders.
A stocking is the same as a Christmas stocking.

Chinesesense: (对令人反胃的东西的)承受能力；
令人倒胃口;使人感到恶心；
Englishsense: Your stomach is the organ inside your body where food is digested before it moves into the intestines.
You can refer to the front part of your body below your waist as your stomach.
If the front part of your body below your waist feels uncomfortable because you are feeling worried or frightened, you can refer to it as your stomach.
If you say that someone has a strong stomach, you mean that they are not disgusted by things that disgust most other people.
If you cannot stomach something, you cannot accept it because you dislike it or disapprove of it.
If you do something on an empty stomach, you do it without having eaten.
If you have no stomach for something, you do not have the courage to do it.
If you say that you feel sick to your stomach about something, you mean that you feel very angry or upset about it.
If you say that something turns your stomach or makes your stomach turn, you mean that it is so unpleasant or offensive that it makes you feel sick.

Chinesesense: (常指因生气而)跺着脚走，迈着重重的步伐；
Englishsense: If you stomp somewhere, you walk there with very heavy steps, often because you are angry.

Chinesesense: (作为宗教标志的)石碑;纪念碑；
(表示观念或规则固定而不可改变)板上钉钉，铁板钉钉；
英石(重量单位，相当于 14 磅或6.35公斤)；
挖空心思;千方百计;用尽一切手段；
Englishsense: Stone is a hard solid substance found in the ground and often used for building houses.
A stone is a small piece of rock that is found on the ground.
A stone is a large piece of stone put somewhere in memory of a person or event, or as a religious symbol.
Stone is used in expressions such as set in stone and tablets of stone to suggest that an idea or rule is firm and fixed, and cannot be changed.
You can refer to a jewel as a stone.
A stone is a small hard ball of minerals and other substances which sometimes forms in a person’s kidneys or gall bladder.
The stone in a plum, cherry, or other fruit is the large hard seed in the middle of it.
If you stone a fruit, you remove its stone.
If people stone someone or something, they throw stones at them.
A stone is a measurement of weight, especially the weight of a person, equal to 14 pounds or 6.35 kilograms. See usage note at: weight
If you say that one place is a stone’s throw from another, you mean that the places are close to each other.
If you say that you will leave no stone unturned, you are emphasizing that you will try every way you can think of in order to achieve what you want.
A stool is a seat with legs but no support for your arms or back.
If someone has fallen between two stools, they are unable to decide which of two courses of action to take and as a result they have not done either of them successfully.
Stools are the pieces of solid waste matter that are passed out of a person’s body through their bowels.

Chinesesense: (机器等)停止运转;使停止工作；
使(移动着的人或车)停下;把…拦住；
做事很有分寸;懂得如何把持自己；
Englishsense: If you have been doing something and then you stop doing it, you no longer do it.
If you stop something happening, you prevent it from happening or prevent it from continuing.
If an activity or process stops, it is no longer happening.
If something such as machine stops or is stopped, it is no longer moving or working.
When a moving person or vehicle stops or is stopped, they no longer move and they remain in the same place.
If something that is moving comes to a stop or is brought to a stop, it slows down and no longer moves.
If someone does not stop to think or to explain, they continue with what they are doing without taking any time to think about or explain it.
If you say that a quality or state stops somewhere, you mean that it exists or is true up to that point, but no further.
A stop is a place where buses or trains regularly stop so that people can get on and off.
If you stop somewhere on a journey, you stay there for a short while.
A stop is a time or place at which you stop during a journey.
In music, organ stops are the knobs at the side of the organ, which you pull or push in order to control the type of sound that comes out of the pipes.
If you say that someone will stop at nothing to get something, you are emphasizing that they are willing to do things that are extreme, wrong, or dangerous in order to get it.
If you pull out all the stops, you do everything you can to make something happen or succeed.
If you put a stop to something that you do not like or approve of, you prevent it from happening or continuing.
If you say that someone does not know when to stop, you mean that they do not control their own behaviour very well and so they often annoy or upset other people.
If you refer to the storage of something, you mean that it is kept in a special place until it is needed.
Storage is the process of storing data in a computer.

Chinesesense: 商店(英国英语中主要指大型百货商店，而美国英语中可指任何规模的商店)；
就要出现在…身上;即将发生在…身上；
重视;珍惜;认为…极为必要；
Englishsense: A store is a building or part of a building where things are sold. In British English, store is used mainly to refer to a large shop selling a variety of goods, but in American English a store can be any size of shop.
When you store things, you put them in a container or other place and leave them there until they are needed.
When you store information, you keep it in your memory, in a file, or in a computer.
A store of things is a supply of them that you keep somewhere until you need them.
A store is a place where things are kept while they are not being used.
If you have a store of knowledge, jokes, or stories, you have a large amount of them ready to be used.
If something is in store for you, it is going to happen at some time in the future.
If you set great store by something, you think that it is extremely important or necessary.

Chinesesense: 强烈的反应;群情激愤;激动人心；
Englishsense: A storm is very bad weather, with heavy rain, strong winds, and often thunder and lightning.
If something causes a storm, it causes an angry or excited reaction from a large number of people.
A storm of applause or other noise is a sudden loud amount of it made by an audience or other group of people in reaction to something.
If you storm into or out of a place, you enter or leave it quickly and noisily, because you are angry.
If you storm, you say something in a very loud voice, because you are extremely angry.
If a place that is being defended is stormed, a group of people attack it, usually in order to get inside it.
If someone or something takes a place by storm, they are extremely successful.
If someone weathers the storm, they succeed in reaching the end of a very difficult period without much harm or damage.

Chinesesense: 但那是另一回事了;那就不相干了；
另一回事，不同情况(通常指不好的一面)；
又来了，又是老一套(表示不好的事情似乎总是重复发生)；
不是事情的全部;只是部分情况；
Englishsense: A story is a description of imaginary people and events, which is written or told in order to entertain.
A story is a description of an event or something that happened to someone, especially a spoken description of it.
The story of something is a description of all the important things that have happened to it since it began.
If someone invents a story, they give a false explanation or account of something.
A news story is a piece of news in a newspaper or in a news broadcast.
You say ’ but that’s another story ’ when you have mentioned a subject that you are not going to talk about or explain in detail.

In British English, you use to cut a long story short to indicate that you are going to state the final result of an event and not give any more details. In American English, you say to make a long story short.
You use a different story to refer to a situation, usually a bad one, which exists in one set of circumstances when you have mentioned that it does not exist in another set of circumstances.
If you say it’s the same old story or it’s the old story, you mean that something unpleasant or undesirable seems to happen again and again.
If you say that something is only part of the story or is not the whole story, you mean that the explanation or information given is not enough for a situation to be fully understood.
If someone tells you their side of the story, they tell you why they behaved in a particular way and why they think they were right, when other people think that person behaved wrongly.

Chinesesense: 讲故事的人;说书人;小说作家；
Englishsense: A storyteller is someone who tells or writes stories.
Storytelling is the activity of telling or writing stories.
A stove is a piece of equipment which provides heat, either for cooking or for heating a room.
A stove is the top of a cooker.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 直截了当的;直率的;坦诚的；
只涉及两人(或两物)的;(选择)非此即彼的；
正经的;正统的;规矩本分的；
(尤指酒精饮料)纯的，不掺水的；
改过自新;改邪归正;重新做人；
Englishsense: A straight line or edge continues in the same direction and does not bend or curve.
Straight hair has no curls or waves in it.
You use straight to indicate that the way from one place to another is very direct, with no changes of direction.
If you go straight to a place, you go there immediately.
If you give someone a straight answer, you answer them clearly and honestly.
Straight means following one after the other, with no gaps or intervals.
A straight choice or a straight fight involves only two people or things.
If you describe someone as straight, you mean that they are normal and conventional, for example in their opinions and in the way they live.
If you describe someone as straight, you mean that they are heterosexual rather than homosexual.
A straight drink, especially an alcoholic drink, has not had another liquid such as water added to it.
On a racetrack, a straight is a section of the track that is straight, rather than curved.
If you get something straight, you make sure that you understand it properly or that someone else does.
If a criminal is going straight, they are no longer involved in crime.
If something keeps people on the straight and narrow, it helps to keep them living an honest or healthy life.
If you straighten something, you make it tidy or put it in its proper position.
If you are standing in a relaxed or slightly bent position and then you straighten, you make your back or body straight and upright.
If you straighten something, or it straightens, it becomes straight.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.
If you describe a person or their behaviour as straightforward, you approve of them because they are honest and direct, and do not try to hide their feelings.

Chinesesense: 带来压力的情况;造成紧张的因素；
应力;张力;拉力;作用力;压力；
努力做;竭力做;费力做事；
过滤;滤掉(食物中)的液体；
(病菌的)类型;(植物或其他有机物的)系，品系，品种；
Englishsense: If strain is put on an organization or system, it has to do more than it is able to do.
To strain something means to make it do more than it is able to do.
Strain is a state of worry and tension caused by a difficult situation.
If you say that a situation is a strain, you mean that it makes you worried and tense.
Strain is a force that pushes, pulls, or stretches something in a way that may damage it.
Strain is an injury to a muscle in your body, caused by using the muscle too much or twisting it.
If you strain a muscle, you injure it by using it too much or twisting it.
If you strain to do something, you make a great effort to do it when it is difficult to do.
When you strain food, you separate the liquid part of it from the solid parts.
You can use strain to refer to a particular quality in someone’s character, remarks, or work.
A strain of a germ, plant, or other organism is a particular type of it.
If you hear the strains of music, you hear music being played.
A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.
A strand of a plan or theory is a part of it.
If you are stranded, you are prevented from leaving a place, for example because of bad weather.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 奇怪的;怪异的;意料之外的；
局促不安的;不自在的;不舒服的；
Englishsense: Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.
A strange place is one that you have never been to before. A strange person is someone that you have never met before.
If you feel strange, you have an unpleasant or uncomfortable feeling, either physical or emotional.

Englishsense: A stranger is someone you have never met before.

If you are a stranger in a place, you do not know the place well.
If you are a stranger to something, you have had no experience of it or do not understand it.
To strangle someone means to kill them by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe.
To strangle something means to prevent it from succeeding or developing.
A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material. Straps are used to carry things, fasten things together, or to hold a piece of clothing in place.
If you strap something somewhere, you fasten it there with a strap.

If you put something in a strategic position, you place it cleverly in a position where it will be most useful or have the most effect.

Chinesesense: (尤指军事)战略家，善于策划的人；
Englishsense: A strategist is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to gain an advantage or to achieve success, especially in war.

Englishsense: A strategy is a general plan or set of plans intended to achieve something, especially over a long period.
Strategy is the art of planning the best way to gain an advantage or achieve success, especially in war.

Chinesesense: 抓救命稻草;采取极端措施;作绝望的挣扎；

Englishsense: Straw consists of the dried, yellowish stalks from crops such as wheat or barley.
A straw is a thin tube of paper or plastic, which you use to suck a drink into your mouth.
If you are clutching at straws or grasping at straws, you are trying unusual or extreme ideas or methods because other ideas or methods have failed.

If an event is the last straw or the straw that broke the camel’s back, it is the latest in a series of unpleasant or undesirable events, and makes you feel that you cannot tolerate a situation any longer.
If you draw the short straw, you are chosen from a number of people to perform a job or duty that you will not enjoy.
If you say that an incident or piece of news is a straw in the wind, you mean that it gives an indication of what might happen in the future.
A strawberry is a small red fruit which is soft and juicy and has tiny yellow seeds on its skin.

Englishsense: If someone strays somewhere, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.
A stray dog or cat has wandered away from its owner’s home.
If your mind or your eyes stray, you do not concentrate on or look at one particular subject, but start thinking about or looking at other things.
You use stray to describe something that exists separated from other similar things.

Chinesesense: 在…上留下条纹(或条痕);使布满条纹(或条痕)；
(赌博或体育比赛等中的)运气，手气；
Englishsense: A streak is a long stripe or mark on a surface which contrasts with the surface because it is a different colour.
If something streaks a surface, it makes long stripes or marks on the surface.
If someone has a streak of a particular type of behaviour, they sometimes behave in that way.
If something or someone streaks somewhere, they move there very quickly.
A winning streak or a lucky streak is a continuous series of successes, for example in gambling or sport. A losing streak or an unlucky streak is a series of failures or losses.

Chinesesense: 一连串;接二连三;源源不断；
(把孩子按年龄和能力编在一起的)班，组；
Englishsense: A stream is a small narrow river.
A stream of smoke, air, or liquid is a narrow moving mass of it.
A stream of vehicles or people is a long moving line of them.
A stream of things is a large number of them occurring one after another.
If a liquid streams somewhere, it flows or comes out in large amounts.
If your eyes are streaming, liquid is coming from them, for example because you have a cold. You can also say that your nose is streaming.
If people or vehicles stream somewhere, they move there quickly and in large numbers.
When light streams into or out of a place, it shines strongly into or out of it.
If something such as a flag or someone’s hair streams in the wind, it is blown so that it is almost horizontal.
In a school, a stream is a group of children of the same age and ability who are taught together.
To stream pupils means to divide them into groups according to their ability.
If something such as a new factory or a new system comes on stream or is brought on stream, it begins to operate or becomes available.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词
Englishsense: A street is a road in a city, town, or village, usually with houses along it.
You can use street or streets when talking about activities that happen out of doors in a town rather than inside a building.
If someone is streets ahead of you, they are much better at something than you are.
If you talk about the man in the street or the man or woman in the street, you mean ordinary people in general.
If a job or activity is up your street, it is the kind of job or activity that you are very interested in.

(军队或队伍)人员不足，阵容不全；
Englishsense: Your strength is the physical energy that you have, which gives you the ability to perform various actions, such as lifting or moving things.
Someone’s strength in a difficult situation is their confidence or courage.
The strength of an object or material is its ability to be treated roughly, or to carry heavy weights, without being damaged or destroyed.
The strength of a person, organization, or country is the power or influence that they have.
If you refer to the strength of a feeling, opinion, or belief, you are talking about how deeply it is felt or believed by people, or how much they are influenced by it.
Someone’s strengths are the qualities and abilities that they have which are an advantage to them, or which make them successful.
If you refer to the strength of a currency, economy, or industry, you mean that its value or success is steady or increasing.
The strength of a group of people is the total number of people in it.
The strength of a wind, current, or other force is its power or speed.
The strength of a drink, chemical, or drug is the amount of the particular substance in it that gives it its particular effect.
You can talk about the strength of a flavour, smell, colour, sound, or light to describe how intense or easily noticed it is.
If a person or organization goes from strength to strength, they become more and more successful or confident.
If a team or army is at full strength, all the members that it needs or usually has are present.
If a group turns out in strength, they arrive in large numbers.
If one thing is done on the strength of another, it is done because of the influence of that other thing.
If an army or team is under strength or below strength, it does not have all the members that it needs or usually has.

Englishsense: If something strengthens a person or group or if they strengthen their position, they become more powerful and secure, or more likely to succeed.
If something strengthens a case or argument, it supports it by providing more reasons or evidence for it.
If a currency, economy, or industry strengthens, or if something strengthens it, it increases in value or becomes more successful.
If a government strengthens laws or measures or if they strengthen, they are made more severe.
If something strengthens you or strengthens your resolve or character, it makes you more confident and determined.
If something strengthens a relationship or link, or if a relationship or link strengthens, it makes it closer and more likely to last for a long time.
If something strengthens an impression, feeling, or belief, or if it strengthens, it becomes greater or affects more people.
If something strengthens your body or a part of your body, it makes it healthier, often in such a way that you can move or carry heavier things.
If something strengthens an object or structure, it makes it able to be treated roughly or able to support heavy weights, without being damaged or destroyed.
If the wind, current, or other force strengthens, it becomes faster or more powerful.

Chinesesense: 精神压力;心理负担;紧张；
Englishsense: If you stress a point in a discussion, you put extra emphasis on it because you think it is important.
If you feel under stress, you feel worried and tense because of difficulties in your life.
Stresses are strong physical pressures applied to an object.
If you stress a word or part of a word when you say it, you put emphasis on it so that it sounds slightly louder.

Englishsense: Something that stretches over an area or distance covers or exists in the whole of that area or distance.
A stretch of road, water, or land is a length or area of it.
When you stretch, you put your arms or legs out straight and tighten your muscles.
A stretch of time is a period of time.
If an event or activity stretches or is stretched into a further period of time, it continues into that period, which is later than expected.
If something stretches from one time to another, it begins at the first time and ends at the second, which is longer than expected.
If a group of things stretch from one type of thing to another, the group includes a wide range of things.
When something soft or elastic stretches or is stretched, it becomes longer or bigger as well as thinner, usually because it is pulled.
Stretch fabric is soft and elastic and stretches easily.
If you stretch an amount of something or if it stretches, you make it last longer than it usually would by being careful and not wasting any of it. [V n] [V]
If your resources can stretch to something, you can just afford to do it.
If something stretches your money or resources, it uses them up so you have hardly enough for your needs.

If you say that a job or task stretches you, you mean that you like it because it makes you work hard and use all your energy and skills so that you do not become bored or achieve less than you should.
If you are at full stretch, your arm is straight and extended as far as possible, usually because you are trying to reach something that is almost too far away.
If you are at full stretch, you are using the maximum amount of effort or energy.
If you say that something is not true or possible by any stretch of the imagination, you are emphasizing that it is completely untrue or absolutely impossible.
If you stretch your legs, you go for a short walk, usually after you have been sitting down for a long time.
If you stretch a point, you describe something in a way which is not accurate, although it may be partly true.

If you strike someone or something, you deliberately hit them.
If something that is falling or moving strikes something, it hits it.
If you strike one thing against another, or if one thing strikes against another, the first thing hits the second thing.
If something such as an illness or disaster strikes, it suddenly happens.

If something strikes at the heart or root of something, it attacks or conflicts with the basic elements or principles of that thing.

If something strikes you as being a particular thing, it gives you the impression of being that thing.
If you are struck by something, you think it is very impressive, noticeable, or interesting.
If you strike a deal or a bargain with someone, you come to an agreement with them.
If you strike a balance, you do something that is halfway between two extremes.
If you strike a pose or attitude, you put yourself in a particular position, for example when someone is taking your photograph.
If something strikes fear into people, it makes them very frightened or anxious.
If you are struck dumb or blind, you suddenly become unable to speak or to see.
When a clock strikes, its bells make a sound to indicate what the time is.
If you strike words from a document or an official record, you remove them. [V n from n] [Also V n] [V P n (not pron)] [Also V n P] [Formal]
When you strike a match, you make it produce a flame by moving it quickly against something rough.
If someone strikes oil or gold, they discover it in the ground as a result of mining or drilling.
When a coin or medal is struck, it is made.
If someone has two strikes against them, things cause them to be in a bad situation or at a disadvantage.
If you are within striking distance of something, or if something is within striking distance, it is quite near, so it could be reached or achieved quite easily.
If you strike gold, you find, do, or produce something that brings you a lot of money or success.
If you strike it rich, you make a lot of money, especially in a short time.

Something that is striped has stripes on it.
If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

The strokes of a pen or brush are the movements or marks that you make with it when you are writing or painting.
When you are swimming or rowing, your strokes are the repeated movements that you make with your arms or the oars.
A swimming stroke is a particular style or method of swimming.
The strokes of a clock are the sounds that indicate each hour.
In sports such as tennis, baseball, cricket, and golf, a stroke is the action of hitting the ball.
A stroke of luck or good fortune is something lucky that happens.
A stroke of genius or inspiration is a very good idea that someone suddenly has.
If something happens at a stroke or in one stroke, it happens suddenly and completely because of one single action.
If someone does not do a stroke of work, they are very lazy and do no work at all.
If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

Englishsense: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.

Strong objects or materials are not easily broken and can support a lot of weight or resist a lot of strain.
A strong wind, current, or other force has a lot of power or speed, and can cause heavy things to move.

A strong colour, flavour, smell, sound, or light is intense and easily noticed.
If someone has a strong accent, they speak in a distinctive way that shows very clearly what country or region they come from.
You can say that someone has strong features or a strong face if their face has large, distinctive features.

A structure is something that has been built.
If you structure something, you arrange it in a careful, organized pattern or system.
If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though other people or things may be making it difficult for you to succeed.
A struggle is a long and difficult attempt to achieve something such as freedom or political rights.
If you struggle when you are being held, you twist, kick, and move violently in order to get free.
If two people struggle with each other, they fight.
If you struggle to move yourself or to move a heavy object, you try to do it, but it is difficult.
If you struggle somewhere, you succeed in moving there, but only with great difficulty.
If a person or organization is struggling, they are likely to fail in what they are doing, even though they might be trying very hard.

Englishsense: You use tactical to describe an action or plan which is intended to help someone achieve what they want in a particular situation.
Tactical weapons or forces are those which a military leader can decide for themselves to use in a battle, rather than waiting for a decision by a political leader.

Englishsense: A tag is a small piece of card or cloth which is attached to an object or person and has information about that object or person on it.
An electronic tag is a device that is firmly attached to someone or something and sets off an alarm if that person or thing moves away or is removed.
If you tag something, you attach something to it or mark it so that it can be identified later.
You can refer to a phrase that is used to describe someone or something as a tag.

Tag is a children’s game in which one child chases the others and tries to touch them.

Englishsense: The tail of an animal, bird, or fish is the part extending beyond the end of its body.
You can use tail to refer to the end or back of something, especially something long and thin.
If a man is wearing tails, he is wearing a formal jacket which has two long pieces hanging down at the back.
To tail someone means to follow close behind them and watch where they go and what they do.
A tail is someone who is paid to watch and to follow another person.
If you toss a coin and it comes down tails, you can see the side of it that does not have a picture of a head on it.
If you say that the tail is wagging the dog, you mean that a small or unimportant part of something is becoming too important and is controlling the whole thing.
If you say that you have your tail between your legs, you are emphasizing that you feel defeated and ashamed.
If you turn tail, you turn and run away.
A tailor is a person whose job is to make men’s clothes.
If you tailor something such as a plan or system to someone’s needs, you make it suitable for a particular person or purpose by changing the details of it.

Englishsense: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say ’ she took a shower ’ instead of ’she showered’.

In ordinary spoken or written English, people use take with a range of nouns instead of using a more specific verb. For example people often say ’ he took control ’ or ’ she took a positive attitude ’ instead of ’he assumed control’ or ’she adopted a positive attitude’.
If you take something, you reach out for it and hold it.
If you take something with you when you go somewhere, you carry it or have it with you.
If a person, vehicle, or path takes someone somewhere, they transport or lead them there.
If something such as a job or interest takes you to a place, it is the reason for you going there.
If you take something such as your problems or your business to someone, you go to that person when you have problems you want to discuss or things you want to buy.
If one thing takes another to a particular level, condition, or state, it causes it to reach that level or condition.
If you take something from a place, you remove it from there.
If you take something from someone who owns it, you steal it or go away with it without their permission.
If an army or political party takes something or someone, they win them from their enemy or opponent.
If you take one number or amount from another, you subtract it or deduct it.
If you cannot take something difficult, painful, or annoying, you cannot tolerate it without becoming upset, ill, or angry.
If you take something such as damage or loss, you suffer it, especially in war or in a battle.
If something takes a certain amount of time, that amount of time is needed in order to do it.
If something takes a particular quality or thing, that quality or thing is needed in order to do it. [V n] [it V n to-inf] [it V n before cl] [no passive]
If you take something that is given or offered to you, you agree to accept it.
If you take a feeling such as pleasure, pride, or delight in a particular thing or activity, the thing or activity gives you that feeling.
If a shop, restaurant, theatre, or other business takes a certain amount of money, they get that amount from people buying goods or services.
You can use take to refer to the amount of money that a business such as a store or theatre gets from selling its goods or tickets during a particular period.
If you take a prize or medal, you win it.
If you take the blame, responsibility, or credit for something, you agree to accept it.
If you take patients or clients, you accept them as your patients or clients.
If you take a telephone call, you speak to someone who is telephoning you.
If you take something in a particular way, you react in the way mentioned to a situation or to someone’s beliefs or behaviour.
You use take when you are discussing or explaining a particular question, in order to introduce an example or to say how the question is being considered. [V n] [V n prep/adv] [V-ed] [usu imper]
If you take someone’s meaning or point, you understand and accept what they are saying.
If you take someone for something, you believe wrongly that they are that thing.
If you take something from among a number of things, you choose to have or buy it.
If you take a road or route, you choose to travel along it.
If you take a house or flat, you rent it, usually for only a short time.
If you take something such as a newspaper, you buy it or have it delivered to your home on a regular basis.
If you take a car, train, bus, or plane, you use it to go from one place to another.
If you take a subject or course at school or university, you choose to study it.
If you take a test or examination, you do it in order to obtain a qualification.
If you take someone for a subject, you give them lessons in that subject.
If someone takes drugs, pills, or other medicines, they take them into their body, for example by swallowing them.
If you take food or drink, you eat or drink it.
If you take a note or a letter, you write down something you want to remember or the words that someone says.
If you take a particular measurement, you use special equipment to find out what something measures.
If a place or container takes a particular amount or number, there is enough space for that amount or number.
If you take a particular size in shoes or clothes, that size fits you.
If something such as a drug or a dye takes, it has the effect or result that is intended.
A take is a short piece of action which is filmed in one continuous process for a cinema or television film.
Someone’s take on a particular situation or fact is their attitude to it or their interpretation of it.
You can say ’ I take it ’ to check with someone that what you believe to be the case or what you understand them to mean is in fact the case, or is in fact what they mean.
You can say ’ take it from me ’ to tell someone that you are absolutely sure that what you are saying is correct, and that they should believe you.
If you say to someone ’ take it or leave it ’, you are telling them that they can accept something or not accept it, but that you are not prepared to discuss any other alternatives.
If someone takes an insult or attack lying down, they accept it without protesting.
If something takes a lot out of you or takes it out of you, it requires a lot of energy or effort and makes you feel very tired and weak afterwards.
If something takes you out of yourself, it makes you feel better and so you forget all your worries and unhappiness.
If someone tells you to take five or to take ten, they are telling you to have a five or ten minute break from what you are doing.
A takeover is the act of gaining control of a company by buying more of its shares than anyone else.
A takeover is the act of taking control of a country, political party, or movement by force.

Englishsense: A tale is a story, often involving magic or exciting events.
You can refer to an interesting, exciting, or dramatic account of a real event as a tale.
If you survive a dangerous or frightening experience and so are able to tell people about it afterwards, you can say that you lived to tell the tale.
If someone tells tales about you, they tell other people things about you which are untrue or which you wanted to be kept secret.

Englishsense: When you talk, you use spoken language to express your thoughts, ideas, or feelings.
If you talk to someone, you have a conversation with them. You can also say that two people talk.
If you talk to someone, you tell them about the things that are worrying you. You can also say that two people talk.
If you talk on or about something, you make an informal speech telling people what you know or think about it.
Talks are formal discussions intended to produce an agreement, usually between different countries or between employers and employees.
If one group of people talks to another, or if two groups talk, they have formal discussions in order to do a deal or produce an agreement.
When different countries or different sides in a dispute talk, or talk to each other, they discuss their differences in order to try and settle the dispute.
If people are talking about another person or are talking, they are discussing that person.
If someone talks when they are being held by police or soldiers, they reveal important or secret information, usually unwillingly.
If you talk a particular language or talk with a particular accent, you use that language or have that accent when you speak.
If you talk something such as politics or sport, you discuss it.

You can use talk to say what you think of the ideas that someone is expressing. For example, if you say that someone is talking sense, you mean that you think the opinions they are expressing are sensible.
You can say that you are talking a particular thing to draw attention to your topic or to point out a characteristic of what you are discussing.

If you say that something such as an idea or threat is just talk, or all talk, you mean that it does not mean or matter much, because people are exaggerating about it or do not really intend to do anything about it.
You can say talk about before mentioning a particular expression or situation, when you mean that something is a very striking or clear example of that expression or situation.
You can use the expression talking of to introduce a new topic that you want to discuss, and to link it to something that has already been mentioned.

If you tap your fingers or feet, you make a regular pattern of sound by hitting a surface lightly and repeatedly with them, especially while you are listening to music.
If you tap a resource or situation, you make use of it by getting from it something that you need or want.
If someone taps your telephone, they attach a special device to the line so that they can secretly listen to your conversations.
If drinks are on tap, they come from a tap rather than from a bottle.
If something is on tap, you can have as much of it as you want whenever you want.

If you tape one thing to another, you attach it using sticky tape.

If someone or something is on target, they are making good progress and are likely to achieve the result that is wanted.

If you are tasked with doing a particular activity or piece of work, someone in authority asks you to do it.
If you take someone to task, you criticize them or tell them off because of something bad or wrong that they have done.

Englishsense: Taste is one of the five senses that people have. When you have food or drink in your mouth, your sense of taste makes it possible for you to recognize what it is.

The taste of something is the individual quality which it has when you put it in your mouth and which distinguishes it from other things. For example, something may have a sweet, bitter, sour, or salty taste.
If you have a taste of some food or drink, you try a small amount of it in order to see what the flavour is like.
If food or drink tastes of something, it has that particular flavour, which you notice when you eat or drink it.
If you taste some food or drink, you eat or drink a small amount of it in order to try its flavour, for example to see if you like it or not.
If you can taste something that you are eating or drinking, you are aware of its flavour.
If you have a taste of a particular way of life or activity, you have a brief experience of it.
If you taste something such as a way of life or a pleasure, you experience it for a short period of time.
If you have a taste for something, you have a liking or preference for it.

A person’s taste is their choice in the things that they like or buy, for example their clothes, possessions, or music. If you say that someone has good taste, you mean that you approve of their choices. If you say that they have poor taste, you disapprove of their choices.

If you say that something that is said or done is in bad taste or in poor taste, you mean that it is offensive, often because it concerns death or sex and is inappropriate for the situation. If you say that something is in good taste, you mean that it is not offensive and that it is appropriate for the situation.
When a recipe tells you to add a particular spice or other flavouring to taste, it means that you can add as much of that ingredient as you like.

Englishsense: Tax is an amount of money that you have to pay to the government so that it can pay for public services.

Taxation is the system by which a government takes money from people and spends it on things such as education, health, and defence.
Taxation is the amount of money that people have to pay in taxes.

The chopped dried leaves of the plant that tea is made from is referred to as tea.

Some people refer to the main meal that they eat in the early part of the evening as tea.

Teaching is the work that a teacher does in helping students to learn.
The teachings of a particular person, group of people, or religion are all the ideas and principles that they teach.

Englishsense: Tears are the drops of salty liquid that come out of your eyes when you are crying.

A tear in paper, cloth, or another material is a hole that has been made in it.
If something tears your flesh or skin, it cuts it badly.
If you tear one of your muscles or ligaments, or if it tears, you injure it by accidentally moving it in the wrong way.
To tear something from somewhere means to remove it roughly and violently.
If a person or animal tears at something, they pull it violently and try to break it into pieces.

If you say that a place is torn by particular events, you mean that unpleasant events which cause suffering and division among people are happening there.

If you refer to someone as a tease, you mean that they pretend to offer someone what they want, especially sex, but then do not give it to them.

Technology refers to methods, systems, and devices which are the result of scientific knowledge being used for practical purposes.

You say one thing led to another when you are explaining how something happened, but you do not really want to give the details or you think people will be able to imagine the details.
If you do your own thing, you live, act, or behave in the way you want to, without paying attention to convention or depending on other people.
If something is a thing of the past, it no longer exists or happens, or is being replaced by something new.
If you say that someone is seeing or hearing things, you mean that they believe they are seeing or hearing something that is not really there.
You can say there is no such thing as something to emphasize that it does not exist or is not possible.

You say the thing is to introduce an explanation, comment, or opinion, that relates to something that has just been said. The thing is is often used to identify a problem relating to what has just been said.
If you say that something is just the thing or is the very thing, you are emphasizing that it is exactly what is wanted or needed.
If you say that a person knows a thing or two about something or could teach someone a thing or two about it, you mean that they know a lot about it or are good at it.

Chinesesense: 认为，以为(人或物具有某特点或用途)；
(用来引出例子或进一步解释)考虑,想到(某方面、某主题)；
(用于问句，表示生气、震惊)认为，以为；
想来，想想看(用于评论过去所做或经历过的事情现在看来不可思议、愚蠢或令人震惊)；
本来以为，原以为(用于批评别人该做某事而未做)；
谁都会以为/你会认为(用于对他人的行为表示惊讶或不满)；
(表示突然记起或意识到某事)想起来了，想想看；
我想，我觉得(用于委婉地解释等)；
我认为，我想(用于会话或讲话中，使语气稍显婉转)；
你想一想，想象一下(表示激动、着迷或震惊，同时希望谈话对方也有同感)；
重新考虑，再三斟酌(常指最终改变主意)；
认为…没什么了不起;觉得…很容易;认为…无所谓；
对…不在意;不觉得…奇怪(或重要)；
Englishsense: If you think that something is the case, you have the opinion that it is the case.
If you say that you think that something is true or will happen, you mean that you have the impression that it is true or will happen, although you are not certain of the facts.
If you think in a particular way, you have those general opinions or attitudes.
When you think about ideas or problems, you make a mental effort to consider them.
If you think in a particular way, you consider things, solve problems, or make decisions in this way, for example because of your job or your background.
If you think of something, it comes into your mind or you remember it.
If you think of an idea, you make a mental effort and use your imagination and intelligence to create it or develop it.
If you are thinking something at a particular moment, you have words or ideas in your mind without saying them out loud.
If you think of someone or something as having a particular quality or purpose, you regard them as having this quality or purpose.
If you think a lot of someone or something, you admire them very much or think they are very good.
If you think of someone, you show consideration for them and pay attention to their needs.
If you are thinking of taking a particular course of action, you are considering it as a possible course of action.
You can say that you are thinking of a particular aspect or subject, in order to introduce an example or explain more exactly what you are talking about.
You use think in questions where you are expressing your anger or shock at someone’s behaviour.
You use think when you are commenting on something which you did or experienced in the past and which now seems surprising, foolish, or shocking to you.
You can use think in expressions such as you would think or I would have thought when you are criticizing someone because they ought to or could be expected to do something, but have not done it.
You can use think in expressions such as anyone would think and you would think to express your surprise or disapproval at the way someone is behaving.
You use expressions such as come to think of it, when you think about it, or thinking about it, when you mention something that you have suddenly remembered or realized.
You use ’ I think ’ as a way of being polite when you are explaining or suggesting to someone what you want to do, or when you are accepting or refusing an offer.
You use ’ I think ’ in conversations or speeches to make your statements and opinions sound less forceful, rude, or direct.
You say just think when you feel excited, fascinated, or shocked by something, and you want the person to whom you are talking to feel the same.
If you think again about an action or decision, you consider it very carefully, often with the result that you change your mind and decide to do things differently.

If you think nothing of doing something that other people might consider difficult, strange, or wrong, you consider it to be easy or normal, and you do it often or would be quite willing to do it. [V inflects]
If something happens and you think nothing of it, you do not pay much attention to it or think of it as strange or important, although later you realize that it is.
A thinker is a person who spends a lot of time thinking deeply about important things, especially someone who is famous for thinking of new or interesting ideas.
The general ideas or opinions of a person or group can be referred to as their thinking.
Thinking is the activity of using your brain by considering a problem or possibility or creating an idea.
If you describe someone as a thinking man or woman, you mean that they are intelligent and take an interest in important events and issues, and you approve of this.

Chinesesense: 三等学位(英国大学颁发的最低级荣誉学位)；
Englishsense: The third item in a series is the one that you count as number three.
A third is one of three equal parts of something.
You say third when you want to make a third point or give a third reason for something.
A third is the lowest honours degree that can be obtained from a British university.
Thirteen is the number 13.

Chinesesense: 三十多，三十几(指 30 至 39 之间的数字)；
三十年代(指 1930 年至 1939 年)；
Englishsense: Thirty is the number 30.

When you talk about the thirties, you are referring to numbers between 30 and 39. For example, if you are in your thirties, you are aged between 30 and 39. If the temperature is in the thirties, the temperature is between 30 and 39 degrees.
The thirties is the decade between 1930 and 1939.

Chinesesense: (指代先前提及的人或物)这，这个；
(引出将要谈论的人或物)下面(这个)，以下；
这一点(指前一句或几句话中提到的观点或情况)；
(叙述时引出新出现的人或物)这个，一个；
这个，这位(尤指所触碰或指向的离自己较近的人或物，有两个以上时，用于指最近的一个)；
这个，这(指代正在发生或刚刚发生的与自己有关的一般情况、活动或事件)；
这，该，此(指当前所处地点或时间)；
本，今，这个，下一个(指接下来将要发生某事的特定时间)；
这么，这样(用于用手比划大小、形状时)；
这么，这样(用于说明自己知道或能告知的内容)；
(用于电话、广播或电视中，表明身份或所代表的机构)我是，这里是；
这个(指说话、写作时的媒介)；
各种各样的东西;这样那样；
Englishsense: You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.
You use this to introduce someone or something that you are going to talk about.
You use this to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
In spoken English, people use this to introduce a person or thing into a story.
You use this to refer to a person or thing that is near you, especially when you touch them or point to them. When there are two or more people or things near you, this refers to the nearest one.
You use this when you refer to a general situation, activity, or event which is happening or has just happened and which you feel involved in.
You use this when you refer to the place you are in now or to the present time.
You use this to refer to the next occurrence in the future of a particular day, month, season, or festival.
You use this when you are indicating the size or shape of something with your hands.
You use this when you are going to specify how much you know or how much you can tell someone.
If you say this is it, you are agreeing with what someone else has just said.
You use this in order to say who you are or what organization you are representing, when you are speaking on the telephone, radio, or television.
You use this to refer to the medium of communication that you are using at the time of speaking or writing.
If you say that you are doing or talking about this and that, or this, that, and the other you mean that you are doing or talking about a variety of things that you do not want to specify.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (行为、活动)详细的，全面的，彻底的；
完全的，绝对的(用来强调程度)；
Englishsense: A thorough action or activity is one that is done very carefully and in a detailed way so that nothing is forgotten.
Someone who is thorough is always very careful in their work, so that nothing is forgotten.
Thorough is used to emphasize the great degree or extent of something.

Chinesesense: (指代已经提及的人或物)那些；
那些(尤用于指示或指向在时间、空间上离自己稍远的人或物)；
(用来对已经提及的事物作补充说明)；
(用于认为谈话对象知道所谈事物或确认双方所想为相同的人或事物时)；
Englishsense: You use those to refer to people or things which have already been mentioned.
You use those when you are referring to people or things that are a distance away from you in position or time, especially when you indicate or point to them.
You use those to refer to someone or something when you are going to give details or information about them.
You use those to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
You use those to mean ’people’.
You use those when you refer to things that you expect the person you are talking to to know about or when you are checking that you are both thinking of the same people or things.

Chinesesense: 你，汝，尔(旧用词，现亦用于诗歌或宗教类语境，用作主语)；
Englishsense: Thou is an old-fashioned, poetic, or religious word for ’you’ when you are talking to only one person. It is used as the subject of a verb.

You use though to introduce a statement in a subordinate clause which contrasts with the statement in the main clause. You often use though to introduce a fact which you regard as less important than the fact in the main clause.
You use though to introduce a subordinate clause which gives some information that is relevant to the main clause and weakens the force of what it is saying.
You use though to indicate that the information in a clause contrasts with or modifies information given in a previous sentence or sentences.
You can say though I say so myself or even though I say it myself when you are praising yourself or something you have done, but do not want to sound too proud.

Chinesesense: 关心，善意，帮助(尤用于感谢或表达钦佩之情)；
(宗教、哲学、科学、政党等的)思想体系，观念体系；
Englishsense: A thought is an idea that you have in your mind.
A person’s thoughts are their mind, or all the ideas in their mind when they are concentrating on one particular thing.
A person’s thoughts are their opinions on a particular subject.
Thought is the activity of thinking, especially deeply, carefully, or logically.
A thought is an intention, hope, or reason for doing something.
A thought is an act of kindness or an offer of help; used especially when you are thanking someone, or expressing admiration of someone.
Thought is the group of ideas and beliefs which belongs, for example, to a particular religion, philosophy, science, or political party.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 沉思的;默想的;认真思考的；
体贴入微的;考虑周到的；
(书籍、电影、讲话等)严肃的，思想性强的；
Englishsense: If you are thoughtful, you are quiet and serious because you are thinking about something.
If you describe someone as thoughtful, you approve of them because they remember what other people want, need, or feel, and try not to upset them.
If you describe something such as a book, film, or speech as thoughtful, you mean that it is serious and well thought out.
A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.
If you refer to thousands of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

Chinesesense: 使(细长的物体)穿过;使穿进；
(活动中断后)继续下去/(经历失败、霉运后)恢复生机；
Englishsense: Thread or a thread is a long very thin piece of a material such as cotton, nylon, or silk, especially one that is used in sewing.
The thread of an argument, a story, or a situation is an aspect of it that connects all the different parts together.
A thread of something such as liquid, light, or colour is a long thin line or piece of it.
You can refer to clothes as threads.
The thread on a screw, or on something such as a lid or a pipe, is the raised spiral line of metal or plastic around it which allows it to be fixed in place by twisting.
If you thread your way through a group of people or things, or thread through it, you move through it carefully or slowly, changing direction frequently as you move.
If you thread a long thin object through something, you pass it through one or more holes or narrow spaces.
If you thread small objects such as beads onto a string or thread, you join them together by pushing the string through them.
When you thread a needle, you put a piece of thread through the hole in the top of the needle in order to sew with it.
If you say that something is hanging by a thread, you mean that it is in a very uncertain state and is unlikely to survive or succeed.
If you pick up the threads of an activity, you start it again after an interruption. If you pick up the threads of your life, you become more active again after a period of failure or bad luck.

Chinesesense: 构成威胁的人(或事物);祸根；
Englishsense: A threat to a person or thing is a danger that something unpleasant might happen to them. A threat is also the cause of this danger.
A threat is a statement by someone that they will do something unpleasant, especially if you do not do what they want.
If a person or thing is under threat, there is a danger that something unpleasant might be done to them, or that they might cease to exist.
If a person threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.
If something or someone threatens a person or thing, they are likely to harm that person or thing.
If something unpleasant threatens to happen, it seems likely to happen.
Three is the number 3.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (照片、图像、电影)三维的，有立体感的(缩略形式为 3-D)；
(虚构的人物)栩栩如生的，逼真的，鲜活的；
(艺术、设计)立体的(缩略形式为 3-D)；
Englishsense: A three-dimensional object is solid rather than flat, because it can be measured in three different directions, usually the height, length, and width. The abbreviation 3-D can also be used.
A three-dimensional picture, image, or film looks as though it is deep or solid rather than flat. The abbreviation 3-D can also be used.
If you describe fictional characters as three-dimensional you mean that they seem real and natural.
Three-dimensional art or design is produced by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay, or other materials. The abbreviation 3-D can also be used.
Three-quarters is an amount that is three out of four equal parts of something.

Chinesesense: (某事发生或改变的)界限，阈，起始点；
在…开端;将要经历;面临着；
Englishsense: The threshold of a building or room is the floor in the doorway, or the doorway itself.
A threshold is an amount, level, or limit on a scale. When the threshold is reached, something else happens or changes.
If you are on the threshold of something exciting or new, you are about to experience it.

Chinesesense: (突然而强烈的)激动，狂喜，恐惧；
使狂喜;使激动;使极度兴奋；
Englishsense: If something gives you a thrill, it gives you a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.
If something thrills you, or if you thrill at it, it gives you a feeling of great pleasure and excitement.
If you refer to thrills and spills, you are referring to an experience which is exciting and full of surprises.
A thriller is a book, film, or play that tells an exciting fictional story about something such as criminal activities or spying.

Chinesesense: 欣欣向荣;茁壮成长;兴旺发达；
(尤指在别人觉得困难的时候)以…为乐，可以出色应对；
Englishsense: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong.
If you say that someone thrives on a particular situation, you mean that they enjoy it or that they can deal with it very well, especially when other people find it unpleasant or difficult.

Chinesesense: 向…反复灌输;向…不断强调;迫使…接受；
Englishsense: Your throat is the back of your mouth and the top part of the tubes that go down into your stomach and your lungs.
Your throat is the front part of your neck.
If you clear your throat, you cough once in order to make it easier to speak or to attract people’s attention.
If you ram something down someone’s throat or force it down their throat, you keep mentioning a situation or idea in order to make them accept it or believe it.
If two people or groups are at each other’s throats, they are quarrelling or fighting violently with each other.
If something sticks in your throat, you find it unacceptable.
A throne is a decorative chair used by a king, queen, or emperor on important official occasions.
You can talk about the throne as a way of referring to the position of being king, queen, or emperor.

Chinesesense: 穿过,通过(洞、口子、管道等);从…的一端到另一端；
穿过，通过(城市、地区、国家);遍及；
(感觉、态度、品质)遍布，遍及，贯穿；
完成的;结束的;(与…)关系了结的；
(提议、观点)获得通过，得到批准；
通过(考试);(在比赛中)胜出；
Englishsense: To move through something such as a hole, opening, or pipe means to move directly from one side or end of it to the other.
To cut through something means to cut it in two pieces or to make a hole in it.
To go through a town, area, or country means to travel across it or in it.
If you move through a group of things or a mass of something, it is on either side of you or all around you.
To get through a barrier or obstacle means to get from one side of it to the other.
If a driver goes through a red light, they keep driving even though they should stop.
If something goes into an object and comes out of the other side, you can say that it passes through the object.
To go through a system means to move around it or to pass from one end of it to the other.
If you see, hear, or feel something through a particular thing, that thing is between you and the thing you can see, hear, or feel.
If something such as a feeling, attitude, or quality, happens through an area, organization, or a person’s body, it happens everywhere in it or affects all of it.
If something happens or exists through a period of time, it happens or exists from the beginning until the end.
If something happens from a particular period of time through another, it starts at the first period and continues until the end of the second period.
If you go through a particular experience or event, you experience it, and if you behave in a particular way through it, you behave in that way while it is happening.
If you are through with something or if it is through, you have finished doing it and will never do it again. If you are through with someone, you do not want to have anything to do with them again.
You use through in expressions such as half-way through and all the way through to indicate to what extent an action or task is completed.
If something happens because of something else, you can say that it happens through it.
You use through when stating the means by which a particular thing is achieved.
If you do something through someone else, they take the necessary action for you.
If something such as a proposal or idea goes through, it is accepted by people in authority and is made legal or official.
If someone gets through an examination or a round of a competition, they succeed or win.
When you get through while making a telephone call, the call is connected and you can speak to the person you are phoning.
If you look or go through a lot of things, you look at them or deal with them one after the other.
If you read through something, you read it from beginning to end.
A through train goes directly to a particular place, so that the people who want to go there do not have to change trains.
If you say that someone or something is wet through, you are emphasizing how wet they are.
Through and through means completely and to the greatest extent possible.

Chinesesense: 自始至终;从头到尾;贯穿；
Englishsense: If you say that something happens throughout a particular period of time, you mean that it happens during the whole of that period.
If you say that something happens or exists throughout a place, you mean that it happens or exists in all parts of that place.

Chinesesense: 急伸，猛动(身体或某部位)；
使处境不利;使进展不顺；
投下，洒下，抛下(光线或影子)；
飞快看一眼;迅速笑一下；
Englishsense: When you throw an object that you are holding, you move your hand or arm quickly and let go of the object, so that it moves through the air.
If you throw your body or part of your body into a particular position or place, you move it there suddenly and with a lot of force.
If you throw something into a particular place or position, you put it there in a quick and careless way.
To throw someone into a particular place or position means to force them roughly into that place or position.
If you say that someone is thrown into prison, you mean that they are put there by the authorities, especially if this seems unfair or cruel.
If a horse throws its rider, it makes him or her fall off, by suddenly jumping or moving violently.
If a person or thing is thrown into an unpleasant situation or state, something causes them to be in that situation or state.
If something throws light or a shadow on a surface, it causes that surface to have light or a shadow on it.
If something throws doubt on a person or thing, it causes people to doubt or suspect them.
If you throw a look or smile at someone or something, you look or smile at them quickly and suddenly.
If you throw yourself, your energy, or your money into a particular job or activity, you become involved in it very actively or enthusiastically.
If you throw a fit or a tantrum, you suddenly start to behave in an uncontrolled way.
If something such as a remark or an experience throws you, it surprises you or confuses you because it is unexpected.
If you throw a punch, you punch someone.
When someone throws a party, they organize one, usually in their own home.
When someone throws a switch, they turn it on or off.
In sports, if a player throws a game or contest, they lose it as a result of a deliberate action or intention.
A throw is a light rug, blanket, or cover for a sofa or bed.
If things cost a particular amount of money a throw, they cost that amount each.
If someone throws themselves at you, they make it very obvious that they want to begin a relationship with you, by behaving as though they are sexually attracted to you.

Chinesesense: (车辆等的)推力，反压力，侧向压力；
(活动、思想的)要点，主要内容，要旨；
Englishsense: If you thrust something or someone somewhere, you push or move them there quickly with a lot of force.
If you thrust your way somewhere, you move there, pushing between people or things which are in your way.
If something thrusts up or out of something else, it sticks up or sticks out in a noticeable way.
Thrust is the power or force that is required to make a vehicle move in a particular direction.
The thrust of an activity or of an idea is the main or essential things it expresses.
You can refer to a violent person or criminal as a thug.

Chinesesense: (站在路边，伸出手，拇指向上)请求搭便车，拦车；
Englishsense: Your thumb is the short thick part on the side of your hand next to your four fingers.
The thumb of a glove is the part which a person’s thumb fits into.
If you thumb a lift or thumb a ride, you stand by the side of the road holding out your thumb until a driver stops and gives you a lift.

If you say that someone or something sticks out like a sore thumb or stands out like a sore thumb, you are emphasizing that they are very noticeable, usually because they are unusual or inappropriate.
If you say that someone is twiddling their thumbs, you mean that they do not have anything to do and are waiting for something to happen.
If you are under someone’s thumb, you are under their control, or very heavily influenced by them.
Thunder is the loud noise that you hear from the sky after a flash of lightning, especially during a storm.
When it thunders, a loud noise comes from the sky after a flash of lightning.
The thunder of something that is moving or making a sound is the loud deep noise it makes.
If something or someone thunders somewhere, they move there quickly and with a lot of noise.
If something thunders, it makes a very loud noise, usually continuously.
If you thunder something, you say it loudly and forcefully, especially because you are angry.
If you steal someone’s thunder, you get the attention or praise that they thought they would get, usually by saying or doing what they had intended to say or do.
You use thus to show that what you are about to mention is the result or consequence of something else that you have just mentioned.
If you say that something is thus or happens thus you mean that it is, or happens, as you have just described or as you are just about to describe.
If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.
Thyme is a type of herb used in cooking.

Chinesesense: (某人的思想、愿望或情感使其)做出…举动;有…的行为；
Englishsense: A tick is a written mark like a V: ✓. It is used to show that something is correct or has been selected or dealt with.
If you tick something that is written on a piece of paper, you put a tick next to it.
When a clock or watch ticks, it makes a regular series of short sounds as it works.
The tick of a clock or watch is the series of short sounds it makes when it is working, or one of those sounds.
You can use tick to refer to a very short period of time.
If you talk about what makes someone tick, you are talking about the beliefs, wishes, and feelings that make them behave in the way that they do.
A tick is a small creature which lives on the bodies of people or animals and uses their blood as food.

Chinesesense: (剧院、运动场、表演等的)入场券，门票，票；
(交通)罚款通知单，违章通知单；
(竞选时所代表的)政党;(竞选时所支持的)纲领，政见；
Englishsense: A ticket is a small, official piece of paper or card which shows that you have paid to enter a place such as a theatre or a sports ground, or shows that you have paid for a journey.
A ticket is an official piece of paper which orders you to pay a fine or to appear in court because you have committed a driving or parking offence.
A ticket for a game of chance such as a raffle or a lottery is a piece of paper with a number on it. If the number on your ticket matches the number chosen, you win a prize.
The particular ticket on which a person fights an election is the party they represent or the policies they support.
A ticket is the list of candidates who are representing a particular political party or group in an election.
If you say that something is just the ticket, you mean that it is exactly what is needed.
When you tickle someone, you move your fingers lightly over a sensitive part of their body, often in order to make them laugh.
If something tickles you or tickles, it causes an irritating feeling by lightly touching a part of your body.
If a fact or a situation tickles you, it amuses you or gives you pleasure.
If you are tickled pink, you are extremely pleased about something.
Tidal means relating to or produced by tides.
The tide is the regular change in the level of the sea on the shore.
A tide is a current in the sea that is caused by the regular and continuous movement of large areas of water towards and away from the shore.
The tide of opinion, for example, is what the majority of people think at a particular time.
People sometimes refer to events or forces that are difficult or impossible to control as the tide of history, for example.
You can talk about a tide of something, especially something which is unpleasant, when there is a large and increasing amount of it.

Chinesesense: 打(结或蝴蝶结)；将…打成(结或蝴蝶结)；
使紧密相连；使关系密切；
Englishsense: If you tie two things together or tie them, you fasten them together with a knot.
If you tie something or someone in a particular place or position, you put them there and fasten them using rope or string.
If you tie a piece of string or cloth around something or tie something with a piece of string or cloth, you put the piece of string or cloth around it and fasten the ends together.
If you tie a knot or bow in something or tie something in a knot or bow, you fasten the ends together.
When you tie something or when something ties, you close or fasten it using a bow or knot.
A tie is a long narrow piece of cloth that is worn round the neck under a shirt collar and tied in a knot at the front. Ties are worn mainly by men.
If one thing is tied to another or two things are tied, the two things have a close connection or link.
If you are tied to a particular place or situation, you are forced to accept it and cannot change it.
Ties are the connections you have with people or a place.
Railroad ties are large heavy beams that support the rails of a railway track.
If two people tie in a competition or game or if they tie with each other, they have the same number of points or the same degree of success.
In sport, a tie is a match that is part of a competition. The losers leave the competition and the winners go on to the next round.
A tier is a row or layer of something that has other layers above or below it.
A tier is a level in an organization or system.
A tiger is a large fierce animal belonging to the cat family. Tigers are orange with black stripes.

Chinesesense: 紧紧地;密不透风地;滴水不漏地；
紧密的;密集的;装得满满的；
