小气的;抠门儿的;吝啬的；
Englishsense: Tight clothes or shoes are rather small and fit closely to your body.
If you hold someone or something tight, you hold them firmly and securely.
Tight controls or rules are very strict.
Something that is shut tight is shut very firmly.
Skin, cloth, or string that is tight is stretched or pulled so that it is smooth or straight.
Tight is used to describe a group of things or an amount of something that is closely packed together.
If a part of your body is tight, it feels rather uncomfortable and painful, for example because you are ill, anxious, or angry.
A tight group of people is one whose members are closely linked by beliefs, feelings, or interests.
A tight bend or corner is one that changes direction very quickly so that you cannot see very far round it.
A tight schedule or budget allows very little time or money for unexpected events or expenses.
A tight contest is one where none of the competitors has a clear advantage or looks likely to win, so that it is difficult to say who the winner will be.
If you say that someone is tight, you disapprove of them because they are unwilling to spend their money.
If you are in a tight corner or in a tight spot, you are in a difficult situation.
You can say ’ sleep tight ’ to someone when they are going to bed as an affectionate way of saying that you hope they will sleep well.

Chinesesense: 拧紧，旋紧(螺钉、螺丝帽等)；
(身体局部)变僵硬，产生憋闷感，产生阻塞感；
使(规定、政策、制度)更加严格；使更加有效；
Englishsense: If you tighten your grip on something, or if your grip tightens, you hold the thing more firmly or securely.
If you tighten a rope or chain, or if it tightens, it is stretched or pulled hard until it is straight.
If a government or organization tightens its grip on a group of people or an activity, or if its grip tightens, it begins to have more control over it.
When you tighten a screw, nut, or other device, you turn it or move it so that it is more firmly in place or holds something more firmly.
If a part of your body tightens, the muscles in it become tense and stiff, for example because you are angry or afraid.
If someone in authority tightens a rule, a policy, or a system, they make it stricter or more efficient.

Chinesesense: 纵情玩乐，花天酒地(到深夜)；
Englishsense: Tiles are flat, square pieces of baked clay, carpet, cork, or other substance, which are fixed as a covering onto a floor or wall.
Tiles are flat pieces of baked clay which are used for covering roofs.
When someone tiles a surface such as a roof or floor, they cover it with tiles.
If someone has a night on the tiles or is out on the tiles, they go out in the evening, for example to a bar or a club, and do not return home until very late.

Chinesesense: (常于口语与非正式书面语中代替 until)；
(商店等处的)现金出纳机，收银机；
(收银机中的)钱柜，放钱的抽屉；
Englishsense: In spoken English and informal written English, till is often used instead of until.
In a shop or other place of business, a till is a counter or cash register where money is kept, and where customers pay for what they have bought.
A till is the drawer of a cash register, in which the money is kept.
When people till land, they prepare the earth and work on it in order to grow crops.

Chinesesense: (略微)倾侧(身体部位)，仰头，把头歪向一边；
Englishsense: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.
If you tilt part of your body, usually your head, you move it slightly upwards or to one side.
The tilt of something is the fact that it tilts or slopes, or the angle at which it tilts or slopes.
If a person or thing tilts towards a particular opinion or if something tilts them towards it, they change slightly so that they become more in agreement with that opinion or position.
If there is a tilt towards a particular opinion or position, that opinion or position is favoured or begins to be favoured.
A tilt at something is an attempt to win or obtain it.
To move full tilt or at full tilt means to move with as much speed, energy, or force as possible.
Timber is wood that is used for building houses and making furniture. You can also refer to trees that are grown for this purpose as timber.
The timbers of a ship or house are the large pieces of wood that have been used to build it.

Chinesesense: (用来做某事或某事发生的)时间；
(某事发生的)一段(或特定)时间；
给…确定时间;为…安排时间；
在…出生以前；在…有记忆前；
不喜欢/喜欢;不赞成/赞成；
在业余时间;在空闲时间；
有史以来最…的;前所未有的;空前的；
迟早的事;只是时间问题；
Englishsense: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.
You use time to ask or talk about a specific point in the day, which can be stated in hours and minutes and is shown on clocks.
The time when something happens is the point in the day when it happens or is supposed to happen.
You use time to refer to the system of expressing time and counting hours that is used in a particular part of the world.
You use time to refer to the period that you spend doing something or when something has been happening.
If you say that something has been happening for a time, you mean that it has been happening for a fairly long period of time.

You use time to refer to a period of time or a point in time, when you are describing what is happening then. For example, if something happened at a particular time, that is when it happened. If it happens at all times, it always happens.
You use time or times to talk about a particular period in history or in your life.

You can use the times to refer to the present time and to modern fashions, tastes, and developments. For example, if you say that someone keeps up with the times, you mean they are fashionable or aware of modern developments. If you say they are behind the times, you mean they are unfashionable or not aware of them.
When you describe the time that you had on a particular occasion or during a particular part of your life, you are describing the sort of experience that you had then.
Your time is the amount of time that you have to live, or to do a particular thing.
If you say it is time for something, time to do something, or time you did something, you mean that this thing ought to happen or be done now.
When you talk about a time when something happens, you are referring to a specific occasion when it happens.
You use time after numbers to say how often something happens.
You use times after numbers when comparing one thing to another and saying, for example, how much bigger, smaller, better, or worse it is.
You use times in arithmetic to link numbers or amounts that are multiplied together to reach a total.
Someone’s time in a race is the amount of time it takes them to finish the race.
The time of a piece of music is the number of beats that the piece has in each bar.
If you time something for a particular time, you plan or decide to do it or cause it to happen at this time.
If you time an action or activity, you measure how long someone takes to do it or how long it lasts.
If you say it is about time that something was done, you are saying in an emphatic way that it should happen or be done now, and really should have happened or been done sooner.
If you do something ahead of time, you do it before a particular event or before you need to, in order to be well prepared.
If someone is ahead of their time or before their time, they have new ideas a long time before other people start to think in the same way.
If something happens or is done all the time, it happens or is done continually.
You say at a time after an amount to say how many things or how much of something is involved in one action, place, or group.
If something could happen at any time, it is possible that it will happen very soon, though nobody can predict exactly when.
You say at the best of times when you are making a negative or critical comment to emphasize that it is true even when the circumstances are as favourable as possible.
If you say that something was the case at one time, you mean that it was the case during a particular period in the past.
If two or more things exist, happen, or are true at the same time, they exist, happen, or are true together although they seem to contradict each other.
At the same time is used to introduce a statement that slightly changes or contradicts the previous statement.
You use at times to say that something happens or is true on some occasions or at some moments.
If you say that something was before your time, you mean that it happened or existed before you were born or before you were able to know about it or remember it.
If someone has reached a particular stage in life before their time, they have reached it at a younger age than is normal.
If you say not before time after a statement has been made about something that has been done, you are saying in an emphatic way that you think it should have been done sooner.
If you call time on something, you end it.
Someone who is doing time is in prison.
If you say that something will be the case for all time, you mean that it will always be the case.
If something is the case or will happen for the time being, it is the case or will happen now, but only until something else becomes possible or happens.
If you do something from time to time, you do it occasionally but not regularly.
If you say that something is the case half the time you mean that it often is the case.

If you say that you have no time for a person or thing, you mean you do not like them or approve of them, and if you say that you have a lot of time for a person or thing, you mean you like them or approve of them very much.
If you say that it is high time that something happened or was done, you are saying in an emphatic way that it should happen or be done now, and really should have happened or been done sooner.
If you are in time for a particular event, you are not too late for it.
If you say that something will happen in time or given time, you mean that it will happen eventually, when a lot of time has passed.

If you are playing, singing, or dancing in time with a piece of music, you are following the rhythm and speed of the music correctly. If you are out of time with it, you are not following the rhythm and speed of the music correctly.
If you say that something will happen, for example, in a week ’s time or in two years ’ time, you mean that it will happen a week from now or two years from now.
If you arrive somewhere in good time, you arrive early so that there is time to spare before a particular event. [PHR after v]
If you tell someone that something will happen in good time or all in good time, you are telling them to be patient because it will happen eventually.
If something happens in no time or in next to no time, it happens almost immediately or very quickly.
If you do something in your own time, you do it at the speed that you choose, rather than allowing anyone to hurry you.
If you do something such as work in your own time in British English, or on your own time in American English, you do it in your free time rather than, for example, at work or school.
If you keep time when playing or singing music, you follow or play the beat, without going too fast or too slowly.
When you talk about how well a watch or clock keeps time, you are talking about how accurately it measures time.
If you make time for a particular activity or person, you arrange to have some free time so that you can do the activity or spend time with the person.
If you say that you made good time on a journey, you mean it did not take you very long compared to the length of time you expected it to take.
If someone is making up for lost time, they are doing something actively and with enthusiasm because they have not had the opportunity to do it before or when they were younger.
If you are marking time, you are doing something that is not particularly useful or interesting while you wait for something more important or interesting to happen.

If you say that something happens or is the case nine times out of ten or ninety-nine times out of a hundred, you mean that it happens on nearly every occasion or is almost always the case. [PHR with cl]

If you say that someone or something is, for example, the best writer of all time, or the most successful film of all time, you mean that they are the best or most successful that there has ever been.
If you are on time, you are not late.
If you say that it is only a matter of time or only a question of time before something happens, you mean that it cannot be avoided and will definitely happen at some future date.
When you refer to our time or our times you are referring to the present period in the history of the world.
If you do something to pass the time you do it because you have some time available and not because you really want to do it.
If you pass the time of day with someone, you have a short friendly conversation with them.
If you play for time, you try to make something happen more slowly, because you do not want it to happen or because you need time to think about what to do if it happens.
If you say that something will take time, you mean that it will take a long time.
If you take your time doing something, you do it quite slowly and do not hurry.
If a child can tell the time, they are able to find out what the time is by looking at a clock or watch.
If something happens time after time, it happens in a similar way on many occasions. [PHR with cl]
If you say that time flies, you mean that it seems to pass very quickly.
If you have the time of your life, you enjoy yourself very much indeed.
If you say there is no time to lose or no time to be lost, you mean you must hurry as fast as you can to do something.
If you say that time will tell whether something is true or correct, you mean that it will not be known until some time in the future whether it is true or correct.
If you waste no time in doing something, you take the opportunity to do it immediately or quickly.

Englishsense: If you describe something as timeless, you mean that it is so good or beautiful that it cannot be affected by changes in society or fashion.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: A timely event happens at a moment when it is useful, effective, or relevant.

Chinesesense: 时间表;时间安排;日程表；
Englishsense: A timetable is a plan of the times when particular events are to take place.

In a school or college, a timetable is a list that shows the times in the week at which particular subjects are taught. You can also refer to the range of subjects that a student learns or the classes that a teacher teaches as their timetable.
A timetable is a list of the times when trains, boats, buses, or aeroplanes are supposed to arrive at or leave from a particular place.
If something is timetabled, it is scheduled to happen or do something at a particular time.
Timing is the skill or action of judging the right moment in a situation or activity at which to do something.
Timing is used to refer to the time at which something happens or is planned to happen, or to the length of time that something takes.
Tin is a soft silvery-white metal.
A tin is a metal container which is filled with food and sealed in order to preserve the food for long periods of time.
A tin is a metal container with a lid in which things such as biscuits, cakes, or tobacco can be kept.
A baking tin is a metal container used for baking things such as cakes and bread in an oven.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: Something or someone that is tiny is extremely small.

Chinesesense: 认定…会(做某事或获得成功)；
(对赛马、比赛结果的)预测，内幕消息；
(事物的)端倪，表面一小部分，冰山一角；
Englishsense: The tip of something long and narrow is the end of it.
If you tip an object or part of your body or if it tips, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.
If you tip something somewhere, you pour it there.
To tip rubbish means to get rid of it by leaving it somewhere.
A tip is a place where rubbish is left.
If you describe a place as a tip, you mean it is very untidy.
If you tip someone such as a waiter in a restaurant, you give them some money in order to thank them for their services.
If you give a tip to someone such as a waiter in a restaurant, you give them some money to thank them for their services.
A tip is a useful piece of advice.

If a person is tipped to do something or is tipped for success at something, experts or journalists believe that they will do that thing or achieve that success. [be V-ed to-inf] [be V-ed for n] [usu passive] [BRIT 英]
Someone’s tip for a race or competition is their advice on its likely result, especially to someone who wants to bet money on the result.
If you say that a problem is the tip of the iceberg, you mean that it is one small part of a much larger problem.
If something tips the scales or tips the balance, it gives someone a slight advantage.
If a comment or question is on the tip of your tongue, you really want to say it or ask it, but you decide not to say it.
If something tires you or if you tire, you feel that you have used a lot of energy and you want to rest or sleep.
If you tire of something, you no longer wish to do it, because you have become bored of it or unhappy with it.
A tire is the same as a tyre.

Chinesesense: (身体部位)显出倦意的，感到疲乏的；
Englishsense: If you are tired, you feel that you want to rest or sleep.
You can describe a part of your body as tired if it looks or feels as if you need to rest it or to sleep.
If you are tired of something, you do not want it to continue because you are bored of it or unhappy with it.
If you describe something as tired, you are critical of it because you have heard it or seen it many times.

Chinesesense: (用于包装易损物品的)薄纸，绵纸；
Englishsense: In animals and plants, tissue consists of cells that are similar to each other in appearance and that have the same function.
Tissue or tissue paper is thin paper that is used for wrapping things that are easily damaged, such as objects made of glass or china.
A tissue is a piece of thin soft paper that you use to blow your nose.
The title of a book, play, film, or piece of music is its name.
When a writer, composer, or artist titles a work, they give it a title.
Publishers and booksellers often refer to books or magazines as titles.
A person’s title is a word such as ’Sir’, ’Lord’, or ’Lady’ that is used in front of their name, or a phrase that is used instead of their name, and indicates that they have a high rank in society.
Someone’s title is a word such as ’Mr’, ’Mrs’, or ’Doctor’, that is used before their own name in order to show their status or profession.
Someone’s title is a name that describes their job or status in an organization.
If a person or team wins a particular title, they win a sports competition that is held regularly. Usually a person keeps a title until someone else defeats them.
Title is the legal ownership of something, especially land or property.

Chinesesense: (表示动作或情感的对象)对，于；
(与某些名词、形容词连用，表示关联)对于，关于；
Englishsense: You use to when indicating the place that someone or something visits, moves towards, or points at.
If you go to an event, you go where it is taking place.
If something is attached to something larger or fixed to it, the two things are joined together.
You use to when indicating the position of something. For example, if something is to your left, it is nearer your left side than your right side.
When you give something to someone, they receive it.
You use to to indicate who or what an action or a feeling is directed towards.
You use to with certain nouns and adjectives to show that a following noun is related to them.
If you say something to someone, you want that person to listen and understand what you are saying.

You use to when indicating someone’s reaction to something or their feelings about a situation or event. For example, if you say that something happens to someone’s surprise you mean that they are surprised when it happens.
You use to when indicating the person whose opinion you are stating.
You use to when indicating what something or someone is becoming, or the state or situation that they are progressing towards.
To can be used as a way of introducing the person or organization you are employed by, when you perform some service for them.
You use to to indicate that something happens until the time or amount mentioned is reached.
You use to when indicating the last thing in a range of things, usually when you are giving two extreme examples of something.
If someone goes from place to place or from job to job, they go to several places, or work in several jobs, and spend only a short time in each one.
If someone moves to and fro, they move repeatedly from one place to another and back again, or from side to side.
You use to when you are stating a time which is less than thirty minutes before an hour. For example, if it is ’five to eight’, it is five minutes before eight o’clock.
You use to when giving ratios and rates.
You use to when indicating that two things happen at the same time. For example, if something is done to music, it is done at the same time as music is being played.
If you say ’ There’s nothing to it ’, ’ There’s not much to it ’, or ’ That’s all there is to it ’, you are emphasizing how simple you think something is.
If you push or shut a door to, you close it but may not shut it completely.

Chinesesense: 深受敬慕的人;最受推崇的人；
Englishsense: Toast is bread which has been cut into slices and made brown and crisp by cooking at a high temperature.
When you toast something such as bread, you cook it at a high temperature so that it becomes brown and crisp. See usage note at: cook
When you drink a toast to someone or something, you drink some wine or another alcoholic drink as a symbolic gesture, in order to show your appreciation of them or to wish them success.
When you toast someone or something, you drink a toast to them.
If someone is the toast of a place, they are very popular and greatly admired there, because they have done something very successfully or well.
If someone is toast, you mean that they are certain to be defeated or destroyed.
Tobacco is dried leaves which people smoke in pipes, cigars, and cigarettes. You can also refer to pipes, cigars, and cigarettes as a whole as tobacco.
Tobacco is the plant from which tobacco is obtained.
You use today to refer to the day on which you are speaking or writing.
You can refer to the present period of history as today.
A toddler is a young child who has only just learned to walk or who still walks unsteadily with small, quick steps.
Your toes are the five movable parts at the end of each foot.
The toe of a shoe or sock is the part that covers the end of your foot.

If you dip your toes into something or dip your toes into the waters of something, you start doing that thing slowly and carefully, because you are not sure whether it will be successful or whether you will like it.
If you say that someone or something keeps you on your toes, you mean that they cause you to remain alert and ready for anything that might happen.
If you toe the line, you behave in the way that people in authority expect you to.
If you tread on someone’s toes, you offend them by criticizing the way that they do something or by interfering in their affairs.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (两人)结婚的，有性关系(或恋爱关系)的；
Englishsense: If people do something together, they do it with each other.
If things are joined together, they are joined with each other so that they touch or form one whole.
If things or people are situated together, they are in the same place and very near to each other.
If a group of people are held or kept together, they are united with each other in some way.
If two people are together, they are married or having a sexual relationship with each other.
If two things happen or are done together, they happen or are done at the same time.
You use together when you are adding two or more amounts or things to each other in order to consider a total amount or effect.
If you say that two things go together, or that one thing goes together with another, you mean that they go well with each other or cannot be separated from each other.
If you describe someone as together, you admire them because they are very confident, organized, and know what they want. [approval] [Informal]
You use together with to mention someone or something else that is also involved in an action or situation.
A toilet is a large bowl with a seat, or a platform with a hole, which is connected to a water system and which you use when you want to get rid of urine or faeces from your body.
A toilet is a room in a house or public building that contains a toilet.
You can say that someone goes to the toilet to mean that they get rid of waste substances from their body, especially when you want to avoid using words that you think may offend people.

Chinesesense: 同样地;由于同样的原因；
Englishsense: You use token to describe things or actions which are small or unimportant but are meant to show particular intentions or feelings which may not be sincere.
A token is a piece of paper or card that can be exchanged for goods, either in a particular shop or as part of a special offer.
A token is a round flat piece of metal or plastic that is sometimes used instead of money.
If you give something to a person or do something for them as a token of your feelings, you give it or do it as a way of expressing those feelings.
You use by the same token to introduce a statement that you think is true for the same reasons that were given for a previous statement.
Tolerance is the quality of allowing other people to say and do as they like, even if you do not agree or approve of it.
Tolerance is the ability to bear something painful or unpleasant.
If someone or something has a tolerance to a substance, they are exposed to it so often that it does not have very much effect on them.

Englishsense: The tone of a sound is its particular quality.
Someone’s tone is a quality in their voice which shows what they are feeling or thinking.
The tone of a speech or piece of writing is its style and the opinions or ideas expressed in it.
The tone of a place or an event is its general atmosphere.
The tone of someone’s body, especially their muscles, is its degree of firmness and strength.
Something that tones your body makes it firm and strong.
A tone is one of the lighter, darker, or brighter shades of the same colour.
If one thing tones with another, the two things look nice together because their colours are similar in quality or brightness.
A tone is one of the sounds that you hear when you are using a telephone, for example the sound that tells you that a number is engaged or busy, or no longer exists.
A tone is a difference in pitch between two musical notes equal to two semitones.
If you say that something lowers the tone of a place or event, you mean that it is not appropriate and makes the place or event seem less respectable.
If you tone down a colour or a flavour, you make it less bright or strong.

Englishsense: Your tongue is the soft movable part inside your mouth which you use for tasting, eating, and speaking.
You can use tongue to refer to the kind of things that a person says.
A tongue is a language.
Tongue is the cooked tongue of an ox or sheep. It is usually eaten cold.
The tongue of a shoe or boot is the piece of leather which is underneath the laces.
A tongue of something such as fire or land is a long thin piece of it.
A tongue-in-cheek remark or attitude is not serious, although it may seem to be.
If you hold your tongue, you do not say anything even though you might want to or be expected to, because it is the wrong time to say it.
If you say that you can not get your tongue round or around a particular word or phrase, you mean that you find it very difficult to pronounce.
If you describe something you said as a slip of the tongue, you mean that you said it by mistake.
Tonight is used to refer to the evening of today or the night that follows today.

Englishsense: You use too after mentioning another person, thing, or aspect that a previous statement applies to or includes.

You use too at the end of a sentence to emphasize an opinion that you have added after a statement made by you or by another person.

You use too with a negative to make what you are saying sound less forceful or more polite or cautious.

Englishsense: A tool is any instrument or simple piece of equipment that you hold in your hands and use to do a particular kind of work. For example, spades, hammers, and knives are all tools.
You can refer to anything that you use for a particular purpose as a particular type of tool.

If you describe someone as a tool of a particular person, group, or system, you mean that they are controlled and used by that person, group, or system, especially to do unpleasant or dishonest things.
If you say that workers down tools, you mean that they stop working suddenly in order to strike or to make a protest of some kind.
The tools of your trade or the tools of the trade are the skills, instruments, and other equipment that you need in order to do your job properly.

Chinesesense: 齿状物;(梳子、锯、齿轮、拉链等的)齿；

Englishsense: Your teeth are the hard white objects in your mouth, which you use for biting and chewing.
The teeth of something such as a comb, saw, cog, or zip are the parts that stick out in a row on its edge.
If you say that something such as an official group or a law has teeth, you mean that it has power and is able to be effective.
Someone who is armed to the teeth is armed with a lot of weapons or with very effective weapons.

If you say that someone cut their teeth doing a particular thing, at a particular time, or in a particular place, you mean that that is how, when, or where they began their career and learned some of their skills.
If you say that something sets your teeth on edge, you mean that you find it extremely unpleasant or irritating.
If you fight tooth and nail to do something, you do everything you can in order to achieve it. If you fight something tooth and nail, you do everything you can in order to prevent it.
If you describe a task or activity as something you can get your teeth into, you mean that you like it because it is interesting, complex, and makes you think hard.
If you do something in the teeth of a difficulty or danger, you do it in spite of the difficulty or danger.
If you say that someone is lying through their teeth, you are emphasizing that they are telling lies.
If you describe someone as long in the tooth, you are saying unkindly or humorously that they are old or getting old.
If you have a sweet tooth, you like sweet food very much.

Chinesesense: 最高的;最上面的;最上层的；
最高层;最高地位(或职位)；
出人头地;拔得头筹;占得上风；

Englishsense: The top of something is its highest point or part.
The top thing or layer in a series of things or layers is the highest one.
The top of something such as a bottle, jar, or tube is a cap, lid, or other device that fits or screws onto one end of it.
The top of a street, garden, bed, or table is the end of it that is farthest away from where you usually enter it or from where you are.
A top is a piece of clothing that you wear on the upper half of your body, for example a blouse or shirt.
You can use top to indicate that something or someone is at the highest level of a scale or measurement.
You can use top to say that you think something is excellent.
The top of an organization or career structure is the highest level in it.
You can use top to describe the most important or famous people or things in a particular area of work or activity.
If someone is at the top of a table or league or is the top of the table or league, their performance is better than that of all the other people involved.
You can use top to indicate that something is the first thing you are going to do, because you consider it to be the most important.
You can use top to indicate that someone does a particular thing more times than anyone else or that something is chosen more times than anything else.
To top a list means to be mentioned or chosen more times than anyone or anything else.
If something tops a particular amount, it is larger than that amount.
If something is topped with something, it has that thing as its highest part.
If you top a story, remark, or action, you follow it with a better or more impressive one.
You can use tops after mentioning a quantity, to say that it is the maximum possible.
If you say that something is tops or is the tops, you mean that it is better or more successful than anything else.
If someone blows their top, they become very angry about something.
If a person, organization, or country comes out on top, they are more successful than the others that they have been competing with.
If someone pays top dollar for something, they pay the highest possible price for it.
If you say that you clean, tidy, or examine something from top to bottom, you are emphasizing that you do it completely and thoroughly.
You can use from top to toe to emphasize that the whole of someone’s body is covered or dressed in a particular thing or type of clothing.
When something gets on top of you, it makes you feel unhappy or depressed because it is very difficult or worrying, or because it involves more work than you can manage.
If you say something off the top of your head, you say it without thinking about it much before you speak, especially because you do not have enough time.
If one thing is on top of another, it is placed over it or on its highest part.
You can use on top or on top of to indicate that a particular problem exists in addition to a number of other problems.
You say that someone is on top when they have reached the most important position in an organization or business.
If you are on top of or get on top of something that you are doing, you are dealing with it successfully.
If you say that you feel on top of the world, you are emphasizing that you feel extremely happy and healthy.
If one thing is over the top of another, it is placed over it so that it is completely covering it. [PHR after v]
You describe something as over the top when you think that it is exaggerated, and therefore unacceptable.
If you top and tail fruit or vegetables such as French beans, you cut off the tops and the bottoms of them when you are preparing them to be eaten.
If you say that someone is at the top of the tree, you mean that they have reached the highest level in their career or profession.
If you say something at the top of your voice, you say it very loudly.
A topic is a particular subject that you discuss or write about.

A tour is a journey during which you visit several places that interest you.
A tour is a short trip that you make round a place, for example round a historical building, so that you can look at it.

If you have someone in tow, they are following you closely because you are looking after them or you are leading them somewhere.
If you move, look, or point towards something or someone, you move, look, or point in their direction.
If things develop towards a particular situation, that situation becomes nearer in time or more likely to happen.
If you have a particular attitude towards something or someone, you have that attitude when you think about them or deal with them.
If something happens towards a particular time, it happens just before that time.
If something is towards part of a place or thing, it is near that part.
If you give money towards something, you give it to help pay for that thing.
A towel is a piece of thick soft cloth that you use to dry yourself.
If you towel something or towel it dry, you dry it with a towel.
If you throw in the towel, you stop trying to do something because you realize that you cannot succeed.

You use town in order to refer to the central area of a town where most of the shops and offices are.
If you refer to the town, you are referring to town and city areas in general, as opposed to country areas.
If you say that someone goes to town on something, you mean that they deal with it with a lot of enthusiasm or intensity.
If you describe someone as a man about town or a woman about town, you mean that they are sophisticated, like to go out and spend money, and have a busy social life.

To track someone or something means to follow their movements by means of a special device, such as a satellite or radar.

If an animal or bird is trained to do particular things, it is taught to do them, for example in order to be able to work for someone or to be a good pet.

诡计多端的;奸诈的;狡猾的；
Englishsense: If you describe a task or problem as tricky, you mean that it is difficult to do or deal with.
If you describe a person as tricky, you mean that they are likely to deceive you or cheat you.
The trigger of a gun is a small lever which you pull to fire it.
The trigger of a bomb is the device which causes it to explode.
To trigger a bomb or system means to cause it to work.
If something triggers an event or situation, it causes it to begin to happen or exist.
If something acts as a trigger for another thing such as an illness, event, or situation, the first thing causes the second thing to begin to happen or exist.
A trillion is a million million.

Englishsense: Something that is trim is neat, tidy, and attractive.
If you describe someone’s figure as trim, you mean that it is attractive because there is no extra fat on their body.
If you trim something, for example someone’s hair, you cut off small amounts of it in order to make it look neater and tidier.
If a government or other organization trims something such as a plan, policy, or amount, they reduce it slightly in extent or size.
If something such as a piece of clothing is trimmed with a type of material or design, it is decorated with it, usually along its edges.
The trim on something such as a piece of clothing is a decoration, for example along its edges, that is in a different colour or material.
When people are in trim or in good trim, they are in good physical condition.

Chinesesense: 三人组合;尤指三重唱;三个一组;三件一套；
Englishsense: A trio is a group of three people together, especially musicians or singers, or a group of three things that have something in common.

Chinesesense: 使绊;将…绊倒; 使跌倒；
(对权力等的)迷恋;(内疚、怀旧感等的)困扰；
Englishsense: A trip is a journey that you make to a particular place. See usage note at: journey
If you trip when you are walking, you knock your foot against something and fall or nearly fall.
If you trip someone who is walking or running, you put your foot or something else in front of them, so that they knock their own foot against it and fall or nearly fall.
If you say that someone is, for example, on a power trip, a guilt trip, or a nostalgia trip, you mean that their behaviour is motivated by power, guilt, or nostalgia.
A trip is an experience that someone has when their mind is affected by a drug such as LSD.
If someone is tripping, they are having an experience in which their mind is affected by a drug such as LSD.
If someone trips somewhere, they walk there with light, quick steps.

Chinesesense: 三个的;三方的;三部分的；
使变成三倍;使增至三倍；
Englishsense: Triple means consisting of three things or parts.
If something triples or if you triple it, it becomes three times as large in size or number.
If something is triple the amount or size of another thing, it is three times as large.

Chinesesense: 非凡的成功;杰出的成就；
(成功或获胜时的)极大的满足，狂喜，骄傲；
Englishsense: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.
Triumph is a feeling of great satisfaction and pride resulting from a success or victory.
If someone or something triumphs, they gain complete success, control, or victory, often after a long or difficult struggle.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 琐碎的;不重要的;微不足道的；
Englishsense: If you describe something as trivial, you think that it is unimportant and not serious.

Chinesesense: (常指疲惫或忧伤地)成群移动，结队前行；
Englishsense: Troops are soldiers, especially when they are in a large organized group doing a particular task.
A troop is a group of soldiers within a cavalry or armoured regiment.
A troop of boy scouts is a local group of them that meets regularly.
A troop of people or animals is a group of them.
If people troop somewhere, they walk there in a group, often in a sad or tired way.

POS: N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词
Englishsense: A trooper is a soldier of low rank in the cavalry or in an armoured regiment in the army.
In the United States, a trooper is a police officer in a state police force.

Chinesesense: (用于一些竞赛或赛跑的名称后)…杯，…奖；
Englishsense: A trophy is a prize, for example a silver cup, that is given to the winner of a competition or race.
Trophy is used in the names of some competitions and races in which the winner receives a trophy.
A trophy is something that you keep in order to show that you have done something very difficult.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 湿热的;典型热带气候的；
Englishsense: Tropical means belonging to or typical of the tropics.
Tropical weather is hot and damp weather that people believe to be typical of the tropics.
If you trot somewhere, you move fairly fast at a speed between walking and running, taking small quick steps.
When an animal such as a horse trots, it moves fairly fast, taking quick small steps. You can also say that the rider of the animal is trotting.
If something happens several times on the trot, it happens that number of times without a break.

Chinesesense: 麻烦;问题;引起麻烦的事；
需劳神费力的人(或动物)；
处于困境;惹麻烦;将受惩罚；
Englishsense: You can refer to problems or difficulties as trouble.
If you say that one aspect of a situation is the trouble, you mean that it is the aspect which is causing problems or making the situation unsatisfactory.
Your troubles are the things that you are worried about.
If you have kidney trouble or back trouble, for example, there is something wrong with your kidneys or your back.
If there is trouble somewhere, especially in a public place, there is fighting or rioting there.
If you tell someone that it is no trouble to do something for them, you are saying politely that you can or will do it, because it is easy or convenient for you.
If you say that a person or animal is no trouble, you mean that they are very easy to look after.
If something troubles you, it makes you feel rather worried.
If a part of your body troubles you, it causes you physical pain or discomfort.
If you say that someone does not trouble to do something, you are critical of them because they do not behave in the way that they should do, and you think that this would require very little effort.
You use trouble in expressions such as I’m sorry to trouble you when you are apologizing to someone for disturbing them in order to ask them something.
If someone is in trouble, they are in a situation in which a person in authority is angry with them or is likely to punish them because they have done something wrong.
If you take the trouble to do something, you do something which requires a small amount of additional effort.

If you say that someone or something is more trouble than they are worth, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or take a lot of time and effort and you do not achieve or gain very much in return.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 问题多的;动乱的;混乱的；
Englishsense: Someone who is troubled is worried because they have problems.
A troubled place, situation, organization, or time has many problems or conflicts.
Trousers are a piece of clothing that you wear over your body from the waist downwards, and that cover each leg separately.
A trout is a fairly large fish that lives in rivers and streams.

Chinesesense: (铁路)运货车皮，敞篷货运火车；
用卡车装运;用货车运送；
不愿参与;不与…来往;不掺和；
Englishsense: A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.
A truck is an open vehicle used for carrying goods on a railway.
When something or someone is trucked somewhere, they are driven there in a lorry.
If you say that you will have no truck with someone or something, you are refusing to be involved with them in any way.

Chinesesense: (用于正式信件末尾)你忠实的；
Englishsense: You use truly to emphasize that something has all the features or qualities of a particular thing, or is the case to the fullest possible extent.
You can use truly in order to emphasize your description of something.
You use truly to emphasize that feelings are genuine and sincere.
You can use truly in order to emphasize that what you are saying is true.
You write Yours truly at the end of a formal letter to someone you do not know very well. You write your signature after the words ’Yours truly’.
You can say yours truly as a way of referring to yourself.

Chinesesense: 大力鼓吹;积极宣扬;大力宣传；
Englishsense: A trumpet is a musical instrument of the brass family which plays quite high notes.
If someone trumpets something that they are proud of or that they think is important, they speak about it publicly in a very forceful way.
When an elephant trumpets, it makes a loud sound.
The trunk of a tree is the large main stem from which the branches grow.
A trunk is a large, strong case or box used for storing things or for taking on a journey.
An elephant’s trunk is its very long nose that it uses to lift food and water to its mouth.
The trunk of a car is a covered space at the back or front in which you put luggage or other things.
Trunks are shorts that a man wears when he goes swimming.
Your trunk is the central part of your body, from your neck to your waist.

Chinesesense: 希望…是对的;估计…是对的；
信托基金机构;财产托管机构；
公立医院(由政府资助、独立经营)；
Englishsense: If you trust someone, you believe that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.
Your trust in someone is your belief that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.
If you trust someone to do something, you believe that they will do it.
If you trust someone with something important or valuable, you allow them to look after it or deal with it.
If you do not trust something, you feel that it is not safe or reliable.
If you trust someone’s judgment or advice, you believe that it is good or right.
If you say you trust that something is true, you mean you hope and expect that it is true.
If you trust in someone or something, you believe strongly in them, and do not doubt their powers or their good intentions.
A trust is a financial arrangement in which a group of people or an organization keeps and invests money for someone.
A trust is a group of people or an organization that has control of an amount of money or property and invests it on behalf of other people or as a charity.

In Britain, a trust or a trust hospital is a public hospital that receives its funding directly from the national government. It has its own board of governors and is not controlled by the local health authority.
If something valuable is kept in trust, it is held and protected by a group of people or an organization on behalf of other people.
If you take something on trust after having heard or read it, you believe it completely without checking it.
A trustee is someone with legal control of money or property that is kept or invested for another person, company, or organization.
The truth about something is all the facts about it, rather than things that are imagined or invented.
If you say that there is some truth in a statement or story, you mean that it is true, or at least partly true.
A truth is something that is believed to be true.
You say in truth in order to indicate that you are giving your honest opinion about something.
You say to tell you the truth or truth to tell in order to indicate that you are telling someone something in an open and honest way, without trying to hide anything.

Chinesesense: 到(某处)试试;找(某人)试试；
(橄榄球的)达阵得分(在对方球门线内带球触地得分)；
没努力尝试;没竭尽全力；
Englishsense: If you try to do something, you want to do it, and you take action which you hope will help you to do it.
To try and do something means to try to do it.
If you try for something, you make an effort to get it or achieve it.
If you try something new or different, you use it, do it, or experience it in order to discover its qualities or effects.
If you try a particular place or person, you go to that place or person because you think that they may be able to provide you with what you want.
If you try a door or window, you try to open it.

When a person is tried, he or she has to appear in a law court and is found innocent or guilty after the judge and jury have heard the evidence. When a legal case is tried, it is considered in a court of law.
In the game of rugby, a try is the action of scoring by putting the ball down behind the goal line of the opposing team.
If you say that something fails but not for want of trying or not for lack of trying, you mean that everything possible was done to make it succeed.

Chinesesense: T恤衫;短袖无扣棉汗衫;短袖无领衫；
Englishsense: A T-shirt is a cotton shirt with no collar or buttons. T-shirts usually have short sleeves.
A tub is a deep container of any size.
A tub is the same as a bathtub.

Chinesesense: 公司、经济、机构完全垮掉，彻底崩溃，告吹；
Englishsense: A tube is a long hollow object that is usually round, like a pipe.
A tube of something such as paste is a long, thin container which you squeeze in order to force the paste out.
Some long, thin, hollow parts in your body are referred to as tubes.
The tube is the underground railway system in London.
You can refer to the television as the tube.
a business, economy, or institution goes down the tubes or goes down the tube, it fails or collapses completely.

Chinesesense: 肺结核;结核病(缩略形式为 TB)；
Englishsense: Tuberculosis is a serious infectious disease that affects someone’s lungs and other parts of their body. The abbreviation TB is also used.
If you tuck something somewhere, you put it there so that it is safe, comfortable, or neat.
Tuck is food that children eat as a snack at school.
You can use tuck to refer to a form of plastic surgery which involves reducing the size of a part of someone’s body.
If you tug something or tug at it, you give it a quick and usually strong pull.
A tug or a tug boat is a small powerful boat which pulls large ships, usually when they come into a port.

Chinesesense: 尤指大专院校或私立学校的学费；
Englishsense: If you are given tuition in a particular subject, you are taught about that subject.
You can use tuition to refer to the amount of money that you have to pay for being taught particular subjects, especially in a university, college, or private school.

Chinesesense: 滚下;摔倒;跌落;翻滚而下；
突然闯入某地;陷入，浑然不觉地进入(某种状态)；
Englishsense: If someone or something tumbles somewhere, they fall there with a rolling or bouncing movement.
If prices or levels of something are tumbling, they are decreasing rapidly.
If water tumbles, it flows quickly over an uneven surface.
If you say that someone tumbles into a situation or place, you mean that they get into it without being fully in control of themselves or knowing what they are doing.
Tuna or tuna fish are large fish that live in warm seas and are caught for food.

Chinesesense: 调试，调整(发动机或机器)；
改变调子;变卦;改变态度；
被…牵着鼻子走;受…的控制；
合调的/走调的;在调子上/不在调子上；
一致/不一致;赞同/不赞同；
Englishsense: A tune is a series of musical notes that is pleasant and easy to remember.
You can refer to a song or a short piece of music as a tune.
When someone tunes a musical instrument, they adjust it so that it produces the right notes.
When an engine or machine is tuned, it is adjusted so that it works well.
If your radio or television is tuned to a particular broadcasting station, you are listening to or watching the programmes being broadcast by that station.
If you say that a person or organization is calling the tune, you mean that they are in a position of power or control in a particular situation.
If you say that someone has changed their tune, you are criticizing them because they have changed their opinion or way of doing things.
If you say that someone is dancing to someone else’s tune, you mean that they are allowing themselves to be controlled by the other person.
A person or musical instrument that is in tune produces exactly the right notes. A person or musical instrument that is out of tune does not produce exactly the right notes.
If you are in tune with a group of people, you are in agreement or sympathy with them. If you are out of tune with them, you are not in agreement or sympathy with them.
To the tune of a particular amount of money means to the extent of that amount.
A tunnel is a long passage which has been made under the ground, usually through a hill or under the sea.
To tunnel somewhere means to make a tunnel there.
A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.
Turf is short, thick, even grass.
A turf is a small rectangular piece of grass which you lay on the ground in order to make a lawn.
Someone’s turf is the area which is most familiar to them or where they feel most confident.
A Turk is a Turkish citizen, or a person of Turkish origin.
A turkey is a large bird that is kept on a farm for its meat.

Chinesesense: 土耳其的;土耳其人的;土耳其语的;土耳其文化的；
Englishsense: Turkish means belonging or relating to Turkey, or to its people, language, or culture.
Turkish is the main language spoken in Turkey.
Turmoil is a state of confusion, disorder, uncertainty, or great anxiety.

Chinesesense: 转动;使转向;使改变方向；
转动，旋动(钥匙、把手、开关等)；
开始思考;开始讨论;把(注意力等)转向；
(时局或趋势的)逆转，转变，变化；
(依次轮流时的)轮班，次序，轮番；
表示两种感情或品质的交替时而，间或；
彻底搜查;把…翻个底朝天；
彻底改变，完全搅乱体制或生活方式；
Englishsense: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction.
When you turn something, you move it so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction, or is in a very different position.
When something such as a wheel turns, or when you turn it, it continually moves around in a particular direction.
When you turn something such as a key, knob, or switch, or when it turns, you hold it and twist your hand, in order to open something or make it start working.
When you turn in a particular direction or turn a corner, you change the direction in which you are moving or travelling.
The point where a road, path, or river turns, is the point where it has a bend or curve in it.
When the tide turns, it starts coming in or going out.
When someone turns a cartwheel or a somersault, they do a cartwheel or somersault.
When you turn a page of a book or magazine, you move it so that is flat against the previous page, and you can read the next page.
If you turn a weapon or an aggressive feeling on someone, you point it at them or direct it at them.
If you turn to a particular page in a book or magazine, you open it at that page.
If you turn your attention or thoughts to a particular subject or if you turn to it, you start thinking about it or discussing it.
If you turn to someone, you ask for their help or advice.
If you turn to a particular activity, job, or way of doing something, you start doing or using it.
To turn or be turned into something means to become that thing.
You can use turn before an adjective to indicate that something or someone changes by acquiring the quality described by the adjective.
You can use turn to indicate that there is a change to a particular kind of weather. For example, if it turns cold, the weather starts being cold.
If a situation or trend takes a particular kind of turn, it changes so that it starts developing in a different or opposite way.
In sports, if a game turns, or is turned, something significant happens which changes the way the game is developing.
If a business turns a profit, it earns more money than it spends.
When someone turns a particular age, they pass that age. When it turns a particular time, it passes that time.
Turn is used in expressions such as the turn of the century and the turn of the year to refer to a period of time when one century or year is ending and the next one is beginning.
When someone turns a wooden or metal object that they are making, they shape it using a special tool.
If it is your turn to do something, you now have the duty, chance, or right to do it, when other people have done it before you or will do it after you.
If you say that someone is having a turn, you mean they feel suddenly very unwell for a short period of time.
You can use by turns to indicate that someone has two particular emotions or qualities, one after the other.
If there is a particular turn of events, a particular series of things happen.
If you say that something happens at every turn, you are emphasizing that it happens frequently or all the time, usually so that it prevents you from achieving what you want.
If you do someone a good turn, you do something that helps or benefits them.
If someone turns a place inside out or upside down, they search it very thoroughly and usually make it very untidy.
If something such as a system or way of life is turned inside out or upside down, it is changed completely, making people confused or upset.
You use in turn to refer to actions or events that are in a sequence one after the other, for example because one causes the other.
If each person in a group does something in turn, they do it one after the other in a fixed or agreed order.
If someone is of a particular turn of mind, they have that kind of mind or character.
If you speak out of turn or talk out of turn, you say something that you do not have the right or authority to say.
If a person, animal, or vehicle has a good turn of speed, they have the ability to move fast.
If two or more people take turns to do something, or in British English take it in turns to do something, they do it one after the other several times, rather than doing it together.
If a situation takes a turn for the worse, it suddenly becomes worse. If a situation takes a turn for the better, it suddenly becomes better.

Chinesesense: (观点、态度或方法的)彻底转变，完全改变；
(尤指生意或经济的)突然好转，起色，转机；
工作所需时间;(飞机或轮船卸货的)停航时间；
Englishsense: A turnaround is a complete change in opinion, attitude, or method.
A turnaround is a sudden improvement, especially in the success of a business or a country’s economy.
The turnaround or turnaround time of a task, for example the unloading of an aircraft or ship, is the amount of time that it takes.
If you take a particular turning, you go along a road which leads away from the side of another road.

Chinesesense: 出席人数;到场人数;参加人数；
Englishsense: The turnout at an event is the number of people who go to it or take part in it.
The turnout in an election is the number of people who vote in it, as a proportion of the number of people who have the right to vote in it.
The turnover of a company is the value of the goods or services sold during a particular period of time.
The turnover of people in an organization or place is the rate at which people leave and are replaced.
A turtle is a large reptile which has a thick shell covering its body and which lives in the sea most of the time.
A turtle is any reptile that has a thick shell around its body, for example a tortoise or terrapin.
If a boat turns turtle, it turns upside down when it is in the water.

Chinesesense: (英国大学或学院中的)导师;(某些美国大学或学院中的)助教；
Englishsense: A tutor is a teacher at a British university or college. In some American universities or colleges, a tutor is a teacher of the lowest rank.
A tutor is someone who gives private lessons to one pupil or a very small group of pupils.
If someone tutors a person or a subject, they teach that person or subject.
TV means the same as television.
Twelve is the number 12.
The twentieth item in a series is the one that you count as number twenty.
A twentieth is one of twenty equal parts of something.

Chinesesense: (20 至 29 之间的数字)二十几；
二十世纪二十年代(1920 至 1929 年间)；
Englishsense: Twenty is the number 20.

When you talk about the twenties, you are referring to numbers between 20 and 29. For example, if you are in your twenties, you are aged between 20 and 29. If the temperature is in the twenties, the temperature is between 20 and 29 degrees.
The twenties is the decade between 1920 and 1929.

Chinesesense: (表示频率)每天两次/一周两次；
重新考虑;慎重考虑;思忖再三；
Englishsense: If something happens twice, there are two actions or events of the same kind.
You use twice in expressions such as twice a day and twice a week to indicate that two events or actions of the same kind happen in each day or week.

If one thing is, for example, twice as big or old as another, the first thing is two times as big or old as the second. People sometimes say that one thing is twice as good or hard as another when they want to emphasize that the first thing is much better or harder than the second.
If you think twice about doing something, you consider it again and decide not to do it, or decide to do it differently.

Chinesesense: 顿悟;突然醒悟;豁然开窍；
Englishsense: A twig is a very small thin branch that grows out from a main branch of a tree or bush.
If you twig, you suddenly realize or understand something.

Chinesesense: 蒙眬的;含混的;界限模糊的；
Englishsense: Twilight is the time just before night when the daylight has almost gone but when it is not completely dark.
Twilight is the small amount of light that there is outside just after the sun has gone down.
The twilight of a particular period of time is the final stages of it, when the most important events have already happened.
A twilight state or a twilight zone is a situation of confusion or uncertainty, which seems to exist between two different states or categories.

Chinesesense: 双胞胎之一;孪生儿之一；
使结成友好地区;使结为特殊关系；
Englishsense: If two people are twins, they have the same mother and were born on the same day.
Twin is used to describe a pair of things that look the same and are close together.
Twin is used to describe two things or ideas that are similar or connected in some way.
When a place or organization in one country is twinned with a place or organization in another country, a special relationship is formally established between them.
Twin towns or cities are twinned with each other.

Chinesesense: 使(尤指身体部位)弯曲变形;使扭曲；
Englishsense: If you twist something, you turn it to make a spiral shape, for example by turning the two ends of it in opposite directions.

If you twist something, especially a part of your body, or if it twists, it moves into an unusual, uncomfortable, or bent position, for example because of being hit or pushed, or because you are upset.
If you twist part of your body such as your head or your shoulders, you turn that part while keeping the rest of your body still.
If you twist a part of your body such as your ankle or wrist, you injure it by turning it too sharply, or in an unusual direction.
If you twist something, you turn it so that it moves around in a circular direction.
If a road or river twists, it has a lot of sudden changes of direction in it.
If you say that someone has twisted something that you have said, you disapprove of them because they have repeated it in a way that changes its meaning, in order to harm you or benefit themselves.
A twist in something is an unexpected and significant development.
A twist is the shape that something has when it has been twisted.
The twist is a dance that was popular in the 1960’s, in which you twist your body and move your hips in an energetic way.
If something happens by a twist of fate, it happens by chance, and it is strange, interesting, or unfortunate in some way.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you describe a person as twisted, you dislike them because you think they are strange in an unpleasant way.

Chinesesense: 使(尤指身体部位)抽搐;使抽动;急拉;急扯；
Englishsense: If something, especially a part of your body, twitches or if you twitch it, it makes a little jumping movement.

You refer to the people who live in a village, especially the people who have lived there for most or all of their lives, as the villagers.

Englishsense: A vine is a plant that grows up or over things, especially one which produces grapes.
Vinegar is a sharp-tasting liquid, usually made from sour wine or malt, which is used to make things such as salad dressing.

Chinesesense: 某优质葡萄酒的产地和年份;特定年份酿的葡萄酒；
葡萄酒优质的，上等的，佳酿的；
[汽车或飞机)老式的，古色古香的；
Englishsense: The vintage of a good quality wine is the year and place that it was made before being stored to improve it. You can also use vintage to refer to the wine that was made in a certain year.
Vintage wine is good quality wine that has been stored for several years in order to improve its quality.
Vintage cars or aeroplanes are old but are admired because they are considered to be the best of their kind.
You can use vintage to describe something which is the best and most typical of its kind.

Chinesesense: 尤指区别于磁带和光盘的塑料唱片，黑胶唱片；

If you violate someone’s privacy or peace, you disturb it.
If someone violates a special place, for example a grave, they damage it or treat it with disrespect.
Violence is behaviour which is intended to hurt, injure, or kill people.
If you do or say something with violence, you use a lot of force and energy in doing or saying it, often because you are angry.

Englishsense: Virtue is thinking and doing what is right and avoiding what is wrong.

Your vision of a future situation or society is what you imagine or hope it would be like, if things were very different from the way they are now.
If you have a vision of someone in a particular situation, you imagine them in that situation, for example because you are worried that it might happen, or hope that it will happen.
A vision is the experience of seeing something that other people cannot see, for example in a religious experience or as a result of madness or taking drugs.
Your vision is your ability to see clearly with your eyes.
Your vision is everything that you can see from a particular place or position.

Englishsense: If you visit someone, you go to see them and spend time with them.
If you visit a place, you go there for a short time.
If you visit a website, you look at it.

If something very unpleasant is visited upon you, it happens to you.
A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

Englishsense: Visual means relating to sight, or to things that you can see.

If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

Vodka is a strong, clear, alcoholic drink.

Chinesesense: 表达意见的权利;发言权；

If you say that a writer finds his or her voice, you mean that he or she finds a style and subject matter that are personal and original.
If you give voice to an opinion, a need, or a desire, you express it aloud.

If you lose your voice, you cannot speak for a while because of an illness.
If you raise your voice, you speak more loudly. If you lower your voice, you speak more quietly.
If you say something at the top of your voice, you say it as loudly as possible.
If a number of people say something with one voice, they all express the same opinion about something.

If you are void of something, you do not have any of it.
To void something means to officially say that it is not valid.

If something such as an action speaks volumes about a person or thing, it gives you a lot of information about them.

If you volunteer to do something, you offer to do it without being forced to do it.
If you volunteer information, you tell someone something without being asked.
A volunteer is someone who chooses to join the armed forces, especially during a war, as opposed to someone who is forced to join by law.
If you vomit, food and drink comes back up from your stomach and out through your mouth.
Vomit is partly digested food and drink that has come back up from someone’s stomach and out through their mouth.

Englishsense: A vote is a choice made by a particular person or group in a meeting or an election.
A vote is an occasion when a group of people make a decision by each person indicating his or her choice. The choice that most people support is accepted by the group.
The vote is the total number of votes or voters in an election, or the number of votes received or cast by a particular group.
If you have the vote in an election, or have a vote in a meeting, you have the legal right to indicate your choice.
When you vote, you indicate your choice officially at a meeting or in an election, for example by raising your hand or writing on a piece of paper.

If a government or other organization votes money for something or to do something, they decide to spend the money in that way.
If people vote someone a particular title, they choose that person to have that title.
If you vote with your feet, you show that you do not support something by leaving the place where it is happening or leaving the organization that is supporting it.
If you say ’ vote that ’ a particular thing should happen, you are suggesting that this is what should happen.

One man one vote or one person one vote is a system of voting in which every person in a group or country has the right to cast their vote, and in which each individual’s vote is counted and has equal value.
Voters are people who have the legal right to vote in elections, or people who are voting in a particular election.
A voucher is a ticket or piece of paper that can be used instead of money to pay for something.
If you vow to do something, you make a serious promise or decision that you will do it.
A vow is a serious promise or decision to do a particular thing.
Vows are a particular set of serious promises, such as the promises two people make when they are getting married.
A voyage is a long journey on a ship or in a spacecraft. See usage note at: journey
To voyage to a place means to travel there, especially by sea.

If an employee waits on you, for example in a restaurant or hotel, they take orders from you and bring you what you want.
If you say that you can’t wait to do something or can hardly wait to do it, you are emphasizing that you are very excited about it and eager to do it.
You say ’ wait for it ’ to stop someone from doing something too soon because you have not yet given them the command to do it.
You can use ’ wait for it ’ to indicate that you are about to say something that is amusing or surprising.
If you tell someone to wait and see, you tell them that they must be patient or that they must not worry about what is going to happen in the future because they have no control over it.

If one thing follows in the wake of another, it happens after the other thing is over, often as a result of it.
Your waking hours are the times when you are awake rather than asleep.
If you leave something or someone in your wake, you leave them behind you as you go.
If you are following in someone’s wake, you are following them or their example.

A walk is the action of walking rather than running.

If a person or animal wanders from a place where they are supposed to stay, they move away from the place without going in a particular direction.
If your mind wanders or your thoughts wander, you stop concentrating on something and start thinking about other things.
If your eyes wander, you stop looking at one thing and start looking around at other things.

Want is the state of being extremely poor.
Your wants are the things that you want.
If you do something for want of something else, you do it because the other thing is not available or not possible.

If you say to someone ’ what do you want? ’, you are asking them in a rather rude or angry way why they have come to the place where you are or why they want to speak to you.

Chinesesense: (国家或组织之间的)经济竞争；
Englishsense: A war is a period of fighting or conflict between countries or states.
War is intense economic competition between countries or organizations.
If you make war on someone or something that you are opposed to, you do things to stop them succeeding.
If someone has been in the wars, they have been injured, for example in a fight or in an accident.
If a country goes to war, it starts fighting a war.
If two people, countries, or organizations have a war of words, they criticize each other because they strongly disagree about something.
A ward is a room in a hospital which has beds for many people, often people who need similar treatment.
A ward is a district which forms part of a political constituency or local council.

A ward or a ward of court is a child who is the responsibility of a person called a guardian, or of a court of law, because their parents are dead or because they are believed to be in need of protection.
A warden is a person who is responsible for a particular place or thing, and for making sure that the laws or regulations that relate to it are obeyed.
The warden of a prison is the person in charge of it.
A wardrobe is a tall cupboard or cabinet in which you can hang your clothes.
Someone’s wardrobe is the total collection of clothes that they have.
The wardrobe in a theatre company is the actors’ and actresses’ costumes.
A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods are stored until they are exported to other countries or distributed to shops to be sold.
Warfare is the activity of fighting a war.
Warfare is sometimes used to refer to any violent struggle or conflict.

ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
