Englishsense: If you wince, the muscles of your face tighten suddenly because you have felt a pain or because you have just seen, heard, or remembered something unpleasant.

Chinesesense: (影响事件的)趋势或因素常作新闻用语；
可能发生何事;事态的发展；
(道路、河流或一队人)蜿蜒向前，曲折而行，迂回；
给(钟表等)上发条;给…上弦；
Englishsense: A wind is a current of air that is moving across the earth’s surface.
Journalists often refer to a trend or factor that influences events as a wind of a particular kind.
If you are winded by something such as a blow, the air is suddenly knocked out of your lungs so that you have difficulty breathing for a short time.
Wind is the air that you sometimes swallow with food or drink, or gas that is produced in your intestines, which causes an uncomfortable feeling.
If you wind a baby, you hit its back gently in order to help it to release air from its stomach.
The wind section of an orchestra or band is the group of people who produce musical sounds by blowing into their instruments.
If someone breaks wind, they release gas from their intestines through their anus.
If you get wind of something, you hear about it, especially when someone else did not want you to know about it.
If something is in the wind, it is likely to happen.
If something or someone puts the wind up you, they frighten or worry you.
If you sail close to the wind, you take a risk by doing or saying something that may get you into trouble.
If something takes the wind out of your sails, it suddenly makes you much less confident in what you are doing or saying.
If you realize or find out which way the wind is blowing or how the wind is blowing, you realize or find out what is likely to happen, for example whether something is likely to succeed.
If a road, river, or line of people winds in a particular direction, it goes in that direction with a lot of bends or twists in it.
When you wind something flexible around something else, you wrap it around it several times.
When you wind a mechanical device, for example a watch or a clock, you turn a knob, key, or handle on it several times in order to make it operate.
To wind a tape or film back or forward means to make it move towards its starting or ending position.

Chinesesense: (银行、邮局、火车站、博物馆等处柜台的)窗口；
消失殆尽;烟消云散;化为乌有；
转瞬即逝的机会;稍纵即逝的机会；
Englishsense: A window is a space in the wall of a building or in the side of a vehicle, which has glass in it so that light can come in and you can see out.
A window is a large piece of glass along the front of a shop, behind which some of the goods that the shop sells are displayed.
A window is a glass-covered opening above a counter, for example in a bank, post office, railway station, or museum, which the person serving you sits behind.
On a computer screen, a window is one of the work areas that the screen can be divided into.
If you have a window in your diary for something, or if you can make a window for it, you are free at a particular time and can do it then.
If you say that something such as a plan or a particular way of thinking or behaving has gone out of the window or has flown out of the window, you mean that it has disappeared completely.

If you say that there is a window of opportunity for something, you mean that there is an opportunity to do something but that this opportunity will only last for a short time and so it needs to be taken advantage of quickly.
The windshield of a car or other vehicle is the glass window at the front through which the driver looks.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If it is windy, the wind is blowing a lot.
Wine is an alcoholic drink which is made from grapes. You can also refer to alcoholic drinks made from other fruits or vegetables as wine.
Wine is used to describe things that are very dark red in colour.
If you wine and dine, or if someone wines and dines you, you go out, for example to expensive restaurants, and spend a lot of money.

Chinesesense: (舞台两侧用帘幕或布景遮住的)边厢,翼部,侧面；
(足球、曲棍球等的)边锋位置；边锋；
飞机驾驶资格；飞行资格；
将…置于羽翼之下；对…呵护有加；
Englishsense: The wings of a bird or insect are the two parts of its body that it uses for flying.
The wings of an aeroplane are the long flat parts sticking out of its side which support it while it is flying.
A wing of a building is a part of it which sticks out from the main part.
A wing of an organization, especially a political organization, is a group within it which has a particular function or particular beliefs.
In a theatre, the wings are the sides of the stage which are hidden from the audience by curtains or scenery.

In a game such as football or hockey, the left wing and the right wing are the areas on the far left and the far right of the pitch. You can also refer to the players who play in these positions as the left wing and the right wing.
A wing of a car is a part of it on the outside which is over one of the wheels.
When pilots get their wings, they become qualified to fly aeroplanes.
If you say that something or someone wings their way somewhere or wings somewhere, you mean that they go there quickly, especially by plane.
If you say that something or someone clips your wings, you mean that they restrict your freedom to do what you want.
If you say that someone is waiting in the wings, you mean that they are ready and waiting for an opportunity to take action.
If you spread your wings, you do something new and rather difficult or move to a new place, because you feel more confident in your abilities than you used to and you want to gain wider experience.
If you take someone under your wing, you look after them, help them, and protect them.
When you wink at someone, you look towards them and close one eye very briefly, usually as a signal that something is a joke or a secret.
If a lamp winks, it shines or reflects light in short flashes.
If you say that you did not sleep a wink or did not get a wink of sleep, you mean that you tried to go to sleep but could not.

Chinesesense: 成功者;可能成功的人(或事物)；
(足球、网球等比赛中的)制胜球；
Englishsense: The winner of a prize, race, or competition is the person, animal, or thing that wins it.
If you say that something or someone is a winner, you mean that they are popular and successful, or that they are likely to be popular and successful.
The winners in a particular situation are the people who have benefited from it and are in a better position than they previously were because of it.
In games such as football or tennis, the winner is the goal or shot that wins a particular match or point.
You can use winning to describe a person or thing that wins something such as a competition, game, or election.
You can use winning to describe actions or qualities that please other people and make them feel friendly towards you.
Winter is the season between autumn and spring. In the winter the weather is usually cold.
If an animal or plant winters somewhere or is wintered there, it spends the winter there.
If you winter somewhere, you spend the winter there.

Chinesesense: 让…笑容顿失;使…兴致全无;使…丧失优势；
Englishsense: If you wipe something, you rub its surface to remove dirt or liquid from it.
If you wipe dirt or liquid from something, you remove it, for example by using a cloth or your hand.
A wipe is a small moist cloth for cleaning things and is designed to be used only once.
If you say that something wipes the smile off someone’s face, you mean that it suddenly spoils their enjoyment or removes an advantage that they had and that you are pleased about it.
A wire is a long thin piece of metal that is used to fasten things or to carry electric current.
A wire is a cable which carries power or signals from one place to another.
If you wire something such as a building or piece of equipment, you put wires inside it so that electricity or signals can pass into or through it.
A wire is the same as a telegram.
If you wire a person, you send them a telegram.
If you wire an amount of money to a person or place, you tell a bank to send it to the person or place using a telegram message.
If something goes to the wire, it continues until the last possible moment.

Chinesesense: 无线的;用无线电波传送的；
无线电;无线电收发系统；
Englishsense: Wireless technology uses radio waves rather than electricity and therefore does not require any wires.
Wireless is a system by which messages are sent over a distance by radio signals.
A wireless or wireless set is a radio.

Chinesesense: (社会或文化长期积累的)知识，学问；
Englishsense: Wisdom is the ability to use your experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions or judgments.
Wisdom is the store of knowledge that a society or culture has collected over a long period of time.
If you talk about the wisdom of a particular decision or action, you are talking about how sensible it is.
You can use wisdom to refer to ideas that are accepted by a large number of people.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 人充满智慧的，英明的，睿智的；
明白，察觉(尤指他人试图保密之事)；
在事后或作出解释后仍然不明白，仍旧不完全知晓；
Englishsense: A wise person is able to use their experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions and judgments.
A wise action or decision is sensible.
If someone says to you that it would be wise to do something, they are advising you to do it, because it is the most sensible and reasonable action or decision in a particular situation.
If you get wise to something, you find out about it, especially when someone has been trying to keep it secret.

If you say that someone is none the wiser after an event or an explanation, or that nobody is any the wiser after it, you mean that they have failed to understand it, or are not fully aware of what happened.

Chinesesense: (用于要说的话可能使人不快或担心等时)不想，无意；
希望(不可能或可能性很小的事发生)；
这是再好不过的;没有比这更好的了；
Englishsense: A wish is a desire or strong feeling that you want to have something or do something.
If you wish to do something or to have it done for you, you want to do it or have it done.

Wish is used in expressions such as I don’t wish to be rude or without wishing to be rude as a way of apologizing or warning someone when you are going to say something which might upset, annoy, or worry them.
If you wish something were true, you would like it to be true, even though you know that it is impossible or unlikely.
If you wish for something, you express the desire for that thing silently to yourself. In fairy stories, when a person wishes for something, the thing they wish for often happens by magic.
Wish is used in sentences such as I could not wish for anything better to indicate that you are very pleased with what you have and could not imagine anything better.
If you say that you would not wish a particular thing on someone, you mean that the thing is so unpleasant that you would not want them to be forced to experience it. [V n on n] [no cont]
If you wish someone something such as luck or happiness, you express the hope that they will be lucky or happy.
If you express your good wishes towards someone, you are politely expressing your friendly feelings towards them and your hope that they will be successful or happy.

Chinesesense: 时刻保持警惕;随机应变；
智穷才尽;黔驴技穷;无计可施；
用于更准确地描述亦即，也就是；
Englishsense: Wit is the ability to use words or ideas in an amusing, clever, and imaginative way.
If you describe someone as a wit, you mean that they have the ability to use words or ideas in an amusing, clever, and imaginative way.
If you say that someone has the wit to do something, you mean that they have the intelligence and understanding to make the right decision or take the right action in a particular situation.
You can refer to your ability to think quickly and cleverly in a difficult situation as your wits.
You can use wits in expressions such as frighten someone out of their wits and scare the wits out of someone to emphasize that a person or thing worries or frightens someone very much.
If you have your wits about you or keep your wits about you, you are alert and ready to act in a difficult situation.
If you say that you are at your wits’ end, you are emphasizing that you are so worried and exhausted by problems or difficulties that you do not know what to do next.
If you pit your wits against someone, you compete against them in a test of knowledge or intelligence.
To wit is used to indicate that you are about to state or describe something more precisely.

Chinesesense: 童话故事中的女巫，巫婆；
Englishsense: In fairy stories, a witch is a woman, usually an old woman, who has evil magic powers. Witches often wear a pointed black hat, and have a pet black cat.
A witch is a man or woman who claims to have magic powers and to be able to use them for good or bad purposes.

Chinesesense: 人与…在一起,同…一道，和，跟；
和，与，同(…打斗、争论或竞争)；
用，使用(某种工具、物品或材料)；
有，拥有(某种特征或所有物)；
用(某种方式)；带着(某种感情)；
伴着(声音或手势);带着(表情)；
由于，因为(某种感情而使某人有某种表现或行为)；
表示以某姿势、外表或伴随某事件做某事与…同时，随着；
随着，跟着(…的变化而变化)；
与(风、水流等)方向一致；顺着…；
Englishsense: If one person is with another, they are together in one place.
If something is put with or is with something else, they are used at the same time.
If you do something with someone else, you both do it together or are both involved in it.
If you fight, argue, or compete with someone, you oppose them.
If you do something with a particular tool, object, or substance, you do it using that tool, object, or substance.
If someone stands or goes somewhere with something, they are carrying it.
Someone or something with a particular feature or possession has that feature or possession.
Someone with an illness has that illness.
If something is filled or covered with a substance or with things, it has that substance or those things in it or on it.
If you are, for example, pleased or annoyed with someone or something, you have that feeling towards them.
You use with to indicate what a state, quality, or action relates to, involves, or affects.
You use with when indicating the way that something is done or the feeling that a person has when they do something.
You use with when indicating a sound or gesture that is made when something is done, or an expression that a person has on their face when they do something.
You use with to indicate the feeling that makes someone have a particular appearance or type of behaviour.
You use with when mentioning the position or appearance of a person or thing at the time that they do something, or what someone else is doing at that time.
You use with to introduce a current situation that is a factor affecting another situation.
You use with when making a comparison or contrast between the situations of different people or things.
If something increases or decreases with a particular factor, it changes as that factor changes.
If something moves with a wind or current, it moves in the same direction as the wind or current.
If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they understand what you are saying.
If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they support or approve of what you are doing.

Chinesesense: 退出，返回(至另一个房间)；
收回，撤回(所说的话或声明)；
Englishsense: If you withdraw something from a place, you remove it or take it away.
When groups of people such as troops withdraw or when someone withdraws them, they leave the place where they are fighting or where they are based and return nearer home.
If you withdraw money from a bank account, you take it out of that account.
If you withdraw to another room, you go there.
If you withdraw from an activity or organization, you stop taking part in it.
If you withdraw a remark or statement that you have made, you say that you want people to ignore it.

Chinesesense: 对所说的话或声明的撤回，收回；
Englishsense: The withdrawal of something is the act or process of removing it, or ending it.
Someone’s withdrawal from an activity or an organization is their decision to stop taking part in it.
A withdrawal is an amount of money that you take from your bank account.
The withdrawal of a remark or statement that you have made is the act of saying that you want people to ignore it.
Withdrawal is the period during which someone feels ill after they have stopped taking a drug which they were addicted to.
Withdrawal is behaviour in which someone prefers to be alone and does not want to talk to other people.
If you withhold something that someone wants, you do not let them have it.

Chinesesense: 在没有(发生或做某事)的情况下；
Englishsense: You use without to indicate that someone or something does not have or use the thing mentioned.
If one thing happens without another thing, or if you do something without doing something else, the second thing does not happen or occur.
If you do something without a particular feeling, you do not have that feeling when you do it.
If you do something without someone else, they are not in the same place as you are or are not involved in the same action as you.
If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

Chinesesense: 为(文件的签署)作证;连署；
是…的见证人;是…的目击者；
Englishsense: A witness to an event such as an accident or crime is a person who saw it.
If you witness something, you see it happen.
A witness is someone who appears in a court of law to say what they know about a crime or other event.
A witness is someone who writes their name on a document that you have signed, to confirm that it really is your signature.
If someone witnesses your signature on a document, they write their name after it, to confirm that it really is your signature.
If you say that a place, period of time, or person witnessed a particular event or change, you mean that it happened in that place, during that period of time, or while that person was alive.
You use witness to introduce an example of what you have just been talking about.
If you are witness to something, you see it happen.
If a person or thing bears witness to something, they show or say that it exists or happened.

Chinesesense: 传说或童话故事中的魔法师；
Englishsense: In legends and fairy stories, a wizard is a man who has magic powers.
If you admire someone because they are very good at doing a particular thing, you can say that they are a wizard.
A wizard is a computer program that guides you through the stages of a particular task.
Woe is very great sadness.
You can refer to someone’s problems as their woes.
A wolf is a wild animal that looks like a large dog.
If someone wolfs their food, they eat it all very quickly and greedily.
If someone cries wolf, they say that there is a problem when there is not, with the result that people do not believe them when there really is a problem.
If you keep the wolf from the door, you succeed in providing food and other necessary things for yourself or your family.

Chinesesense: 爱好…的女人;喜欢做…的女子；
来自…的女人;在…上大学的女子；
(公司或组织的)女代表，女代理人；
(命令性的或生气、不耐烦时的称呼)婆娘，娘儿们；
Englishsense: A woman is an adult female human being.
You can refer to women in general as woman.
If you say that a woman is, for example, a gambling woman or an outdoors woman, you mean that she likes gambling or outdoor activities. a woman about town
If you say that a woman is, for example, a London woman or an Oxford woman, you mean that she comes from London or Oxford, or went to university there.
Some people refer to a man’s wife, lover, or girlfriend as his woman.
You can refer to a female representative of a company or organization as that company or organization’s woman.
People sometimes address a woman as woman when they are ordering her to do something or when they are angry or impatient with her. This use could cause offence.
If you say that a woman is her own woman, you approve of the fact that she makes her plans and decisions herself, and does not depend on other people.
A woman’s womb is the part inside her body where a baby grows before it is born.

Chinesesense: 感到疑惑;纳闷儿;想弄明白；
神奇的;奇妙的;有奇效的；
昙花一现的人(或事物);惊艳一时的人(或事物)；
(用于礼貌地请人做事、征求意见或打听消息时)不知…，请问…；
表示找出某事的原因难怪，怪不得；
Englishsense: If you wonder about something, you think about it, either because it interests you and you want to know more about it, or because you are worried or suspicious about it.
If you wonder at something, you are very surprised about it or think about it in a very surprised way.
If you say that it is a wonder that something happened, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.
Wonder is a feeling of great surprise and pleasure that you have, for example when you see something that is very beautiful, or when something happens that you thought was impossible.
A wonder is something that causes people to feel great surprise or admiration.
If you refer, for example, to a young man as a wonder boy, or to a new product as a wonder drug, you mean that they are believed by many people to be very good or very effective.

If you say that someone or something is a nine -day wonder or a one -day wonder, you disapprove of the fact that they are attracting so much interest and attention, because you think that their popularity will only last for a very short time.
You can say ’ I wonder ’ if you want to be very polite when you are asking someone to do something, or when you are asking them for their opinion or for information.
If you say ’ no wonder ’, ’ little wonder ’, or ’ small wonder ’, you mean that something is not surprising.
You can say ’ No wonder ’ when you find out the reason for something that has been puzzling you for some time.
If you say that a person or thing works wonders or does wonders, you mean that they have a very good effect on something.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: If you describe something or someone as wonderful, you think they are extremely good.

Chinesesense: 追求(女人);向(女人)求爱或求婚；
Englishsense: If you woo people, you try to encourage them to help you, support you, or vote for you, for example by promising them things which they would like.
If a man woos a woman, he spends time with her and tries to persuade her to marry him.

Chinesesense: 树林，林子[美国英语通常用woods] ；
上天保佑(表示希望继续走好运)；
Englishsense: Wood is the material which forms the trunks and branches of trees.
A wood is a fairly large area of trees growing near each other. You can refer to one or several of these areas as woods, and this is the usual form in American English.
If something or someone is not out of the woods yet, they are still having difficulties or problems.

You can say ’ touch wood ’ in British English, or ’ knock on wood ’ in American English, to indicate that you hope to have good luck in something you are doing, usually after saying that you have been lucky with it so far.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (演员)呆板的，死板的，无活力的；
Englishsense: Wooden objects are made of wood.
If you describe an actor as wooden, you are critical of them because their performance is not at all lively or natural.
Wool is the hair that grows on sheep and on some other animals.
Wool is a material made from animal’s wool that is used to make things such as clothes, blankets, and carpets.
If you say that someone is pulling the wool over your eyes, you mean that they are trying to deceive you, in order to have an advantage over you.

Chinesesense: 短时间的谈话;短暂的聊天；
一句话，一个字(也没有听到、明白或说)；
收回前言，承认说错了话(尤指此举令说话人显得愚蠢时)；
沉默寡言的，少言寡语的，话不多的(尤指不谈及自己的意见和感情)；
(因为仰慕或尊敬而)仔细倾听，一字不落地认真听；
从来没一句好话／从来没一句坏话；
(尤指因为一方抱怨了另一方的行为)与…争论,与…严肃讨论；
用…的话说;引用…的原话说；
总而言之;简言之;一句话；
(讨论、争论、分歧中的)最终决定权；
(尤指因非常吃惊而)说不出话来，无以言表；
没有直接说;拐弯抹角地说；
(用于强调刚刚警告对方的话很可能成真，尤其是认为对方应改变态度或行为予以避免时)你听着，记住我的话；
说话算数的人;一诺千金的人；
换言之;换句话说;也就是说；
发话，下令(示意某事应该开始)；
极其愚蠢/荒唐得让人无语；
信守诺言;说话算话;说到做到；
Englishsense: A word is a single unit of language that can be represented in writing or speech. In English, a word has a space on either side of it when it is written.
Someone’s words are what they say or write.
The words of a song consist of the text that is sung, in contrast to the music that is played.
If you have a word with someone, you have a short conversation with them.
If you offer someone a word of something such as warning, advice, or praise, you warn, advise, or praise them.
If you say that someone does not hear, understand, or say a word, you are emphasizing that they hear, understand, or say nothing at all.
If there is word of something, people receive news or information about it.
If you give your word, you make a sincere promise to someone.
If someone gives the word to do something, they give an order to do it.
To word something in a particular way means to choose or use particular words to express it.
If you say that people consider something to be a dirty word, you mean that they disapprove of it.
If you say that someone has to eat their words, you mean that they have to admit that they were wrong about something they said in the past, especially when this makes them look foolish.
A person of few words says very little, especially about their opinions or feelings.
If you do something from the word go, you do it from the very beginning of a period of time or situation.
If you hang on someone’s every word, you listen very carefully to what they are saying, because you admire or respect them.
You can use expressions such as never have a good word to say or never have a bad word to say to emphasize that a person always criticizes someone or something, or that they never criticize them.
If one person has words with another, or if two or more people have words, they have a serious discussion or argument, especially because one has complained about the other’s behaviour.
You can use in their words or in their own words to indicate that you are reporting what someone said using the exact words that they used.
You use in a word to indicate that you are giving a summary of what you have just been saying, or are giving a reply, in as brief a way as possible.
If someone has the last word or the final word in a discussion, argument, or disagreement, they are the one who wins it or who makes the final decision.
If you say that something is the last word in luxury, comfort, or some other quality, you are emphasizing that it has a great deal of this quality. [【搭配模式】：PHR n][emphasis] ]
If someone is lost for words, they cannot think of anything to say, especially because they are very surprised by something.
If you say that someone has said something, but not in so many words, you mean that they said it or expressed it, but in a very indirect way.

If you say ’ mark my words ’ to someone, you are emphasizing that something you have just warned them about is very likely to happen, especially when you think they should change their attitude or behaviour to prevent it.
If news or information passes by word of mouth, people tell it to each other rather than it being printed in written form.
If you say that someone is putting words into your mouth or is putting words in your mouth, you mean that they are suggesting that you mean one thing when you really mean something different.
If you refer to someone as a man of his word or a woman of her word, you mean that they always keep their promises and can be relied on.
You say in other words in order to introduce a different, and usually simpler, explanation or interpretation of something that has just been said.
If you say something in your own words, you express it in your own way, without copying or repeating someone else’s description.
If you pass the word, you tell someone something that another person has told you.
If someone says the word, they give their approval as a sign that something should start to happen.
If you spread the word, you tell people about something.
If you take someone at their word, you believe what they say, when they did not really mean it or when they meant something slightly different.
If you say to someone ’ take my word for it ’, you mean that they should believe you because you are telling the truth.
You can use expressions such as too silly for words and too ridiculous for words to emphasize that someone or something is extremely silly or ridiculous.
If you are true to your word or as good as your word, you do what you say you will do.
If you repeat something word for word, you repeat it exactly as it was originally said or written.

Chinesesense: (艺术家、作家、作曲家等的)作品；著作；
产生(有利或不利的)影响；
对…产生(神奇的影响);使…深受魅力感染；
以(某种假定或思想)为基础(或前提)；
在(某地或某类场所)工作;在…奔波；
(常指政客或艺人)博得，赢得(众人的支持或欢心)；
使用，采用(某种材料或物质)；
(某种类型的)全部物件，全套物品；
干活儿;做工作;忙着做事；
费力或轻而易举地做，完成；
艰难地移动；缓慢地取得进展；
Englishsense: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
People who have work or who are in work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.
Your work consists of the things you are paid or required to do in your job.
When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.
Work is the place where you do your job.
Work is something which you produce as a result of an activity or as a result of doing your job.
A work is something such as a painting, book, or piece of music produced by an artist, writer, or composer.
If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.
If you work with a person or a group of people, you spend time and effort trying to help them in some way.
If a machine or piece of equipment works, it operates and performs a particular function.
If an idea, system, or way of doing something works, it is successful, effective, or satisfactory.
If a drug or medicine works, it produces a particular physical effect.
If something works in your favour, it helps you in some way. If something works to your disadvantage, it causes problems for you in some way.
If something or someone works their magic or works their charms on a person, they have a powerful positive effect on them.
If your mind or brain is working, you are thinking about something or trying to solve a problem.
If you work on an assumption or idea, you act as if it were true or base other ideas on it, until you have more information.
If you work a particular area or type of place, you travel around that area or work in those places as part of your job, for example trying to sell something there.
If you work someone, you make them spend time and effort doing a particular activity or job.
If someone, often a politician or entertainer, works a crowd, they create a good relationship with the people in the crowd and get their support or interest.
When people work the land, they do all the tasks involved in growing crops.
When a mine is worked, minerals such as coal or gold are removed from it.
If you work a machine or piece of equipment, you use or control it.
If something works into a particular state or condition, it gradually moves so that it is in that state or condition.
If you work a substance such as dough or clay, you keep pressing it to make it have a particular texture.
If you work a material such as metal, leather, or stone, you cut, sew, or shape it in order to make something or to create a design.
If you work with a particular substance or material, you use it in order to make something or to create a design.
If you work a part of your body, or if it works, you move it.
A works is a place where something is manufactured or where an industrial process is carried out. Works is used to refer to one or to more than one of these places.
Works are activities such as digging the ground or building on a large scale.
You can say the works after listing things such as someone’s possessions or requirements, to emphasize that they possess or require everything you can think of in a particular category.
If someone is at work they are doing their job or are busy doing a particular activity.
If a force or process is at work, it is having a particular influence or effect.
If you say that you will have your work cut out to do something, you mean that it will be a very difficult task.
If something is in the works, it has already been planned or begun.

You can use work to talk about how easily or quickly a particular task is done. For example, if a person or thing makes short work of doing something or makes light work of it, they do it quickly and easily.
If you describe someone as a nasty piece of work, you think they are very unpleasant or cruel.
If you put someone to work or set them to work, you give them a job or task to do.
If you work your way somewhere, you move or progress there slowly, and with a lot of effort or work.
You can say to someone ’ nice work ’ or ’ good work ’ in order to thank or praise them for doing something well or quickly.
A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.
Workers are people who are employed in industry or business and who are not managers.
You can use worker to say how well or badly someone works.

Chinesesense: (某一国家或地区的)劳动力，劳动人口；
(某公司的)全体员工，职工总数；
Englishsense: The workforce is the total number of people in a country or region who are physically able to do a job and are available for work.
The workforce is the total number of people who are employed by a particular company.

Chinesesense: 上班时间的;工作时间的；
人生阶段工作的，处于就业年龄的；
(某一地区的人口)就业的，处于就业年龄的；
条件或常规做法工作的，工作上的；
关系工作上的，同事间的；
(农场或企业)经营性的，营利性的；
(机器零部件)能运转的，用于操作的；
(设备、组织或系统的)工作方式，运行方式；
Englishsense: Working people have jobs which they are paid to do.
Working people are ordinary people who do not have professional or very highly paid jobs.
A working day or week is the amount of time during a normal day or week which you spend doing your job.
A working day is a day on which people go to work.
Your working life is the period of your life in which you have a job or are of a suitable age to have a job.
The working population of an area consists of all the people in that area who have a job or who are of a suitable age to have a job.
Working conditions or practices are ones which you have in your job.
Working clothes are designed for doing work in, and are intended to be practical rather than attractive.
A working relationship is the relationship you have with someone when you work with them.
A working farm or business exists to do normal work and make a profit, and not only for tourists or as someone’s hobby.
The working parts of a machine are the parts which move and operate the machine, in contrast to the outer case or container in which they are enclosed.
A working model is one that has parts that move.
A working knowledge or majority is not very great, but is enough to be useful.
A working title or definition is one which you use when starting to make or do something, but which you are likely to change or improve.
The workings of a piece of equipment, an organization, or a system are the ways in which it operates and the processes which are involved in it.
You can use workings to refer to deep tunnels or holes which have been dug in the ground in order to remove coal, metal, or stone.
A workout is a period of physical exercise or training.
Your workplace is the place where you work.

Chinesesense: (尤指使用到木材或金属的)车间，工场，作坊；
Englishsense: A workshop is a period of discussion or practical work on a particular subject in which a group of people share their knowledge or experience.
A workshop is a building which contains tools or machinery for making or repairing things, especially using wood or metal.

Chinesesense: 世界上最重要的;举世瞩目的；
(指某一群国家或历史时期)世界，国家，时代；
有某种特色的地方，环境；某种生活的世界，境况；
让…感觉好很多；对…大有好处；
(尤用于强调惊讶或愤怒)究竟，到底；
在理想或完美的世界中；在理想状况下；
认为自己生来就该享福；
阅历丰富的人;见过世面的人；老成稳重的人；
极好的;一流的；非常棒的；
在自己的世界里;在自己的小天地里；
发迹/落魄;飞黄腾达/潦倒；
Englishsense: The world is the planet that we live on.
The world refers to all the people who live on this planet, and our societies, institutions, and ways of life.
You can use world to describe someone or something that is one of the most important or significant of its kind on earth.
You can use world in expressions such as the Arab world, the western world, and the ancient world to refer to a particular group of countries or a particular period in history.
Someone’s world is the life they lead, the people they have contact with, and the things they experience.
You can use world to refer to a particular field of activity, and the people involved in it.
You can use world to refer to a place or way of life by describing its strongest features.
You can use world in expressions such as this world, the next world, and the world to come to refer to the state of being alive or a state of existence after death.
You can use world to refer to a particular group of living things, for example the animal world, the plant world, and the insect world.
A world is a planet.
If you say that two people or things are worlds apart, you are emphasizing that they are very different from each other.
If you say that someone has the best of both worlds, you mean that they have only the benefits of two things and none of the disadvantages.
If a woman brings a child into the world, she gives birth to it.
If you say that there is a world of difference between one thing and another, you are emphasizing that they are very different from each other.
If you say that you would not do something for the world, you are emphasizing that you definitely would not do it.
If you say that something has done someone the world of good or a world of good, you mean that it has made them feel better or improved their life.
You use in the world to emphasize a statement that you are making.
You can use in the world in expressions such as what in the world and who in the world to emphasize a question, especially when expressing surprise or anger.
You can use in an ideal world or in a perfect world when you are talking about things that you would like to happen, although you realize that they are not likely to happen.
If you say that someone thinks that the world owes them a living, you are criticizing them because they think it is their right to have a comfortable life without having to make any effort at all.

If you say that someone is a man of the world or a woman of the world, you mean that they are experienced and know about the practical or social aspects of life, and are not easily shocked by immoral or dishonest actions.
If you say that something is out of this world, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good or impressive.
You can use the outside world to refer to all the people who do not live in a particular place or who are not involved in a particular situation.
If you say that something happens or exists the world over, you mean that it happens or exists in every part of the world.
If you say that someone is in a world of their own, you mean that they seem not to notice other people or the things going on around them.
If you think the world of someone, you like them or care about them very much.

If you say that someone has gone up in the world, you mean they have become richer or have a higher social status than before. If you say they have come down in the world, you mean they have become poorer or have a lower social status.
A world-class sports player, performer, or organization is one of the best in the world.

Chinesesense: 遍及全世界地;世界各地地；
Englishsense: If something exists or happens worldwide, it exists or happens throughout the world.

Chinesesense: (动物或人体内的)寄生虫，肠虫；
艰难地移动；蜷缩着身子走；
(通常为欺骗别人或得到好处)逐渐取得(成功或好感)；
可怜虫;软蛋;卑鄙的家伙；
蠕虫被踩，也会翻腾；兔子急了也咬人；
Englishsense: A worm is a small animal with a long thin body, no bones and no legs.
If animals or people have worms, worms are living in their intestines.
If you worm an animal, you give it medicine in order to kill the worms that are living in its intestines.
If you worm your way somewhere, you move there with difficulty, twisting or bending your body or making it narrow.

If you say that someone is worming their way to success, or is worming their way into someone else’s affection, you disapprove of the way that they are gradually making someone trust them or like them, often in order to deceive them or gain some advantage.
If you call a person a worm, you are insulting them by saying that they have a very weak or unpleasant character and you have no respect for them.
A worm is a computer program that contains a virus which duplicates itself many times in a network.

If you say that someone is opening a can of worms, you are warning them that they are planning to do or talk about something which is much more complicated, unpleasant, or difficult than they realize and which might be better left alone.
If you say that the worm turns, you mean that someone who usually obeys another person or accepts their bad behaviour unexpectedly starts resisting that person or expresses their anger.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Englishsense: When you are worried, you are unhappy because you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen in the future.

Chinesesense: 使人担心(或发愁)的问题；烦心事；
表示自己并不烦恼或生气别担心；没关系；
Englishsense: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.
If someone or something worries you, they make you anxious because you keep thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might be connected with them.
If someone or something does not worry you, you do not dislike them or you are not annoyed by them.
Worry is the state or feeling of anxiety and unhappiness caused by the problems that you have or by thinking about unpleasant things that might happen.
A worry is a problem that you keep thinking about and that makes you unhappy.
You say not to worry to someone to indicate that you are not upset or angry when something has gone wrong.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 令人担心的;使人发愁的；
Englishsense: If something is worrying, it causes people to worry. See usage note at: worried

Chinesesense: 使变得更坏(或更糟);使恶化；
Englishsense: If a bad situation worsens or if something worsens it, it becomes more difficult, unpleasant, or unacceptable.
If you worship a god, you show your respect to the god, for example by saying prayers.
If you worship someone or something, you love them or admire them very much.

POS: COMB in QUANT 与数量词构成的词
COMB in QUANT 与数量词构成的词
Chinesesense: 拼命地; 全力以赴地；热情高涨地；
尽可能地利用;充分利用；
(尤为避免显得傲慢)不管好坏，不管有没有用；
(行为或活动)值得…去做，对…有好处；
Englishsense: Worth combines with amounts of money, so that when you talk about a particular amount of money ’s worth of something, you mean the quantity of it that you can buy for that amount of money.

Worth combines with time expressions, so you can use worth when you are saying how long an amount of something will last. For example, a week’s worth of food is the amount of food that will last you for a week.
Someone’s worth is the value, usefulness, or importance that they are considered to have.
If you do something for all you are worth, you do it with a lot of energy and enthusiasm.
If someone does something for all it is worth, they do it as much as possible and for as long as they can get benefit from it.

If you add for what it’s worth to something that you say, you are suggesting that what you are saying or referring to may not be very valuable or helpful, especially because you do not want to appear arrogant.
If an action or activity is worth someone’s while, it will be helpful, useful, or enjoyable for them if they do it, even though it requires some effort.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 无价值的;不值钱的;没用处的；
Englishsense: Something that is worthless is of no real value or use.
Someone who is described as worthless is considered to have no good qualities or skills.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 有价值的;令人愉快的；值得花费时间或金钱、精力的；
Englishsense: If something is worthwhile, it is enjoyable or useful, and worth the time, money, or effort that is spent on it.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 值得尊敬的;可敬的；令人称许的；
Englishsense: If a person or thing is worthy of something, they deserve it because they have the qualities or abilities required.
A worthy person or thing is approved of by most people in society and considered to be morally respectable or correct.

Chinesesense: (表示曾经相信、希望或期待)将，将会；
(表示可能出现的情况的结果或影响)会，将会；
(would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示有充分理由认为或猜测是某种情况)肯定，一定，应该；
(用于if，unless等引导的条件状语从句的主句，表示认为某事不大可能发生)就，该；
(表示尽管付出很大努力却没有发生)就不，偏不；
(尤与like, love 和 wish 连用，表示想做某事或拥有某物，或希望某事发生)要，会；
(用于带if从句的疑问句中，表示请求许可做某事)会；
(通常在疑问句中与 like 连用，表示礼貌地给予或邀请)；
(通常用于疑问句中，表示礼貌地请求某人做某事)请；
(用于批评，表示对某人做某事并不感到意外，此时 would 须重读)；
(would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示发表看法或了解他人是否赞同自己的看法，尤用于对自己的话没有把握时)；
(用于以随便的口气向人提出建议)我就会；
(用于否定句，与 guess, know 等动词连用，表示某事不明显，尤用于某事令人吃惊时)；
(表示某事过去惯常发生, 而现在不再发生了)就，会；
(would have 与过去分词连用，表示某个时间前可能发生的事情)就，会；
(would have 与过去分词连用，表示过去可能发生的事情的结果或影响)就，会；
(通常用于否定句，批评某人所为，表示不满)不会；
Englishsense: You use would when you are saying what someone believed, hoped, or expected to happen or be the case.
You use would when saying what someone intended to do.
You use would when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible situation.
You use would, or would have with a past participle, to indicate that you are assuming or guessing that something is true, because you have good reasons for thinking it.
You use would in the main clause of some ’if’ and ’unless’ sentences to indicate something you consider to be fairly unlikely to happen.
You use would to say that someone was willing to do something. You use would not to indicate that they refused to do something.
You use would not to indicate that something did not happen, often in spite of a lot of effort.
You use would, especially with ’like’, ’love’, and ’wish’, when saying that someone wants to do or have a particular thing or wants a particular thing to happen. would rather
You use would with ’if’ clauses in questions when you are asking for permission to do something.
You use would, usually in questions with ’like’, when you are making a polite offer or invitation.
You use would, usually in questions, when you are politely asking someone to do something.
You say that someone would do something when it is typical of them and you are critical of it. You emphasize the word would when you use it in this way.

You use would, or sometimes would have with a past participle, when you are expressing your opinion about something or seeing if people agree with you, especially when you are uncertain about what you are saying.
You use I would when you are giving someone advice in an informal way.
You use you would in negative sentences with verbs such as ’guess’ and ’know’ when you want to say that something is not obvious, especially something surprising.
You use would to talk about something which happened regularly in the past but which no longer happens.
You use would have with a past participle when you are saying what was likely to have happened by a particular time.
You use would have with a past participle when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible event in the past.
If you say that someone would have liked or preferred something, you mean that they wanted to do it or have it but were unable to.
You use would, usually in negative sentences, to criticize something that someone has done and to express your disapproval of it.
If you say ’ would that ’ something were the case, you are saying that you wish it were the case.
You can use would-be to describe someone who wants or attempts to do a particular thing. For example, a would-be writer is someone who wants to be a writer.

Chinesesense: (刀、枪或其他武器所致的)创伤，伤口；
武器或其他利器伤害，使受伤；
失败或被羞辱后舔伤，重整旗鼓；
揭旧伤疤(指重提他人不愿提起的痛苦往事)；
Englishsense: A wound is damage to part of your body, especially a cut or a hole in your flesh, which is caused by a gun, knife, or other weapon.
If a weapon or something sharp wounds you, it damages your body.
A wound is a lasting bad effect on someone’s mind or feelings caused by a very upsetting experience.
If you are wounded by what someone says or does, your feelings are deeply hurt.
If you say that someone is licking their wounds, you mean that they are recovering after being defeated or made to feel ashamed or unhappy.
Something that opens old wounds or reopens old wounds reminds someone about an upsetting experience in the past which they would prefer to forget.

Chinesesense: (表示赞叹、非常吃惊或喜悦)哇，呀；
Englishsense: You can say ’ wow ’ when you are very impressed, surprised, or pleased.
You say that someone wows people when they give an impressive performance and fill people with enthusiasm and admiration.

Chinesesense: 用(手臂、指头或腿)围紧;用…绕住；
保密，秘而不宣常指待日后宣布；
Englishsense: When you wrap something, you fold paper or cloth tightly round it to cover it completely, for example in order to protect it or so that you can give it to someone as a present.
Wrap is the material that something is wrapped in.
When you wrap something such as a piece of paper or cloth round another thing, you put it around it.
If someone wraps their arms, fingers, or legs around something, they put them firmly around it.
A wrap is a piece of clothing which women wear round their shoulders, either to keep them warm when wearing an evening dress, or for decoration over a coat.
If you keep something under wraps, you keep it secret, often until you are ready to announce it at some time in the future.

Chinesesense: 失事的船只(或汽车、飞机);损毁的建筑；
精疲力竭的人;身体状况极差的人；
Englishsense: To wreck something means to completely destroy or ruin it.
If a ship is wrecked, it is damaged so much that it sinks or can no longer sail.
A wreck is something such as a ship, car, plane, or building which has been destroyed, usually in an accident.
A wreck is an accident in which a moving vehicle hits something and is damaged or destroyed.
If you say that someone is a wreck, you mean that they are very exhausted or unhealthy.

Chinesesense: (飞机、汽车等的)残骸；建筑物等的废墟；
(计划等失败或遭到破坏后的)残余；
Englishsense: When something such as a plane, car, or building has been destroyed, you can refer to what remains as wreckage or the wreckage.
If something such as a plan has failed or been spoilt completely, you can refer to what remains as the wreckage of it.

Chinesesense: 试图解决;绞尽脑汁处理；
Englishsense: When you wrestle with a difficult problem, you try to deal with it.
If you wrestle with someone, you fight them by forcing them into painful positions or throwing them to the ground, rather than by hitting them. Some people wrestle as a sport.
If you wrestle a person or thing somewhere, you move them there using a lot of force, for example by twisting a part of someone’s body into a painful position.
Wrestling is a sport in which two people wrestle and try to throw each other to the ground.

Chinesesense: 布或纸的褶皱，皱痕，褶子；
Englishsense: Wrinkles are lines which form on someone’s face as they grow old.
When someone’s skin wrinkles or when something wrinkles it, lines start to form in it because the skin is getting old or damaged.
A wrinkle is a raised fold in a piece of cloth or paper that spoils its appearance.
If cloth wrinkles, or if someone or something wrinkles it, it gets folds or lines in it.
When you wrinkle your nose or forehead, or when it wrinkles, you tighten the muscles in your face so that the skin folds.
Your wrist is the part of your body between your hand and your arm which bends when you move your hand.

Chinesesense: 写作，著述通常以出版为目的；
写信;给…写信(美国英语亦可用 write someone)；
Englishsense: When you write something on a surface, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers on the surface.
If you write something such as a book, a poem, or a piece of music, you create it and record it on paper or perhaps on a computer.
Someone who writes creates books, stories, or articles, usually for publication.

When you write to someone or write them a letter, you give them information, ask them something, or express your feelings in a letter. In American English, you can also write someone. nothing to write home about
If someone writes that something is the case, they say it in a letter, book, or article.
When someone writes something such as a cheque, receipt, or prescription, they put the necessary information on it and usually sign it.
If you write to a computer or a disk, you record data on it.

Chinesesense: 特定文章、报告、信件或故事的作者，撰写者；
Englishsense: A writer is a person who writes books, stories, or articles as a job.
The writer of a particular article, report, letter, or story is the person who wrote it.

Chinesesense: (尤指评论语言风格时的)文字作品，文章；
(尤指为赚取稿费而进行的)写作；
(尤指某一作者有关某一专题的全部)著作，作品；
凶兆毕现；有大难临头的预兆；
Englishsense: Writing is something that has been written or printed.
You can refer to any piece of written work as writing, especially when you are considering the style of language used in it.
Writing is the activity of writing, especially of writing books for money.
Your writing is the way that you write with a pen or pencil, which can usually be recognized as belonging to you.
An author’s writings are all the things that he or she has written, especially on a particular subject.
If you say that the writing is on the wall, you mean that there are clear signs that a situation is going to become very difficult or unpleasant.

Chinesesense: (协议、规定、法律等)成文的，书面的；
Englishsense: A written test or piece of work is one which involves writing rather than doing something practical or giving spoken answers.
A written agreement, rule, or law has been officially written down.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: (决定、选择、行动等)错误的，不适当的；
不正确的;与事实不符的；
机器设备出毛病的，出故障的；
(通常用于生气时)你想错了／你听错了；
做某事是不对的，不道德的；
(活动或行动)不道德的，不可取的；
不公平行为;不道德行为；
不能被社会所接受的;不可取的；
Englishsense: If you say there is something wrong, you mean there is something unsatisfactory about the situation, person, or thing you are talking about.
If you choose the wrong thing, person, or method, you make a mistake and do not choose the one that you really want.
If something such as a decision, choice, or action is the wrong one, it is not the best or most suitable one.
If something is wrong, it is incorrect and not in accordance with the facts.
If something is wrong or goes wrong with a machine or piece of equipment, it stops working properly.
If you are wrong about something, what you say or think about it is not correct.
You can use wrong in expressions such as you thought wrong and you heard wrong to tell someone that what they thought or were told is incorrect, usually when you are annoyed.
If you think that someone was wrong to do something, you think that they should not have done it because it was bad or immoral.
Wrong is used to refer to activities or actions that are considered to be morally bad and unacceptable.
A wrong is an unfair or immoral action.
If someone wrongs you, they treat you in an unfair way.
You use wrong to describe something which is not thought to be socially acceptable or desirable.
You say ’ Don’t get me wrong ’ when you want to make sure that someone does not get an incorrect idea about what you are doing or saying, or about why you are doing or saying it.
If a situation goes wrong, it stops progressing in the way that you expected or intended, and becomes much worse.
If someone who is involved in an argument or dispute has behaved in a way which is morally or legally wrong, you can say that they are in the wrong.
If someone says ’ Two wrongs don’t make a right ’, they mean that you should not do harm to a person who has done harm to you, even if you think that person deserves it.

Chinesesense: 违法行为;犯罪行为;不道德行为；
Englishsense: Wrongdoing is behaviour that is illegal or immoral.
A yacht is a large boat with sails or a motor, used for racing or pleasure trips.

Chinesesense: 码长度单位，等于36英寸或约91.4厘米；
进行某项作业的区域，场地，工场；
Englishsense: A yard is a unit of length equal to thirty-six inches or approximately 91.4 centimetres.
A yard is a flat area of concrete or stone that is next to a building and often has a wall around it.
You can refer to a large open area where a particular type of work is done as a yard.
A yard is a piece of land next to someone’s house, with grass and plants growing in it.

Chinesesense: 你们，汝等，尔辈[you的过时用法，诗歌或宗教用语] ；
Englishsense: Ye is an old-fashioned, poetic, or religious word for you when you are talking to more than one person.
Ye is sometimes used in imitation of an old written form of the word ’the’.
Yeah means yes.

Chinesesense: 学年英国和美国的学年从9月开始；
在某地或做某事的年头，时期；
他那样年纪的男子/她那样年纪的女子；
经历或衣着使显得年老，使觉得老迈；
经历或衣着使显得年轻，使觉得年轻；
Englishsense: A year is a period of twelve months or 365 or 366 days, beginning on the first of January and ending on the thirty-first of December.
A year is any period of twelve months.
Year is used to refer to the age of a person. For example, if someone or something is twenty years old or twenty years of age, they have lived or existed for twenty years.

A school year or academic year is the period of time in each twelve months when schools or universities are open and students are studying there. In Britain and the United States, the school year starts in September.
You can refer to someone who is, for example, in their first year at school or university as a first year.
A financial or business year is an exact period of twelve months which businesses or institutions use as a basis for organizing their finances.
You can use years to emphasize that you are referring to a long time.
You can refer to the time you spend in a place or doing an activity as your years there or your years of doing that activity.
If something happens year after year, it happens regularly every year.
If something changes year by year, it changes gradually each year.
If something happens year in, year out, it happens every year without changing and is often boring.
You can say a man of his years or a woman of her years to refer to that person’s age in relation to something else you are talking about.
If you say that something such as an experience or a way of dressing has put years on someone, you mean that it has made them look or feel much older.
If you say something happens all year round or all the year round, it happens continually throughout the year.
If you say that something such as an experience or a way of dressing has taken years off someone, you mean that it has made them look or feel much younger.

Chinesesense: 一年一度的;每年一次的；
Englishsense: A yearly event happens once a year or every year.
You use yearly to describe something such as an amount that relates to a period of one year.
If someone yearns for something that they are unlikely to get, they want it very much.
Year-round is used to describe something that happens, exists, or is done throughout the year.

Chinesesense: 常指因激动、生气或痛苦叫喊，大喊，吼叫；
Englishsense: If you yell, you shout loudly, usually because you are excited, angry, or in pain.
A yell is a loud shout given by someone who is afraid or in pain.
Something that is yellow is the colour of lemons, butter, or the middle part of an egg.
If something yellows, it becomes yellow in colour, often because it is old.
Yep means yes.

Chinesesense: 用于肯定回答是的，对的；
用于接受提议或请求，或表示许可可以，好的；
用于告诉对方其所说的话正确对，是的；
用于表示准备或愿意作出应答什么事，来啦；
用于表示同意、接受或理解前一讲话者的话是这样，确实如此；
用于鼓励某人继续讲往下说，接着呢；
[常接but，用于礼貌地引出与前一讲话者意见不同的话] ；
用于表示前一讲话者的否定陈述或问题是错误的不是，不对；
用于暗示不赞成或不同意前面讲话者的话，尤用于表示厌烦真的吗，行啦；
用于表示刚刚想起忘记的事情对了；
用于强调并确认自己的陈述对，一点没错；
Englishsense: You use yes to give a positive response to a question.
You use yes to accept an offer or request, or to give permission.
You use yes to tell someone that what they have said is correct.
You use yes to show that you are ready or willing to speak to the person who wants to speak to you, for example when you are answering a telephone or a knock at your door.
You use yes to indicate that you agree with, accept, or understand what the previous speaker has said.
You use yes to encourage someone to continue speaking.
You use yes, usually followed by ’but’, as a polite way of introducing what you want to say when you disagree with something the previous speaker has just said.
You use yes to say that a negative statement or question that the previous speaker has made is wrong or untrue.
You can use yes to suggest that you do not believe or agree with what the previous speaker has said, especially when you want to express your annoyance about it.
You use yes to indicate that you had forgotten something and have just remembered it.
You use yes to emphasize and confirm a statement that you are making.
You say yes and no in reply to a question when you cannot give a definite answer, because in some ways the answer is yes and in other ways the answer is no.
A yes is a person who has answered ’yes’ to a question or who has voted in favour of something, or the answer or vote they have made.

Chinesesense: 过去；尤指不久前，近日，日前；
Englishsense: You use yesterday to refer to the day before today.
You can refer to the past, especially the recent past, as yesterday.

Chinesesense: 用于否定句中表示某事尚未发生但有可能发生，在疑问句中用来询问某事是否已发生。英国英语中，表示此义时通常不与一般过去时连用尚未，还，仍；
与谈论过去的否定句连用，表示当时并非如此还，尚未；
用于否定句，表示某事以后会做但现在不该或不能做还，尚；
用于最高级后，表示到目前为止最差或最好迄今为止，到目前为止；
用于表示仍有可能还是，仍然；
用于表示一段时间的表达后，表示时间的延续还要，还；
表示从未做过某事，尤指惊人的事或坏事还未，尚未；
用于引出颇令人惊讶的事实可是却，却又；
用于强调，尤指相对于以前同类事物更为极端等还要，甚至，更；
用于否定句迄今为止，目前为止；
Englishsense: You use yet in negative statements to indicate that something has not happened up to the present time, although it probably will happen. You can also use yet in questions to ask if something has happened up to the present time. In British English the simple past tense is not normally used with this meaning of ’yet’.
You use yet with a negative statement when you are talking about the past, to report something that was not the case then, although it became the case later.
If you say that something should not or cannot be done yet, you mean that it should not or cannot be done now, although it will have to be done at a later time.
You use yet after a superlative to indicate, for example, that something is the worst or the best of its kind up to the present time.
You can use yet to say that there is still a possibility that something will happen.
You can use yet after expressions which refer to a period of time, when you want to say how much longer a situation will continue for.
If you say that you have yet to do something, you mean that you have never done it, especially when this is surprising or bad.
You can use yet to introduce a fact which is rather surprising after the previous fact you have just mentioned.
You can use yet to emphasize a word, especially when you are saying that something is surprising because it is more extreme than previous things of its kind, or a further case of them.
You use as yet with negative statements to describe a situation that has existed up until the present time.

Chinesesense: 农作物或牲畜的产量，产出；
税收或投资产生，带来收益或效益；
产生[结果]; 得出信息；
Englishsense: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them.
If you yield something that you have control of or responsibility for, you allow someone else to have control or responsibility for it
If one thing yields to another thing, it is replaced by this other thing.
If a moving person or a vehicle yields, they slow down or stop in order to allow other people or vehicles to pass in front of them.
If something yields, it breaks or moves position because force or pressure has been put on it.
If an area of land yields a particular amount of a crop, this is the amount that is produced. You can also say that a number of animals yield a particular amount of meat.
A yield is the amount of food produced on an area of land or by a number of animals.
If a tax or investment yields an amount of money or profit, this money or profit is obtained from it.
A yield is the amount of money or profit produced by an investment.
If something yields a result or piece of information, it produces it. [V n]

Chinesesense: 瑜伽派起源于印度、崇尚身体锻炼和冥想的哲学派别；
Englishsense: Yoga is a type of exercise in which you move your body into various positions in order to become more fit or flexible, to improve your breathing, and to relax your mind.
Yoga is a philosophy which first developed in India, in which physical exercises and meditation are believed to help people to become calmer and united in spirit with God.
Yogurt is a food in the form of a thick, slightly sour liquid that is made by adding bacteria to milk. A yogurt is a small pot of yogurt.

Chinesesense: 你,您,你们可用于名词前指定谈话对象；
用于口语和非正式书面语中表示泛指你，任何人；
[某些方言中指两个或多个人时有时用yous代替you] 你们；
Englishsense: A speaker or writer uses you to refer to the person or people that they are talking or writing to. It is possible to use you before a noun to make it clear which group of people you are talking to.
In spoken English and informal written English, you is sometimes used to refer to people in general.
In some dialects of English, yous is sometimes used instead of ’you’ when talking to two or more people.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 年幼的;幼小的;未成熟的；
显得年轻的;显得岁数不大的；
Englishsense: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature.
You use young to describe a time when a person or thing was young.
Someone who is young in appearance or behaviour looks or behaves as if they are young.
The young of an animal are its babies.
Young people, especially children, are sometimes referred to as youngsters.

Chinesesense: 有时用于口语和非正式书面语中表示泛指你的，任何人的；
[口语中有时用于typical, normal等形容词前表示典型] ；
Englishsense: A speaker or writer uses your to indicate that something belongs or relates to the person or people that they are talking or writing to.
In spoken English and informal written English, your is sometimes used to indicate that something belongs to or relates to people in general.
In spoken English, a speaker sometimes uses your before an adjective such as ’typical’ or ’normal’ to indicate that the thing referred to is a typical example of its type.

Chinesesense: 用于书信结尾的签名前你的/您的诚挚的/您的忠实的；
Englishsense: A speaker or writer uses yours to refer to something that belongs or relates to the person or people that they are talking or writing to.
People write yours, yours sincerely, or yours faithfully at the end of a letter before they sign their name. yours truly

Chinesesense: 你自己;您自己;你们自己；
用于强调所指对象你自己，你本人，你们自己，你们本人；
[代替作宾语的you，用于强调或表示礼貌] 你自己，你们自己；
Englishsense: A speaker or writer uses yourself to refer to the person that they are talking or writing to. Yourself is used when the object of a verb or preposition refers to the same person as the subject of the verb.
You use yourself to emphasize the person that you are referring to.
You use yourself instead of ’you’ for emphasis or in order to be more polite when ’you’ is the object of a verb or preposition. by yourself

Chinesesense: 新闻用语，尤指惹麻烦的青年，小伙子；
Englishsense: Someone’s youth is the period of their life during which they are a child, before they are a fully mature adult.
Youth is the quality or state of being young.
Journalists often refer to young men as youths, especially when they are reporting that the young men have caused trouble.
The youth are young people considered as a group.

POS: ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
Chinesesense: 年轻的;显得年轻的;富有青春活力的;朝气蓬勃的；
Englishsense: Someone who is youthful behaves as if they are young or younger than they really are.
Zero is the number 0.
Zero is a temperature of 0˚. It is freezing point on the Centigrade and Celsius scales, and 32˚ below freezing point on the Fahrenheit scale.
You can use zero to say that there is none at all of the thing mentioned.

A zip or zip fastener is a device used to open and close parts of clothes and bags. It consists of two rows of metal or plastic teeth which separate or fasten together as you pull a small tag along them.
When you zip something, you fasten it using a zip.
To zip a computer file means to compress it so that it needs less space for storage on disk and can be transmitted more quickly.
If you say that something or someone zips somewhere, you mean that they move there very quickly.
If you say that someone or something has zip, you mean that they show a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

Chinesesense: 有某些特色或特点的地区，地带，区域；
将…划为特殊区域;指定…为某项用途区域；
Englishsense: A zone is an area that has particular features or characteristics.
If an area of land is zoned, it is formally set aside for a particular purpose.

POS: N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 可数名词；名称名词
Englishsense: A zoo is a park where live animals are kept so that people can look at them

Chinesesense: 价格或销量飙升，急剧增长，猛涨；
Englishsense: If you zoom somewhere, you go there very quickly.
If prices or sales zoom, they increase greatly in a very short time.
A zoom is the same as a zoom lens.
